docs.title: resonances
docs.text:
resonances is an open-source Python package that finds small bodies in resonances and decides, from a numerical integration, whether they really are in them. It handles

  • mean-motion resonances: two-body (including retrograde orbits and co-orbitals, 1:1) and three-body;
  • secular resonances: linear and non-linear, with apsidal and nodal frequencies (ν6, z1, …);
  • Lidov-Kozai (ZLK) resonances: libration of the argument of perihelion.

For each body and resonance the package integrates the orbit with the planets (REBOUND), builds the resonant angle, and gives it a verdict: a status, the geometry of the angle, the physical origin of a libration, a confidence level and the next action. The data come from NASA Horizons, AstDyS or the Minor Planet Center (MPCORB). The finders, catalogs and simulation workflow target the Solar System.

docs.title: The statuses
docs.text:
status what it means physically resonant the resonant angle librates over the whole integration, with the evidence its type requires (MMR: the pendulum checks; secular: the angle's geometry; ZLK: the free-ω gate). For an MMR the dynamical origin may still be unknown: reason and libration_origin say whether it was measured transient the angle librates in episodes (a capture, an exit, or both) that do not cover the record as one sustained libration; circulation, a drift or a change of regime may separate them near_separatrix the angle stalls or slips at the top of its own potential well: the orbit sits on the border of the resonance non_resonant the angle circulates, or it is bounded by something else: the perihelion precession, another resonance, a too weak resonant term uncertain the record cannot decide: too short, or the physics contradicts the geometry invalid the record cannot be measured: the output step aliases the angle, or the orbit is unphysical

How each status is reached, with the formulas and thresholds, is explained in How the status is determined; the Gallery shows one example of each.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Installation and the Quick start: check one asteroid in three lines.
  • Command line: the resonances command and its options.
  • Simulations, bodies, resonances and Examples: the main objects and practical recipes (catalogs, clones, many bodies, restore).
  • Configuration: every option; Output data: every column.
  • How to read the figures: every panel of the verdict figures.
  • Rule index: every rule of the classifier, with its settings.
  • Using with AI agents: resonances skill install gives a coding agent (Claude Code and others) the package's skill: how to set up runs and how to read the verdicts.
import resonances

sim = resonances.check(463, '4J-2S-1', integration_years=2_000)  # (463) Lola in 4J-2S-1; 100_000 years for a verdict
sim.run()

What changed in 1.0.0, and how to update code written for 0.5.x: Changelog.

docs.title: Using the package with AI agents
docs.text:
The package ships an agent skill: instructions for a coding agent (Claude Code and other agents that read Agent Skills) on how to set up a resonance study, run it and read its verdicts. Install it into your project:

resonances skill install            # ./.claude/skills/resonances
resonances skill install --user     # ~/.claude/skills/resonances, for every project
resonances skill install --force    # replace an installed copy, e.g. after upgrading the package

--path DIR installs into another project folder. An existing copy is never replaced without --force. The agent loads the skill in its next session; ask it, for example, "check 463 in 4J-2S-1 over 100 kyr and tell me whether it is resonant", or "why is this row uncertain with short_period_aliased?".

docs.title: What the skill contains
docs.text:
• SKILL.md: the workflow and the judgment: which entry point to use (check, find, Simulation), how to plan the span, the output step and the integrator (dry-run), clones, batch runs and restore, what each verdict field claims and does not claim, the usual traps, and a checklist before a status is reported to a person.
  • references/: a copy of the pages of this documentation, generated from docs/ (the installed package has no docs/). The formulas, columns and settings are therefore never written twice.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text: The references are generated by docs/tools/build_skill.py (make skill); the list of copied pages is PAGES in that script. Snippet includes are replaced by the code of docs/examples/, and links to pages that are not copied or to images point to the published site. A fast test (tests/resonances/skills/test_skill.py) fails when the references are out of date with docs/, so after editing a page run make skill. When a change alters the interface, the statuses, reasons or caps, the settings or the output layout, update resonances/skills/resonances/SKILL.md too.

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text: The thresholds of the analysis are conventions. They are chosen and tested on a benchmark of real integrations whose verdicts were given by eye, from the one-page figures; the labels are the visual verdicts of the package's author. The benchmark lives in benchmark/ (tracked: the catalog, the labels, the tools); the series and figures are outside git, in benchmark/data/ (RESONANCES_BENCHMARK_DATA overrides the folder).

docs.title: What it holds
docs.text:
Each example is one body in one resonance, with its saved series (series.csv.gz), the run's metadata and, where saved, the planets. Nothing is integrated to classify it again.

type examples two-body MMR (mmr2) 289 three-body MMR (mmr3) 178 co-orbital (coorbital) 265 secular 64 Lidov-Kozai (zlk) 37

The 732 MMR and co-orbital examples cover 601 bodies, from near-Earth space to the trans-Neptunian region.

benchmark/candidates.csv is the working catalog (the visual verdict where one was given, the sources), benchmark/labels.csv the labels, benchmark/DECISIONS.md the decisions on disputed cases. Labels proposed by a program or a language model are marked as such and never count as labels. The examples of every status shown in the Gallery are benchmark examples.

docs.title: Reclassifying
docs.text:
uv run python benchmark/tools/reclassify.py --out benchmark/data/<run>                    # MMR and co-orbital
uv run python benchmark/tools/reclassify_secular_zlk.py --out benchmark/data/<run>-secular-zlk
uv run python benchmark/tools/known_disagreements.py <run> --secular-zlk <run>-secular-zlk  # against the labels
uv run python benchmark/tools/episode_expectations.py <run>                                # the episode cases

reclassify.py writes summary.csv (with the derived subresonance rows), mmr_numbers.csv, episodes.csv, candidates.csv, constants.csv and agreement.csv into the run folder. Use a folder of your own for --out. The option --figures draws the combined figure into each example's folder in benchmark/data/examples; the documentation's figures are drawn elsewhere by make docs-figures (see Gallery). Workers: --workers auto (BENCHMARK_WORKERS, else min(CPUs − 2, available RAM / 3 GB, 8)); about 5–7 minutes for the 727 MMR examples with 4 workers, seconds for the secular and ZLK ones.

docs.title: The two gates of make test-benchmark
docs.text:
make test-benchmark reclassifies every saved example into benchmark/data/test-benchmark (and test-benchmark-secular-zlk) and runs two checks on that run.

  1. Agreement with the labels. Every disagreement (example, field) with the labels (status, angle_status, confidence where given) and with the unambiguous verdicts of candidates.csv must be listed in benchmark/KNOWN_DISAGREEMENTS.csv. A new disagreement, a listed one that now agrees, and a listed one whose values changed all fail the gate. The list's category and reason are explanations, not labels.
  2. Episodes. benchmark/EPISODE_EXPECTATIONS.csv holds 177 cases of episodes named in the visual review, each with machine checks ("one accepted episode covers the record", "no episode in 39.5–40.2 kyr") and the reviewer's verbatim words in benchmark/EPISODE_QUOTES.json. Tiers: A, the reviewer's own words (79 cases); B, a reading the reviewer accepted (35); C, old verdicts or provisional readings (63); D, analogies (none at present). A failing A or B case that is not flagged known_fail fails the gate, and so does a flagged case that passes; C and D are only printed. No case is flagged known_fail: all A and B cases pass (15 of the 63 C cases fail and are printed only).

docs.title: Current agreement
docs.text:
Run v2-qs-final (MMR and co-orbital, 2026-11-15, settings hash 553e42ee7dc6) with v2-w37-clean-secular-zlk (secular and ZLK, 2026-11-14; the shared end-of-record witness since then leaves its verdicts unchanged), checked by known_disagreements.py against the labels of 2026-11-15:

field agree / labeled status 238 / 238 angle_status 188 / 188 confidence 181 / 181 the verdicts in candidates.csv 150 / 150 secular and ZLK: status / angle_status / confidence / verdicts 53 / 53, 22 / 22, 38 / 38, 8 / 8

No disagreement is listed. Labeled examples are a minority of the benchmark, and the labels are themselves revised when a figure is read again; the numbers say that the rules reproduce today's labels, not that they are right on unlabelled bodies.

docs.title: Synthetic tests
docs.text:
The benchmark checks the rules on real integrations, where the true cause is a judgement. The test suite also checks them on synthetic records whose source of the libration is known by construction (make test-fast). Examples:

known source built in tested in a pendulum (the force law holds exactly) and a kinematic swing (σ moves by its ϖ part, a stays flat) tests/resonances/analysis/impl_response_pendulum_synthetic.py test_impl_response_pendulum_*.py, test_pendulum.py, test_kinematics.py a libration copied from another resonance (the owner librates, the catalog angle follows it) tests/resonances/analysis/test_impl_w2_owner_synthetic.py the same file aliasing by the output step tests/resonances/analysis/test_w22_alias.py, test_impl_w15_alias_gate.py the same files members of a multiplet tests/resonances/analysis/test_impl_w15_owner_multiplet.py the same file

Each test states its expected numbers as worked out by hand in its docstring, not taken from the code.

docs.title: Calibration of the confidence
docs.text: The same labels give, for every cell (status, angle_status, reason) of the verdicts, how many labeled verdicts at high or certain exist and how many of them were wrong, with the Wilson 95 % interval of the accuracy (benchmark/tools/calibrate.py → resonances/data/confidence_cells.json). summary.csv reports the cell of every verdict (cell_n_examples, cell_n_errors, cell_accuracy_low_95, cell_accuracy_high_95). The counts never change a level (Confidence).

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to resonances are listed here. The format follows Keep a Changelog, and the project uses Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Requires rebound<5. REBOUND 5 (released after 1.0.0) renamed the particle hash to name and does not read the archives REBOUND 4 wrote, so with it a fresh install of 1.0.0 failed on the first integration.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Requires Python 3.11.5 or newer (the security fixes of soupsieve, which astroquery uses, need it).
  • The development dependencies are updated for security fixes (pillow, tornado, cryptography, urllib3, black and others); the code is formatted with black 26.

The first stable release, and a large one: changes since 0.5.0. One libration analysis now classifies mean-motion, secular and Lidov-Kozai angles. Each verdict states what the angle does, what causes it and how certain the result is, and every number the decision used is written to summary.csv. The documentation explains the physics behind each status: How the status is determined.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
Code and scripts written for 0.5.x must be updated for these changes:

  • Statuses are strings, not integers. body.statuses[key] and the status column of summary.csv hold resonant, transient, near_separatrix, non_resonant, uncertain or invalid. Comparisons such as status > 0 or status == 2 no longer work, and the save, plot and layout code refuses an integer status (TypeError). body.librations[key] is the full verdict (a Verdict object). The old integer survives only in the column status_code, for comparison with old runs (legacy codes).
  • The old classifier is removed. The module resonances.libration, the body attributes libration_pure, libration_metrics and monotony, and the .env keys LIBRATION_CRITICAL, LIBRATION_PERIOD_CRITICAL, LIBRATION_MONOTONY_CRITICAL, LIBRATION_PERIOD_MIN and LIBRATION_FREQ_MIN no longer exist.
  • summary.csv columns renamed or removed. type is now resonance_type (mmr, secular, lidov_kozai). The initial elements a, e, inc, Omega, omega, M are now a0, e0, inc0, Omega0, omega0, M0. pure, num_libration_periods, max_libration_length, monotony and overlapping are removed.
  • Save and plot settings. The keys SAVE_MODE and PLOT_MODE are now SAVE and PLOT (the arguments are still save and plot). A mode now selects rows by their status string, and the default is review instead of nonzero. candidates has a new meaning: resonant, transient, near_separatrix and uncertain. The new modes are extended, review and negative (Configuration).
  • Integrator arguments renamed. integrator_corrector and integrator_safe_mode are now integration_corrector and integration_safe_mode (arguments and SimulationConfig attributes). The old names, and the old classifier's libration_period_critical and periodogram_critical, are refused with a TypeError that names the replacement.

  • Output layout.

    • Each saved body has one series file, data/data-<body>.csv, with every angle, plus data/data-<body>-periodograms.csv. Before, the run folder held one file per body and resonance.
    • Figures go to figures/, and the one-page verdict figures to combined/, both in confidence/status subfolders.
    • simulation.json replaces simulation.cfg.

    To get a flat folder, set data_folder='' and plot_layout='flat' (Output data). - check and find. - check returns one Simulation for any mix of resonance types. Before, it returned a list of simulations when the types were mixed. - Without type, find searches MMRs, secular and Lidov-Kozai resonances. To search only one kind, pass type='mmr', 'secular' or 'lidov_kozai'. - The order argument of find is removed. - find no longer defaults to 1 Myr: the span is the configured one (100 kyr unless set). - Python API. - Removed from the top level: find_asteroids_in_mmr, secular_check (use resonances.check(asteroids, 'g-g6')), Nu6Resonance, Nu5Resonance, Nu16Resonance and GeneralSecularResonance (use SecularResonance, or create_secular_resonance('nu6')), Resonance and datetime_from_string. - resonances.resonance.plot is replaced by resonances.plotting. - The MMR classes and catalogues moved to resonances.mmr. The top-level names MMR, TwoBody, ThreeBody, TwoBodyMatrix, ThreeBodyMatrix, create_mmr and find_mmrs stay. - Removed .env keys. The planetary frequencies g5–g8 and s5–s8 are now constants of the package (resonances/data/const.py). ASTDYS_URL, ASTDYS_CATALOG and CATALOG_PATH are removed. - Packaging. The project is built with uv and hatchling instead of Poetry. Python 3.11 or newer is still required. The new dependencies are click, mpmath and gmpy2.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Libration analysis. One classifier for every resonance type. It filters the angle at a physical cutoff, finds turning points and episodes, and describes the geometry in angle_status (libration, episodic, near_separatrix, circulation, drift, insufficient_time). It then checks the physics:

    • the identity σ̇ = c (a − a*);
    • the force law of the semi-major axis;
    • the energy and period law of the potential;
    • the strength from the directly averaged disturbing function;
    • for co-orbitals (1:1), their own force law, with horseshoe, tadpole and quasi-satellite regimes.

    A search for the cause tells a libration of the resonance itself from a kinematic one (driven by the perihelion term), from a libration induced by another resonance (owner or driver), from a member of the same multiplet (subresonance) and from a joint capture. The verdict columns are status, angle_status, reason, libration_origin (dynamic, induced, subresonance, kinematic, joint, unknown), origin_detail, owner, final_regime and veto (Rule index). - Confidence and actions. - Each verdict has a confidence level (certain, high, medium, low) and an action: none, spot_check, review, extend (integrate longer, to extend_to_years) or resample (integrate again at resample_step_yr). - review_required marks the rows that need a look, and the review save/plot mode keeps them (Confidence). - The minimal policy. The status comes from the geometry of the filtered angle. Only a measured contradiction (column veto: owner, kinematic, forced_wave, strength, zlk_kinematic, zlk_free_e, zlk_integral) turns a bounded angle non_resonant. Every other finding is a flag. The full status tree's own verdict is kept in v2_verdict (minimal policy). - Mean-motion resonances. Retrograde two-body resonances (1J-3r0) of bodies with i > 90°, and co-orbitals (1:1). - Secular resonances, rebuilt. A formula parser (g-g6, 2(g-g6)+(s-s6), aliases such as nu6 and z1). Angles are built from the planets' proper mode longitudes in the invariable plane (secular_angle_mode='proper', the default). find looks for candidates in the AstDyS synthetic proper elements (Secular resonances). - Lidov-Kozai resonances. LidovKozaiResonance (key LK), Lidov's integrals c1 and c2, and the quadrupole Hamiltonian h_quad. The free elements split the perihelion into its forced and free parts, and the free-ω gate decides whether a libration of ω is the body's own (check_zlk_free_omega): confirmed, kinematic or no verdict (Lidov-Kozai resonances). - Cross-spectral coherence of e and i (coherence.csv). - Clones (virtual asteroids) drawn from the covariance of the orbit fit (AstDyS, NEODyS, JPL SBDB, MPC): clones=N. clones.csv gives the status shares with Wilson 95 % intervals (Clones). - Minor Planet Center as a data source (source='mpc', MPCORB), with an epoch policy that integrates rows at another epoch to the run's date. - Dry-run. sim.dry_run() and resonances dry-run check the output step for aliasing, along with the integrator and the cost, before a long run. output_step='auto' chooses a safe step (Dry-run). - Command line. resonances check, find, dry-run, mpc-search, mpc-update, secular-candidates and skill install (Command line). - The combined verdict figure (plots=['combined'], the default). One page per verdict shows the angle, a, e, the counted episodes and a column that explains the verdict. A variant for papers is plot_options={'combined': {'figure': 'panels'}}. The other figure kinds are evolution, ecc_vector, cross_spectrum, free_omega, clones, recurrence, fair, portrait, cycles, angle and rate (Plots, How to read the figures). - New output. - New tables: mmr_numbers.csv, episodes.csv, candidates.csv, constants.csv, coherence.csv and clones.csv. - New summary.csv columns: the verdict, the physical checks (check_*), the margins (mrg_*), flags, rules_fired, decision_path, the policy columns (n_cycles, n_counted_episodes, veto, v2_verdict, pol_*), settings_hash and package_commit (Output data). - Large runs. Batches on several cores (BATCH_*), resume of a batched run in the same folder, and SimulationSerializer.restore to read a saved run back (recompute_librations=True runs the analysis again) (Serialization). - The Moon as a separate body (solar_system_moon, with IAS15). - Agent skill. resonances skill install [--user] [--path DIR] [--force] installs instructions for coding agents (how to set up runs and read the verdicts) into .claude/skills/resonances (Using with AI agents). - Time in libration. summary.csv columns lib_time_yr and lib_share: the years of the record inside the counted episodes and their share of the record. - Short co-orbital episodes. A quasi-satellite or horseshoe run shorter than the tadpole period floor counts when its own loops and its own 1:1 force law support it (MMR_COORBITAL_QS_LOOP_FACTOR, MMR_COORBITAL_PAIR_LOOP_FLOOR, MMR_COORBITAL_PAIR_LOOP_MIN_HILL); a 1:1 run whose late cycles leave the well keeps its well-holding core and ends only at a separatrix crossing. The record's end is read from the last turning point of any run, for mean-motion, secular and Lidov-Kozai angles alike. - One run per output folder. A second run into a folder that a run (or a worker of an earlier run) is still writing stops with an error instead of doubling the rows of summary.csv (.run.lock). The lock is an flock: on Windows, which has none, it is not taken. - Settings for every threshold. Each threshold of the analysis has an .env key and a line in Configuration. Thresholds that are conventions are marked as such. - A benchmark of 833 real integrations, part of them with visual labels, on which the thresholds are tested (Benchmark).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Secular angles are built from the planets' secular modes (mode longitudes in the invariable plane), not from the planets' osculating elements, which do not give the angle of an s_j term correctly.
  • The documentation is rewritten. It now includes physics pages for every status, a rule index, a guide to the figures, references for configuration and output, and a gallery of benchmark examples.
  • Requires astdys>=1.0.2: the earlier versions held pyarrow<18, which has no wheels for Python 3.13 and later.

docs.title: 0.5.0 and earlier
docs.text: See "Changes before 1.0.0" in the README.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Installing the package adds the resonances command (with uv: uv run resonances ...). resonances --help lists the commands and resonances <command> --help shows the options of one.

command what it does check integrate the given bodies and classify the given resonances find look for candidate resonances of the given bodies, integrate them and classify every angle dry-run check a planned find or check run (output step, aliasing, integrator, cost) without integrating it mpc-search select objects of the MPC catalogue by their elements and flags mpc-update download the MPC catalogue again secular-candidates list the asteroids near a secular resonance in the AstDyS synthetic proper elements skill install install the agent skill into a project (or for the user)

docs.title: How check, find and dry-run read their options
docs.text:
These three commands take any keyword of Simulation as an option: --integration-years=50000 is integration_years=50000 (Simulations, bodies, resonances; every key in Configuration). Dashes become underscores. A value is read as an integer, a float, a boolean (true, false, yes, no) or a string; a comma makes a list (--asteroids=463,490, --planets=Jupiter,Saturn), with no shell quoting. --key=value and --key value both work; an option without a value is True. Unset options take the defaults of .env and .env.dist, as in Python.

The options used most:

option default meaning --asteroids (required) numbers or designations, comma-separated --source nasa elements from nasa (Horizons), astdys or mpc --date today (nasa), the catalog epoch (astdys, mpc) start of the integration --integration-years (or --tmax) 100000 the span in years (tmax in REBOUND units, 2π per year; negative = backwards) --integrator, --dt SABA(10,6,4), 1.0 the REBOUND integrator and its step (REBOUND units) --output-step (or --Nout) |tmax| / 100 points years between saved points; auto lets the dry-run choose --save, --plot review which rows get series and figures, by status (Configuration) --save-path, --plot-path, --name cache/resonance_find where the output goes (Output data) --clones, --clones-source, --clones-seed 0, auto, 0 virtual asteroids from the orbit's covariance (Clones)

check and find print the parameters they read and, at the end, the folder with the results.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
Checks the given resonances for the given bodies (resonances.check). Required: --asteroids, --resonances (MMR keys such as 4J-2S-1, secular formulas such as g-g6, or LK for Lidov-Kozai; the resonance keys).

resonances check --asteroids=463 --resonances=4J-2S-1
resonances check --asteroids=463,490 --resonances=4J-2S-1,3J-1S-1 --integration-years=50000 --save=all --plot=all
resonances check --asteroids=463 --resonances=4J-2S-1 --source=astdys --clones=100

docs.title: find
docs.text:
Finds the candidate resonances of the given bodies and checks them all (resonances.find). Required: --asteroids. Its own options:

option default meaning --type all three mmr, secular, lidov_kozai (comma-separated) --planets the package's default list planets of the MMR search --sigma2, --sigma3, --sigma-retro 0.1, 0.02, 0.5 how far (au) the resonant semi-major axis may lie from the body's: two-body, three-body, retrograde --formulas from the proper elements secular resonances to check instead of the search 
resonances find --asteroids=463
resonances find --asteroids=463 --planets=Mars,Jupiter,Saturn --integration-years=100000 --type=mmr,secular --plot=resonant

docs.title: dry-run
docs.text:
Checks a run before integrating it (Dry-run): the aliasing of every angle at the output step, the auto step, the integrator and its step, the cost. It takes the options of find (or of check when --resonances is given) and its own:

option default meaning --years the run's span the span of the run (--integration-years) --step the run's step auto or a step in years (--output-step) --pilot off a short fine integration per body (seconds each) instead of the elements alone --fair off the step must also resolve the FAIR plot (DRYRUN_FAIR=required) --out none write dryrun_rows.csv, dryrun_bodies.csv and dryrun_run.json into this folder 
resonances dry-run --asteroids=463 --years=100000 --step=auto
resonances dry-run --asteroids=1865 --resonances=10E-11+0+1 --years=20000 --integrator=ias15 --Nout=4000 --pilot

docs.title: Clones (virtual asteroids)
docs.text:
An orbit is known only within its errors. A clone, or virtual asteroid, is one orbit the observations allow; the nominal orbit is one of them, "without any special significance" (Milani, Chesley & Valsecchi 2000, p. 947). A run with N clones of an asteroid classifies each clone like any body and reports, per resonance, the share of clones with each status and its 95 % interval: the probability of a status given the provider's orbit solution, the package's model and the integration span. It says nothing about the model's or the classifier's own errors.

import resonances


def main():
    solution = resonances.orbit_solution(463, source='astdys')  # nominal orbit + covariance (cached in cache/clones/)
    ensemble = solution.sample(n=10, seed=0)  # 10 clones and the nominal; 100-1000 for real shares

    sim = resonances.Simulation(name='clones-demo', date='2026-01-01', integration_years=2_000)
    sim.create_solar_system()
    sim.add_ensemble(ensemble, resonances=['4J-2S-1'])  # clones drawn at another epoch are integrated to the date first
    sim.run()
    shares = sim.clone_summary  # the rows of clones.csv: the share of each status with its 95 % Wilson interval
    print(shares[['resonance', 'n_clones', 'nominal_status', 'modal_status', 'modal_share', 'f_resonant_lo', 'f_resonant_hi']])


if __name__ == '__main__':  # the clones run in worker processes: the guard is required
    main()

The clones run in worker processes, so a script needs the if __name__ == '__main__': guard (without it a run on macOS or Windows stops with an error that names the missing guard). Use 100–1000 clones and the full span for real shares.

Short forms: sim.add_body(463, '4J-2S-1', clones=100), resonances.check(463, '4J-2S-1', clones=100), resonances.find(463, clones=100) (candidates from the whole cloud), CLONES=100 in .env, and on the command line resonances check --asteroids=463 --resonances=4J-2S-1 --clones=100. The body itself is then added from DATA_SOURCE as without clones; its clones come from the orbit solution of CLONES_SOURCE (auto = the same provider: AstDyS for astdys, MPC for mpc, JPL SBDB for nasa).

Your own clones: resonances.Ensemble.from_elements('name', rows, epoch_mjd=..., nominal=...) (rows with a, e, inc, Omega, omega, M in radians, one epoch), or an ensemble saved by Ensemble.save / read by Ensemble.load.

docs.title: Where the covariance comes from
docs.text:
An orbit is fitted to the astrometry by least squares. With the residuals linearized around the best fit X₀, the orbit's density is approximated by the Gaussian

\[ p(X) \propto \exp\!\left(-\tfrac12\,\Delta X^{\mathsf T} C^{-1} \Delta X\right), \qquad \Delta X = X - X_0, \qquad C = (B^{\mathsf T} W B)^{-1}, \]

B the derivatives of the observations by the six coordinates, W their weights. The clones use the Gaussian approximation in the published covariance coordinates: C as each provider publishes it, in its coordinates and at one epoch (whether these are the coordinates the fit was solved in is not stated). A Gaussian is a local approximation and depends on the coordinates; carrying its draws through the nonlinear map does not repair a poor one. The shares below are probabilities under this approximation, not the true astrometric posterior:

source coordinates X units epoch file astdys (numbered) equinoctial a, h = e sin ϖ, k = e cos ϖ, p = tan(i/2) sin Ω, q = tan(i/2) cos Ω, λ au, λ in degrees (in the covariance too) .eq1: the catalog's standard epoch (default); .eq0: the fit's own OEF2.0 newton.spacedys.com/~astdys2/epoch/numbered/<n/1000>/<n>.eq1 neodys (NEAs) as AstDyS as AstDyS .eq0: the fit's own, near the middle of the arc (default); .eq1 ~neodys2/epoch/<designation>.eq0 sbdb (JPL) cometary e, q, t_p, Ω, ω, i au, JD TDB, degrees the orbit-solution epoch (not the epoch of the listed elements) ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.api?sstr=..&cov=mat&full-prec=1 mpc Cartesian x, y, z, vx, vy, vz (heliocentric) au, au/day the orbit's epoch data.minorplanetcenter.net/api/get-orb

All in the J2000 ecliptic, heliocentric, as the package; a file stating another frame (OEF refsys other than ECLM J2000, MPC system_data not ecliptic/ICRF or another obliquity than 84381.448″, SBDB equinox not J2000) is refused, nothing is rotated. An OEF file is read as one record: a second one (a bulk .ctc) is refused. The units were checked on the providers' own numbers (tests in tests/resonances/clones/): the OEF EIG line is √eig(C) only with λ converted to radians; MPC's eigenvalues are √eig of its CAR covariance; MPC's CAR and COM blocks give its own KEP block; AstDyS and MPC agree on 463 to 3·10⁻⁸ au.

A file is downloaded once into CLONES_CACHE_DIR/<source>/ with <file>.meta.json (URL, download time, sha256); orbit_solution(..., refresh=True) fetches it again (an orbit improves with new observations). The ensemble's JSON keeps the whole solution.

docs.title: Why a multivariate normal in the published coordinates
docs.text:
The coordinates are strongly correlated: in JPL's covariance of 463, |corr(e, q)| = 0.99999. Independent errors per element, as several papers draw them, put the clones outside the orbit's confidence region; with e and q independent σ_a comes out 4–900 times too large. Each clone is therefore

\[ X_i = X_0 + L z_i, \qquad C = L L^{\mathsf T}\ \text{(Cholesky)}, \qquad z_i \sim \mathcal N(0, I_6), \]

in the published coordinates, and converted exactly to Keplerian elements (equinoctial: e = √(h² + k²), ϖ = atan2(h, k), i = 2 atan √(p² + q²), Ω = atan2(p, q), ω = ϖ − Ω, M = λ − ϖ; cometary: a = q/(1 − e), M = k a^−3/2 (t − t_p); Cartesian: the two-body map with μ = k², the phase from the argument of latitude, so a circular orbit keeps it). L is computed from the correlation matrix (a covariance of a good orbit has a condition number of 10¹³–10¹⁹ in its raw units). A draw that is no bound ellipse (e < 0, e ≥ 1 or a ≤ 0) is kept in the ensemble (valid False), never redrawn, and never integrated: it is no observation of any status, so it is left out of the shares. When such draws are more than CLONES_MAX_INVALID (5 %) of the sample, the Gaussian is no usable model of the orbit's uncertainty (a linear covariance of a 1-day arc: SBDB gives 2010 CG236 σ_e = 13, all 100 draws unbound; 2010 DH65 83 of 100) and its clones.csv row gets no shares at all (cloud_usable False).

Each clone's \(d^2 = \Delta X^{\mathsf T} C^{-1} \Delta X = \lvert z\rvert^2\) is stored: it follows \(\chi^2\) with 6 degrees of freedom. When float64 finds C singular (Cholesky fails), the eigen factor keeps its rank modes (Ensemble.rank, in the JSON as covariance_rank) and d² is the pseudo-inverse distance ΔXᵀ C⁺ ΔX, χ² with rank degrees of freedom. In six dimensions the "3σ" ellipsoid d ≤ 3 holds only 82.6 % of the clones (P(χ²₆ ≤ 9) = 1 − e^−4.5 (1 + 4.5 + 4.5²/2)); 95 % lie within d ≤ 3.55. The draws are not truncated.

The draws of a body are seeded by (CLONES_SEED, crc32(name)) and prefix-stable: the first 100 of 400 clones are the 100 clones.

docs.title: Why the covariance's own epoch
docs.text:
.eq1 is the .eq0 covariance propagated linearly, C₁ = J C₀ Jᵀ. For an NEA observed over a short arc years ago this no longer describes the orbits: for 2013 RZ53 (a 3-day arc in 2013) σ_a grows 47 times and σ_λ 359 times from .eq0 to .eq1, through Earth encounters a linear map does not follow, and the .eq1 matrix is numerically indefinite. The clones are drawn where the fit was made and each one is integrated to the run's date (IAS15, the run's planets, propagate.py; the nominal alone, the clones together); all of them then start together. Hence the defaults .eq0 for NEODyS, the solution epoch for SBDB, and MPC refused for U ≥ 3 (MPC publishes the covariance only at its standard epoch; U ≥ 3 is a conservative policy, not a physical boundary). For numbered main-belt asteroids .eq1 is fine and needs no integration (its epoch is AstDyS's catalog epoch).

Any gap between the covariance's epoch and the run's date is crossed: up to 10⁻⁴ d (8.6 s) on the two-body ellipses (5 s already move 463's mean anomaly by 3.8 σ_λ), beyond that by integration. clones.csv records the span (propagation_days) and the way (propagation: none, kepler, ias15). The integration was validated against a provider's own propagation only for MPC elements over 138 days (Configuration, MPC_EPOCH_POLICY); with MPC_PROPAGATE_MAX_DAYS set, a longer span of the clones gets a warning (not a refusal). A timezone-aware run date is taken as its UTC value, the same instant for the planets and the clones.

The carried cloud is in the package's model: no relativity, no asteroid perturbers, no non-gravitational force. A body added from another source (the short forms) can then lie off its cloud: nominal_offset_sigma in clones.csv is max(|Δa|/sd(a), |Δλ|/sd(λ)) of the body against its clones at the date, with a warning above 3.

Non-gravitational parameters (Yarkovsky A2, comet-like A1–A3) are not modeled: the orbital 6×6 block of the covariance (the marginal over them) is used, a warning is logged and clones.csv says so (nongrav).

Main belt. A numbered main-belt asteroid has σ_a ~ 10⁻⁹ au, orders of magnitude below any resonance width: its clones differ only through chaos, and a regular orbit gives the nominal's verdict to every clone.

docs.title: How many clones
docs.text:
A share k/N is a binomial estimate; its 95 % interval is Wilson's score interval (Wilson 1927), with \(\hat p = k/N\) and \(z = 1.96\):

\[ \text{center} = \frac{\hat p + z^2/2N}{1 + z^2/N}, \qquad \text{half-width} = \frac{z}{1 + z^2/N}\sqrt{\frac{\hat p(1 - \hat p)}{N} + \frac{z^2}{4N^2}}, \]

which stays within [0, 1] and is not empty at 0/N or N/N.

N half-width at p = 0.5 0 of N: upper bound use 100 (default) ±10 % 3.7 % resonant, split or not 400 ±5 % 0.95 % the share itself is the result 1000 ±3 % 0.38 % rare outcomes

Integration is cheap (about 0.04 s per clone per 10 kyr with SABA); the classification is not: 1–2 CPU-min per clone and resonance for a 1-Myr record. Choose the span and the output step with that in mind.

docs.title: How a run treats them
docs.text:
• The nominal is an ordinary body of the run: in its own simulation, as without clones, so its verdict does not change.
  • The clones <name>~c001, ... are test particles run after the ordinary bodies by the batch workers, CLONES_BATCH (20) per REBOUND simulation, on BATCH_N_CORES processes. Each has its rows in summary.csv and, by SAVE, its data files; its own figures only with CLONES_PLOT_EACH=True.
  • In a find (resonances.find(..., clones=N) or add_ensemble(ens) without resonances), every clone gets the union of the MMR candidates of the whole cloud (a clone may sit in a resonance the nominal never visits); the nominal keeps its own, so its rows and the OUTPUT_STEP=auto step planned from them are those of a run without clones. The clones run at that step; a clone-only row it undersamples is flagged by the analysis' own sampling caps.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• clones.csv (top of save_path), one row per body and resonance: n_clones, n_classified, n_missing, n_draw_invalid (draws that are no bound orbit, not integrated), f_draw_invalid (their share of n_clones), cloud_usable (f_draw_invalid ≤ CLONES_MAX_INVALID); for each status n_<status>, f_<status>, f_<status>_lo, f_<status>_hi (Wilson 95 %); modal_status, modal_share; nominal_status, nominal_confidence, nominal_agreement (share of clones with the nominal's status, with _lo, _hi: a diagnostic, the nominal has no special weight); nominal_offset_sigma; source, product (eq0, eq1, sbdb, get-orb), epoch_mjd (the covariance's), run_date_mjd, propagated, propagation (none, kepler, ias15), propagation_days (run date − epoch), seed, nongrav. The shares' denominator is n_classified: the bound clones with a verdict (the unbound draws are not in it, and invalid is only the classifier's verdict on a clone's record; clones without a verdict are n_missing, left out). A row with cloud_usable False keeps its counts but its shares, modal status and nominal agreement are empty. A kinematic Lidov-Kozai libration and one without a gate verdict stay apart (why).
  • data/ensemble-<name>.csv and .json: every draw (clone index and name, Keplerian elements at the covariance's epoch, valid, d2, the draw in the fit's coordinates x_<label>, the elements at the run's date <element>_start) and the orbit solution with its provenance. resonances.Ensemble.load reads it back (to the bit).
  • data/ensemble-<name>-results.npz (with SAVE on, kept): every clone's verdict per row (status, confidence, angle_status, reason, libration_origin), its initial a, half-widths and derived rows, and the angles of the clones and of the nominal thinned to 2000 points for the figure (years float64, degrees float32: a thumbnail, never analyzed). Restore reads it (below).
  • figures/<layout>/<name>-<resonance>-clones.png (plot kind clones, also drawn with combined; in the folder of the nominal's row; drawn when PLOT selects the nominal's row or any clone's): (a) the angle of every clone colored by its status, the nominal in black; (b) the status of every clone against its initial a (a jitter separates the points vertically), with the catalog resonant axis \(a_{\rm res}\) of an MMR (dotted, legend a_res (catalog)) and \(a_{\rm res}\) ± the median libration half-width the clones' episodes measured (dashed); (c) the shares with their Wilson intervals, the nominal's status starred (How to read the figures).

The settings (CLONES, CLONES_SOURCE, CLONES_EPOCH, CLONES_SEED, CLONES_BATCH, CLONES_PLOT_EACH, CLONES_CACHE_DIR) are listed in Configuration.

docs.title: Resume and restore
docs.text:
Resume. A run with clones keeps one checkpoint for the ordinary bodies and the clones, clones_state/ in save_path, and removes it (and simulation_state.json) only after the whole run has succeeded. An interrupted run is resumed by running the same script again with the same save_path (resume_enabled, on by default):

  • each finished clone batch left clones_state/batch-<i>.npz (published atomically; checked when read: run, members, rows, numbers): it is not run again; a batch without a valid file runs again and its old rows are replaced;
  • a finished ordinary part is not run again: in one simulation its verdicts are read back from summary.csv (this needs save_summary; without it the ordinary bodies run again), in batches through simulation_state.json. The nominal is never moved into another grouping (its trajectory depends on its simulation's particles);
  • the run's identity is checked first: the ordinary bodies with their elements and grouping, the planets' initial state, the settings, the clone settings and batches, each ensemble (the provider's file sha256, the solution, the draws, seed and rank) and the clones' starting elements at the date, which clones_state/starts.npz keeps and a resume compares bit for bit; and the versions of resonances, rebound and numpy. Any difference raises ValueError saying what changed (an orbit solution fetched again with orbit_solution(..., refresh=True) is another cloud). To start over, remove clones_state/.

Restore. simulation.json lists the ensembles (simulation.ensembles, Serialization); SimulationSerializer.restore rebuilds sim.ensembles (names, starting elements, the stored verdicts and thumbnails) and sim.clone_summary (clones.csv), and ensemble_run.plot_ensembles draws the figure again. With SAVE off there is no manifest: only sim.clone_summary comes back (a warning). recompute_librations=True reclassifies the nominal from its saved series; the clones keep their stored verdicts (clone_verdicts = 'stored'), and the nominal columns of clones.csv (nominal_status, nominal_confidence, nominal_agreement) and the nominal's summary.csv rows are rewritten in the run's folder from the one new verdict. The clones are not reclassified even when their series were saved: a SAVE mode other than all keeps the series of the clones its status filter selected, so recomputing only those would bias the shares, and each clone costs as much analysis as the nominal.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Not done: a clone's own series are not reclassified by a restore; no line-of-variations sampling or statistical ranging for orbits too weak for a Gaussian; no weighted ensembles.

No shortcut that gives every clone the nominal's verdict without classifying it. A small spread of the cloud in a does not certify that every clone shares the nominal's verdict: chaos inside a resonance separates clones of any spread over a long enough span (33128 6N-7 librates with a Lyapunov time of about 4 kyr), the classifier has thresholds a tiny difference can cross, and a nominal from another source can lie off its own cloud (nominal_offset_sigma). And integrating the clones is cheap next to classifying them, so skipping the integration would save little.

References: Milani, A., Chesley, S. R. & Valsecchi, G. B. (2000), Planet. Space Sci. 48, 945; Milani, A. et al. (2005), A&A 431, 729 (multiple solutions, the line of variations); Broucke, R. A. & Cefola, P. J. (1972), Celest. Mech. 5, 303 (equinoctial elements); Wilson, E. B. (1927), JASA 22, 209; Newcombe, R. G. (1998), Stat. Med. 17, 857.

docs.title: Cross-spectral coherence
docs.text:
Periodograms answer "which periods are present in this series". Cross spectra answer a different question: do two series share a period, and with what phase shift?

That is what distinguishes a real resonance from a coincidence:

  • in a mean-motion resonance, the resonant angle \(\sigma\) and the semi-major axis share the libration frequency, a quarter period apart. From \(\dot\sigma = c\,(a - a_*)\) with \(c = -3kn/(2a)\), a libration \(\sigma = A\sin\omega t\) gives \(a - a_* = (A\omega/c)\cos\omega t\): \(a\) leads \(\sigma\) by +90° when \(c > 0\) (the usual prograde angle, \(k < 0\)) and by −90° when \(c < 0\). The preset target below is +90°, a convention for the usual sign, not a law (The resonant pendulum);
  • in a Lidov-Kozai resonance, \(e\) and \(i\) share the ZLK-cycle frequency in antiphase: the body trades eccentricity for inclination at constant \(H = \sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\).

The second point is not decorative. The argument of pericentre ω can librate without any Lidov-Kozai resonance: when the forced eccentricity vector dominates the free one, the geometry alone keeps ω bounded. Asteroid 591986 is exactly this case — its osculating ω librates, but its free ω circulates; at its 6-kyr cycle e and i move in phase (a forced-eccentricity beat), not in the ZLK antiphase.

No status depends on this page

The cross spectra are diagnostics. The e-i criterion gives the columns zlk_coherent and zlk_check (confirmed_ei is now the e–i coupling at the row's own period, Free elements); what makes 591986 non_resonant is the free-ω gate (Free elements). The reason is the baseline, see below.

docs.title: How it is measured
docs.text:
Welch's method on non-overlapping segments, via scipy.signal.coherence and scipy.signal.csd with identical parameters. Each of the \(n_{\rm seg}\) segments is linearly detrended and windowed (Hann by default), the two series are Fourier transformed (\(X\), \(Y\)), and the spectra are averaged over segments: \(P_{xx} = \langle |X|^2\rangle\), \(P_{yy} = \langle |Y|^2\rangle\), \(P_{xy} = \langle X^* Y\rangle\). Then

\[ \gamma^2(f) = \frac{|P_{xy}|^2}{P_{xx}P_{yy}} \in [0, 1], \qquad \varphi(f) = \arg P_{xy}, \qquad \text{amplitude ratio} = \sqrt{P_{yy}/P_{xx}} . \]

\(\gamma^2\) is the magnitude-squared coherence (1: the two series share that frequency with a fixed phase); a positive \(\varphi\) means the second series leads.

Non-overlapping is deliberate. The significance threshold

\[ \gamma^2_{\rm crit} = 1 - \alpha^{1/(n_{\rm seg} - 1)} \]

is exact only for statistically independent segments. Measured false-alarm rate on white noise, alpha = 0.01:

segmentation gamma2_crit measured fraction of significant bins non-overlapping 0.785 (n=4) 0.0100 50% overlap 0.785 (n=4) 0.0001

With overlap the same threshold is roughly a hundred times too conservative. \(\alpha\) is a false-alarm probability per frequency bin, not for the whole searched spectrum.

docs.title: Validity limits
docs.text:
\[ P_{\min} = 4\,\Delta t \quad\text{(a margin over Nyquist)}, \qquad P_{\max} = \frac{T}{5\,n_{\rm seg}} \quad\text{(at least 5 cycles in every segment)}. \]

Nothing outside [P_min, P_max] is reported. This is the constraint that usually bites: to see a 50 kyr Lidov-Kozai cycle at n_seg = 4 you need at least 1 Myr of integration. A shorter run reports short_baseline rather than a verdict.

docs.title: Segmentation levels
docs.text: P_max shrinks as n_seg grows, while the threshold gets easier. Rather than fixing one segmentation, several levels are computed (COHERENCE_N_SEGMENTS, default 4,8,16) and the verdict is taken from the coarsest level whose validity band is non-empty — the one reaching the longest periods with the strictest threshold. Levels that cannot be computed (fewer than 512 samples per segment, empty band) are reported as invalid rather than silently dropped.

docs.title: Lines, not bins
docs.text:
Contiguous runs of significant bins are grouped into lines. A line's period, \(\gamma^2\) and amplitude ratio are those of its strongest bin (largest |Pxy|, not largest coherence — a wide coherent band's most coherent bin is often not the one carrying the power); its phase is the \(|P_{xy}|\)-weighted circular mean over all its bins (spread in phase_std). Lines are ranked by integrated cross-amplitude sum(|Pxy|).

The phase criterion is applied to the top-ranked line only. Ranking matters: in the 30 Myr integration of 591986 the e–i search band holds tens of significant lines, one of which happens to sit at −166° and would satisfy a naive "is there any antiphase line" test. The amplitude-dominant line sits at +125° at every segmentation level, which is the correct answer.

docs.title: Phase criteria
docs.text:
A criterion is (target_deg, tolerance_deg) per pair, preset per resonance type:

resonance type pairs phase target search band lidov_kozai e-i 180° ± 30° periods > 10 kyr mmr sigma-a 90° ± 30° (for \(c > 0\), see above) full validity band secular sigma-e — periods > 10 kyr

Phase sign convention: positive means the second series leads the first.

Override per resonance type when creating the simulation; types you do not mention keep their presets:

import resonances

sim = resonances.check(
    463,
    '4J-2S-1',
    integration_years=2_000,  # 100_000 years for a real verdict
    coherence_pairs={'mmr': ['sigma-a', 'sigma-e', 'sigma-i']},
    coherence_phase_targets={'mmr': {'sigma-a': (90.0, 20.0)}},
)

docs.title: Why phase alone is not enough
docs.text:
A line's cross-phase is a weighted mean over a few adjacent bins, and those bins lie when several close lines blend into them. On 591986 the e–i line near 54 kyr is really a triplet (53.9 / 54.0 / 54.2 kyr). Truncating one 30 Myr integration to different lengths and running the same code gives:

window decisive line phase band-passed r broadband r 2 Myr 11.4 kyr −2.9° −0.25 −0.05 3 Myr 11.0 kyr +29.5° −0.26 −0.02 5 Myr 54.3 kyr +177.7° −0.15 −0.01 7.5 Myr 27.2 kyr +134.0° −0.38 −0.00 10–30 Myr 27–56 kyr +120…+128° −0.12…−0.18 ±0.00

The phase says "antiphase" in exactly one window out of nine. The correlations say the same thing in all nine: e and i never actually trade. So the flag requires both.

docs.title: The e-i exchange flag
docs.text:
Measured after the verdict, for Lidov-Kozai rows that are not non_resonant (with COHERENCE_SKIP_NON_RESONANT). It changes no status: it records whether the strongest coherent e–i line is an exchange, as zlk_coherent and zlk_check. The flag confirmed_ei and the check check_zlk_ei no longer come from here: they are the e–i coupling measured at the row's own decisive period, for every ZLK row (zlk_ei_coupling, Free elements: beyond the gate), because this line can sit on a harmonic or outside the ZLK band (3040, 4257 and 162474 pass here on lines at 10–21 kyr while their ZLK periods are 40–59 kyr).

situation zlk_coherent zlk_check antiphase line and e/i anticorrelate True passed no antiphase line False failed antiphase line, but no exchange False weak_exchange baseline too short to measure empty short_baseline ZLK_COHERENCE_CHECK=False empty disabled no e-i pair, or no phase target for it empty no_target

no_target appears when coherence_pairs or the phase targets of lidov_kozai were overridden without e-i; restoring coherence_pairs['lidov_kozai'] = ['e-i'] with its target enables the check.

The 180° target is a prograde diagnostic. At constant \(H\) a retrograde orbit (\(\cos i < 0\)) has \(e\) and \(i\) varying in phase, and the anticorrelation test does not confirm that branch. The exchange also assumes \(i\) measured from the perturber's plane and \(H\) conserved (quadrupole approximation); this line uses the ecliptic \(i\) of an N-body run, so the comparison is approximate. The period-specific coupling (zlk_ei_coupling) reads \(i\) from the invariable plane and the tilt of a retrograde orbit. No status depends on either.

short_baseline is the important distinction: a check that could not run must not be read as a negative result, so the reason is recorded and a researcher can filter on the column instead of guessing.

docs.title: Why it does not decide the status
docs.text:
Earlier versions demoted a librating Lidov-Kozai angle on this check alone. The baseline is what took that away. The validity band tops out at T / (5 · n_seg), which is 25 kyr on a 500 kyr run at four segments, while the real Lidov-Kozai lines in the reference set sit at 27–58 kyr. On the short integrations this package now targets, the check would be judging on a line outside its own validity band — it happened to agree with the free-omega gate on all ten reference objects at 500 kyr, but by luck rather than by measurement.

The status decision moved to the forced/free split, which has no such band: see free elements. The cross spectra, coherence.csv and the figures are unchanged; the line columns sit next to the status as independent evidence.

The ZLK_MIN_ANTICORRELATION = 0.5 default is provisional. It sits between the only two objects measured so far — 591986 never exceeds 0.38 and is not in resonance, 162474 reaches 0.79 and is — but two objects do not calibrate a threshold. The raw r_band and r_broadband values are written to coherence.csv for every pair, so a larger sample can be collected and the threshold revisited from data.

The correlation condition is deliberately ZLK-only: it encodes cos(180°) = −1, and would be meaningless against the MMR target of 90°, where quadrature puts the correlation at zero by construction. For MMR and secular resonances the cross spectrum is pure diagnostics.

docs.title: Forced and free eccentricity
docs.text:
In the (k, h) = (e cos ω, e sin ω) plane the forced term is the offset of the cloud from the origin and the free term is the radius it traces:

\[ e_{\rm forced} = \sqrt{\langle k\rangle^2 + \langle h\rangle^2}, \qquad e_{\rm free} = \sqrt{\operatorname{var} k + \operatorname{var} h}. \]

Note the sum of the two variances. A free vector of radius R sweeping the circle uniformly puts \(R^2/2\) into each coordinate, so summing recovers R; averaging instead would under-report by a factor √2.

Both go into summary.csv. On the 30 Myr integration of 591986 they come out as e_forced = 0.0392 and e_free = 0.0308, the latter matching the AstDyS tro.syn proper eccentricity e_p = 0.0308.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
summary.csv gains, per body and resonance: e_forced, e_free, zlk_coherent (True/False/empty), zlk_check, zlk_line_period, zlk_line_phase, zlk_line_gamma2, zlk_line_r_band.

coherence.csv — one row per detected line, appended per run like summary.csv (written only when save_summary is on):

column meaning body, resonance, pair what was analyzed n_seg, rank, decisive segmentation level, rank by cross-amplitude, whether this is the line the criterion used period, gamma2, gamma2_crit the line and the threshold it cleared phase_deg, phase_std cross-phase and its spread across the line's bins amp_ratio sqrt(Pyy/Pxx) — how much the second series moves per unit of the first r_band Pearson r of the two series band-passed around this line; filled for the strongest line only r_broadband Pearson r of the two raw series, unfiltered cross_amplitude, n_bins integrated \|Pxy\| and width of the line period_min, period_max validity band of that level phase_target, phase_tolerance criterion applied, if any n_levels_valid, n_levels_passed, n_levels_agreeing how many levels could be computed, how many satisfied the criterion, how many reproduce the decisive line

amp_ratio is a useful independent check. Conservation of \(H = \sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\) gives the signed derivative

\[ \frac{{\rm d}i}{{\rm d}e} = -\frac{e\cos i}{(1 - e^2)\sin i}, \]

so the amplitude ratio \(\lvert\delta i\rvert/\lvert\delta e\rvert\) (i in radians) should be the absolute value of the right-hand side (with \(i\) from the perturber's plane; for ecliptic elements this is approximate). The sign is negative only for a prograde orbit. amp_ratio is non-negative, an amplitude ratio, not the signed derivative. A line whose ratio is far from it is shared but not driven by the Lidov-Kozai mechanism.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
Add to plots:

sim = resonances.check(
    162474,
    'lidov-kozai',
    integration_years=20_000,  # 500 kyr or more for the Lidov-Kozai periods
    plots=['evolution', 'ecc_vector', 'cross_spectrum'],
    plot='all',
)
sim.run()
  • ecc_vector → {body}-ecc-vector.png (How to read the figures): the offset of the cloud is e_forced, its radius e_free. It explains why ω is bounded, not whether that is a resonance: genuine librators and forced-geometry cases both show an offset cloud, with e_free/e_forced below 1 for both (0.27–0.35 for 3040, 4257 and 162474, 0.79 for 591986).
  • cross_spectrum → {body}-{resonance}-coherence-{pair}.png per pair: coherence, cross-phase and the two series band-passed at the decisive line (How to read the figures). The yellow bands there mark agreement across levels at one of the strongest lines; agreement alone is reported but is not a gate condition, since for e-i it mostly measures the conservation of H = √(1−e²)·cos i: the share of the band where all levels agree tracks how well i is predicted from e through H (3040 78 %, 4257 44 %, 88899 24 %, 10563 0 %; R² = 0.86, 0.64, 0.06, 0).

Both plotters are usable directly:

body = sim.bodies[0]
resonance = body.lidov_kozai_resonances[0]  # key 'LK'
resonances.EccentricityVectorPlotter.from_body(body, resonance, sim).plot().save('kh.png')
resonances.CrossSpectrumPlotter.from_body(body, resonance, 'e-i').plot().save('coh.png')

docs.title: Using the primitives directly
docs.text:
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402

times_yrs = np.asarray(sim.times) / (2 * np.pi)  # a uniform grid, in years
e, inc = body.ecc, body.inc  # a, e and i are not unwrapped; angles must be (np.unwrap)

result = resonances.cross_spectrum(times_yrs, e, inc, n_seg=4, alpha=0.01, period_min=10_000)
if result.valid and result.top_line:
    line = result.top_line
    print(line.period, line.gamma2, line.phase_deg, line.amp_ratio)
    print(resonances.phase_matches(line.phase_deg, 180.0, 30.0))

Angles must be np.unwraped before being passed in; a, e and i must not be. The grid must be uniform — a non-uniform one returns valid=False with a reason rather than a wrong number.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The options are listed in Configuration.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The defaults of every option are in resonances/.env.dist, with a comment each. Do not edit that file. To change a value, in order of priority (the first wins):

  1. an argument of Simulation (lower-case name), or an attribute of sim.config set before sim.run();
  2. a .env file in the working directory (upper-case key);
  3. an environment variable (upper-case key);
  4. the default of .env.dist.
import resonances

sim = resonances.Simulation(name='test', integrator='whfast', save='all', save_path='output/my_run')
sim.config.plot = 'nonzero'  # after creation: through sim.config
resonances.config.set('INTEGRATION_DT', '0.5')  # a .env.dist key, as a string; read when a Simulation is created
print(resonances.config.has('INTEGRATION_DT'), resonances.config.get('INTEGRATION_DT'))

config holds the merged mapping of .env.dist, the environment variables and .env. config.set raises for a key that is not in that mapping; config.get raises for a missing key unless a default (not None) is given. The mapping is not a list of supported options: an environment-only key is accepted. find() and check() pass their extra keyword arguments to Simulation.

docs.title: Saving and plotting
docs.text:
The save and plot filters select rows by their verdict: the status string, and for review also the confidence and the action (status_selected in resonances/simulation/config.py; the statuses are explained in How the status is determined). Save, plot and the release of the arrays of an unplotted row use the same selection. These are output settings, not analysis settings: they do not enter settings_hash.

mode rows selected all every row resonant resonant, transient candidates resonant, transient, near_separatrix, uncertain extended candidates, and non_resonant rows with a libration_origin (kinematic, induced, subresonance: a bounded angle that is not this resonance's own; a joint row keeps its own status) nonzero everything except non_resonant without a libration_origin review nonzero, and the review queue (review_required in summary.csv): a non_resonant row at medium or low confidence (medium = a spot check, low = a review). The default: a doubtful negative is seen, while its status stays physical. It keeps more series than nonzero (the benchmark: 540 rows instead of 490); after the run the log prints the rows by status × confidence, the queue size and how many more rows SAVE=review keeps negative near_separatrix, uncertain, invalid none nothing (also Python None or False) option / key default meaning save / SAVE review which rows' series are written (mode above) save_path / SAVE_PATH cache the run folder. Without the argument it is SAVE_PATH/<name>, where name defaults to the current timestamp (find and check use name='resonance_find'). The tables (summary.csv, episodes.csv, …) and simulation.json go to its top data_folder / DATA_FOLDER data the folder of the series CSVs under save_path (data-<body>.csv, periodograms, <body>-omega-free.csv, data-planet-<planet>.csv); empty = save_path itself. Restore reads the series from there (the manifest of simulation.json); a batch run resumes only into the same folder save_summary / SAVE_SUMMARY True write summary.csv, episodes.csv and coherence.csv (every resonance type) and, for MMRs, mmr_numbers.csv, candidates.csv, constants.csv. Writing the same bodies again replaces their rows (Output data) save_planets / SAVE_PLANETS analysis which planets are kept and written: all, analysis (those of the bodies' resonances, plus MMR_OWNER_PLANETS when the owner search is on) or none (a bool: True = all). The MMR analysis reads them for FAIR, the removal of the planetary ripple, the directly averaged strength, the moving center and the subresonances; without them the owner search falls back to catalog longitudes (confidence ≤ medium). secular_planet_phases='measured' needs all. A planet costs 64 bytes per output step (about 6 MB for 100 kyr at 1 yr) plot / PLOT review which rows get figures (mode above) plots / PLOTS combined the figure kinds: combined (the one-page verdict figure, MMR, secular, ZLK), evolution, ecc_vector, cross_spectrum, free_omega (ZLK), clones, MMR recurrence, fair, portrait, cycles, secular/ZLK portrait, angle, rate. An unknown name is an error (Plots) plot_always / PLOT_ALWAYS empty resonance types (mmr, secular, lidov_kozai) plotted whatever their status (not when plot is none) plot_type / PLOT_TYPE save save the figures, show them, or both image_type / PLOT_IMAGE_TYPE png the image format, png or pdf plot_config / PLOT_CONFIG full the panel preset of the evolution figure: full or simple plot_options / PLOT_OPTIONS empty options of the diagnostic figures (dict, or JSON in .env), merged over the defaults and validated (Plots) plot_path / PLOT_PATH cache the figures' folder; without the argument PLOT_PATH/<name>, as save_path plot_figures_folder / PLOT_FIGURES_FOLDER figures the individual figures under plot_path; empty = plot_path itself plot_combined_folder / PLOT_COMBINED_FOLDER combined the combined figures under plot_path; empty = plot_path itself plot_layout / PLOT_LAYOUT confidence/status subfolders inside both figure folders: flat, or levels joined by / from status, confidence (none for a verdict without a level), type, resonance, body. Presets: flat, status, confidence, confidence/status, status/confidence, type/status, type/confidence/status, resonance, body. A row without a verdict goes to unclassified (Output data) plot_combined_layout / PLOT_COMBINED_LAYOUT empty the layout of the combined figures alone; empty = plot_layout

docs.text: option / key default meaning save_episodes / SAVE_EPISODES True write episodes.csv (every run of turning points, every resonance type) save_candidates / SAVE_CANDIDATES top rows of candidates.csv: the best and the accepted subresonances and owners (top), or all save_constants / SAVE_CONSTANTS True write constants.csv (mean motions, frequencies, great inequality), once per run output_step / OUTPUT_STEP empty the output step in years: sets Nout = ⌈span / step⌉ + 1 (the step is an upper bound); auto lets the dry-run choose a step that folds no short period (Dry-run); empty = Nout = |tmax| / 100. An explicit Nout wins

docs.title: Cross-spectral coherence
docs.text:
The σ–a, σ–e, σ–i and e–i cross spectra (Cross-spectral coherence). They change no status.

option / key default meaning coherence_enabled / COHERENCE_ENABLED True master switch coherence_skip_non_resonant / COHERENCE_SKIP_NON_RESONANT True skip rows with status non_resonant (kinematic and induced included); they dominate surveys coherence_alpha / COHERENCE_ALPHA 0.01 per-bin false-alarm probability α of the threshold \(\gamma^2_{\rm crit} = 1 - \alpha^{1/(n_{\rm seg}-1)}\) coherence_n_segments / COHERENCE_N_SEGMENTS 4,8,16 Welch segmentation levels; the coarsest level with a non-empty validity band decides coherence_window / COHERENCE_WINDOW hann Welch window coherence_max_lines / COHERENCE_MAX_LINES 10 strongest lines per pair and level written to coherence.csv coherence_period_min, coherence_period_max / COHERENCE_PERIOD_MIN, COHERENCE_PERIOD_MAX empty narrower search band in years; empty = the preset of the resonance type (10 kyr for secular and ZLK). The limits \(4\,\Delta t\) and \(T/(5 n_{\rm seg})\) always apply coherence_pairs (argument only) preset pairs per resonance type, e.g. {'mmr': ['sigma-a', 'sigma-e']} coherence_phase_targets (argument only) preset (target_deg, tolerance_deg) per type and pair, e.g. {'lidov_kozai': {'e-i': (180.0, 30.0)}} zlk_coherence_check / ZLK_COHERENCE_CHECK True measure zlk_coherent / zlk_check (do e and i trade at the strongest coherent line); a column only (confirmed_ei is zlk_ei_coupling, measured at the row's own period, ZLK_EI_*) zlk_min_anticorrelation / ZLK_MIN_ANTICORRELATION 0.5 minimum |r| of the band-passed e and i for that flag; provisional, calibrated on two objects

docs.title: Free elements and the free-ω gate
docs.text:
The forced/free split of the e and i vectors and the free-ω gate (Free elements). The gate is a step of the Lidov-Kozai analysis; how its outcome sets the status: Secular and Lidov-Kozai.

option / key default meaning free_elements_enabled / FREE_ELEMENTS_ENABLED True split the vectors of bodies with a Lidov-Kozai resonance; off means no split and no gate free_elements_sampling_years / FREE_ELEMENTS_SAMPLING_YEARS 500 decimate to about this step (with an anti-aliasing filter) before the split; empty keeps the integration grid free_gate_enabled / FREE_GATE_ENABLED True whether the gate's outcome enters the status; off computes and reports it only free_gate_min_cycles / FREE_GATE_MIN_CYCLES 3 libration periods the record must hold before the gate judges; fewer is no verdict free_gate_mask_quantile / FREE_GATE_MASK_QUANTILE 0.15 samples with |z_free| below this fraction of its median are dropped before unwrapping (the argument is undefined near the origin)

The planetary fundamentals of the fit are \(g_5 \ldots g_8\) and \(s_5 \ldots s_8\) of PLANETARY_FREQUENCIES (resonances/data/const.py).

docs.title: Secular angles
docs.text: option / key default meaning secular_angle_mode / SECULAR_ANGLE_MODE proper proper: the angle against the planets' mode longitudes \(g_j t + \phi_j\), the body's node from the invariable plane (what the classifier reads); osculating: from the planets' osculating elements, right only for \(g_1\), \(g_5\), \(g_6\) terms (Secular resonances) secular_remove_forced / SECULAR_REMOVE_FORCED True reduce the proper angle: subtract the forced terms at the fundamentals that are not in the angle; False removes only the invariable plane secular_planet_phases / SECULAR_PLANET_PHASES linear the planets' mode phases: the linear law of const.py, or measured in the integration (needs save_planets='all') secular_phase_window / SECULAR_PHASE_WINDOW 5000000 the sliding window of the measured phases [yr]

docs.title: Body-level filter and periodograms
docs.text:
These feed the evolution figure and the periodograms only. The classifier chooses its own cutoff for every angle (From the integration to the angle).

option / key default meaning oscillations_cutoff / LIBRATION_FILTER_CUTOFF 0.0005 cutoff [1/yr] of the Butterworth low-pass of a (a_filtered) and of the portrait edge: periods below 2000 yr are damped oscillations_filter_order / LIBRATION_FILTER_ORDER 2 order of that filter filter / FILTER butter the body-level filter; only the Butterworth filter (butter) exists periodogram_frequency_max / LIBRATION_FREQ_MAX 0.002 highest frequency of the periodograms [1/yr] periodogram_frequency_min (argument only) 1/span lowest frequency of the periodograms periodogram_soft / LIBRATION_SOFT 0.05 power above which periodogram peaks are reported libration_period_min (argument only) 5 % of the span cut from each end of a series before its periodogram

docs.title: Libration analysis settings
docs.text:
Every threshold of the libration analysis and the dry-run. Each is a SimulationConfig attribute of the same name in lower case, passed to the analysis as one frozen AnalysisSettings (sim.config.analysis_settings; resonances/resonance/analysis/settings.py). Shared rules have shared names (LIBRATION_*, FILTER_*, SEPARATRIX_*, CONFIDENCE_*), a type's own rules the prefix MMR_, SECULAR_ or ZLK_. Convention marks an agreed threshold, not derived from physics: a decision within CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND of it is a thin margin (Confidence). The rule names (L4, R0, G2c, …) are listed in the rule index. The dry-run keys change no verdict; its step rules reuse the analysis' own (cutoff, MMR_STEP_RESOLVED_DEG, MMR_RESAMPLE_STEPS_PER_CYCLE, MMR_JITTER_MAX_RAD).

The Lidov-Kozai thresholds fall into three classes by what they can change. Most are provisional: they were set on a few objects (591986, 162474) and the second class will be recalibrated on a larger ZLK sample.

class keys a column only (no status, no confidence) ZLK_MIN_ANTICORRELATION, ZLK_COHERENCE_CHECK, ZLK_EI_AMPLITUDE_FACTOR, ZLK_EI_MIN_BAND_R, ZLK_EI_BAND_HALFWIDTH, ZLK_CENTRE_MIN_CYCLES, ZLK_NODE_LOCK_MIN_CYCLES may change a status ZLK_EI_MIN_CYCLES, ZLK_EI_PHASE_TOL_DEG, ZLK_EI_EPISODE_MIN_COHERENCE, ZLK_EI_H_RESIDUAL_MAX (the deciding episode's e–i integral: an objection or, where the forced terms are small, the veto zlk_integral), ZLK_FILTER_GI_FACTOR, ZLK_LIBRATION_PERIOD_MIN_YR, ZLK_TP_PROMINENCE_DEG, ZLK_TP_RIPPLE_FACTOR, ZLK_TP_LOCAL_PROMINENCE, ZLK_TURNING_CENTRE, ZLK_RHO_WINDOW_CYCLES, ZLK_EPISODE_FREE_TURNS_PER_CYCLE, ZLK_GATE_EPISODES, ZLK_COORBITAL_HILL_FACTOR, ZLK_CENTRE_MODEL_R_MIN, ZLK_CENTRE_MODEL_AMP_FACTOR, FREE_GATE_MIN_CYCLES, FREE_GATE_MASK_QUANTILE; also ZLK_RUN_BREAK_HALF_AMPLITUDE_DEG (physical) and ZLK_ANGLE_FRAME (a model choice), which are not provisional a budget (the action and extend_to_years only) ZLK_EXTEND_RESOLUTION_MARGIN, ZLK_EXTEND_MAX_YR, MMR_EXTEND_MIN_SPAN_FACTOR, MMR_NEXT_CHECK_SPAN_FACTOR, MMR_EXTEND_FORCE_WINDOWS

The tables below are generated from the code (uv run python docs/tools/config_table.py).

docs.text: key default meaning FILTER_ORDER 2 Butterworth order N of the sos low-pass; filtfilt gain G(P) = 1/(1 + (tan(pi dt/P)/tan(pi dt/P_c))^(2N)) (-> 1/(1 + (P_c/P)^(2N)) for P_c >> dt) FILTER_EDGE_TRIM_CUTOFFS 1.0 turning points, passes and portrait use [t0 + x P_c, t1 - x P_c]: filtfilt edges spread ~ +-P_c FILTER_MIN_LIBRATION_CUTOFFS 2.0 the floor term of the cutoff is the shortest libration / this (MMR: P_floor, secular/ZLK: P_min): where it sets P_c, that libration keeps G = 1/(1 + this^-4) = 0.94; secular/ZLK: a measured libration period below this many P_c sets filter_too_slow (MMR: G(P_cyc) below MMR_L8_GAIN_FULL); shape checks become not_measured FILTER_GRID_RTOL 0.001 a time grid is uniform for the filter when every step is within this fraction of the median step (REBOUND rounding) MMR_FILTER_SYNODIC_FACTOR 1.5 P_c >= this x the longest synodic period with the planets of the angle (leak <= 0.5 deg) MMR_FILTER_ORBIT_FACTOR 1.5 P_c >= this x the body's own orbital period 2 pi / n() (0 = off): heliocentric elements are osculating about GM_sun alone, while a body moves about the Sun and the planets inside its orbit, so its a and lambda carry a wave at its own P_orb (half-amplitude in a ~ 2 e a sum m_inside / M_sun); it binds only beyond a planet's 1:2, where P_orb > P_syn (TNOs: 15874 5N-23, 523683 2U-9 at 379 yr); barycentric elements are a separate study Convention.
