docs.title: Integration options
docs.text:
See rebound documentation for explanation of the integrator's settings.

  • tmax/INTEGRATION_TMAX (int): the end of the integration in REBOUND units, where 2π is one year: 1000 years is 1000*2π ≈ 6283. Default 628319 (100 kyr). A negative value integrates backwards; every quantity computed on the series puts it in time order first, and plots show the actual negative times. integration_years (argument) sets the span in years and wins over tmax.
  • dt/INTEGRATION_DT (float): the step of the integration in rebound units (2π = 1 yr), or the initial step of an adaptive integrator. By default, 1.0 = 58 days. See Step size.
  • integrator/INTEGRATION_INTEGRATOR (string): the default integrator from rebound. By default, SABA(10,6,4). See rebound documentation.
  • integration_safe_mode/INTEGRATION_SAFE_MODE (int or empty): safe_mode of WHFast and SABA. Empty (default) keeps the integrator's own default: 0 for WHFast (with 1 its corrector would run at every step) and 1 for SABA, which is what earlier versions used, so their runs are reproduced bit for bit. 0 merges the drifts of consecutive steps and is faster; rebound still synchronizes at every output time, but the orbits differ from 1 at round-off level (SABA, dt=1, a = 2.2 AU: |Δa| ≈ 3·10⁻⁹ AU after 20 kyr) and chaotic or planet-crossing orbits diverge, so a run with 0 does not reproduce one with 1. See rebound documentation.
  • integration_corrector/INTEGRATION_CORRECTOR (int): the parameter of the corrector for symplectic integrators. By default, 17. See rebound documentation
  • SOLAR_SYSTEM_FILE (str): the name of the cache file used to store the initial data of the Sun, planets, and Pluto. It is used to speed up the creation of the simulation. By default, cache/solar.bin. Note that in order to avoid issues with initial date&time, the app will automatically add postfix equals to the timestamp of the simulation date, i.e., cache/solar-12345.bin, and cache/solar-moon-12345.bin for the system with the Moon.
  • solar_system_moon/SOLAR_SYSTEM_MOON (bool): the Moon as a separate body. Default: False. See below.

docs.title: Step size
docs.text:
The default dt = 1.0 (58 days) is shorter than the orbit of every planet but Mercury (88 days, 1.5 steps per orbit). With SABA(10,6,4) this is enough for the planets' secular dynamics and for the main belt. Measured against ias15 and SABA with dt = 0.5 (2026-10-13): over 2 Myr the planetary frequencies g1, g2, g5, g6, s1, s6 agree with dt = 0.5 to better than 2e-4″/yr; over 2 kyr Mercury's mean longitude is 1.8° off ias15 (0.04° with dt = 0.5), while a main-belt orbit (a = 1.8–3 AU) is within 3e-4° and Jupiter within 3e-6°. WHFast at the same steps is not: Mercury's longitude was 180° off, an asteroid at 2.5 AU 0.3°.

A fixed step needs about ten steps per orbit of the asteroid itself: the run logs a warning below MIN_STEPS_PER_ORBIT = 10 (a < 1.36 AU at dt = 1). Close encounters are not resolved by a fixed step, whatever the period. Before integrating, the dry-run flags bodies that cross a planet's band (within DRYRUN_HILL_MARGIN Hill radii) or have q < DRYRUN_NEA_Q, and recommends ias15 for them; it screens the orbits, it does not predict each encounter. With dt = 1, 162474 was ejected (an unphysical orbit: status invalid); with dt = 0.5 it was not.

docs.title: Solar system model
docs.text:
By default the massive bodies are the Sun, Mercury–Neptune and Pluto, fetched from NASA Horizons by name. Earth is then Horizons body 3, the Earth–Moon barycenter, with the Earth+Moon mass. That is fine for asteroids that stay far from the Earth.

With solar_system_moon=True (IntegrationEngine.create_solar_system_with_moon) the Earth is the geocenter (Horizons 399) and the Moon (Horizons 301) is an eleventh body, appended after Pluto. The planets keep their particle indices, so every resonant angle is built as before, with the Earth's angles now taken against the geocenter. The Moon is never a planet of an angle and is not in the saved planet series. Earth and Moon together have exactly the mass, position and velocity of the barycenter. The price: the geocenter's heliocentric osculating elements carry the Moon's monthly reflex (about 12.6 m/s). Measured against the barycenter, a differs by up to 1e-3 AU, e by 9e-4, λ by 0.05° and ϖ by 3°. The saved Earth series and every Earth angle (the 1:1 angle by 0.05°, any secular angle with g3 or s3 much more) contain this term, sampled at the output step. Use it for objects with close Earth encounters (Earth co-orbitals, NEAs): within a few lunar distances the barycenter is a poor stand-in for the two bodies.

Only ias15 is accepted with the Moon; any other integrator raises ValueError when the simulation is created or the integrator is set up. A fixed-step symplectic split around the Sun cannot follow a 27-day orbit with steps of days to months. Measured over 100 yr (2023-02-25 start, against ias15): WHFast, SABA(10,6,4), MERCURIUS and TRACE with dt = 0.05 (3 days) all put the Earth 0.03 AU off along its orbit; MERCURIUS and TRACE still 0.0015 AU with dt = 0.01, at 3 and 0.3 times the CPU of ias15. The hybrid integrators gave the same error as WHFast, although the Moon never leaves the Earth's encounter radius.

N_active is set to the number of massive bodies (10, or 11 with the Moon); the asteroids are test particles.

docs.title: Horizons and TLS
docs.text: The planets are fetched by rebound, which uses Python's urllib. Python's default CA bundle may lack the root certificate JPL uses (macOS /etc/ssl/cert.pem had no Sectigo Public Server Authentication Root R46 in October 2026). While it fetches the planets, the package therefore verifies against certifi's bundle, and restores rebound's urlopen afterwards. Verification is never switched off. If SSL_CERT_FILE is set, it is used instead. Setting SSL_CERT_FILE from inside a running Python process is not enough once any HTTPS connection has been verified there: OpenSSL keeps the store it loaded first.

docs.title: Access to the parameters of rebound
docs.text:
While resonances wraps many Rebound integrator settings, you can still manipulate Rebound directly. The rebound simulation is sim.integration_engine.sim; it exists after create_solar_system():

sim = resonances.Simulation()
sim.create_solar_system()
sim.integration_engine.sim.ri_ias15.epsilon = 1e-10

run_integration() calls setup_integrator(), which sets integrator, dt and N_active (the number of massive bodies, 10 or 11 with the Moon), the WHFast corrector when INTEGRATION_CORRECTOR is set and the SABA safe mode. Change those through the config (sim.config.dt = 0.01), not on the rebound object: direct values are overwritten.

docs.title: AstDyS and Catalog options
docs.text:
• source/DATA_SOURCE (str): where the asteroids' elements come from, nasa (default), astdys or mpc (Minor Planet Center, below). The planets always come from NASA Horizons, at date.
  • date (str or datetime): the start of the integration. Default: the catalog epoch for astdys and mpc (whether set by argument, .env or environment), today's midnight for nasa. A timezone-aware datetime is taken as its naive UTC value (one instant for the planets, the bodies and the clones); a naive one as it is. find() and check() take the Horizons elements at this date. Elements that carry an epoch (AstDyS and MPC rows, Horizons, or your own dict, as MJD or a date) must be at date: add_body raises ValueError otherwise, since REBOUND would start the body at the wrong place on its orbit relative to the planets (MPC rows at another epoch are propagated to date by default, below).
  • Numbers passed to Horizons (401 or '401') are always asteroid numbers: a bare '401' would be Phobos.
  • The AstDyS catalog is downloaded and cached by the astdys package.

docs.title: Minor Planet Center (source='mpc')
docs.text:
The elements come from MPCORB.DAT (resonances/mpcorb/, a self-contained subpackage; the package's side, MPC_* keys and the epoch policy, is resonances/simulation/mpc_source.py): heliocentric osculating elements in the J2000 ecliptic with μ = k² (n = k a^−1.5 holds on every row of the file to its rounding), at an epoch in TT. Most rows share the standard epoch (MJD 61200 = 2026-06-09 on the 2026-10-25 file, the epoch of AstDyS too; it moves in steps of 200 days), which is the default date. The date is the TT calendar value, and Horizons reads it as TDB for the planets (TT − TDB < 2 ms), as for AstDyS. The planets come from Horizons (DE441), the MPC's fit used DE431 and the AST17 asteroid perturbers: integrated by the package for 138 days, the MPC elements of 433, 719 and 887 reproduce the MPC's own propagation to the file's rounding (5·10⁻⁸ AU, 5·10⁻⁶ deg).

  • MPC_CATALOG: mpcorb (default, MPCORB.DAT.gz, 94 MB, 1.58 M orbits), nea, neam00 (NEAs at today's epoch), distant, unusual, or the URL (https:// or file://) of a file in the same format.
  • The file is downloaded on first use into MPC_CACHE_DIR/<catalog>/ (default cache/mpc, next to the AstDyS catalog), parsed into a table (the file's own digits) and described in snapshot.json: URL, ETag, Last-Modified, the sha256 of the downloaded bytes, row counts, the standard epoch. Each download is a generation of its own files (<sha12>-MPCORB.DAT.gz, table-<sha12>-p<parser>.csv), published by replacing snapshot.json; the previous generation is kept, older ones are deleted, and so are staging files (*.part) older than a day. A simulation records these in simulation.json (mpc_snapshot), and a batch run resumes only on the same snapshot. Workers get the elements from their parent and never open the catalog.
  • The catalog is refreshed only by resonances mpc-update [--catalog=...] [--force] (or resonances.mpcorb.update_catalog()): a conditional GET on the ETag, then the download, its Content-Length, and a parse that must find MPCORB records with μ = k² before the old snapshot is replaced. A failed update keeps the old one. Older than MPC_MAX_AGE_DAYS (30; 0 = never) days since its Last-Modified, it only warns. MPC_SHA256 refuses any other snapshot.
  • A body is found by number (463, '(463)', packed '00463', 'A1429' = 101429, '~02pM' = 630872), by provisional designation, packed or not ('2001 ND13', '2001ND13', 'K01N13D', the extended '_PO00fh' = 2025 OL723), the principal designation of a numbered object without a name ('1998 VF31'), or a name; designations and names in any case. An empty identifier, or one that matches two rows, raises ValueError. A list is looked up in one pass over the table (64,000 numbers in 0.5 s).
  • MPC_EPOCH_POLICY: propagate (default) integrates every row whose epoch is not date, as test particles with IAS15 in the run's planets taken at their own epoch, to the common date, and the run then integrates all bodies together. Each such body gets a warning (designation, gap in days, U, arc and oppositions), and find adds one line, "N bodies propagated from other epochs, max gap X d"; the element dict has propagated_from_epoch. In the 2026-10-25 file they are 1,891 of 1.58 M rows: the 1,865 unperturbed one-opposition orbits of its last section, each at its own epoch, and 26 others (impactors such as 2008 TC3, orbits left at the previous standard epoch). The propagation was validated against the MPC's own propagation of 433, 719 and 887 to Δa ≤ 5·10⁻⁸ AU over 138 days; asteroid perturbers, relativity and non-gravitational forces are not in the model. A one-opposition orbit with an old epoch is poorly determined whatever the propagation: the integration carries its elements, not its uncertainty. MPC_PROPAGATE_MAX_DAYS (empty by default: no limit) is an optional safety limit on the span; a longer one is refused (for the clones of Clones, only a warning). strict refuses every such row (add_body/check raise; find leaves the body out with a warning, as one not in the catalog).
  • MPC_WARN_U (6): a warning for orbits with the uncertainty parameter U ≥ this, a letter (E: eccentricity assumed) or none, and for unperturbed orbits.
  • mpc_lookup/MPC_LOOKUP: file (default) = an identifier the cached catalog lacks is not found (find leaves it out); file_then_api = its nominal orbit comes from MPC's get-orb API: aliases such as a secondary designation, objects outside an MPC_CATALOG subset, objects newer than the snapshot. The answer is cached in CLONES_CACHE_DIR/mpc/ with its sha256 (in the body's elements, getorb_sha256; a batch run resumes only with the same elements and sha256); only the nominal is read, so an answer without a covariance or with U ≥ 3 is used (U ≥ MPC_WARN_U warns). Elements from its KEP block, else its CAR block (μ = k²), at its epoch, then MPC_EPOCH_POLICY as for a row. A failed request is a refusal (find leaves the body out). Only explicitly named identifiers are asked for, in the main process; a search (query, search_by_axis) is never widened.
  • Each element dict (body.initial_data, simulation.json) carries source, packed, number, designation, mpc_name, U, perturbers and catalog_sha256.
  • Only the elements of the run come from MPCORB. find() without type (or with type='secular' and no formulas) also searches secular resonances, and that search reads the AstDyS synthetic proper frequencies g and s of each body whatever source is (SecularResonanceFinder): a body AstDyS does not list gets no secular candidates (a warning), one listed without g or s stops the search with ValueError. Pass type='mmr', or formulas=[...], to stay off AstDyS. The Lidov-Kozai angle is added to every body without a catalog search. The same holds for source='nasa'.
  • MPC's per-object orbit API (get-orb) gives the covariance: the clones read it (CLONES_SOURCE=mpc, Clones); the elements of a run still come from MPCORB.

docs.title: Selecting objects of the catalog
docs.text:
resonances.mpcorb searches the cached catalog (the one MPC_CATALOG names), as the astdys package does AstDyS:

from resonances import mpcorb  # noqa: E402

mpcorb.search(463)  # the elements of (463) Lola (radians, epoch MJD TT); None if absent
mpcorb.search([1, '2001 ND13'])  # {identifier: elements}
mpcorb.search_by_axis(2.4, sigma=0.01)  # DataFrame of the rows with 2.39 <= a <= 2.41 AU
mpcorb.query(a=(0, 1))  # orbits inside 1 AU
mpcorb.query(q=(None, 1.3), H=(None, 18), U=(0, 3), numbered=True)
mpcorb.query(orbit_type=['apollo', 'aten'], pha=True, epoch='standard')
mpcorb.query(node=(350, 10))  # angle ranges may wrap through 0

query takes inclusive ranges (min, max) (None for an open end) on a, e, i, q = a(1−e), Q = a(1+e), H, node, peri, M (degrees), n_obs, n_opp, arc_years (last minus first year of observation; days/365.25 for a one-opposition orbit) and U (0–9; a row with a letter or no U fails a U range), plus epoch ('any' or 'standard'), numbered (True/False) and the MPC flags of columns 162–165 (MPOrbitFormat): orbit_type (atira, aten, apollo, amor, q_lt_1665 = q < 1.665 AU, hungaria, mpc_internal (value 7, "internal MPC use", 16,289 rows near a = q = 2 AU), hilda, jupiter_trojan, distant) and neo, km_neo, pha, one_opp_earlier, critical_list (True/False). The MPC says its classification "is not 100% reliable". The result has the elements, q, Q, H, U, n_obs, n_opp, arc_years, flags, orbit_type and the flag columns. find and check take it as the list of bodies:

sim = resonances.find(mpcorb.query(a=(2.38, 2.42), numbered=True, U=(0, 2)), planets=['Jupiter', 'Saturn'], type='mmr', source='mpc')

From the shell: resonances mpc-search --a 0:1 --e :0.3 --limit 20 prints a table, --output sel.csv writes every row, --ids prints the identifiers for find --asteroids=... (resonances mpc-search --help lists every option).

resonances/mpcorb/ imports nothing else of the package (settings come as mpcorb.Settings or arguments, messages go to the mpcorb logger), so it can be moved out as a package of its own; inside resonances its defaults are the MPC_* keys.

docs.title: Matrices
docs.text:
The catalogs of mean-motion resonances are bounded by the MATRIX_ keys (Resonance matrices). Each cached file carries a build record (<file>.meta.json); a file built with other limits or planets logs a warning, so delete the cached CSV after changing a limit to rebuild it. A file written by an older version of the package (first line not the current catalog stamp) is rebuilt automatically.

key default meaning MATRIX_2BODY_PRIMARY_MAX 12 the planet's coefficient runs from 1 to this − 1 MATRIX_2BODY_COEF_MAX 11 the asteroid's coefficient runs from −this to −1 MATRIX_2BODY_ORDER_MAX 10 largest order (|sum of the coefficients of the mean longitudes|); also bounds the degree of the subresonances the MMR analysis scans MATRIX_2BODY_FILE cache/mmr-2body.csv the cached two-body catalog (resonant semi-major axes) MATRIX_3BODY_PRIMARY_MAX 8 the first planet's coefficient runs from 1 to this − 1 MATRIX_3BODY_COEF_MAX 7 the coefficients of the second planet and the asteroid run from −this to this − 1 MATRIX_3BODY_ORDER_MAX 6 largest order; also bounds the subresonances scanned MATRIX_3BODY_FILE cache/mmr-3body.csv the cached three-body catalog MATRIX_2BODY_RETRO_COEF_MAX 15 largest p and q of a retrograde p/−q resonance (1J-3r0) MATRIX_2BODY_RETRO_ORDER_MAX 30 largest order p + q of a retrograde resonance (with the coefficient limit: the 143 resonances per planet of Li et al. 2019) MATRIX_2BODY_RETRO_FILE cache/mmr-2body-retro.csv the cached retrograde catalog, every k for every pair

docs.title: Batch options
docs.text:
• batch_enabled/BATCH_ENABLED (bool): run more than batch_threshold bodies in batches, each in its own process. Default: True.
  • batch_threshold/BATCH_THRESHOLD (int): the number of bodies above which batching starts. Default: 100.
  • batch_size/BATCH_SIZE (int or empty): bodies per batch. Empty: 50, or fewer so that every core gets two batches. Default: 100.
  • n_cores/BATCH_N_CORES (int): worker processes. Default: 3.
  • LOW_MEMORY_ALLOCATOR (auto, on, off): the allocator of spawned worker processes (batch runs, benchmark reclassify). On macOS on starts them with MallocLargeCache=0, so freed large blocks return to the system instead of staying in the worker's footprint: benchmark workers peak at 1.4 GB instead of 2.3 GB, with the same results and more CPU time. auto turns it on where memory, not the CPUs, limits the number of workers (the benchmark's --workers auto then sizes them at 1.6 GB instead of 3 GB); a batch run's n_cores is set by the user, so auto leaves it off there. Other systems: no policy (not measured). make test* run the tests with it (LOW_MEMORY_ALLOCATOR=off make ... does not). Default: auto.

A batched run can be resumed in the same save_path; see Serialization.

docs.title: Clone options
docs.text:
Clones (virtual asteroids) drawn from an orbit fit's covariance; see Clones.

  • clones/CLONES (int): clones of every body added by its number or designation (add_body, check, find, CLI --clones=N); 0 = none. 100 gives a status share to ±10 % (95 %, Wilson), 400 to ±5 %, 1000 to ±3 %. Default: 0.
  • clones_source/CLONES_SOURCE: auto (the provider of DATA_SOURCE: astdys → astdys, mpc → mpc, nasa → sbdb), astdys (numbered asteroids), neodys (NEAs), sbdb (JPL) or mpc (refused for U ≥ 3). Default: auto.
  • clones_epoch/CLONES_EPOCH: for AstDyS/NEODyS, fit (.eq0, the fit's own epoch) or standard (.eq1, the catalog's epoch, a linear propagation of .eq0); empty = standard for astdys, fit for neodys. A covariance at another epoch than date is sampled there and every clone integrated to date.
  • clones_seed/CLONES_SEED (int): the seed; each body's generator is seeded by (seed, crc32(name)). Default: 0.
  • clones_batch/CLONES_BATCH (int): clones per REBOUND simulation; the batches run on n_cores processes after the ordinary bodies. Default: 20.
  • clones_max_invalid/CLONES_MAX_INVALID (float, a share): the largest share of draws that are no bound orbit (e < 0, e ≥ 1, a ≤ 0) for which clones.csv gives shares. The shares are over the bound draws only; above this the Gaussian is no usable model of the orbit's uncertainty and the row has cloud_usable False and no shares. A convention. Default: 0.05.
  • clones_plot_each/CLONES_PLOT_EACH (bool): the figures of every clone as of an ordinary body; otherwise only the ensemble figure (plot kind clones, also drawn with combined). Default: False.
  • CLONES_CACHE_DIR (str): the downloaded orbit solutions, <dir>/<source>/<file> and <file>.meta.json. Default: cache/clones.
  • Resume: resume_enabled (default on) covers a run with clones as a whole (checkpoint clones_state/; a changed identity raises ValueError); see Clones.

docs.title: Other
docs.text:
• LOG_FILE (str): the path to the file where the app stores log data.
  • LOG_LEVEL (str): the default level what the app should store in the log file (options: debug, info, warning, error, critical). The default value is info.

docs.title: Simulations, bodies, resonances
docs.text: A run has three parts: a Simulation (the planets, the integrator and every setting), the bodies added to it, each with the resonances to check, and sim.run(), which integrates, analyses every angle and writes the results. resonances.check and resonances.find build such a simulation for you.

docs.title: The simulation
docs.text:
import numpy as np

import resonances

sim = resonances.Simulation(
    name='core-demo',  # the output goes to SAVE_PATH/core-demo (cache/core-demo by default)
    date='2026-01-01',  # start of the integration; the planets and the elements are taken at this date
    integration_years=2_000,  # 100_000 years for a real verdict of a main-belt MMR
    integrator='SABA(10,6,4)',  # the default; 'whfast' or 'ias15' for close encounters
    dt=1.0,  # REBOUND time units: 1.0 = 1/(2 pi) yr = 58.1 days
    output_step=1.0,  # years between saved points (default: about 100 REBOUND units = 15.9 yr)
    save='all',  # which (body, resonance) rows to save: none, all, resonant, candidates, nonzero, ...
    plot='resonant',  # which rows to plot, by the same status filters
    plots=['combined'],  # the one-page verdict figure
)
sim.create_solar_system()

Every keyword becomes an attribute of sim.config (sim.config.integrator, sim.config.save_path, ...) and can be changed there before sim.run(). A keyword not given takes its value from a .env file in the working directory, else from the package defaults; Configuration lists them all. The ones used most:

keyword default meaning date today (source nasa); the catalog epoch (astdys, mpc) start of the integration; the planets come from NASA Horizons at this date source nasa where the elements of a body given by number or name come from: nasa (Horizons), astdys, mpc integration_years or tmax 100 000 yr the span; tmax is in REBOUND units (see below), negative for a backward run integrator, dt SABA(10,6,4), 1.0 the REBOUND integrator and its step in REBOUND units; whfast, ias15 (adaptive) also work output_step or Nout \(N_\text{out} = \lfloor\lvert t_\text{max}\rvert/100\rfloor\) points, i.e. a step of about 100 REBOUND units = 15.9 yr (exactly \(\lvert t_\text{max}\rvert/[2\pi(N_\text{out}-1)]\) yr) years between saved points, or the number of points; 'auto' lets the dry-run choose a step that folds no short-period term save, plot review which (body, resonance) rows are saved and plotted, by status (below) plots ['combined'] figure kinds (Plots) name, save_path, plot_path cache/<name> where the output goes (Output data) plot_layout confidence/status subfolders of the figures (Examples)

Time units. REBOUND works in units where \(G = 1\), the Sun's mass is 1 and the distance unit is the au, so one year is \(2\pi\) time units. tmax, dt and sim.times are in these units: tmax = 2π × years, and dt = 1.0 is \(1/(2\pi)\) yr \(\approx\) 58.1 days. Years are sim.times / (2 * np.pi); integration_years and output_step are in years.

docs.title: Bodies
docs.text:
sim.add_body(463, '4J-2S-1', name='463')  # by number, one resonance
sim.add_body('2001 ND13', ['1V-3', 'g-g6'], name='2001 ND13')  # by designation, several resonances
elements = {  # by elements: heliocentric J2000 ecliptic, angles in radians, epoch in MJD (optional)
    'a': 2.395,
    'e': 0.22,
    'inc': np.radians(13.5),
    'Omega': np.radians(97.0),
    'omega': np.radians(180.0),
    'M': np.radians(10.0),
}
sim.add_body(elements, resonances.TwoBody('3J-1'), name='synthetic')

A body is given by its number or designation (the elements are then taken from source at date) or by a dict of osculating heliocentric elements in the J2000 ecliptic: a in au, e, and inc, Omega, omega, M in radians. An epoch key (MJD) is checked against date: elements at another epoch are refused, since the planets are placed at date. With source='mpc' an MPC row at another epoch is integrated to date first (Configuration).

docs.title: Resonances
docs.text:
A resonance is given as an object or as a string; strings are parsed by resonances.create_resonance.

mmr2 = resonances.create_mmr('3J-1')  # two-body: 3 lambda_J - lambda - 2 varpi
mmr3 = resonances.create_mmr('4J-2S-1')  # three-body: 4 lambda_J - 2 lambda_S - lambda + 0 + 0 - varpi
retro = resonances.RetrogradeTwoBody('1J-3r0')  # retrograde p/-q with k (orbits with i > 90 deg)
nu6 = resonances.SecularResonance('g-g6')  # linear secular resonance
z1 = resonances.create_resonance('g-g6+s-s6')  # the factory reads any notation
lk = resonances.LidovKozaiResonance()  # the argument of perihelion omega
print(mmr2.to_s(), mmr3.to_s(), retro.to_s(), nu6.to_s(), z1.to_s(), lk.to_s())
print(round(mmr3.resonant_axis, 4))  # nominal catalogue axis a_res [au]; the analysed a* is ctx_a_star_au
class notation angle TwoBody 3J-1 (short) or 3J-1+0-2 (full) \(3\lambda_J - \lambda - 2\varpi\) (Resonance matrices) ThreeBody 4J-2S-1 or 4J-2S-1+0+0-1 \(4\lambda_J - 2\lambda_S - \lambda - \varpi\) RetrogradeTwoBody 1J-3r0 (p, planet, q, k) p/−q resonance of an orbit with \(i > 90°\) (Resonance matrices) SecularResonance g-g6, g-g6+s-s6, 2(g-g6)+(s-s6) combinations of the body's and the planets' secular frequencies (Secular resonances) LidovKozaiResonance LK the argument of perihelion \(\omega\) (Lidov-Kozai resonances)

The full key (4J-2S-1+0+0-1) is the one in the output files and in body.statuses. The short form fills the perihelion coefficients so that the coefficients sum to zero (d'Alembert's rule), putting the remainder on the body's \(\varpi\).

docs.title: check and find
docs.text:
• resonances.check(asteroids, resonance, **kwargs) checks the given resonances for the given bodies (Quick start).
  • resonances.find(asteroids, planets=None, type=None, **kwargs) looks for candidates: the MMRs whose resonant semi-major axis is within sigma2 = 0.1 au (two-body) or sigma3 = 0.02 au (three-body) of the body's \(a\) (sigma_retro = 0.5 au for \(i > 90°\)), the secular resonances satisfied by the body's proper frequencies \(g\), \(s\) (from the AstDyS synthetic catalog; formulas= gives your own) and the Lidov-Kozai angle. type='mmr', 'secular' or 'lidov_kozai' limits the search (Examples).

Both return a Simulation with the bodies added; call sim.run(). Their default name is resonance_find, so their output goes to cache/resonance_find (with a time stamp when that folder is not empty).

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
report = sim.dry_run()  # optional: checks the output step and the integrator before integrating
sim.run()

sim.run() first runs the static dry-run (its warnings go to the log), then integrates, analyses every angle and writes the output. With more than BATCH_THRESHOLD (100) bodies, or with clones, the work is split between worker processes: on macOS and Windows such a script needs an if __name__ == '__main__': guard (Examples).

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text:
for body in sim.bodies:
    for key, verdict in body.librations.items():
        print(body.name, key, verdict.status, verdict.angle_status, verdict.reason, verdict.confidence, verdict.action)
    print(body.statuses)  # {key: status string}

body = sim.bodies[0]
t = sim.times / (2 * np.pi)  # years since the start: REBOUND time is years * 2 pi
angle = body.angle(mmr3)  # the resonant angle, radians in [0, 2 pi)
print(len(t), body.axis[:3], angle[:3])

body.librations[key] is the full verdict (a Verdict): status, angle_status, reason, libration_origin, confidence, action, extend_to_years, final_regime, orbit_type, the checks and the decision path. Its values are strings (How the status is determined). body.statuses[key] is the status alone. The time series are body.axis, body.ecc, body.inc, body.Omega, body.omega, body.M, body.longitude, body.varpi and body.angle(resonance) (radians).

summary = sim.data_manager.get_simulation_summary(sim.bodies)
print(summary[['name', 'resonance', 'status', 'angle_status', 'confidence', 'reason']])

docs.title: What is saved and plotted
docs.text: save and plot select the (body, resonance) rows by their status; the modes (review by default, nonzero, all, resonant, candidates, ...) are listed in Configuration. summary.csv always holds every row (save_summary=True). The files and folders are described in Output data; a saved run can be read back with SimulationSerializer.restore.

docs.title: Dry-run: check a run before integrating it
docs.text:
A run of hours or days can be spoiled by its output step (an aliased angle, a filter that cannot see a short libration) or by its integrator (a fixed step through close encounters). The dry-run predicts this from the bodies' elements, before anything is integrated. It changes no verdict. The rules it applies are those of the analysis (From the integration to the angle: alias, cutoff, shortest libration).

import resonances

sim = resonances.Simulation(name='dry-run-demo', integration_years=100_000, output_step='auto')
sim.create_solar_system()
sim.add_body(463, '4J-2S-1', name='463')  # or resonances.find(...) / resonances.check(...)
report = sim.dry_run(level='static')  # elements only: milliseconds per body
report = sim.dry_run(level='pilot')  # a short fine integration per body: 1-3 s each
report.summary()  # tables and warnings
rows, bodies, run = report.rows, report.bodies, report.run  # DataFrame body x MMR, DataFrame of bodies, dict of the run
report.apply()  # set output_step/Nout and the recommended integrator/dt on the config
report.to_csv('out')  # dryrun_rows.csv, dryrun_bodies.csv, dryrun_run.json

Command line: resonances dry-run <arguments of find, or of check with --resonances> [--pilot] [--years N] [--step auto|YR] [--fair] [--out DIR]. resonances find and resonances check run the static level before integrating and write its warnings to the log; with OUTPUT_STEP=auto they set the step from it.

docs.title: What is checked (per MMR row)
docs.text:
Notation: \(\sigma = \sum_j k_j\lambda_j + k\lambda + p\varpi + \sum_j p_j\varpi_j + v\Omega + \sum_j v_j\Omega_j\), \(\Delta t\) the output step, a in au, t in years (2π REBOUND units), rates in rad/yr. For a retrograde angle the body's terms are \(\lambda^* = M + \omega - \Omega\) and \(\varpi^* = \omega - \Omega\) (Resonance matrices). The static body precession is the Laplace-Lagrange free rate of a test particle (Murray & Dermott 1999, §7.9), \(\dot\varpi = A\), \(\dot\Omega = -A\),

\[ A = rac n4\sum_j \mu_j\,\alpha_j ar\alpha_j\,b_{3/2}^{(1)}(\alpha_j), \qquad b_s^{(m)}(\alpha) = rac1\pi\int_0^{2\pi} rac{\cos m\psi\,{ m d}\psi}{(1 - 2\alpha\cos\psi + \alpha^2)^s}, \]

with \(\mu_j = m_j/M_\odot\), \(\alpha_j = \min(a, a_j)/\max(a, a_j)\), \( ar\alpha_j = 1\) for an inner planet and \(\alpha_j\) for an outer one. It is omitted (taken as 0) for planet-crossers and retrograde orbits.

check formula columns rate of σ \( u(a) = \sum_j k_j n_j + k\,n(a) + p\dot\varpi + \sum_j p_j g_j + v\dot\Omega + \sum_j v_j s_j\), \(n = 2\pi a^{-3/2}\); \(n_j\) of the package model (Murray & Dermott 1999, eq. 8.22); docs.title: Secular and Lidov-Kozai rows
docs.text:
Advisory and static (also at the pilot level): warnings only, no step and no verdict change. Table long_period (file dryrun_long_period.csv), one row per secular or ZLK angle, with the analysis' own rules (secular signal):

A 100-kyr run of a secular angle warns span 100000 yr < 500000 yr …: no libration can be confirmed there, and the verdict will be uncertain / baseline_needed with a next check of 400 kyr (How long to extend).

docs.title: Per body
docs.text: class (main, nea for q < DRYRUN_NEA_Q, crosser when [q, Q] overlaps a planet's [q_j − h R_H, Q_j + h R_H], h = DRYRUN_HILL_MARGIN), integrator_recommended and dt_recommended_yr: ias15 for crossers and NEAs (adaptive steps for encounters), otherwise SABA(10,6,4) with dt = min(run dt, P/DRYRUN_STEPS_PER_ORBIT, τ_peri/DRYRUN_STEPS_PER_PERI), τ_peri = P√((1−e)³/(1+e)) the effective period at pericentre (Lu, Hernandez & Rein 2024, eq. 33; the /10 rule is provisional). fair_step_yr = DRYRUN_FAIR_FRACTION × P; the pilot adds moid_<planet> (a grid screen at the epoch: information, nodes precess), the measured ⟨a⟩, δa_sp, δe_sp, ϖ̇, n from λ and its wall time. A crosser's a jumps at encounters, so its static alias verdict holds only for a₀ ± DRYRUN_DA_STATIC (it says so).

docs.title: The run and OUTPUT_STEP=auto
docs.text:
Δt_auto = min(libration, short_period, filter, trend, FAIR, user) (short_period and filter are exclusive bounds), rounded down to DRYRUN_AUTO_STEPS_YR, then walked down DRYRUN_AUTO_STEPS_YR to the first step at which no row folds a harmonic slower than its period floor (binding_rule short_period_harmonic when it moved, step_fold_free_yr in the run; when no step of the grid is fold-free the rounded step stays and its harmonic rows keep short_period_aliased: P_orb 10.001 yr gives short_period 5.0005 yr, but 5 yr folds 2/P_orb to 50 kyr; 2.5 yr folds nothing); Nout = ⌈span/Δt⌉ + 1 (at least 2), so the grid step never exceeds Δt. short_period is the smallest min(P_orb, P_syn)/2 of the rows, trend the smallest predictive safe step, FAIR counts only with DRYRUN_FAIR=required (or --fair), user is DRYRUN_MAX_STEP_YR. With the default settings the short periods decide in the main belt (a = 2.5 au: 1 yr; a Hilda: 2.5 yr) and for NEAs (1999 UQ: 0.5 yr), the libration bound for a Jupiter Trojan (2.5 yr). After a run, each record's own fold-free step is in smp_fold_free_step_yr (the same walk for that row alone on MMR_RESAMPLE_STEPS_YR, see output.md), and action=resample names it when the folded periods withdraw a check the level needs (R-ALIAS-A, rsp_short_period_unmeasured). auto is defined only for runs with MMRs; a purely secular or ZLK run keeps Nout. A numeric OUTPUT_STEP sets Nout = ⌈span/step⌉ + 1; an explicit Nout overrides both. The default step is unchanged (15.9 yr): a Hilda keeps P_c = 75 yr there and its libration, but every main-belt row is flagged short_period_aliased (the full tree, v2_verdict, caps it at medium; the final level drops only where a check is withdrawn). The run warns of each limit the configured step is above; the pilot lifts the short-period warning when it accepts the step for every flagged row (153 Hilda and the Trojans: leaks 0.1–0.7°, ε 0.1–0.2), and keeps it when not (62243 1M-4J-1: 2.4°, ε 5.9). A row below that step whose harmonic folds slower than the floor and whose leak the pilot rejects adds the short_period_harmonic limit, with the fold-free step to use instead. The analysis does not read the pilot: the cap stays on every such row except a plain circulation.

The run also gets the recommended integrator (ias15 if any body needs it; mixed_integrators then suggests separate runs), the cost (rows, disk_GB if every body is saved, ram_per_worker_GB, cpu_hours; coefficients measured in 2026-10, the pilot's own speed when present) and step_spread.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• 1999 UQ 7E+2M-9, ias15, 20 kyr, Nout 4000 (5.0012 yr). Static: aliased_unambiguous, 0.994 turns per step, ghost 1.0941756 au, 1.2·10⁻⁴ au from a₀: the "libration" of the record was a stroboscope. The pilot puts ⟨a⟩ 2·10⁻⁶ au from the ghost, gives 71.98°/yr (3999 turns in 20 kyr, as the 1-yr rerun) and finds the real 97-yr forced wave 7n_E − 8n (9.6°). At 1 yr the angle is resolved (0.2 turns per step).
  • 153 Hilda 3J-2, SABA, 100 kyr. Class main, SABA with dt = 58 d. Pilot: the libration line at 273 yr (the 1-yr record: 268 yr).
  • 1865 Cerberus. Crosses Venus, Earth and Mars: ias15; a SABA run is flagged.

On the 294 benchmark MMR records whose metadata has the initial elements, the static verdict at each record's own step against the verdict measured on the record: 286 agree; every record that the static level calls not resolved is not resolved; 3 records are ambiguous but statically resolved — all crossers whose a moved by 0.03-0.5 au over 20-500 kyr (99942, 2000 YG4, 2020 PP1).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Recipes for common tasks. Every block below is part of a script that make docs-examples runs with short spans; the comments say what to use for real work.

docs.title: Finding resonances
docs.text:
The candidates near a semi-major axis, from the cached catalogs of resonant axes (Resonance matrices):

import resonances

# Candidate MMRs near a = 2.3986 au (463 Lola) with Jupiter and Saturn
for mmr in resonances.find_mmrs(2.3986, planets=['Jupiter', 'Saturn']):
    print(mmr.to_short(), round(mmr.resonant_axis, 4))

find does the same for each body, adds every candidate and returns the simulation. type='mmr' keeps it to MMRs (by default the secular and Lidov-Kozai candidates are added too):

# find: every candidate MMR of each body (type='mmr'; None also adds the secular and Lidov-Kozai candidates)
sim = resonances.find([463, 490], planets=['Jupiter', 'Saturn'], type='mmr', name='find-demo', save='all', integration_years=2_000)
sim.run()
summary = sim.data_manager.get_simulation_summary(sim.bodies)
print(summary[['name', 'resonance', 'status', 'angle_status', 'reason']])

A three-body candidate is accepted within sigma3 = 0.02 au of the body's \(a\), a two-body one within sigma2 = 0.1 au; both are arguments of find and find_mmrs.

docs.title: High-order resonances
docs.text:
The default catalogs hold two-body resonances up to order 10 and three-body resonances up to order 6. For higher orders, raise the limits and give the catalog a new file before anything reads it (a cached file built with other limits is read as it is, with a warning):

import resonances

# Higher orders than the default catalogues (2-body order <= 10, 3-body order <= 6): set the limits and a new file
# before anything reads the catalogue (the cached one, built with the old limits, would be read as it is)
resonances.config.set('MATRIX_2BODY_PRIMARY_MAX', 40)  # exclusive: the planet's coefficient runs up to 39
resonances.config.set('MATRIX_2BODY_COEF_MAX', 39)
resonances.config.set('MATRIX_2BODY_ORDER_MAX', 25)
resonances.config.set('MATRIX_2BODY_FILE', 'cache/mmr-2body-order25.csv')

high = resonances.find_mmrs(2.3986, planets=['Mars', 'Jupiter'], sigma=0.005, mmr_type='two-body')
print([mmr.to_short() for mmr in high])

The three-body keys are MATRIX_3BODY_PRIMARY_MAX, MATRIX_3BODY_COEF_MAX, MATRIX_3BODY_ORDER_MAX and MATRIX_3BODY_FILE. The same keys can be set in .env (Configuration). The strength of a resonance falls fast with its order, so a high-order libration needs a fine output step and a long record to be confirmed (Is it this resonance?).

docs.title: The MPC catalog
docs.text:
With source='mpc' the elements come from the Minor Planet Center's MPCORB (or a subset, MPC_CATALOG), cached in cache/mpc/ on first use and refreshed only by resonances mpc-update. resonances.mpcorb.query selects rows by elements, orbit quality and MPC's orbit-type flags, and its result can be passed to find:

# a selection of the MPC catalogue: a DataFrame (a in au, angles in degrees, H, U, MPC's orbit-type flags)
selection = resonances.mpcorb.query(a=(2.3, 2.45), U=(None, 2), numbered=True)
print(selection[['number', 'name', 'a', 'e', 'inc_deg', 'H']])

# elements from MPCORB at its standard epoch (the default date of a source='mpc' run)
sim = resonances.find(selection, source='mpc', planets=['Jupiter', 'Saturn'], type='mmr', name='mpc-demo', integration_years=2_000)
print(sim.config.date, sim.config.mpc_snapshot['sha256'][:12], [body.name for body in sim.bodies])

Without a date, an MPC run starts at the catalog's standard epoch, where most rows are given. A row at another epoch is integrated to the date first (MPC_EPOCH_POLICY=propagate) or refused (strict).

Note

The tested script reads the 20-row sample tests/fixtures/mpc/MPCORB_sample.DAT (MPC_CATALOG=file://...), so the selection above holds (4) Vesta and (463) Lola. With the default MPC_CATALOG=mpcorb the same code downloads MPCORB (about 94 MB compressed) on first use.

docs.title: Clones
docs.text:
An orbit is known only within its errors. Clones (virtual asteroids) are drawn from the covariance of the orbit solution; the run reports, per resonance, the share of clones with each status and its 95 % interval (Clones):

import resonances


def main():
    solution = resonances.orbit_solution(463, source='astdys')  # nominal orbit + covariance (cached in cache/clones/)
    ensemble = solution.sample(n=10, seed=0)  # 10 clones and the nominal; 100-1000 for real shares

    sim = resonances.Simulation(name='clones-demo', date='2026-01-01', integration_years=2_000)
    sim.create_solar_system()
    sim.add_ensemble(ensemble, resonances=['4J-2S-1'])  # clones drawn at another epoch are integrated to the date first
    sim.run()
    shares = sim.clone_summary  # the rows of clones.csv: the share of each status with its 95 % Wilson interval
    print(shares[['resonance', 'n_clones', 'nominal_status', 'modal_status', 'modal_share', 'f_resonant_lo', 'f_resonant_hi']])


if __name__ == '__main__':  # the clones run in worker processes: the guard is required
    main()

The clones run in worker processes, so a script needs the if __name__ == '__main__': guard on macOS and Windows (where new processes re-import the script). Short forms: sim.add_body(463, '4J-2S-1', clones=100), resonances.check(463, '4J-2S-1', clones=100).

docs.title: Output layout
docs.text:
Tables (summary.csv, episodes.csv, ...) and simulation.json stay at the top of save_path; the series go to data/, the figures to figures/ and the one-page verdict figures to combined/. Both figure folders are split into subfolders by a layout, levels from status, confidence, type, resonance, body joined by / (confidence/status by default; the presets: Output data).

sim = resonances.Simulation(
    name='layout-demo',
    date='2026-01-01',
    integration_years=2_000,
    plot='all',
    plots=['combined', 'evolution'],
    plot_layout='type/status',  # figures/<type>/<status>/...
    plot_combined_layout='confidence/status',  # combined/<confidence>/<status>/... (the default)
)
sim.create_solar_system()
sim.add_body(463, ['4J-2S-1', 'g-g6'], name='463')
sim.run()
print(sim.config.plot_path)

On this short run both angles are uncertain, so the evolution figures go to figures/mmr/uncertain/ and figures/secular/uncertain/, the verdict figures to combined/none/uncertain/ (none is the confidence folder of a verdict without a level).

docs.title: Restoring a run
docs.text:
A saved run is read back from its simulation.json. By default the verdicts come from summary.csv; with recompute_librations=True the saved series are analyzed again, without integrating:

json_file = f'{sim.config.save_path}/simulation.json'
restored = resonances.SimulationSerializer.restore(json_file)  # the verdicts as they are in summary.csv
print(restored.bodies[0].statuses)

# analyse the saved series again (with the settings of simulation.json; current_settings=True: those of today's .env)
again = resonances.SimulationSerializer.restore(json_file, recompute_librations=True)
print(again.bodies[0].statuses)

Only the rows whose series were saved (the save mode) can be analyzed again. See Serialization and restore.

docs.title: The integrator
docs.text:
SABA(10,6,4) with dt = 1.0 (58 days) suits main-belt orbits. Orbits that approach a planet need an adaptive integrator; the dry-run recommends one for each body.

# IAS15 (adaptive) with the Moon as a separate body: for planet-crossing orbits and close encounters
sim = resonances.Simulation(
    name='ias15-demo',
    date='2026-01-01',
    integration_years=500,
    integrator='ias15',
    dt=0.01,  # initial step, REBOUND units (yr / 2 pi); IAS15 adapts it
    solar_system_moon=True,
    output_step=0.2,  # years; a 1:1 or a near-Earth orbit needs a fine output step
)
sim.create_solar_system()
sim.add_body('2002 AA29', '1E-1', name='2002 AA29')  # a co-orbital of the Earth
sim.run()
print(sim.bodies[0].statuses)

solar_system_moon=True integrates the Moon as a separate body (only with ias15); otherwise the Earth and the Moon are one body at their barycenter. The parameters of REBOUND itself are described in Configuration.

docs.title: Free elements and the free-omega gate
docs.text:
An osculating element vector is the sum of a forced part, imposed by the planets and turning at their frequencies, and a free part carrying the object's own secular motion. Splitting the two answers a question the osculating angle cannot: does ω really librate, or does it only look bounded because the forced eccentricity offsets the cloud?

For a Lidov-Kozai resonance this is part of the decision: the free-ω gate below is a step of the ZLK analysis, and its outcome enters the status (Secular and Lidov-Kozai). The cross spectra decide nothing (Cross-spectral coherence).

docs.title: What is computed
docs.text:
Work happens in the non-singular variables (the same ones secular/proper_angle.py builds), because vectors add and angles do not:

\[ z_e(t) = e\,e^{{\rm i}\varpi} \ \ (\text{driven by } g_5 \ldots g_8), \qquad z_i(t) = \sin\tfrac{i}{2}\,e^{{\rm i}\Omega} \ \ (\text{driven by } s_5 \ldots s_8). \]

The forced part is removed by a complex least-squares fit at the known planetary frequencies from resonances/data/const.py. Fitting known frequencies rather than searching for them is deliberate: a frequency analysis (NAFF/FMFT) of a real integration splits the free mode into five or six neighboring terms — on 4257 the spread is ±0.5 ″/yr against a Rayleigh resolution of 0.13 — and any of those splinters can be mistaken for a planetary line and subtracted by accident.

What is left gives

\[ \varpi_{\rm free} = \arg z_{e,\rm free}, \qquad \Omega_{\rm free} = \arg z_{i,\rm free}, \qquad \omega_{\rm free} = \varpi_{\rm free} - \Omega_{\rm free}, \]

with their least-squares rates b_varpi, b_Omega, b_omega in ″/yr.

docs.title: Which modes can be fitted
docs.text:
Not all of them, and the rule is pairwise, not per-mode. The Rayleigh width is \(1/T\) cycles/yr (\(1\,296\,000/T\) ″/yr): two modes closer than that never drift a full turn apart over the window, so no fit can tell them apart and least squares splits their amplitude arbitrarily. To be conservative, candidates are grouped by single linkage at twice that width, \(2/T\) (two relative turns over the window), and one member of each group is fitted. The gate's tolerance (below) is one width.

At 500 kyr the two widths are 2.592 and 5.184 ″/yr; the grouping threshold 5.18 ″/yr and the candidate rates 0, 0.67, 3.09, 4.26, 28.25 have neighbor gaps 0.67, 2.42, 1.17, 23.99 — the first three chain together, the last one breaks:

baseline z_e basis z_i basis 100 kyr one line one line 300 kyr – 1 Myr g5, g6 const, s6 10 Myr full full

docs.title: The representative is a modeling assumption
docs.text:
Which member of a cluster gets fitted is fixed by a documented priority — g5 > g6 > g7 > g8 > const for the eccentricity vector, const > s6 > s7 > s8 for the inclination one. That order is not a free convention. Fitting a different member measurably changes the verdict: on 3752 the gate's outcome moves from confirmed to no verdict, on 591986 from kinematic to no verdict. The order encodes what actually dominates the forcing — Jupiter's g5 for a main-belt eccentricity vector, and the constant offset between the ecliptic and the invariable plane (the s5 mode, zero by construction) for the slow inclination modes — and it reproduces the {g5, g6} / {const, s6} basis that was validated independently against 10 Myr integrations.

What makes it safe rather than merely plausible: no choice of representative ever turns a non-librator into a libration. Errors move the answer towards withholding a verdict, never towards inventing one. That is asserted directly in the tests.

docs.title: Resampling
docs.text: Before the fit both vectors are thinned to about free_elements_sampling_years (500 yr) by the integer factor \(q = {\rm round}(500\ {\rm yr}/\Delta t)\), with an anti-alias filter on the real and imaginary parts: secular work needs nothing finer, and a short-period term folded into the secular band would show up as free motion. Every factor is filtered. Passes of at most 10 use scipy's zero-phase FIR decimate; what no such pass divides (a prime above 10: \(q = 31\) at the 15.918-yr step of the 100-kyr ZLK records) is a last polyphase pass (resample_poly, padded along the end-to-end line). The grid is times[::q]. Earlier versions skipped that leftover and the record kept its 15.9-yr grid: Jupiter's 11.86-yr term aliased to ~47 yr and, where it was larger than the free circle, wound ϖ_free by whole turns (555527: 26 turns of excess in one 2-kyr window; 0.37 after the filter, and the gate goes from kinematic to planetary_residual). A row resampled with a polyphase pass carries the rule free_resample_remainder in rules_fired.

docs.title: The mask
docs.text: Where |z_free| passes near the origin the argument is undefined, and unwrapping through it picks up half-turns that look like circulation. Samples below mask_quantile × median are dropped before unwrapping. ϖ_free and Ω_free each live on their own mask; ω_free lives on the intersection, so |b_omega − (b_varpi − b_Omega)| is a consistency check with a tolerance, not an identity. In practice the masks remove 0–8% of a real series.

docs.title: The gate
docs.text:
The gate (omega_free_gate.evaluate_gate) reads the free elements and returns an outcome:

condition outcome no free elements (fewer than 16 samples after decimation, \(T \lesssim 8\) kyr, or the split failed) unavailable a co-orbital of a planet whose own modes are not fitted: \(\lvert\langle a\rangle/a_P - 1\rvert < k\,(m_P/3M_\odot)^{1/3}\) (ZLK_COORBITAL_HILL_FACTOR \(k = 3\): 0.030 for the Earth), \(P\) = Mercury … Mars unavailable (zlk_gate_detail = coorbital_unfitted_forcing) \(T <\) FREE_GATE_MIN_CYCLES × \(P_{\rm lib}\): the window never held the libration short_window more than half the samples masked: no usable argument undefined_phase \(R < 360°\) and b_varpi at g5…g8 (or 0, see below) or b_Omega at s6…s8 planetary_residual \(R < 360°\) otherwise confirmed \(R \ge 360°\) and b_varpi at g5…g8, b_Omega at s6…s8, or b_omega at any \(g_j - s_k\) (\(j = 5…8\), \(k = 5…8\), \(s_5 = 0\)) planetary_residual \(R \ge 360°\) otherwise: the free ω winds kinematic FREE_GATE_ENABLED=False disabled the osculating ω is not bounded (it circulates): no confirmation asked not_applicable

"At" means a signed difference below one Rayleigh width, \(1\,296\,000/T\) ″/yr. The difference frequencies \(g_j - s_k\) are tested on the winding branch only: \(\omega = \varpi - \Omega\), so an unsubtracted term in either vector shows up in \(\omega\) at such a frequency even when neither b_varpi nor b_Omega matches a mode. not_applicable is not a failed split; the geometric status stands.

\(R\) is the span of \(\omega_{\rm free}\) trimmed by half a percent at each end (a span is an extreme statistic, and one surviving glitch ruins a strict maximum). The 360° threshold is topological and must not be tightened: inside a mean-motion resonance the Lidov-Kozai cycle is asymmetric and its center shifts away from 90°/270°, to 0°/180° for Hildas and by ±60° for Trojans (Vinogradova 2024).

The status decision (analysis.secular.decide.decide_status) turns the outcome into the status: on a librating ω, confirmed (or disabled) keeps resonant, kinematic gives non_resonant / kinematic_libration and any other outcome uncertain / gate_unavailable; on episodes, a drift or too few cycles only kinematic with \(\rho_{\max} < 1\) changes it (\(\rho_{\max}\) = the largest ratio of the free to the forced radius, each a rolling median over about one libration cycle, FreeElements.rho_local_max). The table and \(\rho_{\max}\): Secular and Lidov-Kozai. For screening, uncertain means "re-check on a longer baseline", so the candidates and extended save/plot modes keep it; extend_to_years says how long (short_window: the missing cycles; planetary_residual: the baseline that resolves the residual's distance to the planetary rate, zlk_gate_d_min_arcsec_yr), and undefined_phase or unavailable asks for review (How long to extend). The gate itself has no amplitude test (below).

docs.title: Why the same check stands on both branches
docs.text:
A Lidov-Kozai libration lives on the object's own rates, so it can only be confirmed when ϖ_free and Ω_free turn at speeds that are not planetary. A residual sitting at a planetary rate is either a defect of the subtraction or a genuine linear secular resonance (g near some g_j, the ν5/ν6 family) where the forced/free split is undefined to begin with. Both make a verdict unsafe, and telling them apart is not required.

Comparison is signed and the tolerance is one Rayleigh width, 1296000/T ″/yr. Signed because every s_j is retrograde: a prograde free node is not s8 however close the magnitudes are. Zero is a target only for the eccentricity vector, and only when the constant term was clustered away and so left in the residual — an unsubtracted constant is exactly what makes an angle look confined.

The honest cost: an object whose own g or s sits within one Rayleigh width of a planetary fundamental is withheld rather than confirmed. That is a real ambiguity, not a gap.

The free node near s_j. When the only match is the free node (b_Omega within one width of s_j, b_varpi and, on a winding ω, b_omega away from every planetary rate), the column zlk_gate_node_near names s_j, with zlk_gate_node_near_d_arcsec_yr (\(d\)), zlk_gate_node_near_resolution_arcsec_yr and zlk_gate_node_separation_yr = \(1\,296\,000/d\), the free-element baseline whose width is \(d\). 1981 Midas over 500 kyr: ω librates 19 cycles (the gate needs 3), but the free node is \(d = 1.85\)″/yr from s6 against a width of 2.59″/yr; it separates at 0.70 Myr, and the extension asks for 1 Myr (ZLK_EXTEND_RESOLUTION_MARGIN). The status stays uncertain / gate_unavailable.

free_rho_i_max is the inclination's counterpart of \(\rho_{\max}\): the largest rolling ratio of \(|z_{i,\rm free}|\) to the turning forced inclination (the fitted s modes without the constant, which is the tilt of the reference plane; empty when the baseline merged s6…s8 into the constant, 373136 over 100 kyr). Far above one, a free node near s_j could not be a leak of the forced s_j term, which is at most as large as that term. But while \(d\) is below the width, least squares splits the free node between the residual and the s_j term, so the ratio is not yet the physical one (1981: the fitted s6 term 0.30 against a free radius 0.25, ratio 0.5–1.4). No status reads it; a rule on it waits for the 1-Myr run, and a true ν16 lock (s held at s6) is not separated by any length.

docs.title: No amplitude criterion in the gate
docs.text:
An earlier design compared the free eccentricity against an estimated floor of unsubtracted forcing. That floor cannot be measured: estimating how much forcing sits at a frequency the baseline cannot resolve requires resolving it. Measured on the reference set, a ridge prefit of the candidate amplitudes returned |ĉ| of order e_free rather than e_forced — two orders of magnitude too large — because the near-degenerate slow cluster amplifies the projection of the un-modeled free signal. The floor then scaled with the very quantity it was being compared against, and demoted 3040, 162474 and 3752 outright.

Frequency is the direct observable instead: unsubtracted forcing lives, by construction, only at known rates.

docs.title: Where the method stops working
docs.text:
For a co-orbital the forced term is the perturber's own eccentricity vector rather than a planetary fundamental. For a Jupiter Trojan that vector is Jupiter's, g5 + g6, rotated by ±60° for L4/L5 (Milani 1993; Vinogradova 2015), and the split fits it: on 591986 the fitted g5 amplitude is 1.02 × Jupiter's own g5 term (g6: 1.12 ×) and the forced direction swings ±arcsin(|c₆|/|c₅|) = ±22.8° at the g6 − g5 beat, which is the slow wave of the osculating ω's center. So the kinematic outcome stands (Vinogradova 2024 finds no Trojan with a librating ω); the tadpole sidebands are not modeled, and the free rates there are not proper elements.

A co-orbital of Mercury to Mars is different: those planets' own modes (g1–g4, s1–s4) are not candidates of the split, so its forced term is simply not subtracted. Such a body (inside ZLK_COORBITAL_HILL_FACTOR Hill radii of the planet's axis) gets the outcome unavailable, detail coorbital_unfitted_forcing: a libration becomes uncertain / gate_unavailable, and so does an episodic row, a drift or too few cycles (2020 PP1, an Earth co-orbital, and 10563 over 500 kyr; rule zlk_coorbital_episodic): no record length makes the split fit, so the action is review. Never not_applicable, which would keep the geometric status of a libration.

An episodic \(\omega\) circulates between its episodes, so its free \(\omega\) winds over the record; where the record's outcome is kinematic or a winding planetary_residual, the gate reads the librating episodes instead (ZLK_GATE_EPISODES): confirmed (detail episodes) when in every one the free vector is the longer and the free \(\omega\) advances less than half a turn per cycle, with \(b_\varpi\), \(b_\Omega\) off the modes (the gate inside the episodes).

Any other episodic row without a verdict (a planetary residual, a short window, an undefined phase) keeps the geometry's status under the minimal policy (flag gate_unavailable, at most medium); the full tree (v2_verdict) made it transient only when \(e\) and \(i\) trade at constant \(\sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\) inside its deciding episode (zlk_ei_episode_coupling = zlk), else uncertain / gate_unavailable: From the outcome to the status.

docs.title: Beyond the gate
docs.text:
Columns of a ZLK row that change no status (analysis.zlk.diagnostics, analysis.secular.slow):

  • The e–i coupling at the decisive period \(P\) (\(P_{\rm cyc}\); for a circulating ω the \(\cos 2\omega\) harmonic \(\pi/|\dot\omega|\)), for every row whatever its status. One sinusoid of \(e\) and one of \(i\) (from the invariable plane by an exact rotation; the tilt \(\min(i, 180° - i)\) of a retrograde orbit; an orbit that crosses 90° is not_measured) on the record less one period at each edge, and \(e\), \(i\) band-passed to \([(1 \mp 0.2)/P]\) for their correlation \(r\). Two laws predict \(\delta i/\delta e\): constant \(\sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\) (ZLK, \(-e\cot i/(1-e^2)\), antiphase) and constant \(\sqrt{1-e^2}(1-\cos i)\) (the momentum conjugate to Ω when the forcing acts on ϖ only, as a forced-eccentricity beat does: \(+e\tan(i/2)/(1-e^2)\), in phase). zlk_ei_coupling is zlk or forced_beat when the phase is within ZLK_EI_PHASE_TOL_DEG of the law's sign, \(r\) has that sign with \(|r| \ge\) ZLK_EI_MIN_BAND_R and \(|\delta i|/|\delta e|\) is within a factor ZLK_EI_AMPLITUDE_FACTOR of the law; none when every number is finite and neither law matches. A band the sampling cannot hold (above the Nyquist frequency: undersampled), one the filter cannot pass (band_unmeasured) or a law that is not finite (law_undefined) is not_measured (zlk_ei_reason), never none. The librators 3040, 162474, 4257, 1373, 1981: zlk, phase 177–182°, \(r \approx -0.995\), 1.0–1.6 × the law. 591986's 6-kyr cycle: forced_beat, phase 328°, \(\delta i\) 1.2 × the beat law. Coupling is not libration: 15527 circulates and shows zlk coupling at its 2.05-kyr harmonic. The deciding episode's own coupling (zlk_ei_episode_*: demodulated on the episode's samples, with the residual \(\eta_H\) of the integral) is the one the status of an episodic row without a gate verdict reads; on 88899 over 500 kyr the record says none and so does the episode, on 2020 PP1 the record says zlk and the deciding episode none.
  • Attribution of a kinematic libration: the fitted mode with the largest \(|c_j|\) (named with the modes the baseline merged into it) holds ϖ, provided the free circle stays off the origin (\(\rho_{\max} < 1\), or the strict pin \(\max_t|z_{\rm free}| + \sum_{k \ne j}|c_k| < |c_j|\): the largest free radius of the record, not its median, since the bound must hold at every sample), the predicted beat \(2\pi/|b_\varpi - g_j|\) is \(P_{\rm cyc}\) within a Rayleigh width, and the free node follows the mode (\(|b_\Omega - g_j|\,T\) under one turn). 591986: g5 (g5+g7+g8+const), \(e_{\rm free}/|c_5| = 0.25\), beat 5.96 kyr against \(P_{\rm cyc}\) 6.0 kyr, node − g5 = −0.17″/yr (0.06 turn). Otherwise "forcing not attributed" with the condition that failed. An episodic \(\omega\) that the gate demoted inside its episodes (median local \(\rho < 1\) in each, the free \(\omega\) turning with each cycle) is attributed with zlk_attribution_scope episodes: the node need not follow the mode there (624 Hektor: node − g5 = −17.2″/yr, 6.6 turns of the center \(\varpi_5 - \Omega\), which keeps the librations apart). The per-mode amplitudes are persisted in {body}-omega-free.csv, so a restored run gets its attribution back.
  • Node lock (zlk_node_lock, a flag no status reads): the osculating node against the longitude of the fitted mode with the nearest rate, \(\varpi_j(t) = g_j t + \arg c_j\). Locked when \(|b_\Omega - g_j| < 1296000/T\) (one Rayleigh width), \(\Omega - \varpi_j\) stays within a turn, and, low-passed at the node's longest forced wave (\(2\pi/|b_\Omega - s_k|\)) inside the filter's edge trim, it closes at least ZLK_NODE_LOCK_MIN_CYCLES full cycles ((turning points − 1)/2): a drift or a slow circulation within the resolution closes none. 591986 over 4 Myr: g5, 50–130°, 2 cycles of 1.4 Myr; over 500 kyr the rate matches and \(\Omega - \varpi_5\) stays within 52–91°, but no cycle closes: unresolved (one period of 1.4 Myr does not fit). Columns: the mode, the reason when none (rate_mismatch, unbounded, unresolved, …), the candidate, \(b_\Omega - g_j\) and the resolution, the range, the period and the cycles.
  • The slow line of the center of a libration or a drift (zlk_centre_*): the strongest sinusoid of the center between its smoothing \(W_c\) and half the record, and its origin: forced_beat:<gk>-<gj> when its period is a beat \(2\pi/|g_k - g_j|\) of two fitted forced modes with nonzero amplitudes within a Rayleigh width and the phase wave of the fitted forced vector, smoothed like the center, explains it in shape (\(r \ge\) ZLK_CENTRE_MODEL_R_MIN) and in size (zlk_centre_model_gain, its swing over the center's, within a factor ZLK_CENTRE_MODEL_AMP_FACTOR: correlation alone is blind to size), node when the node's own wave does, forced_direction when \(\arg z_{\rm forced} - \Omega\) does (the center of \(\omega\) itself when the forced vector holds \(\varpi\): 591986 over 4 Myr, a 1.43-Myr wave of the node locked to g5 plus the g6−g5 beat, \(r = 0.998\); the node alone gives 0.82), else unexplained. Fewer than two nonzero per-mode amplitudes: no forced beat. 591986: 53.8 kyr, ±21.6°, forced_beat:g6-g5, \(r = 0.991\), gain 1.00, model ±22.8°. A modulated secular angle gets the same line (sec_centre_*), named forced_wave:<mode> after a forced wave of its own modes.
  • The scale guard: a libration at the center scale whose period is such a forced beat, whose forced phase wave explains the center (as above), while \(\rho_{\max} < 1\) never becomes the decisive libration (sec_centre_rejected); the gate's period stays the fast one (a clean synthetic 591986 otherwise decided at 54 kyr instead of 5.95 kyr). It acts only where the gate does: a disabled gate, no split, or a co-orbital with unfitted forcing keeps the geometric scale.

docs.title: Reference values
docs.text:
Measured on 500 kyr of mercurius integrations at 100 yr, the baseline the gate is calibrated for:

object outcome b_varpi b_Omega b_omega R, deg rho 4257 confirmed −19.08 −19.05 −0.02 34 26.5 3040 confirmed −21.27 −21.30 0.02 63 9.7 162474 confirmed −15.55 −15.55 0.00 55 12.1 3752 confirmed −13.81 −15.60 1.79 352 6.4 591986 kinematic 221.62 4.09 217.53 29896 0.23

The other five reference objects (373136, 797204, 88899, 555527, 10563) do not librate over the whole 500 kyr record; there the gate changes the status only on a kinematic outcome with \(\rho_{\max} < 1\).

docs.title: How long an integration is needed
docs.text:
baseline librating and confirmed 591986 false positives 300 kyr 4257, 3040, 162474, 3752 kinematic 88899 librates, gate: no verdict 500 kyr 4257, 3040, 162474, 3752 kinematic none 1 Myr 4257, 3040, 162474 kinematic none 10 Myr 4257 kinematic none

Longer is not better here. Most of these objects lose the lock well before 10 Myr — 3752 at 850 kyr, 162474 at 1.33 Myr, 3040 at 2.83 Myr — so a long baseline answers "does it stay?" rather than "is it in resonance?". 500 kyr recovers librators that 10 Myr loses while keeping every false positive out.

Two things a 500 kyr run does not buy. The rates b_varpi, b_Omega cannot be quoted as numbers: the Rayleigh resolution there is 2.59 ″/yr, and the Lidov-Kozai signature g − s = 0.09 ″/yr on 4257 sits thirty times below it. The verdict is safe because it comes from the winding, not the rate; for numbers use 2 Myr (0.65 ″/yr) or 10 Myr (0.13). And the calibration assumes Lidov-Kozai cycles of 27–58 kyr, as in this set — the rule of thumb is \(T \ge \max(500\ {\rm kyr},\ 10\,P_{\rm ZLK})\), which in practice means a short run to measure the period and an extension if it turns out long.

docs.title: Columns in summary.csv
docs.text:
Written for Lidov-Kozai rows only, since ω = ϖ − Ω is the angle they describe.

The decomposition: free_basis_e, free_basis_i, free_e, free_e_forced, free_rho, free_rho_min, free_rho_max (the median free radius over the largest and the smallest smoothed forced amplitude; descriptive, the status reads zlk_gate_rho_max), free_omega_range_deg, free_omega_revolutions, free_b_varpi, free_b_Omega, free_b_omega, free_drift_flag, free_mask_e, free_mask_i, free_resolution.

The gate: free_gate (the outcome), free_n_cycles (\(T/P_{\rm lib}\)), free_gate_matches (the planetary rates a residual could not be told apart from), and the same as the analysis read them: zlk_gate, zlk_gate_n_cycles (\(T/P_{\rm cyc}\): cycles of the osculating ω, not turns of the free one), zlk_gate_min_cycles, zlk_gate_period_yr, zlk_gate_matches, zlk_gate_detail (coorbital_unfitted_forcing), zlk_gate_rho_max (the local ratio the status reads), zlk_gate_rho_global (the former median ratio, descriptive), free_rho_i_max and zlk_gate_node_near* (the free node near s_j, numbers only). The check check_zlk_free_omega is pass (confirmed), fail (kinematic) or not_measured. The columns of Beyond the gate are listed in Output.

Two notes on reading them. free_e / free_e_forced come from this fit, while the older e_free / e_forced columns come from the (k, h) scatter in cross_spectrum and exist for every resonance type — different estimators, expected to differ. And free_rho is an annotation (the status reads only \(\rho_{\max}\), Secular and Lidov-Kozai): for a large-amplitude librator e_forced is inflated by the same free signal the fit could not represent, so read it in the small-amplitude regime.

free_drift_flag marks a span under a full turn that nonetheless carries a reproducible monotonic ramp — worth a longer integration, but not a demotion.

docs.title: Files and figures
docs.text:
{body}-omega-free.csv carries the series themselves — the free and forced amplitudes of both vectors, the three unwrapped angles, and the two masks. Masked samples are NaN rather than dropped, so the file stays aligned with its times column. The fitted complex amplitude of every mode is in amp_<e|i>_<mode>_re / _im on the first row (its value at \(t = 0\) of the times column), so a restored run rebuilds the forced vectors with their phases.

Add free_omega to PLOTS (or plots=[...]) for three figures (How to read them):

  • …-free-omega-drift.png — ω accumulated over the baseline, free against osculating;
  • …-free-omega-portrait.png — the Kozai diagram in free variables, free e against free ω;
  • …-free-omega-vector.png — the free eccentricity vector, on the same axes as the osculating ecc_vector figure of the same body: side by side they show whether the ring bounding ω is the object's own or the forced offset.

No figure carries numbers. Read free_gate and the rates from summary.csv.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The options are listed in Configuration.

docs.title: Using it directly
docs.text:
from resonances.resonance.omega_free_gate import evaluate_gate  # noqa: E402

elements = body.build_free_elements()
gate = evaluate_gate(elements, libration_period_yr, config)  # an outcome: confirmed, kinematic, or no verdict
print(gate.outcome, elements.b_omega)

config is sim.config of the run, libration_period_yr the period of the bounded ω in years.

In a run the gate is a step of analyse_zlk (resonances/resonance/analysis/zlk/), and analysis.secular.decide.decide_status turns its outcome into the status (above).

Or on bare arrays, without a Body:

from resonances.secular.free_elements import free_elements  # noqa: E402

elements = free_elements(times_years, ecc, inc, Omega, omega)

Times in years, angles in radians.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: resonances needs Python 3.11.5 or newer. It depends on REBOUND 4 for the integration and on Astropy/astroquery for NASA Horizons; both are installed automatically.

docs.title: With uv (recommended)
docs.text:
uv manages the Python version, the virtual environment and the dependencies:

uv init my-study        # a new project
cd my-study
uv add resonances

docs.title: With pip
docs.text:
In a virtual environment:

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install resonances

docs.title: First run
docs.text:
Create test.py:

import resonances  # noqa: E402,F811

sim = resonances.check(463, '4J-2S-1', integration_years=2_000)  # (463) Lola in 4J-2S-1; 100_000 years for a verdict
sim.run()
print(sim.bodies[0].statuses)
print(sim.config.save_path)

and run it with uv run python test.py (or python test.py). The Quick start explains the output.

What happens on the first run:

  • The elements of the asteroid and of the planets are downloaded from NASA Horizons at the start date (today, by default; the default data source is DATA_SOURCE=nasa). The planets are cached in cache/solar-*.bin. AstDyS and the MPC catalog are optional sources (Configuration, Examples).
  • The catalogs of resonances are built once and cached in cache/mmr-2body.csv, cache/mmr-3body.csv (Resonance matrices).
  • The default integration is 100 000 years with SABA(10,6,4) and a saved point every 15.9 years.
  • The results go to sim.config.save_path: cache/resonance_find for check and find (their default name), or cache/<name> for Simulation(name=...). If that folder is not empty, a time stamp is appended, so a new run never overwrites an old one. The log is cache/resonances.log.

All paths are relative to the working directory. Settings can be changed per run (Simulation(...) keywords) or in a .env file in the working directory (Configuration).

If the download from Horizons fails with a certificate error, see Horizons and TLS.

docs.title: Jupyter
docs.text: Add ipykernel to the same environment (uv add ipykernel or pip install ipykernel) and choose that environment's kernel. On macOS and Windows, code that starts worker processes (batches of more than BATCH_THRESHOLD bodies, clones) must run in a script with an if __name__ == '__main__': guard, not in a notebook cell (Examples).

docs.title: From the source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/smirik/resonances.git
cd resonances
uv sync          # the package, the test tools and the documentation tools
make test-fast   # every test of at most 1 s, about 2 minutes on 4 processes
make test-slow   # integrations and longer tests, about 10 minutes (Horizons over the network)
make docs        # build this site (mkdocs build --strict)

Both need nothing beyond the clone; XDIST= runs them in one process. make test-benchmark needs the benchmark's saved series, which are not in git.

docs.title: Agent skill
docs.text: For a coding agent (Claude Code and others that read Agent Skills), install the package's skill into your project: resonances skill install (see Using with AI agents). After upgrading the package, run resonances skill install --force to refresh it.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
uv lock --upgrade-package resonances && uv sync     # uv
pip install --upgrade resonances                    # pip

docs.title: Rule index
docs.text:
Start with the physics

This page lists the rule IDs that appear in the combined figure, in decision_path, in rec_rule and in the output columns, each with a one-line meaning, its settings, the page that explains it and the code that runs it. The physics and the formulas are on the pages of How the status is determined; the values of the settings are in Configuration and resonances/.env.dist. The column rules_fired names the rules that acted on a row by meaning; their doc ids are the IDs on this page.

Code paths are relative to resonances/resonance/analysis/. MMRs (two-body, three-body, retrograde, co-orbital) go through analyse_mmr (mmr/analyse.py; the order of its steps: Overview). Secular and Lidov-Kozai angles share the geometry, the ledger and the confidence rule and have their own signal step and physics (Secular and Lidov-Kozai).

docs.title: The verdict
docs.text: The verdict fields (status, angle_status, angle_subtype, reason, libration_origin, origin_detail, confidence, action, …) are described on the Overview; every reason with its status and origin is in Every reason; the old integer status_code is in Legacy integer codes. Every column of the output files is in Output data.

docs.title: Angle word: G rules
docs.text:
The first rule that fires gives angle_status (mmr/decide.py, decide_angle; the geometry in geometry.py). Full table: From geometry to angle_status.

rule meaning settings physics code G0 the record cannot be read: unphysical orbit, unwrap residual over its limits, \(\varpi\) undefined, \(P_c \le 2\Delta t\) → undefined / invalid MMR_UNWRAP_MAX_RESID_*, MMR_JITTER_MAX_RAD, MMR_VARPI_UNDEFINED_MAX_SHARE signal, can the record be read mmr/sampling.py, mmr/models.py (domain_problems), mmr/analyse.py (_g0) G1 a confirmed jump of \(a\) (or a step of the action): the rules run on the last regime LIBRATION_JUMP_* jumps geometry.py (jump_candidates, confirm_jumps) G1c after the last turning point the center completes a revolution → episodic, final_regime = circulation — jumps mmr/decide.py G1e the last regime holds no episode, episodes precede the jump → episodic; cap episode_before_jump — jumps mmr/decide.py G1l a libration after a jump, none before it (a capture) → episodic, final_regime = libration — jumps mmr/decide.py G1q a 1:1 angle that turns in the quasi-satellite well during a stay of one loop through its turns: analyzed again at the quasi-satellite floor (rule qs_trigger); in that pass a run inside the well whose turns all lie in it has the floor min(the QS floor, 0.7 × the loop of the averaged potential through its own turns, not below the period its filter keeps at gain MMR_L8_GAIN_FAIL), read by the TP prominence too (rule coorbital_qs_run_floor) MMR_COORBITAL_QS_* co-orbitals mmr/quasi_satellite.py G1f a two-body angle without a libration, analyzed again at the floor of its own averaged potential \(T_{0,\text{th}}/\sqrt{x}\); kept when its cycle is below the floor and F (direct), the center and L4 pass (rule subfloor_pass) MMR_SUBFLOOR_PASS, MMR_STRENGTH_CHECK_RATIO status tree, signal mmr/analyse.py (_subfloor_pass), mmr/preprocess.py (profile_period_floor), mmr/strength.py (theory_period) G2 a librating episode: covering → libration, else episodic; for a 1:1 angle also a union of episodes; a 1:1 run whose turns reflect on the planet's or L3's top has the floor of the loop through its own turns (rule coorbital_floor_profile, MMR_COORBITAL_PROFILE_FLOOR), a run with a turn that is no reflection that of its reflecting pairs when its own force law passes (rule coorbital_pair_loop_floor, MMR_COORBITAL_PAIR_LOOP_FLOOR); a 1:1 run that misses the turning point the filter's edge trim hides takes it from the orbit-averaged raw angle, only to close a cycle (rule coorbital_edge_turn); a 1:1 episode ends only at a separatrix, its changes of well and amplitude are episodes.csv marks (rule coorbital_well_cut); a 1:1 run some of whose cycles miss the well is kept from its well-holding core, continued to the next crossing of the planet or L3 (rule coorbital_well_core); every accepted 1:1 run stores its core, sub-regimes and inferred residence (rule coorbital_residence); an accepted run that does not count for the status (forced wave, induced, below the period floor, a center that turns, before the last jump) has eligible false and its ineligible_reason (rule eligible_reason); an exit or entry is read against the local center at the edge (rule local_centre_entry where the mean center would read it otherwise) LIBRATION_* (episodes, coverage), MMR_COORBITAL_EDGE_TURN*, MMR_COORBITAL_TURN_ENERGY_TOL, MMR_COORBITAL_WELL_EPISODES, MMR_COORBITAL_WELL_CORE, MMR_COORBITAL_RESIDENCE runs and episodes, coverage, edge turn, 1:1 boundary, 1:1 residence, exits and entries, eligible geometry.py (_edge_raw_turns, _accept_in_wells, _accept_well_core, _join_in_wells, coorbital_marks, residence_of, episode_eligibility, _edge_reading), mmr/coorbital_geometry.py (CoorbitalEdgeTurn, CoorbitalWells) G2z a Lidov-Kozai \(\omega\): a run breaks at half a turn (a \(2\omega\) island;
