docs.title: The status tree
docs.text:
decide.decide_status (mmr/decide.py) is the only place a status is set; rec_rule names the step that decided (The status tree), geo_angle_rule the G rule that set the angle word (they differ on insufficient_time: the leaf is G6, the angle rule G5a, G5w or G6).

step meaning physics G6 insufficient_time → uncertain / baseline_needed steps C circulation → non_resonant / circulation; R0 failing with turns: no_resonant_potential steps C5 an aliased circulation: unique branch and far ratio ≥ MMR_C5_FAR_RATIO_MIN → non_resonant / alias, else invalid / alias step resolution 1 an accepted subresonance → the member's status / subresonance_librates steps 2 an accepted owner covering the episode → non_resonant / induced_libration steps 2j 'both resonances at once?': the remainder \(x = \Psi/u\) closes cycles of a well of its own → the tree goes on, origin joint; one such cycle → uncertain / baseline_needed, origin joint, extend (rule both_resonances_confirmed; MMR_OWNER_CAPTURE_*, MMR_OWNER_X_MIN_CYCLES) step 2, owner 3, 3k2, 3b5 B1 or K1 fails → kinematic_libration; K2 → kinematic_drift; B5 finds an exact commensurability → uncertain / baseline_needed steps 4 drift without a kinematic cause → uncertain / drift_mechanism_unknown steps 5f L4 contaminated by a forced line, R0σ not failing → uncertain / origin_unknown step 5 5s, 5s* implausible strength → non_resonant / implausible_strength, its accepted episodes marked forced waves of route strength (rule forced_strength_mark, MMR_FORCED_WAVE_STRENGTH); 5s*: a three-body ratio the small-divisor envelope could close → uncertain step 5 5a, 5a*, 5b, 5e, 5g a measurement objects (L4 fails; L4 passes but R0 fails; R0 fails; the identity fails on an episode) → uncertain / origin_unknown (non_resonant for a near-separatrix angle) step 5 5c, 5d → 6 the force is measured → by the behavior, origin dynamic step 6 5o, 5n unmeasured branch: O1 or F objects; fewer than two independent cycles → uncertain / origin_unknown unmeasured branch 5x unmeasured branch: the order-of-magnitude strength \(\mu e^q\) (\(\mu_i\mu_j e^q\)) out of range is a diagnostic, no objection (rule eq_scale_not_objection) → uncertain / origin_unknown, origin not established unmeasured branch 5u → 6 nothing measured → geometric_libration / geometric_episode, origin unknown unmeasured branch 6 by the observed behavior: resonant, transient, near_separatrix step 6 6u a G2u union that reached transient / dynamic_episode → resonant / dynamic_libration (decide.promote_union; rec_rule 5c/6u or 5d/6u) step 6u K3s after the leaf: a non_resonant / circulation whose slow scale has the period of a secular cycle and fails its own identity → kinematic_libration, detail secular_cycle (rule secular_cycle_kinematic, MMR_SECULAR_CYCLE_KINEMATIC) step 3

docs.title: Secular and Lidov-Kozai
docs.text:
Their shorter tree is on Secular and Lidov-Kozai; the G rules G2z, G5s and G5p above are theirs. The rules that decide which runs of a secular or ZLK angle are its episodes, and those that act on the frame, the free elements and the gate:

ID meaning settings physics code G2p each run of turning points found at the floor takes the prominence measured on its own samples, never above the record's: a circulation elsewhere must not set the threshold of a quiet libration; a run keeps the record's when its own would lose a librating episode the record's finds (the approach to a libration joining it) SECULAR_TP_LOCAL_PROMINENCE, ZLK_TP_LOCAL_PROMINENCE signal secular/preprocess.py (run_prominence), secular/analyse.py (measure_fine), geometry.py (local_thresholds) G2t a run rejected only for its moving center is modulated when it closes a cycle, its turning points span less than a turn, its center turns back at least once and one cycle swings over every center (rule turning_centre) SECULAR_TURNING_CENTRE, ZLK_TURNING_CENTRE a center that turns back geometry.py (accept_turning_centre) G2w secular only: an episode that is a wave on a slower motion of the angle (a ripple carried by a slow swing below a turn, or a stall of a circulation) does not count (Geometry.slow_wave_ids, reason slow_wave; ledger slow_swing_ripple, slow_swing_carried, stall_rate): the slower scale decides SECULAR_SLOW_WAVES, SECULAR_SLOW_SWING_RIPPLE_RATIO, SECULAR_SLOW_SWING_CARRY_RATIO, SECULAR_STALL_RATE_RATIO, SECULAR_STALL_ARM_MIN_FRACTION a wave on a slower motion secular/decide.py (slow_waves), secular/analyse.py G2c′ secular only: when \(W_c\) shows no more libration than the fine scale, the scale of the center's own turns (the MMR second scale) SECULAR_CENTRE_TURNS_SCALE the center scale secular/analyse.py, geometry.py (centre_turns_window_yr) G2e \(\sigma_f\) runs ≥ 1 turn monotonically after the last turning point (before the first): the exit (entry) is observed, that end is not covered, final_regime circulation, no center scale behind it (ledger exit_arc, entry_arc) LIBRATION_EDGE_ARC_REV exit and entry geometry.py (_edge_reading), secular/decide.py (observed_edges) end_travel the policy: a record too short for one cycle that ends in circulation by an end travel of \(\sigma_f\) below \(1 +\) CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND turns is non_resonant at most medium (pol_level_inputs end_travel:thin) CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND confidence policy.py (_travel_thin) ZF a Lidov-Kozai \(\omega\), \(i\), \(\Omega\), the free elements and the \(e\)–\(i\) coupling are measured from the invariable plane by an exact rotation; rule zlk_invariable_frame marks a row whose ecliptic and invariable \(\omega\) part by a whole turn or more (zlk_frame_shift_turns) ZLK_ANGLE_FRAME the frame data/invariable_plane.py, zlk/analyse.py FE the free elements: every decimation factor is filtered, a remainder no pass of ≤ 10 divides by a last polyphase pass (rule free_resample_remainder) FREE_ELEMENTS_SAMPLING_YEARS resampling secular/free_elements.py (decimation_steps, _resample) SZ.G the free-\(\omega\) gate: confirmed, kinematic or no verdict; docs.title: Lidov-Kozai resonances
docs.text: In the classical prograde quadrupole problem the Lidov-Kozai (ZLK) resonance is a libration of the argument of perihelion \(\omega\) about 90° or 270°, with \(e\) and \(i\) varying in antiphase at constant \(\sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\). Inside a mean-motion resonance the center can shift, so the classifier tests that \(\omega\) and its free counterpart are confined (free-omega gate), not that the center is at 90° or 270°; the e–i phase is a flag (Coherence). The package checks it as a resonance with the angle \(\omega\): resonances.LidovKozaiResonance(), key LK. A run may combine it with MMRs and secular resonances.

docs.title: Lidov's integrals
docs.text:
In the quadrupole approximation of the doubly averaged, circular restricted three-body problem (an inner body, a distant perturber), \(a\) is constant and the motion has two more integrals (Lidov 1962, eqs. 58–60; Kozai 1962, eqs. 26–28):

\[ c_1 = (1 - e^2)\cos^2 i, \qquad c_2 = e^2\left(\tfrac{2}{5} - \sin^2 i \,\sin^2\omega\right). \]

Here \(i\) is the inclination to the perturber's orbital plane and \(\omega\) is measured from the node on that plane; \(c_1\) is then the squared normalized component of the angular momentum normal to the perturber's orbit. In that limit \(\omega\) librates about 90° or 270° when \(c_1 < 3/5\) and \(c_2 < 0\), and circulates otherwise; for an initially circular orbit this needs \(\arccos\sqrt{3/5} \approx 39.2° < i < 140.8°\) (not a classifier threshold). LidovKozaiParameters.evaluate rotates nothing: it uses the angles it is given. The package reads them from the invariable plane (evaluate_invariable: the angular momentum and the perihelion rotated exactly, no angle subtracted), the plane of the planets' total angular momentum, as an approximate Solar-system stand-in for the perturber's plane. The summary columns c1, c2, h_quad are these: osculating, at the epoch, invariable plane. From the ecliptic \(c_1\) moves by up to 0.02 and the sign of \(c_2\) can flip (1373 Cincinnati: \(+0.0014\) ecliptic, \(-0.0011\) invariable). The quadrupole energy, without its constant factor, is

\[ h_\text{quad} = (2 + 3e^2)(3\cos^2 i - 1) + 15 e^2 \sin^2 i \cos 2\omega = 6c_1 - 2 + 30 c_2 . \] 
import numpy as np

import resonances
from resonances import LidovKozaiParameters

# osculating ecliptic e, i, Omega, omega of three main-belt asteroids (the benchmark's epoch)
samples = {
    '1373 Cincinnati': (0.3152, 38.953, -62.561, 98.882),
    '3040 Kozai': (0.2003, 46.647, 143.473, 290.213),
    '15527': (0.1529, 21.259, 173.771, 168.872),
}
for name, (e, inc_deg, node_deg, omega_deg) in samples.items():
    # i and omega read from the invariable plane (an exact rotation), as the summary columns c1, c2, h_quad
    c1, c2, h_quad = LidovKozaiParameters.evaluate_invariable(e, *np.radians([inc_deg, node_deg, omega_deg]))
    print(f'{name:16s} c1 = {c1:.3f}  c2 = {c2:+.4f}  h_quad = {h_quad:.3f}')

1373 Cincinnati  c1 = 0.521  c2 = -0.0011  h_quad = 1.091
3040 Kozai       c1 = 0.474  c2 = -0.0021  h_quad = 0.778
15527            c1 = 0.855  c2 = +0.0092  h_quad = 3.404

These numbers are diagnostics, not the verdict. The criterion is exact only for \(a/a_\text{pert} \to 0\); a main-belt asteroid has \(a/a_J \approx 0.5\) and several perturbers, and a value this close to zero (1373's \(c_2 = -0.0011\); \(+0.0014\) from the ecliptic) says nothing on its own. The sign of \(h_\text{quad}\) is not a criterion either: \(e = 0.1\), \(i = 70°\), \(\omega = 0\) gives \(h_\text{quad} < 0\) while \(\omega\) circulates (\(c_2 > 0\)). The osculating elements are used here, at one instant.

docs.title: Checking a body
docs.text:
sim = resonances.Simulation(
    name='lk-demo',
    date='2026-01-01',
    integration_years=5_000,  # 500_000 years for a real verdict: the omega cycles last 10-100 kyr
    integrator='SABA(10,6,4)',
    dt=0.5,  # REBOUND units: 0.5 / (2 pi) yr = 29 days
    output_step=10.0,  # years
    plot_always=['lidov_kozai'],  # draw the omega figure whatever the status
)
sim.create_solar_system()
for number in (1373, 3040, 15527):
    sim.add_body(number, resonances.LidovKozaiResonance(), name=str(number))
sim.run()

for body in sim.bodies:
    verdict = body.verdict('LK')
    print(body.name, verdict.status, verdict.angle_status, verdict.reason, verdict.libration_origin)

The cycles of \(\omega\) last tens of thousands of years, so a verdict needs a long record: 500 000 years with a saved point every 10 years is a good default. SABA(10,6,4) with dt = 0.5 (29 days) is safe for perihelion distances \(q \gtrsim 1.3\) au; closer to the planets use ias15 (dry-run). The short run above gives uncertain / insufficient_time; over 500 000 years 3040 Kozai is resonant with certain confidence (Gallery).

The angle is a series like any other:

body = sim.bodies[1]  # 3040 Kozai
t = sim.times / (2 * np.pi)  # years
omega = body.angle(resonances.LidovKozaiResonance())  # radians in [0, 2 pi)
print(f'{len(t)} points, omega from {np.degrees(omega.min()):.0f} to {np.degrees(omega.max()):.0f} deg')

docs.title: How the status is decided
docs.text:
\(\omega\), \(i\) and \(\Omega\) are measured from the invariable plane (ZLK_ANGLE_FRAME = invariable, the default): the orbit's angular momentum and perihelion are rotated exactly, as for Lidov's integrals. The free elements, the diagnostics below and the figure read the same frame. From the ecliptic, the node of an orbit tilted from the invariable plane by about the plane's own 1.58° or less librates about the plane's node instead of turning, and \(\omega = \varpi - \Omega\) with it: 555527 (\(i_\text{inv} \approx 1.6°\)) looked bounded from the ecliptic and circulates from the invariable plane. Where the two frames' \(\omega\) part by a whole turn or more, the row carries the rule zlk_invariable_frame (column zlk_frame_shift_turns). The integration stores the ecliptic \(\omega\); the analysis writes the classified angle back, so the data files hold it too.

The angle \(\omega\) goes through the same geometry as every other angle (turning points, cycles, episodes; What the angle does). A libration of the osculating \(\omega\) is not enough: the forced eccentricity, driven by the planets, can hold the osculating perihelion while the body's own (free) perihelion circulates. The free-ω gate splits \(e\) and \(i\) into forced and free parts and asks whether the free \(\omega\) is confined (Free elements, Secular and Lidov-Kozai).

On a librating \(\omega\) the gate's outcome sets the status: confirmed keeps resonant, kinematic gives non_resonant / kinematic_libration, no verdict gives uncertain / gate_unavailable; the full rule, also for episodes and short records: Secular and Lidov-Kozai. Gallery shows the Jupiter Trojan 591986, whose osculating \(\omega\) librates while its free \(\omega\) winds.

Four measurements sit next to the status and change none of it (Free elements):

  • e–i coupling at the row's decisive period (zlk_ei_coupling, every row whatever its status): zlk when \(e\) and the inclination to the invariable plane trade in antiphase at the amplitude of constant \(\sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\), forced_beat when they move in phase at the amplitude of constant \(\sqrt{1-e^2}(1-\cos i)\) (a forced eccentricity beating against the free one), none, or not_measured. Coupling is not libration: 15527 circulates and still trades \(e\) for \(i\) at its 2.05-kyr \(\cos 2\omega\) harmonic. confirmed_ei (and check_zlk_ei) is zlk_ei_coupling == zlk.
  • Attribution of a kinematic libration (zlk_forcing_*): the forced mode that holds \(\varpi\) (591986: g5 with the modes merged into it), when the free circle stays off the origin, the predicted beat is the libration period and the node follows the mode (an episodic row demoted inside its episodes: scope episodes, the node free to turn); otherwise "forcing not attributed". The figure states it as the cause and draws panel (a′).
  • Node lock (zlk_node_lock, a flag): the node's rate one line with a forced mode's and \(\Omega - \varpi_j\) librating through at least one full cycle (591986 over 4 Myr: g5; over 500 kyr not resolved).
  • The slow line of the center (zlk_centre_*): its period and half-amplitude, and its origin (591986: the g6−g5 beat of the forced vector, 54 kyr, ±22°).
  • Co-orbitals of Mercury to Mars have no gate verdict (zlk_gate_detail = coorbital_unfitted_forcing): their forced term is the planet's own vector, which the split does not fit; Jupiter's Trojans are covered.

docs.title: Resonance matrices
docs.text:
A resonance matrix is a catalog of mean-motion resonances with their nominal resonant semi-major axes \(a_{\rm res}\). It is used to find the resonances near a body before integrating it.

  • Two-body (TwoBody): Kepler's third law at the commensurability \(k_P n_P + k n = 0\), \(a_{\rm res} = a_P\,(-k/k_P)^{2/3}\), with \(a_P\) the planet's semi-major axis.
  • Three-body (ThreeBody): one perturbative correction of the commensurability \(k_1 n_1 + k_2 n_2 + k\,n + p\,\dot\varpi = 0\) (the planets' own precession neglected). First the Keplerian \(n_K = -(k_1 n_1 + k_2 n_2)/k\) and \(a_0 = (K/n_K)^{2/3}\); then the body's perihelion rate \(g_0\) at \(a_0\), and \(n = -(k_1 n_1 + k_2 n_2 + p\,g_0)/k\), \(a_{\rm res} = (K/n)^{2/3}\). Here \(n_j = K a_j^{-3/2}\) (rad/day, \(K = 0.0172020989484\), \(a\) in au) and, summed over all planets with \(\mu_j = m_j/M_\odot\) and \(D = 365.2422\) days, \(g_0 = \frac{3\pi}{2D}\sum_j \mu_j F_j\), \(F_j = a_0^{3/2}/a_j^3\) for \(a_0 \le a_j\) and \(F_j = a_j^2/[a_0^{7/2}(1+\mu_j)^{3/2}]\) for \(a_0 > a_j\) (the leading terms \(\tfrac34 n\mu_j (a/a_j)^3\) of an outer planet and \(\tfrac34 n\mu_j (a_j/a)^2\) of an inner one). \(\dot\varpi\) is not iterated to the corrected axis.

These are nominal values from fixed planetary axes. The classifier does not use them: it measures the exact resonance \(a_*\) of each angle from the integration (The resonant pendulum).

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
When the app needs to know the value of the resonant semi-major axis for the first time, it calculates it and stores it in the file (the config items MATRIX_3BODY_FILE, MATRIX_2BODY_FILE and MATRIX_2BODY_RETRO_FILE). The files have the following structure:

  1. The number of an item
  2. The short notation of resonance (i.e. 4J-2S-1 or 1J-1)
  3. The planet(s), one per column (i.e. Jupiter and Saturn)
  4. Two or three integers depending on the type of a MMR (p, q and k for a retrograde one)
  5. The order of a resonance
  6. The value of the resonant semi-major axis

The first line of the file is a stamp with the class and the catalog version (e.g. # TwoBodyMatrix v2). If the app generates the file, it will use it next time; a file with another stamp, written by an older version of the package, is rebuilt automatically. If you change the MATRIX_* limits, delete the output file to recalculate the matrix.

Next to the file the app writes its build record, <file>.meta.json (e.g. cache/mmr-2body.csv.meta.json): the MATRIX_* limits, the planets, the catalog version and the package version. When a cached catalog is read, the record is compared with the current settings. Other limits or planets give a warning in the log naming the file and each differing setting (cached and current); a file without a record (written by an older version) gives one warning that its limits are unknown. The file is still read as it is, nothing is rebuilt or deleted: the paths are relative to the working directory, so a run started elsewhere can silently use a catalog built with other limits, and the warning is how you see it. To rebuild, delete the file (or call TwoBodyMatrix.load(reload=True)), or point MATRIX_*_FILE to another file. The retrograde catalog holds its limits in the stamp and is rebuilt when they change.

docs.title: Prograde resonances
docs.text: TwoBody and ThreeBody are resonances of prograde orbits. A two-body resonance m_p P + m (angle m_p λ_p + m λ + p ϖ) needs n = −m_p/m · n_p > 0, so the body's coefficient m must be negative: 3J-2 is a resonance, 3J+2 is not. TwoBody.calculate_resonant_axis raises for m ≥ 0, and TwoBodyMatrix does not list such combinations. Their angle circulates at about 6 n_J for 3J+2, far above the Nyquist rate of any reasonable output step, so its series would be pure aliasing. ThreeBody likewise raises when the mean motion comes out negative.

docs.title: Retrograde resonances
docs.text:
A body with \(i > 90°\) can be in a p/−q resonance with a planet (Morais & Namouni 2013a, b; Li, Huang & Gong 2019, A&A 630, A60): \(q n = p n'\), at the same axis as the prograde p/q, \(a = (q/p)^{2/3} a'\). With \(\varpi^* = \omega - \Omega\) and \(\lambda^* = M + \omega - \Omega\) the arguments are

\[ \varphi = q\lambda^* - p\lambda' - (p + q - 2k)\,\varpi^* + 2k\,\Omega = qM + (2k - p)\,\omega + p\,\Omega - p\lambda', \qquad 0 \le 2k \le p + q . \]

Each k is a separate angle; the order is p + q, the amplitude \(\propto \cos^{2k}(i/2)\,e^{p+q-2k}\). Near the ecliptic k = 0 dominates, at polar orbits higher k do (2011 KT19 in 7/−9 with Neptune: k = 6).

Notation: <p><planet>-<q>r<k>, planet first, k required. 1J-3r0 is 2000 DG8 (1/−3 with Jupiter), 1J-1r1 is 2015 BZ509 (Ka'epaoka'awela), 7N-9r6 is 2011 KT19. to_s() and to_short() give the same string; it is the key in summary.csv and the data files.

import resonances

mmr = resonances.create_mmr('1J-3r0')  # or RetrogradeTwoBody(p=1, q=3, k=0, planet='Jupiter')
# 2_000 years here; 10_000 and more for a verdict
sim = resonances.check('2000 DG8', '1J-3r0', integrator='ias15', integration_years=2_000, Nout=2_001)
sim.run()
  • RetrogradeTwoBodyMatrix lists every coprime p, q ≤ MATRIX_2BODY_RETRO_COEF_MAX (15) with p + q ≤ MATRIX_2BODY_RETRO_ORDER_MAX (30) and every k: 143 resonances per planet as in Li et al., 1198 angles. The cache stamp holds both limits, so changing either rebuilds the cached catalog.
  • find gives a body with i > 90° only retrograde candidates, within sigma_retro = 0.5 au (Li et al.), and any other body only prograde ones. In find_mmrs, a single sigma overrides sigma_retro too, and retrograde=True with mmr_type='two-body' or 'three-body' is a ValueError. check accepts any combination; a resonance of the other direction is only warned about, since orbits can flip. A run whose inclination crosses 90° is warned about too.
  • The text of Li et al. writes the condition as pn − qn' ≈ 0; their eqs. (1), (2) and the objects give qn − pn' ≈ 0.
  • The angle is built from the body's Ω, ω and M only. For i > 90° REBOUND returns l = −λ* and pomega = −ϖ*; an angle from those runs off on a pure Kepler orbit. The longitude (REBOUND's l) and varpi (Ω + ω) columns of the data files are therefore in different conventions for such orbits, and the FAIR plot is not drawn for retrograde resonances.
  • The libration periods of retrograde Centaurs are 0.7–3 kyr (2000 DG8: 0.71 kyr, 2015 BZ509: 0.70 kyr). The classifier chooses the filter cutoff of each angle itself, from its synodic periods and the shortest libration it allows (From the integration to the angle), so these librations are kept; what they need is an output step of 1–2 yr (the dry-run checks it). oscillations_cutoff changes only the body-level filter of the evolution figure and the periodograms: set it to 0.005 (200 yr) to see these librations there too. Slow TNO librations (2011 KT19: a period of 41 kyr) need a long run.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
There are three classes, ThreeBodyMatrix, TwoBodyMatrix and RetrogradeTwoBodyMatrix, responsible for building the resonant matrices. You might use any of them to find the possible resonances close to the given value of the semi-major axis.

The following code will print the list of three-body MMRs close to the value 2.39 AU of the semi-major axis.

from resonances.mmr.three_body_matrix import ThreeBodyMatrix  # noqa: E402

mmrs = ThreeBodyMatrix.find_resonances(2.39, planets=['Jupiter', 'Saturn', 'Uranus'])
for mmr in mmrs:
    print(mmr.to_short())

Note that there is an optional parameter planets representing the array of the planets involved in the MMR. The app will try all possible configurations. In this particular case, there are three combinations: Jupiter and Saturn, Jupiter and Uranus, and Saturn and Uranus.

If you omit this parameter, the app will use all possible combinations of all planets in the Solar System.

The same workflow is for two-body MMRs. The following code will find all two-body MMRs with Jupiter near 5.2 AU (Trojans, actually):

from resonances.mmr.two_body_matrix import TwoBodyMatrix  # noqa: E402

mmrs = TwoBodyMatrix.find_resonances(5.2, planets=['Jupiter'])
for mmr in mmrs:
    print(mmr.to_short())

The method find_resonances has one more optional parameter sigma (default 0.1 au): the largest distance between the given semi-major axis and the resonant one.

The following code will find all two-body MMRs with Jupiter between 4.2 and 6.2 AU:

mmrs = TwoBodyMatrix.find_resonances(5.2, planets=['Jupiter'], sigma=1.0)
for mmr in mmrs:
    print(mmr.to_short())

resonances.find and find_mmrs have their own tolerances: sigma2 = 0.1 au for two-body, sigma3 = 0.02 au for three-body and sigma_retro = 0.5 au for retrograde resonances. A wide tolerance only adds candidates; the integration decides.

docs.title: Candidates from a catalog
docs.text:
The bodies that might be in a given resonance, from their semi-major axis alone (an integration decides), come from search_by_axis of the astdys package (AstDyS) or of resonances.mpcorb (Minor Planet Center, see Configuration); both take sigma (default 0.1 au).

The following code will print the numbers of asteroids that might be in the three-body resonance 4J-2S-1:

from resonances import mpcorb  # noqa: E402

df = mpcorb.search_by_axis(resonances.create_mmr('4J-2S-1').resonant_axis)  # or astdys.search_by_axis (AstDyS)
print(df['number'].tolist())

Note that the method search_by_axis returns Pandas DataFrame, not simply a list or a dict. The DataFrame consists of the number of an asteroid and its orbital elements. You can use df.head() to see its structure.

docs.title: Output data
docs.text:
A run writes into save_path (see Serialization for simulation.json and restore, Config for what is saved): the tables below and simulation.json at its top, the series (data-*, *-omega-free.csv) in data/ (data_folder), the figures in plot_path (see Layout). Which bodies get data files and figures is set by save and plot (status filters); summary.csv, episodes.csv and the other tables hold every body (save_summary). List cells are ;-separated; an empty cell means not measured, never 0. A unit is in the column name (_yr, _kyr, _deg, _rad, _au, _deg_yr, _rad_kyr, _arcsec_yr).

file rows content summary.csv body × resonance the verdict, the checks and margins, the numbers the decision read mmr_numbers.csv body × MMR every number of the MMR analysis episodes.csv run of turning points accepted and rejected episodes of every resonance type (save_episodes) candidates.csv candidate subresonances and owners of the MMR analysis (save_candidates: top or all) constants.csv planet / term the run's planetary constants (save_constants) coherence.csv coherent line cross spectra (coherence) clones.csv body × resonance status shares of a body's clones with Wilson 95 % intervals (clones) data/data-<body>.csv time elements and angles of a saved body data/data-<body>-periodograms.csv frequency Lomb-Scargle periodograms of a and the angles data/data-planet-<planet>.csv time the planets save_planets keeps (all, analysis, none) data/<body>-omega-free.csv time forced/free series of a Lidov-Kozai body (free elements) data/ensemble-<body>.csv, .json clone every draw of a body's clones and its orbit solution (clones) data/ensemble-<body>-results.npz clone the clones' verdicts and thinned angles, read by restore (clones)

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
The folder names and the figures' subfolders are settings (Config: data_folder, plot_figures_folder, plot_combined_folder, plot_layout, plot_combined_layout; resonances/simulation/layout.py). With the defaults (save_path = plot_path = cache/<name>, data, figures, combined, plot_layout='confidence/status', the benchmark's tree) each figure goes into a subfolder per confidence level and status:

cache/<name>/
  simulation.json  summary.csv  mmr_numbers.csv  episodes.csv  candidates.csv  constants.csv  coherence.csv
  data/        data-463.csv  data-463-periodograms.csv  data-planet-Jupiter.csv  463-omega-free.csv
  figures/     high/resonant/463-4J-2S-1+0+0-1-portrait.png   none/uncertain/490-...png  ...
  combined/    high/resonant/463-4J-2S-1+0+0-1-combined.png   medium/transient/...       ...

The other presets are flat, status, confidence, status/confidence, type/status, type/confidence/status, resonance, body. With plot_layout='flat' the figures lie directly in their folders:

cache/<name>/
  ...
  figures/     463-4J-2S-1+0+0-1.png  463-4J-2S-1+0+0-1-portrait.png  463-ecc-vector.png  ...
  combined/    463-4J-2S-1+0+0-1-combined.png  463-LK-combined.png  ...

An empty folder name puts its files at the top (data_folder=''); a verdict without a confidence level (uncertain, invalid) goes to none, a row without a verdict to unclassified. The data files are per body, the status per body × resonance, so the data folder has no layout of its own. The benchmark sorts its figures with the same function (benchmark/tools/sort_figures.py).

Batch workers append to the same tables; each write holds <table>.lock next to the table, and its holder removes it, so a finished run leaves no *.lock file (one left by a killed worker is reused by the next write). A second run into a folder that a run is still writing is refused (.run.lock). Both locks are flocks: on Windows, which has none, neither is taken, so do not start two runs into one folder there.

docs.title: summary.csv
docs.text:
The meaning of each verdict column is in How the status is determined; the rules behind the columns are in the rule index.

group columns identity name, resonance, resonance_type (mmr, secular, lidov_kozai), added_by (subresonance_check for a derived row), parent (its catalog angle) verdict status, angle_status (episodic for librating episodes in part of the record), angle_subtype, final_regime and final_regime_start_yr (how the record ends: the last regime after librating episodes, or libration when the last episode reaches the end; MMR arc or stall from the last revolution when \(\sigma_f\) slows down after circulating (rule end_arc_extend); empty otherwise), orbit_type (the orbit in its librating episodes, for the figure's header: tadpole L4, horseshoe, compound: horseshoe → quasi-satellite (a 1:1 angle: the wells of its sub-regimes in time order, also in geo_orbit_type_sequence as horseshoe>tadpole_L4; geo_residence_t0_yr/_t1_yr/_bounded_by_end: the inferred residence of the described episode), exterior, asymmetric libration about 72° and 288°, ω libration about 90°; empty without an episode; without a libration when the word is neither libration nor episodic: exterior or empty; episodes about 75° (not this resonance) for a non_resonant or uncertain verdict that is induced, kinematic or implausible_strength), confidence, confidence_raw, cell_n_examples, cell_n_errors, cell_accuracy_low_95, cell_accuracy_high_95 (the calibration cell (status, angle_status, reason): verdicts of the benchmark labeled by eye, at high or certain, their errors, the Wilson 95 % interval of the accuracy; reported only, they change no level), reason (implausible_strength, rule 5s: neither L4 nor R0 passes, a measured failure included, and the period needs ≥ MMR_STRENGTH_IMPLAUSIBLE_RATIO (10³) × a computed strength; for a three-body angle the legal e^q scale must still leave that factor after the small-divisor envelope; a center outside the theoretical well does not count, reference), flags (see Flags below), action, review_required (the review queue: the level is medium or low, or the action spot_check/review, or the bounded angle's origin is unknown, or the row has a 1:1 coverage-audit flag; it changes no status and is what SAVE/PLOT = review adds to nonzero), review_reasons (;-separated, empty outside the queue: confidence:<level>, action:<action> at no such level, origin_unknown, then veto_thin for a thin veto, then the 1:1 coverage audit's uncovered_bounded_run and floor_above_own_loop, which put a row in the queue at any level; the minimal policy leaves no caps or failed supports to list), extend_to_years (with action=extend: the total length to integrate; with the flag extend_time and another action: the length that flag asks for, round_up(2T); for a length-limited origin_unknown row (rule extend_length_limited) the two force windows of the last episode, or 5n's next check; for an insufficient_time angle, and for every secular or ZLK extension, the next check round_up(max(2T, min(N, 4T))), a budget after which the record is analyzed again; secular/ZLK N by cause, How long to extend), extend_direction (MMR, with the flag extend_time: forward past the record's end, backward before its start, or both; empty otherwise), base_extend_to_years (MMR: the physical estimate N = round_up(max(required, 2T)) from the period that decides; empty when the record already holds it or no period is measured, and extend_to_years then falls back to 2T), resample_step_yr (with action=resample: the step to rerun at; for a level held down by a check the folded short periods withdrew (rsp_short_period_unmeasured) it is smp_fold_free_step_yr when the sampling names no other step), libration_origin, origin_detail, the roles of the other resonance (MMR; empty for secular and ZLK; table): owner (only an owner or driver that makes the deciding episode), neighbours (KEY t0–t1 before|during|after;… [yr]: an accepted owner that does not make the row's own episodes, flags owner_outside_episode/owner_psi_too_fast), resonant_argument (the librating member of the multiplet whose status the row takes, rule C, chosen in the decisive episode's window; composite when no member stands and the row's own libration about the composite center stands), cause_role (owner, driver, neighbour, kinematic, joint (origin joint: the other resonance of a confirmed joint capture, also in owner) or empty), cause_term (the key of that resonance, or the secular part of σ of a kinematic libration, e.g. -4varpi; 2J-5S for a ripple of the great inequality), commensurability (the key without its ϖ and node coefficients, 9M-16), multiplet_status (the best status of a catalog row and its subresonance), status_code. A catalog row whose libration an accepted member carries takes that member's status (subresonance_librates): a statistic counts a body once per commensurability, deduplicated on (name, commensurability) checks check_mmr_alias, _filter, _baseline, _identity, _a_response, _potential, _a_amplitude, _kinematic, _subresonances, _owner, _slow_libration, _one_pendulum, _onset, _exit, _separatrix_zone, _strength; check_secular_e_response; check_zlk_free_omega, check_zlk_ei (empty for another type) confidence thin_margins (a U:<name> item there is a decision close to a convention, no mrg_U column), failed_support, caps, mrg_<id> and mrg_<id>_value for every margin. MMR: L1–L8, O1, Z, R0, S, W, F, C1–C5, K1, K1e, B5, N (reference). Secular and ZLK: N (turning points of the decisive episode), S (center stationarity), F (the libration period ≥ FILTER_MIN_LIBRATION_CUTOFFS × the cutoff \(P_c\)), P (a circulation's center pass ≥ 1 turn at every smoothing), and for ZLK G (the free-omega gate) (details); a shared id is read with resonance_type decision rules_fired (the named rules that acted on the row, also when its verdict stayed the same: ;-separated, in the order of the rule index; empty when none did; it changes nothing), decision_path (the ledger's comparisons in order) and the columns they read (geo_*, smp_*, rsp_*, sep_*, ep_*, own_*, sub_*, …; ep_onset_ratio: O1's a-wave before / inside the decisive episode) policy policy (minimal), n_cycles (the complete libration cycles N the level read), n_counted_episodes, counted_episode_ids and candidate_episode_ids (;-joined episode ids; a counted or candidate 1:1 leg is leg, a half-swing half), veto (the measured veto that made a bounded angle non_resonant: owner, kinematic, forced_wave, strength, zlk_kinematic, zlk_free_e, zlk_integral), confidence_basis (N=6.5(cover);M=full;V=clean;S=full;veto=-: N and how it was counted, the amplitude margin, the veto state, the filter stability, the veto and :thin), v2_verdict (the full status tree's status/confidence/reason/action/angle_status before the minimal policy re-reads it), pol_end_travel_rev and pol_t_last_tp_yr (the turns σ_f travels after the record's last turning point, and its time: of any run, accepted or rejected, or (MMR) candidate span in the window, a run past the window's end counting at that end; trailing turning points that only stall a circulation, a swing below a third of the passes on both sides, are no reversal), pol_period_dec_yr, pol_n_last, pol_last_reaches_end, pol_extend_clause (A1 an end-edge 1:1 leg, A2 an end-edge half-swing, A an unfinished libration at the end, B a deciding period above 2T / LIBRATION_MIN_TURNING_POINTS, C a needed veto that a record within MMR_NEXT_CHECK_SPAN_FACTOR x T measures), pol_veto_need_yr (the record a needed but unmeasured veto would need; inf when no record up to ZLK_EXTEND_MAX_YR resolves it, empty when no length is named), pol_core_cycles (the observed cycles \((n_{TP}-1)/2\) of the decisive episode that certain needs, CONFIDENCE_CERTAIN_CORE_CYCLES), lib_time_yr and lib_share (the time in libration: the record's years inside the counted episodes, each from its first to its last turning point and carried to a record edge it covers, with the counted 1:1 legs and half-swings, and its share of the record; empty without a counted episode), pol_level_inputs (each input the level read with the highest level it allows, name:state:ceiling ;-joined, e.g. N:4.12>=3:certain;core:4>=3:certain;M:not_measured:high;S:thin:high;V:clean:certain;F:shown:certain; the level is the lowest ceiling; names N, core, M, S, V, F (resonant, transient), status (near_separatrix), veto (thin(owner)), second_capture, candidate, circulation (non_resonant), table (a level the policy table fixes), thin_veto, end_travel (thin: a secular or ZLK record decided as ending in circulation by an end travel below 1 + CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND turns, at most medium); empty for uncertain and invalid), pol_decided_by (the policy step that gave the status and reason: tree when it kept the tree's and set no veto or upheld the leaf's own; else veto:<name>, member, objection, strength_scale, geometry, drift, insufficient_time, leg, half, forced_wave_drift, gate_confirmed, gate_unavailable; ;not_upheld:<leaf> follows when the tree's leaf vetoed and the policy did not uphold it: veto:forced_wave;not_upheld:5s on 2012 KL9, not_upheld:zlk_gate for a ZLK code -2 of the tree), pol_objection_check (the checks whose measured objection made V ambiguous, empty otherwise: force_law L4, potential R0, identity L3, strength F, onset O1, strength_scale (5s three-body, 5s*), force_line (5f), owner, kinematic, zlk_gate_kinematic, zlk_free_e, zlk_ei_integral; the leaf 5o itself when it records neither O1 nor F failing). A word the policy changes clears the tree's angle_subtype. Under minimal caps is empty (every cap is a flag), confidence_raw equals confidence and the cell_* columns are empty (the minimal policy) slow scale (MMR) slow_period_yr, slow_cause, slow_cause_term, slow_cause_level (the slower libration of the center and its probable cause, identified/possible/unknown; the rest in mmr_numbers.csv slow_*) reproducibility settings_hash, confidence_cells_sha, package_commit orbit a0, e0, inc0, Omega0, omega0, M0 (initial elements) Lidov-Kozai zlk_angle_frame (invariable or ecliptic: the plane ω, i, Ω, the free elements and the e–i coupling are measured from, ZLK_ANGLE_FRAME), zlk_frame_shift_turns (the range of ω(invariable) − ω(ecliptic) over the record, turns; ≥ 1: rule zlk_invariable_frame), c1, c2, h_quad (Lidov's integrals: osculating, at the epoch, invariable plane), e_forced, e_free, zlk_coherent, zlk_check, zlk_line_* (the strongest coherent e–i line), zlk_gate* (with zlk_gate_baseline_yr, the free elements' baseline, zlk_gate_d_min_arcsec_yr, a planetary residual's smallest distance to a planetary rate, zlk_gate_detail = coorbital_unfitted_forcing for a co-orbital of Mercury to Mars, zlk_gate_rho_max the local ratio the status reads, zlk_gate_rho_global the former median ratio), free_* (free-omega gate); columns that change no status (Free elements: beyond the gate): the e–i coupling at the decisive period, every row: zlk_ei_coupling (zlk, forced_beat, none, not_measured), zlk_ei_reason (why not measured: no_period, undersampled, orbit_flip, short_record, band_unmeasured, law_undefined, …), zlk_ei_period_yr, zlk_ei_period_source (libration: P_cyc; circulation_harmonic: π/|ω̇|), zlk_ei_phase_deg (i against e), zlk_ei_band_r, zlk_ei_amp_e, zlk_ei_amp_i_deg, zlk_ei_ratio_h (|δi|/|δe| over the constant-H law), zlk_ei_ratio_beat (over the forced-beat law), confirmed_ei (zlk_ei_coupling == zlk, empty when not measured; also check_zlk_ei); the attribution of a kinematic libration: zlk_attribution (attributed, not_attributed), zlk_attribution_reason, zlk_attribution_scope (record; episodes: an episodic row demoted inside its episodes), zlk_forcing_mode (g5 (g5+g7+g8+const): the mode and the cluster merged into it), zlk_forcing_e (|c_j|), zlk_free_over_forcing, zlk_forcing_strict_pin (max|z_free| + Σ_{k≠j}|c_k| < |c_j| over the record), zlk_beat_period_yr (2π/|b_ϖ − g_j|), zlk_node_minus_mode_arcsec_yr, zlk_node_minus_mode_turns; the node lock (a flag, every row with free elements): zlk_node_lock (the mode, or empty), zlk_node_lock_reason (rate_mismatch, unbounded, unresolved, no_mode_amplitudes, no_node), zlk_node_lock_candidate, zlk_node_lock_rate_diff_arcsec_yr (b_Ω − g_j), zlk_node_lock_resolution_arcsec_yr, zlk_node_lock_min_deg, zlk_node_lock_max_deg (Ω − ϖ_j over the record), zlk_node_lock_period_yr, zlk_node_lock_cycles; the slow line of the center (a libration or a drift): zlk_centre_period_yr, zlk_centre_half_amp_deg, zlk_centre_origin (forced_beat:<gk>-<gj>, node, forced_direction, unexplained), zlk_centre_model_r, zlk_centre_model_gain (the model's swing over the center's), zlk_centre_model_half_amp_deg secular/ZLK analysis sec_* (center scale; sec_centre_rejected: a center-scale libration refused as a measured forced beat that explains the center, forced_beat:<gk>-<gj> (only with the gate enabled); sec_centre_period_yr, sec_centre_half_amp_deg, sec_centre_origin (forced_wave:<mode>, unexplained), the slow line of a modulated secular center), flt_* (cutoff and its bounds), base_required_kyr, base_period_yr, base_period_source, base_extend_to_years, base_extend_cause (an uncertain verdict's extension: baseline, gate_cycles, gate_resolution; with review: gate_unresolvable, gate_undefined_phase, gate_unavailable, unusable_series), geo_*, exit_*, entry_*, rsp_e_*, rsp_i_* (response of e and i); secular rows: free_divisor [″/yr], the angle's divisor \(p\,g_{\text{free}} + q\,s_{\text{free}} + \sum_j(p_jg_j + q_js_j)\) with the rates of the body's free vectors over the whole record and the package's planetary fundamentals (empty when they cannot be measured; a diagnostic, no status reads it; not one of the ZLK free_* columns; Secular resonances) last comments

status_code is the integer status of older versions, kept only to compare with old runs; use the string columns. The codes are in the status tree (never merge −2 with −9). Under the minimal policy a Lidov-Kozai row whose free-omega gate gave no verdict keeps its geometry's status (code 2 or 1, flag gate_unavailable, at most medium): split every ZLK statistic by check_zlk_free_omega (pass: the gate confirmed it; not_measured: no verdict or the gate disabled; fail: measured kinematic). −2 is exactly veto zlk_kinematic, zlk_free_e (the free ω's own vetoes, check fail) or zlk_integral (the e–i integral broken where the forced terms are small; the check stays as the gate left it), −9 occurs only on uncertain rows.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
flags lists marks that change no status by themselves (a cap with the same name is in caps). Most are explained with their rule in the rule index and the pages it links (search for the name); these are not:

flag meaning exit_and_capture an episodic angle that left a libration and came back at least once, with its own force measured; names no mechanism subresonance_composite the accepted member does not dominate the multiplet's composite coefficient (Rouché test) subresonance_theory_disagrees the theoretical center of the member (test D) was measured and disagrees; confidence only subresonance_theory_crossing no theoretical center: the orbits can intersect subresonance_theory_round_off no theoretical center: its coefficients are below round-off subresonance_theory_range no theoretical center: \(e\) or \(e_P\) outside (0, 1), or an empty window owner_catalogue_ambiguous an owner candidate on catalog longitudes lies within the phase error of a threshold: undecided owner_outside_episode an accepted owner covers less than MMR_OWNER_COVER_MIN of an own episode of σ (F7): written in neighbours, not owner; origin from the tree owner_psi_too_fast an accepted owner in its libration regime covers an episode but its Ψ/u turns at least MMR_OWNER_PSI_TURNS_PER_CYCLE_MAX times per cycle (P2): it cannot make those cycles; written in neighbours action_step an accepted run has a step in its libration action (the energy of its cycles jumps) that cuts the record; the run is split there like at a jump rejected_candidate the angle had turning points, but the record ends in circulation and what it had does not count as a libration (a 1:1 leg at the start, a single half-libration, or too short a record): non-resonant / circulation policy_unknown_leaf the minimal policy has no rule for the tree's leaf, so the geometry's status stands; a bug to report uncovered_bounded_run 1:1 coverage audit: the orbit-averaged angle holds a bounded run of at least MMR_COORBITAL_AUDIT_MIN_HALF_CYCLES half-cycles inside the window that no counted episode covers, and the local 1:1 law on it passes the co-orbital force check, not thin (aud_unc_*); a review reason, never a status. Clone rows of an ensemble do not carry it into PLOT=review (the clone archive keeps no flags) floor_above_own_loop 1:1 coverage audit: a period floor rejects a run although it exceeds the loop of the averaged potential through that run's own turns (an accepted run below its floor: the loop over its turn pairs, for a run of mixed turns that of its first pair; or a quasi-satellite pass rejected as below_period_floor, no_turning_points or no_run_in_well, which the floor causes through the pass's cutoff and prominence, whose stay's loop through ≥ 2 turns is below the QS floor; aud_floor_*); a review reason, never a status owner_unresolved no owner accepted; the best candidate's phases cannot separate it from σ and its potential route does not apply: check_mmr_owner not measured zone_eq_only the separatrix zone's modulation is the \(e^q\) estimate, not resolved multiplet members zone_edge_cycle at least one cycle lies within one σ of a zone edge: its class is not stable jump_locator_aliased the jump locator's time τ ≥ \(T_0/\pi\): the resonance's own swing can imitate a step of \(a\) extend_time MMR: a longer integration in extend_direction (forward, backward, both) would show how a record edge ends: an arc or stall after circulation at the end, the mirror at the start, one reflection cut by an edge, a clean 1:1 edge leg or an edge half-libration; extend_to_years holds its length; whatever the action, no status or level changes (the record's edges)

docs.title: mmr_numbers.csv
docs.text:
One row per body × MMR (name, resonance), every number the analysis measured, grouped by prefix:

prefix step examples rec_ record check and leaf rec_rule (the leaf of the status tree that decided, G0 on a refused input; G6 for every insufficient_time angle), geo_angle_rule (MMR: the G rule of the angle decision, AngleDecision.rule: G0 … G6, G5a, G5w; the figure's subtitle and 'Decided at' name it on an insufficient_time row; empty for secular and ZLK, whose angle decision has no rule), rec_unphysical (1 for a rejected orbit, else 0); on a refused input also rec_body_coefficient (\(k\)) and rec_input_problems (the failed input requirements, ;-separated). Present when nothing else was measured ctx_ context ctx_a_mean_au, ctx_a_star_au, ctx_delta_a_au, ctx_c_rad_yr_au, ctx_P_syn_yr, ctx_rate_expected_deg_yr, ctx_rate_measured_deg_yr, ctx_crosses (the angle's planets whose band \(q_j\)…\(Q_j\) the body's band \(q_\min\)…\(Q_\max\) overlaps); secular/ZLK: ctx_a_med_au, ctx_a_min_au, ctx_a_max_au, ctx_e_min, ctx_e_max, ctx_inc_min_deg, ctx_inc_max_deg; every type: ctx_orbit_overlap (radial overlap with all eight planets, \(q_\min < Q_j\) and \(Q_\max > q_j\), e.g. Venus;Earth; none when no band overlaps, empty when \(q\) or \(Q\) is not measured; necessary for an encounter, not sufficient: inclination and phases are ignored; no decision reads it), ctx_orbit_overlap_source (the planet bands: saved = min \(q_j\), max \(Q_j\) of the saved elements for all eight, J2000 = \(a_j(1\mp e_j)\) of the J2000 elements, one value of \(e_j\) and no range, always for secular/ZLK; saved:Earth+Mars = those saved, the others J2000) smp_ step and alias smp_step_yr, smp_verdict, smp_fast_over_half_amp (σ's fast residual over the decisive episode's median half-amplitude: with MMR_SHORT_PERIOD_CAP_RATIO > 0 the cap short_period_aliased is lifted at or below it), smp_branches, smp_far_ratio, smp_ghost_au, smp_nyquist_halfwidth_au, smp_unwrap_resid_p99_deg (λ part, the gate), smp_unwrap_resid_full_p99_deg, smp_unwrap_resid_full_max_deg (whole angle, read by G0 with jitter_low_e), smp_n_slow_element_steps, smp_phase_undefined_fraction (the |p|-scaled proxy: share of samples with |p| s/|z_f| > MMR_JITTER_MAX_RAD, not the share where ϖ is undefined), smp_varpi_undefined_fraction (ϖ's own s/|z_f| over that limit: undefined_phase needs it above MMR_VARPI_UNDEFINED_MAX_SHARE), smp_jitter (|p| δe_sp/ē, G0's jitter), smp_jitter_low_e, smp_undefined_phase, smp_safe_step_pred_yr, smp_resample_step_yr, smp_short_period_step_yr (min(P_orb, P_syn)/2: a step at or above it sets short_period_aliased), smp_folded_slowest_yr (the longest period the step folds P_orb, P_syn and their harmonics up to MMR_SHORT_PERIOD_HARMONICS into: slower than the period floor, it sets short_period_aliased below that step too), smp_fold_free_step_yr (the largest MMR_RESAMPLE_STEPS_YR step below the record's at which nothing folds by that predicate: a rerun there lifts short_period_aliased; empty when the step folds nothing or no grid step is free), smp_da_sp_over_a_excursion (the short-period scatter of a over the decisive episode's a half-excursion: above MMR_SHORT_PERIOD_A_RATIO a record that folds short periods gets the flag a_short_period_scatter, and the tree may read its failed L3/L4 as not measured) flt_ filter flt_cutoff_yr, flt_cutoff_binding (synodic, orbit, floor, user, centre_scale), flt_cutoff_floor_bound_yr, flt_cutoff_orbit_bound_yr (1.5 P_orb), flt_ripple_removed_deg, flt_gain_at_pcyc, flt_filter_too_slow, flt_period_floor_yr, flt_fast_reference_yr (1:1: what the prominence counts as fast), flt_x1_*, flt_x2_* (the ×2 guard: on the decisive episode flt_decisive_episode_id and its counterpart, flt_x1/x2_decisive_bounds_yr, their time overlap over union flt_decisive_overlap, 0 = not reproduced; empty id = the whole interval), flt_withdrawn_before_tree (the passed checks the guard took from the tree, e.g. check_mmr_potential); G1q (1:1): flt_qs_period_yr (the shortest small-amplitude quasi-satellite period of the averaged potential; empty without a well, and for an angle that librates over the record at the first pass or an aliased step, where the well is not measured), flt_qs_floor_yr, flt_qs_cutoff_yr (the floor and cutoff of the quasi-satellite pass) geo_, stall_, exit_, entry_, jump_, regime_start_yr geometry geo_n_tp, geo_period_cycle_yr, geo_n_episodes, geo_centre_max_pass_rev, geo_drift_fraction, geo_n_slips, geo_stall_fraction, jump_times_yr; G2c: geo_centre_scale_cutoff_yr, geo_centre_scale_basis, geo_centre_scale_first_cutoff_yr; the G2c scale ladder: geo_scale_ladder_cutoff_yr (the rung that decided, also geo_centre_scale_cutoff_yr), _above_yr (the scale it replaced), _n_tp/_n_tp_centre (slow extrema there and at that scale), _shift (worst shift of the extrema / P_slow), _slow_yr, _fast_yr (P_fast), _floor_yr; G1l: geo_before_jump_covers_start, geo_before_jump_end_gap_P (the earliest librating episode before the last jump: covers the record start, its gap to the jump zone in periods); G2a (a step of the libration action): geo_action_step_n_cuts, geo_action_step_n_tested, geo_action_step_time_yr and _t_from_yr/_t_to_yr (the transitional half-cycle), _run_t0_yr/_run_t1_yr, _n_before/_n_after (half-cycles), _amp_before_deg/_amp_after_deg, _separation, _ratio, _a_ratio, _transition_P, _cycles_before/_cycles_after, _dh, _dh_threshold, _h_before/_h_after (median cycle h per side); test 7, one potential for both regimes: _shape_cutoff_yr (the cutoff of the reported shape test), _shape_R2 (R² of V_E within the larger swings' cycles), _shape_wells (minima of that V over a turn), _shape_cycles_before/_shape_cycles_after (disjoint cycles per side), _law_before/_law_after (the worst T_obs/T_pred of each side at that cutoff; inf: a cycle V cannot hold), _period_ratio (median period of the smaller swings / of the larger ones: near 1, one forcing frequency explains both), _tp_mismatch (the worst |observed − predicted turning point| / half-swing), _drift_before/_drift_after (each side's spread of cycle energies / the energy step), _held_out (1: the larger side's laws were tested out of sample), _laws (the worst laws at each cutoff factor), _shape_failed (the sub-test that failed, name@factor), _vf_r, _vf_law_small (V_E ~ V_F over the larger swings and the smaller side's worst law in V_F: reported, they decide nothing), _provisional, _failed (the first test that failed; empty when it cut; withheld when the guard kept the record whole), _withheld_checks/_withheld_verdict (the checks the cut left unmeasured that failed on the whole record, the verdict it would have given), jump_action_step (1 for each jump that is an action step); record_entry_* (after a cut: the entry before the record's first run, the entry_* columns read on it); the edge rule: exit_raw_arc_rev/entry_raw_arc_rev (travel of the raw angle averaged over one orbit away from the center, from the last episode's last TP to the record's end / from the start to the first TP, in turns; empty for secular/ZLK) exit_raw_monotonic/entry_raw_monotonic (the monotonic test alone) and exit_observed/entry_observed (≥ LIBRATION_EDGE_ARC_REV turns and monotonic: the edge is not covered); the union of episodes: geo_union_n_episodes (the episodes that cover the record together, 0 for none), geo_union_tp_range_rad, geo_union_raw_range_rad (the largest range of σ_f's TPs and of the orbit-averaged raw angle between two of them), geo_union_span_tp_range_rad, geo_union_span_raw_range_rad (the same over the whole chain), geo_union_gap_max_P (the longest gap over P_left + P_right; a column, no test), geo_union_band_overshoot_deg (how far σ_f gets in a gap beyond the nearest of the neighbors' bands: each one's own c ± A, or the band carried linearly between their centers; ≤ LIBRATION_UNION_BAND_MARGIN_DEG for a union), geo_union_start_shortfall_P, geo_union_end_shortfall_P (how far the TPs beyond an outer episode fall short of the record edge, in its periods; empty where the episode covers the edge), geo_union_read_episodic (1: a G2u union the status read as episodic, not promoted), geo_union_word_centre_scale (1: G2c found such a union at the scale of the center and the fine verdict's word was rewritten to libration; 0 when the word stayed); geo_cs_rej_cutoff_yr, geo_cs_rej_tp_prominence_deg, geo_cs_rej_status, geo_cs_rej_angle_status, geo_cs_rej_reason, geo_cs_rej_origin, geo_cs_rej_caps, geo_cs_rej_n_accepted, geo_cs_rej_union_n, geo_cs_rej_episodes, geo_cs_rej_decisive (diagnostics only: the last G2c analysis that union guard rejected, its W_c, TP prominence, verdict, caps, accepted episodes and their union, as t0-t1 spans in yr; empty when none was rejected); G4b: geo_centre_net_rev (the slow center's net advance over the window, rev); the 1:1 edge turn (rule coorbital_edge_turn): geo_edge_raw_tp_t (the times of the turning points it added, yr), geo_edge_raw_read (every reversal of the averaged raw angle read in an edge trim, side@t:outcome, outcome closes or the test it failed: prominence, site, a_cross, energy, no_profile, no_cycle); the 1:1 single legs (leaf G4c): geo_leg_n and geo_leg_read (every leg outside the accepted runs, t0-t1:topology[:edge]:out/in entry/exit:zone entry/exit:force/energy; topology tadpole, horseshoe, qs or passing, edge start or end), in mmr_numbers.csv the deciding leg geo_leg_t0_yr, geo_leg_t1_yr, geo_leg_topology, geo_leg_outcome (transient, uncertain, extend, scatter) and geo_leg_discrepancy (the first test that failed: passing, force_law, energy, turn); the half-swings of another MMR between passages (leaf G4h): geo_half_libration_read (t0-t1[:edge]:R² h1/h2:restoring); the record's edges (rule end_arc_extend): geo_start_edge_* and geo_end_edge_* with _kind (slowdown, reflection or empty), _pass_rev (revolutions of σ_f in the edge pass), _t_yr (the last completed revolution, or the center turn), _duration_yr (from there to the window edge), _last_rev_yr (the pass's longest revolution), _other_rev (a reflection: the center's revolutions beyond the turn), _range_deg; geo_extend_time_from (what set the flag extend_time: end:slowdown, start:reflection, leg:end, half:start, ;-separated); G5a: geo_centre_n_tp_interior (turns of the slow center farther than W_c from the window's edges), geo_centre_range_rad (the slow center's range: an arc below one revolution); G5w (two slow turns, slow_swing.py): geo_slow_swing_t0_yr, geo_slow_swing_t1_yr (the turns), geo_slow_swing_amp_deg (half the range of σ_s between them), geo_slow_swing_period_yr (2 (t1 − t0)), geo_slow_swing_identity_slope_ratio, geo_slow_swing_identity_corr (the identity on σ and a low-passed at W_c), geo_slow_swing_a_au (the a swing between the turns), geo_slow_swing_a_theory_au (2 ω0 sin(A/2)/|c| of the directly averaged well), geo_slow_swing_t0_theory_yr, geo_slow_swing_period_theory_yr (T0_th and T0_th F(A)), geo_slow_swing_a_ratio, geo_slow_swing_period_ratio (G5w needs both within √MMR_STRENGTH_CHECK_RATIO), geo_slow_swing_reason (why it is not judged: not_two_turns, coorbital, identity_not_measured, not_two_body, …; empty when judged); forced waves (F6): geo_n_forced_wave_episodes and, of the one with most TPs, geo_forced_wave_episode_id, geo_forced_wave_period_yr, geo_forced_wave_line (the lattice line, empty for the wrong-sign route), geo_forced_wave_line_offset (|1/T − 1/P| W P), geo_forced_wave_identity_slope_ratio, geo_forced_wave_identity_slope_offset, geo_forced_wave_identity_corr, geo_forced_wave_identity_corr_abs; G1q: geo_qs_visit_yr (the stay of the orbit-averaged angle inside the quasi-satellite well: the longest one that turns, else the longest), geo_qs_visit_needed_yr (MMR_COORBITAL_QS_TRIGGER_PERIODS × geo_qs_visit_loop_yr, or × the longest P_QS along the stay when that is nan), geo_qs_visit_turns (the turns of the averaged angle in that stay, reversals ≥ MMR_TP_PROMINENCE_FLOOR_DEG; the pass needs one), geo_qs_visit_loop_yr (the period of the loop of the averaged potential through the stay's lowest and highest turn), geo_qs_n_outside_episodes (the kept pass: its librating episodes outside the well), geo_qs_pass (kept: the row is the quasi-satellite pass; rejected: that pass found no libration in the well; resample: the step cannot filter its cutoff; empty: the rule did not fire), geo_qs_reject (a rejected pass: why, read on its best in-well run: no_turning_points, no_run_in_well, keeps_outside, that run's ineligible_reason such as below_period_floor, or not_accepted:<reject_reason>) and that run's geo_qs_run_t0_yr, _t1_yr, _n_tp, _period_yr, _half_amp_deg, _floor_yr, _floor_source, _loop_yr, _K_over_K_theory, _R2 (reporting only); the 1:1 coverage audit (prograde 1:1, after the policy, never a status): aud_n_bounded_runs (bounded runs of the orbit-averaged angle), aud_n_uncovered (stretches of at least MMR_COORBITAL_AUDIT_MIN_HALF_CYCLES half-cycles inside the window that no counted episode covers), aud_edge_half_cycles (uncovered half-cycles of stretches mostly in the edge trim), the longest stretch's aud_unc_t0_yr, _t1_yr, _half_cycles, _period_yr, _half_amp_deg, _centre_deg, _well (qs, tadpole_L4, tadpole_L5, horseshoe, compound), _overlap_reason (the overlapping run's reject or ineligible reason, eligible_not_counted for an eligible run the policy did not count, qs_pass_rejected:<geo_qs_reject>, no_run), _law_K, _law_R2, _law_check (its local 1:1 law and force check: pass, thin, fail, not_measured; the flag needs pass; the reported stretch is the longest that passes, else the longest), aud_n_law_confirmed (missed stretches whose law passes; at most 3 are fitted), aud_noise_deg, aud_swing_deg (the turning points' hysteresis), aud_not_measured (step_not_below_half_window: the step is too coarse for the 3-orbit average; nonfinite_samples), and Layer I's aud_floor_above_loop (run:<id> or qs_pass:<geo_qs_reject>), aud_floor_yr, aud_loop_yr; G1f: geo_subfloor_t0_theory_yr (the shortest small-amplitude period of the averaged potential), geo_subfloor_floor_yr (the pass's floor), geo_subfloor_period_yr (its decisive episode's period), geo_subfloor_kept (1 the row is the G1f pass, 0 the pass ran and was not kept, empty: not run), geo_subfloor_failed (cycle, F, centre, L4: what kept it out) ep_ decisive episode the episodes.csv columns of the episode the verdict rests on (the covering one, else the longest accepted), prefixed ep_ (ep_closed_by_return, ep_forced_wave, ep_force_R2_null_max, …); also ep_onset_ratio (O1) and ep_n_tp_cut_half, ep_n_tp_cut_double (L1: its TPs at P_c × 0.5 and × 2) sep_ energy and zone sep_VE_R2, sep_VE_VF_agree_fraction, sep_VF_period_law_med, sep_VF_period_law_n (R0 with a: the median T_obs/T_pred of the compared cycles in V_F and their count, on the record or the episode R0 was read in; empty/0 when no correlation was computed and for a 1:1 angle whose energy integral replaces the comparison; reference), sep_h_med, sep_zone_J_lo, sep_zone_h_hi, sep_R0_sigma_only, sep_R0_with_a, sep_episodes_in_separatrix_zone, sep_zone_source (pendulum, or averaged_potential: the episode cycles classed by the action J/⟨J_s⟩ of their turning points in a two-body angle's averaged well), sep_h_avgpot_med, sep_h_avgpot_max, sep_h_avgpot_n (their energies, 0 at the bottom, 1 at the barrier), sep_J_avgpot_med, sep_J_avgpot_max, sep_J_avgpot_n (their J/⟨J_s⟩ in that well, J/J_s(t) times J_s(t) over the record's mean: the numbers the classes read; a loop around several wells has none, nor any when that mean is not measured), sep_cycle_classes (deep, zone, above, not_measured: a loop around several wells), sep_n_not_measured, sep_cycle_topology (per cycle: single_well, merged_wells, separatrix, rotation), sep_cycle_J (J/J_s, empty/nan for merged_wells and rotation), sep_cycle_J_loop_rad2_yr (the action of the cycle's own loop, also around several wells), sep_cycle_dJdE_loop_yr (dJ_loop/dE = T_loop/2π), sep_mechanism (kick, trend, pulsation, layer, unexplained, empty without a crossing; reference), sep_n_crossings (distinct boundary times: a slip between librations is one), sep_n_exits, sep_n_captures (directed transitions: that slip is one of each), sep_period_law_med (R0's median T_obs/T_pred), sep_period_law_source (full_well: T_pred of the libration cycles that librate in the full averaged well taken there, two-body with the planet saved; fitted: all in V_E), sep_period_law_n_full_well (those cycles), sep_period_law_fitted_med (the law in V_E, kept beside it) rsp_ response of a rsp_identity_slope_ratio, rsp_force_R2_h1, rsp_force_R2_h2, rsp_force_law, rsp_identity_slope_offset (|slope/c − 1|), rsp_phi0_coherence, rsp_phi0_max_dev_deg, rsp_phi0_tol_deg (the spread of φ0 and its expected bound: diagnostic, they decide nothing), rsp_b1_ratio, rsp_b5_ratio, rsp_b5_route (data, geometry, owner, none), rule R: rsp_force_source, rsp_identity_source, rsp_b1_source (where the status tree read L4, L3, B1: record pooled, witness, before_jump pooled over the episodes before the last jump of a; the rsp_ numbers of each check are those of its source), rsp_witness_episode_id, rsp_n_witnesses, rsp_n_episode_force_fail, rsp_force_line, rsp_force_line_period_yr, rsp_force_line_offset (the forced line of the angle's lattice within the window's resolution of the force law's period, the offset in units of 1/(W P)), rsp_force_contaminated (L4 not_measured by it), rsp_force_raw_check (the measured L4 it replaced), rsp_force_n_windows_jump (force-law windows dropped next to a confirmed jump of a), the line rule: rsp_response_cutoff_ep_yr (the cutoff the force law read), rsp_line_binding_yr (the line of ȧ that raised it; empty when none did), rsp_force_R2_null_max (the largest R² of the same law with a shifted in time), rsp_force_null_gain (R² minus it; the ledger's null test), the N-harmonic force law (read only when L4 fails or passes thin; it caps the row like the decisive window).
