docs.title: episodes.csv
docs.text: One row per run of turning points, accepted or not: name, resonance, episode_id, accepted, for an MMR eligible and ineligible_reason (whether an accepted run counts for the status, i.e. is a librating episode of the angle, and why not: forced_wave, induced, below_period_floor (faster than the angle's period floor, a forced wave the cutoff let through), centre_turns (its center runs a full turn inside it), before_last_jump (a librating run before the last jump of a, read only by G1e/G1l); eligible is False on a rejected run, whose reason is reject_reason, and empty on the slow scale; accepted keeps its meaning), subtype (stationary, modulated, moving_centre), reject_reason (too_few_tp, centre_moves, no_closed_cycle, over_the_top, edge), t_start_yr, t_end_yr, n_tp, tp_times_yr, periods (period_med_yr, _min_, _max_), half-amplitudes (half_amp_min_deg, _med_, _max_), the center (centre_mod_2pi_deg, centre_shift_deg, centre_shift_over_amp, bands_overlap, centre_estimates, centre_stationarity, centre_returns), closure (closed_cycles: full cycles whose net advance is below their swing, an episode needs one; closure_ratio_min: the smallest advance/swing of the run), coverage (coverage_start_gap_P, coverage_end_gap_P from the record's edges; for an MMR also window_start_gap_yr, window_end_gap_yr from the analysis window's edges, tp_step_max_yr, the longest TP-to-TP step, and window_start_hidden_P, window_end_hidden_P, the stretches the filter trims off the record), before_last_jump, tp_prominence_deg (MMR: the prominence its turning points were selected with, that of its run of provisional turning points, else of its regime between jumps of a), the moving center (MMR: frame sigma or psi, the frame whose band test accepted it; margin_sigma_deg, margin_psi_deg, min(m + A) − max(m − A) over the full cycles, > 0 passes; half_swing_margin_deg, every maximum above every minimum, a column only; centre_track: empty when the σ test decided, else ok, invalid_track (the centers do not follow it better than a fixed center and the reversed track), no_well, quadrature_not_converged, close_approach, three_body, planet_not_saved, no_planet_mass; centre_model_drift_deg, c(t_end) − c(t_start); centre_track_rms_deg, centre_fixed_rms_deg, centre_reversed_rms_deg), the MMR edge and return rules (exit_observed, entry_observed: the last / first accepted run whose exit / entry the raw angle shows; closed_by_return, return_t_a_yr, return_t_b_yr, return_level_fraction: a 2-TP run closed by its phase return, the two crossings of its level and where that level lies between the second (0) and the first (1) turning point, 0.5 for the mid-level; such an episode's period is t_b − t_a; edge_raw_tp (1:1, rule coorbital_edge_turn): exit / entry when a turning point read on the orbit-averaged raw angle in the filter's edge trim closed this run's cycle; wells and marks (1:1, rule coorbital_well_cut): the wells of the averaged potential the run's half-cycles swing through in time order (qs, tadpole_L4, tadpole_L5, horseshoe, compound, joined by >), and the changes inside the episode that are no boundary, ;-separated: well_change@t (the turning point where the well changes), amplitude_change@t0:t1 (the transitional half-cycle), kick@t (a jump of a at such a change), unheld@t0:t1 (rule coorbital_well_core: the stretch of the episode beyond its well-holding core) [yr]; for any other MMR (rule regime_cut_mark), centre_step@t0:t1 (the step half-cycle) and stall@t0:t1 (the stall) of a regime cut that separates no libration regions; the core, the residence and the sub-regimes (1:1, rule coorbital_residence): core_t0_yr/core_t1_yr (an accepted run's first and last measured turning points; of a run continued beyond its well-holding cycles, rule coorbital_well_core, the first and last of those; the confidence's core cycles read the core, coverage, the edges and the margins the run's turning points), residence_t0_yr/residence_t1_yr (the stay around the core, inferred, not measured: outwards over the legs of the raw angle averaged over MMR_COORBITAL_EDGE_TURN_ORBITS orbits until a leg sweeps a whole turn), residence_bounded_by_start/_end (circulation, or edge: the record ends inside the stay, its continuation is undetermined — no exit), residence_zone_max (the largest |a − a_P| / Δa_max at the averaged angle's reversals outside the core; reported only), subregimes (well@t0:t1;…, the stretches between those changes) and subregime_checks (force/energy of each sub-regime's own 1:1 law, for a run of two or more); forced_wave: lattice_line or wrong_sign for an accepted run judged a forced wave of another argument, no episode of the angle, F6; strength for every accepted run of a row that rule 5s decided (non_resonant/implausible_strength), marked after the verdict (MMR_FORCED_WAVE_STRENGTH): the name of the ground, the angle's own force cannot give that period, not a driver found; unconfirmed_ripple for an accepted run set aside before G2 as a ripple without measurable physics on an unfinished slow swing (MMR_RIPPLE_ON_ARC, status tree); geo_n_episodes then leaves those runs out, as it leaves out the F6 runs, while geo_n_forced_wave_episodes counts F6 only), cutoff_yr; for an MMR also the pendulum (T0_min_kyr, T0_max_kyr, T0_ratio, omega0_rad_yr, omega0_vmax_rad_yr (max|σ̇| / (2 sin(A_max/2)), the cosine frequency from the peak speed), omega0_vmax_ratio (max|σ̇| / (2 ω0), the peak speed in cosine separatrix units; not a bound for a well that is not a cosine), half_width_au, a_excursion_pred_au, a_excursion_meas_au, mu_eff), the onset bands a_band_std_before/in/after_au (each cut to the episode's regime clear of the record's ends and of the confirmed jumps; the stretch before never holds an accepted episode of the angle: onset_before_t0_yr/_t1_yr are its bounds, onset_group the earlier episodes joined without a circulation between them, the stretch then lying before the first of them; onset_not_measured: record_edge, jump or episode (cut at an earlier episode with a circulation after it) when the stretch before or the episode itself keeps less than a period; O1's three parts, onset: onset_coherence_r2, onset_phase_gap_deg, onset_own_law_r2 and onset_own_law_r2_episode), energy (h_min, h_med, h_max, J_over_Js_min/max, zone_class), the force law on the episode with its own period (force_window_yr, force_n_windows, force_n_windows_jump (windows dropped next to a confirmed jump of a), force_R2_h1/h2 (the 1:1 law's halves for a co-orbital), force_R2_multi, force_law, force_K_au_yr, force_phi0_deg, phi0_coherence, phi0_tol_deg, identity_*, b1_ratio, force_line, force_line_period_yr, force_contaminated, force_raw_check, force_cutoff_yr, force_line_binding_yr, force_R2_null_max: the line rule on that episode; force_harm_N, force_R2_harm, force_harm_reason: the N-harmonic force law when it was consulted, as rsp_force_harm_*; force_dforce_R2, force_dforce_scale, force_dforce_reason: the direct averaged-force law on that episode, as rsp_dforce_*), on a librating episode also its checks (rule R: check_a_response, force_thin, check_identity, check_a_amplitude, empty on the other runs; episode_filter_too_slow: the filter guard at the episode's period), witness (it stands for the dynamics by itself), deciding_witness (the witness the status read), libration_origin, owner (per episode: induced and the owner's key on every episode an accepted owner induces, also when the row's own episodes decided; on the decisive episode the verdict's own owner, never a neighbor) and resonant_argument (the verdict's on the decisive episode; when the verdict names one, every other episode the member, or composite, chosen in its own window). A 1:1 run of at least two turning points also has its own floor reading (rule coorbital_floor_profile, signal): cpl_turn_site_entry, cpl_turn_site_exit (where its first and last turn lie on the averaged potential: planet, l3 (a reflection on that top), tadpole_L4, tadpole_L5, qs (a turn inside that well)), cpl_turn_sites (every turn), cpl_turn_da_ratio_entry/_exit (|a − a_P| / δa_max on the run's side of the turn), cpl_turn_out_in_entry/_exit (|a − a_P| after over before, 1 for a reflection), cpl_loop_period_yr (the loop of the averaged potential through its turns), cpl_law_K_over_K_theory (the local 1:1 law on the run ± one half-cycle; measured only for reflections and, in the G1q pass, for runs of quasi-satellite turns), cpl_law_R2 (that law's R²), cpl_floor_yr (its own floor, empty when the angle's applies) and cpl_floor_source (profile_loop; qs_loop: a run of quasi-satellite turns inside the well of the G1q pass, whose floor is min(QS floor, this); qs_loop_moot: such a run whose loop floor could not change the decision, the QS floor holds; not_reflection, no_loop, law_not_positive, no_profile: why the angle's floor applies). The turns are read on the orbit-averaged angle. mmr_numbers.csv has flt_fast_reference_yr, the period below which the prominence counts σ_f as fast (a 1:1 angle: the shortest floor any of its runs can get; empty: the floor). scale (MMR): main for the runs of the angle at P_c, slow for the runs G2c found at the center scale W_c that hold the slower libration of the center (slow_* in mmr_numbers.csv; geometric columns only, cutoff_yr = W_c, no physics); a reader of the decisive episode or of the main scale filters on main. counted and candidate (every type): the run is one of the episodes the minimal policy counts (n_counted_episodes in summary.csv, drawn solid in the figure), or a candidate it drew faint and did not count (a vetoed episode that keeps its turning points at every cutoff, a near-episode run). A counted or candidate 1:1 leg or half-swing is no run: it appears only in summary.csv (leg, half). bw_outcome (forced, own, not_measured), bw_reason, bw_sigma_hi, bw_sigma_lo, bw_a_hi, bw_reference_P (MMR runs below 45°): the forced-wave test against the episode's background, the median envelope inside over the outside quantiles; forced takes the run out of the count, and when it is every counted run the row is non_resonant by the veto forced_wave.

docs.title: candidates.csv
docs.text: name, resonance, kind (subresonance or owner), candidate (its package notation), rank, accepted, reason (the first test it failed, or accepted:<route>). Subresonances: coefficients, order, j, nodal, member_degree (Σ|slow coefficients|), strength_rel (test E′), the center track (centre_range_deg, centre_rate_rad_kyr, rate_resid_tol (the rate over its tolerance), centre_max_pass_deg), phi0_coherence, force_R2_med, test L (member_tp, member_episodes: turning points and librating episodes of the member's own angle in the scan window, member_reject: why its longest run is not one, member_t0_yr/member_t1_yr: the longest librating episode; empty when step 1 dropped the member), the theory (coef_rel, composite_rms_deg, period_corr, period_ratio, th_centre_range_deg: the range of the member's theoretical center in the scan window). Subresonance reasons besides the tests' (range, rate, pass, E_strength, L_not_librating, A_coherence, B_centre, C_tie, E_t0, …): theory_flatter (another admissible member's theoretical center is flatter). Owners: R2, psi_share, K_au_yr, K_theory_au_yr, strength_ratio, regime, n_windows and the same numbers of the angle itself on the same windows (sigma_R2, sigma_phi0_coherence, sigma_slow_turns, sigma_slow_to_band), the multiplet law where the single phase fails (multiplet_R2, multiplet_coherence, multiplet_planet, sigma_multiplet_R2: σ with constant coefficients on the same long windows) and law; owner_period_yr, rate_admissible (a forced wave at that period lies in the a band; else reason rate_outside_band), lever_owner, lever_sigma, route, and the potential route where it was tried (pot_reason, pot_R2, pot_scale_lo, pot_scale_hi). Owner reasons: rate_outside_band, phase_unresolved, potential_scale_out, potential_unconfirmed, accepted:potential.

docs.title: constants.csv
docs.text: One per run. A row per planet: planet, n_deg_yr and n_source (measured from the saved longitude, else table), mu, a_mean_au, e_mean, g_arcsec_yr, s_arcsec_yr, varpi_dot_meas_arcsec_yr, Omega_dot_meas_arcsec_yr; then the great inequality (period_yr, dlambda_jupiter_deg, dlambda_saturn_deg, measured) and the other planetary near-commensurabilities (period_yr).

docs.title: Data files
docs.text:
data/data-<body>.csv: times (years), a, e, inc, Omega, omega, M, longitude, varpi (rad), a_filtered (the body-level low-pass of a, oscillations_cutoff), then per saved resonance <key>_angle (the angle mod 2π, exact) and <key>_angle_unwrapped (for an MMR the analysis' predictive unwrap). An MMR's filtered angle is not written: the analysis reproduces it from the cutoff in summary.csv. Secular and ZLK rows add <key>_angle_filtered, <key>_angle_filtered_unwrapped (secular: also _osculating, _proper). The elements are ecliptic; a ZLK row's LK_angle is ω from the plane zlk_angle_frame names (default the invariable plane), and so is <body>-omega-free.csv of a body with a ZLK row. data-<body>-periodograms.csv: a_frequency, a_power, a_period and the same per angle. data-planet-<planet>.csv: times, a, e, inc, Omega, omega, M, l, varpi.

import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402

summary = pd.read_csv('output/my_run/summary.csv')
print(summary.groupby(['status', 'angle_status', 'confidence'], dropna=False).size())  # uncertain/invalid: no level
in_resonance = summary[summary['status'].isin(['resonant', 'transient'])]

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
Which figures a simulation draws is set by plots (default ['combined'], the one-page verdict figure). Which rows get them is set by plot (a filter on the verdict, see Configuration) and plot_always. The default review draws every row except a confident plain circulation: the nonzero rows and the doubtful negatives (non_resonant at medium or low confidence, the review queue review_required). After the run the log prints the rows by status × confidence and how many were drawn.

sim = resonances.Simulation(
    plot='nonzero',
    plots=['evolution', 'combined'],
    plot_options={'style': 'screen'},  # optional, see below
)
kind resonances file ({body}-{key}-…) what it shows combined MMR, secular, ZLK combined/…-combined the one-page verdict figure: time panels left, the verdict and every number of the decision right evolution all {body}-{key}.png angle, a, e, i against time, periodograms against period (PLOT_CONFIG preset; a low-passed by the body-level filter, LIBRATION_FILTER_CUTOFF) recurrence MMR -recurrence recurrence of the state \((\sigma, \dot\sigma)\) fair prograde two-body MMR -fair FAIR plane: mean anomaly against the longitude difference to the planet portrait MMR, secular, ZLK -portrait phase portrait: \(\sigma\)–\(\dot\sigma\) (or \(\sigma\)–a) for an MMR, \((r\cos\sigma, r\sin\sigma)\) for a secular or ZLK angle angle secular, ZLK -angle \(\sigma(t)\): osculating, filtered, turning points rate secular, ZLK -rate the rate of the filtered \(\sigma\), with the divisor cycles MMR -cycles oscillation cycles of \(\sigma_f\) and of a (the analysis' \(a_f\), else the osculating a), stacked on one period ecc_vector all {body}-ecc-vector.png the \((k, h) = (e\cos\omega, e\sin\omega)\) plane cross_spectrum all -coherence-{pair} coherence and cross-phase (Cross-spectral coherence) free_omega Lidov-Kozai -free-omega-drift, -portrait, -vector the free argument of pericentre (Free elements) clones all, a body with clones {body}-{key}-clones.png the ensemble: every clone's angle by status, status against initial a (with the catalog \(a_{\rm res}\) of an MMR), the status shares with Wilson intervals, or 'no shares' for an unusable covariance (also drawn with combined; Clones)

An unknown name is an error; a kind is drawn only for the resonance types it lists. The image format is image_type (png or pdf). Combined figures go to plot_path/combined/, the others to plot_path/figures/, both split by plot_layout (confidence/status by default: combined/high/resonant/…; Output data). None of these figures feeds a status.

What every panel, line and icon means: How to read the figures, with an example of each kind. One example for every status: Gallery.

docs.title: Colors and units
docs.text:
One palette gives a quantity the same color in every panel of the combined figures, MMR and secular/ZLK alike:

color what black a filtered series gray the osculating series (a band when the samples are dense) red the center of the angle and the line \(\dot\sigma = 0\) blue a fitted or model quantity (force law, \(\pm 2\omega_0\), \(\pm\Delta a\)) dark gray reference marks (turning points, jumps, \(h = 1\), \(a_*\)) dark orange the warning line at the top of the legend when FAIR (m) is not drawn, with the reason cyan the catalog resonant axis \(a_{\rm res}\) orange, purple an accepted subresonance, the owner resonance

The right column is ten blocks (header, subtitle, key facts, why, confidence, checks, evidence, caveats, numbers, footer; reading the figures), in two halves with a fixed place for each: header to checks on the left, evidence to the footer on the right, on every figure. The time axis is labeled under the last panel and under (b). Its plaque and ◆ take the status color (resonant #1B7A3A, transient #B35400, near_separatrix #6B3FA0, non_resonant #4A4F57, uncertain #2F5D9E, invalid #B2182B; style.STATUS_COLOURS, also used by the clone figures). The icons are ✓ green, ⚠ amber, ✗ red, ? gray and – light gray. The action is one chip in the header: gray no action needed, amber glance at (…), red review figure + numbers, blue extend to … or resample to …. A column that does not fit makes the figure taller, by at most style.COLUMN_MAX_GROWTH_IN (6 in); the left panels keep their place at the top. Beyond that the column trims (the Numbers groups first), and verdict_column.column_text gives the complete text of the column. Every time color bar uses the same map (viridis without its palest yellow). Wrapped angles are labeled in [0°, 360°). Time is in yr, kyr or Myr, whichever suits the span (the evolution figure keeps years).

plot_options={'combined': {'numbers': 'all'}} prints every number of the decision in the right column of the combined figures instead of the ten blocks (explained, the default).

The MMR figure has no empty slot: without FAIR the legend takes the place of (m) under one warning line that says why (mmr_combined.fair_warning). Panel (l) draws each accepted episode over its fill interval of (a), the part beyond its turning points dashed. Panel (e) draws the force law the status read (a witness episode's, rule R, at its own cutoff; under the direct averaged-force law its low-passed \(\dot a\) and \(s\times\) the term's force per window, mmr_combined.draw_direct_law). Accepted runs that are no libration of the angle are labeled #id wave, #id forced (strength) or #id ripple on (l) (mmr_combined.wave_labels; on (a) only a counted one is filled and labeled). The ▼ marks of the strip (b′) on (b) keep their x and step clear of the panel letter and the ALIAS plaque (mmr_combined.strip_marks). The MMR header's second line names who makes the cycles by its role (owner, driver, neighbor with its interval, resonant argument, kinematic term; verdict_text.cause_line); the episodes another resonance induces are hatched \\\\ on (a) (mmr_combined.INDUCED_HATCH, apart from the //// of an episode before a jump) and labeled induced on (l); also in … names the other resonance of a joint capture. Panel (a) of both the MMR and the secular/ZLK figure draws only what the minimal policy counts: the counted episodes (a covered edge filled to the record edge, the filter-trim stretch pale; a counted 1:1 leg labeled leg) and, faint with a dashed outline, the candidates cand; no rejected run and no gray strip (mmr_combined.policy_marks, shade_policy_runs; the ids come from the analysis' PolicyResult, or from the stored verdict's counted_episode_ids/candidate_episode_ids when a standalone panel re-runs the analysis without the scans); (l) is titled (l) episodes, counted solid and the numbers count N accepted, M counted. A 1:1 circulation judged on one leg or a non-1:1 half-swing between passages (leaves G4c, G4h), the flag extend_time, the 1:1 profile floor and a turn read in the edge trim are said in the right column (reading the figures). The 1:1 coverage audit's longest uncovered stretch (aud_unc_t0_yr–aud_unc_t1_yr) is a hatched gray strip xx at the foot of (a), labeled bounded, not counted (audit) (mmr_combined.shade_audit; flag uncovered_bounded_run). One 1:1 episode in parts: (a) brackets its sub-regimes over the panel, named by their well (mmr_combined.draw_subregime_brackets, run_label_items; overlapping names merge, merge_label_items), and hatches its inferred residence beyond the fill lighter, --, labeled inferred (residence_pieces, shade_residences; never on (l)); (d) marks the kicks of \(a\) at such changes with ▼ kick (draw_kicks); the header reads orbit: A → B for a sequence of wells; the EPISODES group of the right column lists the inferred stay and the marks (well, amplitude, kick, no well for the cycles beyond its well-holding core, rule coorbital_well_core) under the episode. Where a slower libration of the center was found (the slow scale, columns slow_*), (i) hatches its intervals (slow #id, mmr_combined.slow_intervals) and the right column's SLOW SCALE group gives its numbers; when its cause is a secular cycle, (j) adds the detrended \(p\varpi\) labeled with \(p\) and the secular period of its column (mmr_combined.varpi_overlay). A kinematic libration's (j) is \(\sigma = \lambda\) part \(+ p\varpi\) on the scale of that swing (mmr_combined.kinematic_scale).

plotting.mmr_combined.draw_combined(analysis, series) draws the MMR figure from an analysis. After a restore without recomputation the analysis is run again on the saved series and checked against summary.csv; a difference is logged and stamped in red in the header.

A figure for a paper: plot_options={'combined': {'figure': 'panels'}} (or draw_combined(analysis, series, options=...), draw_long_period_combined(..., options=...)) draws the panels only: no header, legend or right column, and no empty slot (an (l) without an accepted episode and an undrawn FAIR are left out, with no warning line; the portraits that remain move left and are lettered on from (k); the secular/ZLK figure does the same with its four squares, from (i)). The margin legends right of the panels stay, so the caption explains the rest. The page is cropped to what is drawn (12.45 × 12.8 in); a red stamp is still printed. The portraits keep their square size, so a row with one portrait leaves the rest of the bottom row blank. From a run or a restored one, fig = sim.data_manager.mmr_combined_figure(body, resonance, sim, options={'combined': {'figure': 'panels'}}) returns the MMR figure without saving it (fig.stamp: the mismatch with summary.csv, or None).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
plot_options (or PLOT_OPTIONS in .env as JSON) is merged over the defaults. Unknown keys and invalid values raise an error.

option default meaning style screen standalone diagnostics only: screen (11 pt sans-serif, 150 dpi, a title) or paper (8 pt STIX serif, 300 dpi, no title; panels 88 mm, rows up to 180 mm). The width depends on the kind. The combined verdict figures keep their 24 × 13.5 in layout (taller when the right column needs it) and header in either style (MMR at 120 dpi; secular/ZLK saved at the style's dpi) raw line raw series next to filtered ones: line, markers, none series auto no effect (accepted for old configurations; no figure draws the standalone time series any more) recurrence.max_points None display decimation of the recurrence matrix; None = about 8 samples per cycle, within 700–2500 recurrence.exclude_samples 2 blank band around the diagonal, in decimated steps portrait.y rate the MMR portrait's y axis: rate (\(\dot\sigma\)) or axis (\(a - a_0\)) cycles.prominence None peak prominence in rad; None = 5 % of the range of \(\sigma\) within [0.005, 0.1] fair.max_step_fraction 0.25 the standalone fair figure warns (and still draws) when the output step exceeds this share of the orbit; panel (m) of the combined figure is not drawn above 1/4.2 of it combined.osculating_a full panel (d): full holds the osculating a in view, clipped fits the view to the filtered a, hidden also hides the osculating a beyond that view combined.numbers explained the right column: explained (the verdict in ten blocks: header with the status, level and action chip, subtitle, key facts, why, confidence pills, checks with their margins nested, evidence, caveats, numbers with the DECISIVE lines first, the footer of codes with the full tree's verdict) or all (every number of the decision) combined.figure full the page of the combined verdict figures (MMR, secular, ZLK): full (header, panels, legend, right column) or panels (for a paper: the panels and their margin legends only, see below)

docs.title: Redrawing after a run
docs.text:
Nothing needs to be integrated again. Restore the run, then draw in any style:

from resonances import SimulationSerializer, MMRPlotter  # noqa: E402
from resonances.plotting import SecularPlotter  # noqa: E402

sim = SimulationSerializer.restore('output/my_run/simulation.json')
body = sim.bodies[0]
plotter = MMRPlotter.from_body(body, body.mmrs[0], sim, options={'style': 'paper'})
plotter.plot('recurrence')  # recurrence, fair, portrait or cycles; the combined figure: plot_body below
plotter.save('recurrence.pdf').close()

secular = SecularPlotter.from_body(body, body.secular_resonances[0], sim)  # secular or ZLK rows: pass `sim`
secular.plot('portrait')
secular.save('portrait.png').close()

sim.config.plot, sim.config.plots = 'all', ['combined']
sim.data_manager.plot_body(body, sim)  # the verdict figures, from a re-run analysis

MMRPlotter.plot draws the standalone kinds only (recurrence, fair, portrait, cycles); the combined MMR figure is redrawn by sim.data_manager.plot_body(body, sim) or draw_combined(analysis, series). MMRPlotter.from_body(..., focus=(t0, t1)) restricts cycles, portrait and the recurrence scales to an interval in years. Only bodies that passed the save filter have series on disk. MMRDiagnostics(...) builds the same figures from plain arrays (times in years; axis_analysis, the a of the cycles, of the portrait with portrait.y='axis' and of its reference \(a_0\), defaults to the osculating axis). A backward integration is put in time order internally; the axes show the actual negative times.

docs.title: Secular figures
docs.text: SecularPlotter (resonances.plotting.secular_plots; kinds angle, rate, portrait, combined) draws the angle the classifier read (the reduced proper angle by default, see Secular resonances) next to the angle of the osculating elements. In the combined figure, panel (d) is the semi-major axis (osculating band, filtered at \(P_c\), min – max; for a body in a planet's co-orbital zone, by \(a\) alone, the planet's \(a_P\) dashed and the zone's edges \(\pm k\,r_H\) dotted, ZLK_COORBITAL_HILL_FACTOR \(k\); secular_plots.coorbital_planet_geometric, for drawing only). Panel (g) of a secular angle draws the analysis' own response fit (the element and \(\sigma_f\) at the decisive cutoff, the center's when the center scale decided), the one whose \(R^2\) it prints (how to read it). For a Lidov-Kozai angle panel (g) draws the drift of the free and the osculating \(\omega\) in turns with a legend, as the free_omega drift figure. The right column has the ten blocks of the MMR figure; a ZLK row's Evidence asks what holds \(\omega\) (the forced vector, the center's slow wave, the node lock, the e–i coupling; Free elements: beyond the gate), a secular row's names the period seen on the angle against the FREQUENCIES rows, or unidentified. The numbers of both types include \(a\) in ORBIT and a FREQUENCIES table: the body's rates, the planetary modes (g5, g6, s6 always) and the beats, each in ″/yr with its period (how to read it). An induced ZLK libration (attributed to a forced mode, or a center at a beat of the forced vector) gets one more time panel, (a′) under (a): \(\omega_f\) with the forced direction and the dominant mode against the node (how to read it); every other row keeps eight. A ZLK figure reads \(\omega\), \(i\), \(\Omega\) and the free elements in the plane ZLK_ANGLE_FRAME names (the invariable plane by default; the header says which, panel (f) is i (invariable)). Below the time panels four squares: (i) the osculating portrait, (j) \(\sigma_f\) against its rate (ZLK: the free eccentricity vector), (k) the Charlier portrait of \(\sigma\) and \(e\) filtered at the decisive cutoff (secular_plots.filtered_charlier, charlier_radius), (l) the same per episode of (a); the legend is in a band under them, so this page is 1.45 in taller than the MMR one (how to read it).

docs.title: Eccentricity vector
docs.text:
ecc_vector draws one figure per body (how to read it):

resonances.EccentricityVectorPlotter.from_body(body, resonance, sim).plot().save('kh.png')
resonances.EccentricityVectorPlotter.from_data(times, ecc, omega, body_name='463').plot().save('kh.png')

plot(limit=...) fixes the half-width, which is how the free-vector figure of Free elements is drawn on the scale of the osculating one.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: Three checks: a mean-motion resonance, a secular resonance and a Lidov-Kozai resonance. Each integrates the orbit of an asteroid with the planets, builds the resonant angle and gives it a verdict (How the status is determined).

docs.title: A mean-motion resonance
docs.text:
(463) Lola is in the three-body resonance 4J-2S-1, with the angle \(\sigma = 4\lambda_J - 2\lambda_S - \lambda - \varpi\) (Resonance matrices explain the notation).

import resonances

# (463) Lola in the three-body resonance 4J-2S-1 (4 lambda_J - 2 lambda_S - lambda + ...)
sim = resonances.check(463, '4J-2S-1', integration_years=2_000)  # a real verdict: integration_years=100_000, output_step=1.0
sim.run()

body = sim.bodies[0]
for key, verdict in body.librations.items():  # key: the full angle, 4J-2S-1+0+0-1
    print(key, verdict.status, verdict.angle_status, verdict.confidence, verdict.reason, verdict.action)
print(sim.config.save_path)  # summary.csv, the series and the figures are written here

check downloads the elements from NASA Horizons at today's date, integrates, analyses the angle and saves the results. The code above runs only 2 000 years, so the verdict is

4J-2S-1+0+0-1 uncertain insufficient_time  baseline_needed extend

The libration period of Lola is about 10 000 years: 2 000 years hold no full cycle, the status is uncertain, the reason baseline_needed, and the suggested action extend (verdict.extend_to_years says how long to integrate). With integration_years=100_000, output_step=1.0 the verdict is (from the Gallery run: 100 kyr, step 1 yr, SABA(10,6,4); not re-run by the script above)

status angle_status reason confidence action resonant libration dynamic_libration high none

The output step matters: without output_step the default step of a 100 kyr run is about 15.9 yr, longer than half of Lola's 3.7-yr orbit, so the record folds short periods: the flag short_period_aliased says so (Dry run).

The fields:

  • status: the answer, one of resonant, transient, near_separatrix, non_resonant, uncertain, invalid;
  • angle_status: what the angle does over the whole record (libration, episodic, circulation, ...);
  • reason and libration_origin: why (dynamic_libration: the angle librates and the semi-major axis follows it as the pendulum of this resonance requires);
  • confidence: how well the evidence supports the status (certain, high, medium, low);
  • action: what to do next (none, spot_check, review, extend, resample).

The overview defines every value. All of them are also in summary.csv:

summary = sim.data_manager.get_simulation_summary(sim.bodies)
print(summary[['name', 'resonance', 'status', 'angle_status', 'confidence', 'reason', 'action']])

docs.title: The figure
docs.text:
For every row selected by the plot mode (by default review: everything except a confident non_resonant angle that nothing bounds, such as a plain circulation; doubtful negatives are kept for review) a one-page figure is saved in <save_path>/combined/<confidence>/<status>/: the angle, the semi-major axis and the pendulum's energy in time on the left, and the verdict with every number behind it on the right. This is Lola over 100 000 years at a 1-year output step:

How to read the figures explains every panel; the Gallery shows one example of every status.

docs.title: A secular resonance
docs.text:
(1222) Tina is in the linear secular resonance \(\nu_6\), g-g6: the angle is \(\varpi - (g_6 t + \phi_6)\), the body's longitude of perihelion against the phase of the planetary secular mode \(g_6\) (by default the body's forced terms at the other planetary frequencies are removed first; Secular and Lidov-Kozai).

# (1222) Tina in the linear secular resonance nu6 (angle varpi - varpi of Saturn's mode g6)
sim = resonances.check(1222, 'g-g6', integration_years=5_000)  # 2-10 Myr for a real verdict
sim.run()
print(sim.bodies[0].statuses)  # {'g-g6': 'uncertain'} on this short run

Secular angles librate with periods of hundreds of thousands of years, so a real check needs 2–10 Myr (integration_years=2_000_000 or more); over 10 Myr Tina is resonant with certain confidence (Gallery). See Secular resonances.

docs.title: A Lidov-Kozai resonance
docs.text:
The Lidov-Kozai angle is the argument of perihelion \(\omega\). (3040) Kozai librates about 270°:

# (3040) Kozai: the Lidov-Kozai angle is the argument of perihelion omega
sim = resonances.check(3040, resonances.LidovKozaiResonance(), integration_years=5_000)  # 500 kyr for a real verdict
sim.run()
print(sim.bodies[0].statuses)  # {'LK': ...}

Over 500 000 years the verdict is resonant with certain confidence (Gallery). See Lidov-Kozai resonances.

docs.title: How to read the figures
docs.text: The package draws figures to help a person check a verdict by eye. This page explains every panel, line and mark, in plain words first; the formulas are in the folded "The math" blocks, with links to the pages that explain each quantity in depth. Nothing drawn on a figure changes a status: the verdict is decided before anything is drawn. The numbers in the right column are columns of the output files; a few annotations in the data panels (the \(R^2\) of each force window in (e)) are computed for the drawing and have no column of their own.

docs.title: Which figures there are
docs.text:
figure when it is drawn section the combined figure: one page per body and resonance, the verdict and its evidence by default (plots=['combined']) MMR, secular and Lidov-Kozai standalone figures: evolution, recurrence, fair, portrait, cycles, angle, rate, ecc_vector, cross_spectrum, free_omega, clones when listed in plots Standalone figures

Which rows get figures is set by the status filter plot (by default every row except a plain non-resonant one). The file names, folders and drawing options are on the Plots page. One combined figure for every status is in the Gallery.

docs.title: Shared conventions
docs.text:
These hold for the combined figures; most hold for the standalone ones too.

  • Black and gray. Gray is the osculating series, exactly as integrated; black is the same series with the short periods filtered out. When the samples are too dense to draw one by one, gray becomes a band between the smallest and the largest value.
  • One color per quantity. Red is the center of the angle and the line \(\dot\sigma = 0\); blue is a fitted or model quantity; dark gray marks references (turning points, jumps, \(h = 1\)); cyan is the catalog resonant semi-major axis. The full palette: Plots.
  • Time runs left to right in yr, kyr or Myr, whichever suits the span (below \(10^4\) yr: yr; below \(10^6\) yr: kyr). Time color bars use one color map (viridis without its palest yellow): dark is early, yellow-green late.
  • Angles folded into one turn are labeled from 0° to 360° (270°, not −90°). The unwrapped angle of MMR panels (a) and (i) is in radians; (j) shows offsets in degrees (its kinematic version: detrended terms, in degrees).
  • ▲ and ▼ at the edge of a panel mean "beyond the axis". The view holds 99 % of the osculating samples; the rare samples outside it are grouped in time, and each group is one small triangle at the time it goes furthest out (at most 8 per edge). A reference level outside the view (for example the resonant semi-major axis) is a triangle in the level's color.
  • The ends of the record. A filter spreads near the ends of a record, so the analysis does not read the first and last FILTER_EDGE_TRIM_CUTOFFS cutoff periods. In panels (c), (d), (e) of the MMR figure and (c), (f) of the secular figure, the filtered line is pale and dashed there; a filtered line that would leave the view there is a black triangle. The other panels draw their filtered lines solid to the ends: do not read them near the ends either.
  • No words in the panels. The panels hold only data and a few data numbers. What a line means is in the legend at the bottom of the figure; the values of the reference lines of (c), (d) and (h) are printed right of those panels.
The math: the filter and the cutoff

\(\sigma_f\) is \(\sigma\) passed forward and backward through a Butterworth low-pass filter of order FILTER_ORDER: a period \(P\) keeps a share \(G(P)\) of its amplitude, \(G(P_c) = \tfrac12\) at the cutoff \(P_c\) and \(G \to 1\) for \(P \gg P_c\). For a mean-motion resonance \(P_c\) is the larger of a multiple of the longest synodic period of the angle's planets and a share of the shortest libration the analysis allows. Details: the cutoff and the filter.

docs.title: The combined MMR figure
docs.text:
(1921) Pala in the 2:1 resonance with Jupiter, a textbook libration (Gallery). Click the image to open it at full size.

The page is 24 × 13.5 inches (taller when the right column needs it). The left half holds ten time panels (a)–(j) on one time axis and, below them, two phase portraits (k), (l), the FAIR plane (m) and the legend. The time axis is labeled under (j) and again under (b), so the times of the angle can be read without looking down the page. The right half explains the verdict. With plot_options={'combined': {'figure': 'panels'}} (a figure for a paper) only the left half is drawn, without the header and the legend, and the empty slots of the bottom row are left out (options).

docs.title: The header
docs.text:
The first line names the body, the resonance key, its type (mmr2, mmr3 or mmr2 retrograde) and the kind of orbit in the librating episodes (for example tadpole L4, horseshoe, interior asymmetric libration about 72°). For a non-resonant or uncertain verdict whose episodes come from somewhere else it reads episodes about X° (not this resonance). A row found as a subresonance adds subresonance of <parent>.

When another resonance or term makes the cycles, the second line names it by its role (roles):

  • owner: 5E-16+0+11 (librates in the episode): the owner librates and drives \(a\);
  • driver: 3N-5+0+2 (circulates, P 4.51 kyr): forced wave: the other angle circulates, its forced wave makes the cycles; candidate driver: X when the owner's measured regimes do not cover σ's deciding episode;
  • 6E-11+0+5 librates after the episode (13.7 kyr–17.9 kyr), outside it: a neighbor, a resonance the body is in before or after these episodes, not the cause (… during … but does not make σ's cycles inside them);
  • resonant argument: 9M-16+2+5 (one resonance 9M-16): the member of the multiplet that librates;
  • kinematic: −4ϖ term (2ω cycle, 18 kyr); a does not follow: σ's perihelion term makes the swing, at the secular period σ's period matched;
  • also in: 5J+6S-2+0+0-9 (both resonances at once): origin joint, the other resonance librates at the same time and keeps its own row (both resonances at once).

The next line describes the record: its span and direction, the integrator and its step, the output step and number of rows, the filter cutoff and what set it, the cutoff used for rates, the epoch, and whether the FAIR plane (m) could be drawn.

A red stamp in the top right corner, recomputed != summary, appears only when the figure had to run the analysis again (after a restore) and got a different answer from summary.csv.

docs.title: (a) The angle over the whole record
docs.text:
The resonant angle \(\sigma\), unwrapped: a circulation runs off upwards or downwards, a libration stays in a band.

(a) shows only what the status counts (the minimal policy):

  • gray: the osculating angle; black: the filtered angle \(\sigma_f\); red: its slowly moving center;
  • ▼ and ▲: the turning points of \(\sigma_f\) (a maximum, a minimum), marked only when there are at most 80;
  • solid colored fills labeled #1, #2, …: the counted episodes. A fill runs to a record edge the episode covers (the stretch the filter's trim hides, outside the analysis window, pale), else a quarter period beyond its first and last turning points. A hatched fill is an episode before the last jump of the semi-major axis (////); a fill hatched the other way (\\\\) is an episode another resonance induces (the header names it);
  • a fill labeled leg: a counted 1:1 leg (one clean leg of a co-orbital, half a cycle, no episode row);
  • a faint fill with a dashed outline labeled cand: a candidate the status did not count (an episode a measured veto rejected, as in a kinematic or induced row, the episodes of a parent row whose member librates, a leg or half-swing that is not counted), shown so the reader can judge it;
  • nothing else: rejected runs, runs below the period floor and runs the strength rejected are not drawn; episodes.csv lists them (columns counted, candidate, reject_reason) and (l) still shows the accepted ones;
  • a turning point inside the filter's pale edge of a 1:1 angle: a turn read on the orbit-averaged raw angle; it is added only when it closes a cycle (2006 BZ147, 960 yr);
  • dotted lines (or a hatched band with "N jumps of a"): jumps of the semi-major axis; a shaded half-cycle with "action step (G2a)": a sudden change of the libration's amplitude, treated like a jump;
  • 1:1 only, one episode in parts (one episode of a 1:1 angle): brackets just above the panel, one per sub-regime, named by its well (#0 horseshoe, tadpole L4; new amplitude: the same well after an amplitude change, the gap between two brackets is the transitional half-cycle); names that would overlap merge (#1 compound → quasi-satellite). A lighter fill hatched -- labeled inferred: the stay in the co-orbital region beyond the measured turning points (episodes.csv residence_*), up to the record's edge or a whole turn of the orbit-averaged angle. It is inferred, not measured: coverage, the edges and the status read only the turning points, and (l) does not draw it (2020 CB 1E-1: measured 443–601 yr, hatched from 601 yr to the end: 601 yr is no exit);
  • ×: where the analysis places the exit from the resonance. It may be only suspected: then the Caveats of the right column say so (flag exit_suspected, check_mmr_exit failed).

What to look for: fills that cover the whole record are a libration; fills in part of it are episodes; faint cand fills are librations the status does not count (the EPISODES group of the right column marks them).

The math: angle, turning points, episodes \[ \sigma = k\lambda + \sum_j k_j\lambda_j + p\varpi + \sum_j p_j\varpi_j + v\Omega + \sum_j v_j\Omega_j \]

(body without index, planets with index \(j\)). Turning points are the extrema of \(\sigma_f\) that stand out by at least a prominence set from the noise of \(\sigma_f\). Three alternating turning points close a cycle when the angle comes back by less than its swing (\(Q_i < 1\), cycles and their closure). An episode normally needs at least three turning points and one closed cycle; two opposite turning points also make one cycle when the angle and \(a\) come back to the same state on either side of them (closure by phase return, confidence at most medium). The center is \(\sigma_f\) smoothed again over a few libration periods. Details: turning points, runs and episodes, jumps and action steps.

docs.title: (b) The angle modulo 360°
docs.text:
The same angle folded into one turn, in a 360° window around the center: gray dots are the osculating samples, black is \(\sigma_f\), red the center (the lines are left out when the cycles are too dense to draw). An accepted owner resonance is drawn purple dashed, an accepted subresonance orange dash-dot.

A red boxed note ALIAS step … ≈ P_σ … means that the output step is close to a multiple of the angle's own fast period: the samples, like a stroboscope, make a fast circulation look slow (Gallery: alias).

The strip (b′). When the cycles are too dense to see in (b), a strip below it shows about five cycles from the middle of the deciding episode on their own time axis (in yr): ● the samples, a gray dashed line the path the analysis' unwrap assumes between them (a whole turn may pass between two samples), black \(\sigma_f\). A ▼ on the top edge of (b) marks the middle of the strip's time window; a second strip (b′2) shows the last regime after a jump, and the ▼s are then numbered. A ▼ never moves sideways: next to the panel letter or the ALIAS plaque it is raised just above it, and its number moves level with the ▼ or to its left.

The math: sampling

With the output step \(\Delta t\), a rate \(\nu\) is seen as \(\nu - 2\pi m/\Delta t\) for a whole number \(m\): the sampled angle cannot tell them apart. The analysis follows the angle sample to sample with a predicted rate, so a turn per step is still counted. Details: what the step can resolve, the predictive unwrap.

docs.title: (c) The rate of the angle
docs.text:
How fast \(\sigma\) moves, in units of the speed a pendulum has at the bottom of its well on the separatrix. A libration swings between positive and negative values and changes sign at every turning point; a clean circulation keeps one sign. Brief reversals do not rule out a circulation: what decides it is the center in (i), which completes a turn or keeps advancing over several. The axis is linear between −1 and +1 and logarithmic outside, so a slow libration and a fast circulation are both in view.

  • red line: \(\dot\sigma = 0\);
  • blue dashed: \(\pm 2\omega_0\) of each accepted episode, over its span, with the episode's own \(\omega_0\) (they need not sit at ±1, since the axis uses one reference); without an episode, a thin pair from the theoretical \(\omega_0\);
  • dotted: the rate the mean motion predicts in each regime between jumps;
  • ○ on the zero line: a slip, where the angle's midpoint steps by a full turn.

When no \(\omega_0\) is known at all, the panel shows \(\dot\sigma\) in rad/kyr on an ordinary axis.

The math: the separatrix speed

The black line is \(\dot\sigma / 2\omega_{0,\rm ref}\), with \(\dot\sigma\) taken at the rate cutoff \(\max(P_c, 0.1\,P_{\rm cyc})\). \(\omega_{0,\rm ref}\) is the deciding episode's \(\omega_0\), else the longest other accepted episode's, else the theoretical \(\omega_{0,\rm th} = \lvert k\rvert\, n\sqrt{3\mu_{\rm eff,th}}\), with \(\mu_{\rm eff,th}\) the resonance's effective strength (the three-body strength scale for a three-body angle; how strong must the resonance be). An episode's \(\omega_0\) comes from its cycles: a cycle of period \(P_i\) and amplitude \(A_i\) gives the small-amplitude period \(T_{0,i} = P_i / F(A_i)\) with

\[ F(A) = \frac{2}{\pi}\,\mathsf K\!\left(\sin^2\frac A2\right), \qquad \omega_0 = \frac{2\pi}{\operatorname{median} T_0}, \]

\(\mathsf K\) the complete elliptic integral of the first kind. For the cosine pendulum \(\dot\psi^2 = 4\omega_0^2(h - \sin^2\frac\psi2)\), so the separatrix (\(h = 1\)) passes the bottom at \(\dot\psi = \pm 2\omega_0\): ±1 on this axis. This is a cosine-equivalent scale: a well of another shape has its own separatrix speed \(\sqrt{2(E_{\rm sep} - V_{\min})}\), so ±1 bounds a libration exactly only for a cosine well. The dotted rate is \(\nu = \nu(\langle a\rangle) + k\,(\dot\lambda - n(\langle a\rangle))\) with \(\dot\lambda\) measured in the regime. Details: the pendulum.

docs.title: (d) The semi-major axis
docs.text:
Three levels of \(a\) in au: light gray the osculating \(a\), mid gray \(a\) filtered at the cutoff, black a slower version that shows the resonant swing when the filtered one is a dense band (when there is no slower version, the filtered \(a\) itself is black).

  • dotted: \(a_*\), where the angle would stand still; dashed cyan: \(a_{ m res}\), the value of the resonance catalog;
  • light blue band: \(a_* \pm \Delta a\), the half-width of the resonance measured from the episodes;
  • red dots: the mean of \(a\) over each cycle of \(\sigma_f\) (maximum to maximum), drawn when there are 2 to 200 maxima;
  • ▼ kick at the top edge (1:1): a jump of \(a\) at a change inside an episode that is no boundary, a change of well or of amplitude (episodes.csv marks, kick@t; the jump itself is the dotted line of (a)).

\(a_*\) and \(a_{ m res}\) are mean-motion values, while the curves are osculating. To compare like with like, both lines are moved by the difference between the mean osculating \(a\) and the \(a\) that the measured mean motion gives, separately in each regime between jumps. The margin to the right prints the unshifted values and the shift.

What to look for: in a libration \(a\) swings around \(a_*\) in step with \(\sigma\), inside the band.

The option combined.osculating_a (full, clipped, hidden) chooses how much of the osculating \(a\) stays in view (Plots).

The math: exact resonance and half-width

\(a_*\) solves \( u(a_*) = 0\), where \( u(a) = k\,n(a) + \sum_j k_j n_j + p\dot\varpi + \dots\) and \(n(a) = 2\pi a^{-3/2}\) (yr, au). The shift uses \(a(\dot\lambda) = (GM_\odot/\dot\lambda^2)^{1/3}\). The half-width is

\[ \Delta a = rac{2\omega_0}{\lvert c vert}, \qquad c = rac{\partial u}{\partial a} = - rac{3kn}{2a}, \]

the median over the accepted episodes, and a libration of amplitude \(A\) swings by \(\delta a = \Delta a\sin rac A2\). Like (c), \(\Delta a\) is the cosine-equivalent width. Details: the resonant angle and its rate, the pendulum.

docs.title: (e) The response of the semi-major axis
docs.text:
Black: the rate \(\dot a\) (scaled by the power of ten in the label). Blue: the force law fitted in short sliding windows, \(\dot a\) as a sine of the angle; the blue numbers along the bottom are each window's \(R^2\), written only when there are at most 12 windows (close numbers merge into a range such as 0.74–0.81). For each accepted episode a dotted line at its middle carries #id and the \(R^2\) of its two halves.

What to look for: when the resonance itself drives \(a\), \(\dot a\) follows the sine of \(\sigma\) and the \(R^2\) are high. A low \(R^2\) with a clear libration in (a) suggests that something else bounds the angle.

The blue curve is the law that decided (column rsp_force_law), on the series that law read:

  • single: each window's sine, evaluated on \(\sigma\) smoothed at the response cutoff; on an episode accepted in the frame of its moving well, on \(\psi = \sigma - c(t)\), as the fit read it;
  • multiplet: one curve, the multiplet law (its one fit over its windows, drawn over them), with multiplet law j = …: R² … (single …) at the top: the multiplet's \(R^2\) against the single sine's;
  • harmonic (several harmonics) or a 1:1 law: no blue curve; the panel prints that law's numbers (harmonic law N=k: R² … (single …));
  • direct_force (the direct averaged-force law): a thick black \(\dot a\) and, per window, a blue curve \(s\times\) the term's averaged force with the planet's real mass, both low-passed at the law's cutoff (\(f\,P_\text{large}\)), with direct law 8N-13+0+5 (Neptune's mass) at 3.07 kyr: R² 0.75, s 1.14–1.29 at the top. The single-sine windows are not drawn: they are the law that failed.

When the line rule raised the cutoff (a line of \(\dot a\) rivalled the force), the black \(\dot a\) and the angle are taken at that raised cutoff, and the panel prints cutoff … yr (line … yr) (columns rsp_response_cutoff_ep_yr, rsp_line_binding_yr). The law drawn is the one the status read: when a witness episode decided (rule R, column rsp_force_source = witness), its windows and law, on \(\sigma\) and \(\dot a\) smoothed at its own response cutoff (rsp_response_cutoff_ep_yr, which can differ from the record's); otherwise the fit pooled over the episodes.

The math: the force law

In each window of about 3.5 cycles,

\[ \dot a_f = R\sin(\sigma_f - \phi_0) + C, \qquad R^2 = 1 - \frac{SS_{\rm res}}{SS_{\rm tot}}, \]

fitted as a linear model in \(\sin\sigma_f\), \(\cos\sigma_f\) and 1. Lagrange's equation gives this law for a resonance with one dominant term. Details: the force law.

docs.title: (f), (g) Eccentricity and inclination
docs.text: Gray the osculating value, black the filtered value, \(i\) in degrees. The gray numbers in the top left corner are the smallest and largest filtered values in the analyzed window.

docs.title: (h) The energy of each cycle
docs.text:
One point per cycle of \(\sigma\): its energy \(h\) in the pendulum fitted to the angle, on a logarithmic axis. \(h = 0\) is the bottom of the well, \(h = 1\) the separatrix (dashed).

  • ● a libration cycle, ○ a revolution (a full turn);
  • light blue band: the separatrix zone, where trial orbits in the fitted potential may stay trapped or go over the top: a cycle there can cross the separatrix;
  • triangles at the bottom or top: \(h\) below \(10^{-3}\), or no top to the potential.

What to look for: a deep libration sits well below 1; points in or near the band mean the orbit is at the border of the resonance.

The math: energy and the separatrix zone

The potential \(V\) is fitted to \(\dot\sigma^2 = 2E - 2V(\sigma)\) cycle by cycle; each cycle's energy is

\[ h = \frac{E - V_{\min}}{V_{\max} - V_{\min}}, \qquad \text{for the cosine well } h = \frac{\dot\psi^2}{4\omega_0^2} + \sin^2\frac\psi2 . \]

The zone \([h_{\rm lo}, h_{\rm hi}]\) comes from trial orbits in the fitted potential. With two harmonics a well's own separatrix can lie below \(h = 1\). Details: energy and potential, the separatrix zone.

docs.title: (i) The center of the angle
docs.text:
Gray: \(\sigma_f\) in the analyzed window; red: its center, \(\sigma_f\) smoothed over a few libration periods; large red ▼▲: turns of the center; light red shading: the center's longest one-way run, drawn only when it reaches a full turn. Red vertical hatching labeled slow #id (or slow): the intervals of the slow scale, a slower libration of the center stored apart from the main one (its period, cycles and cause are the slow_* columns and the SLOW SCALE group of the right column); nothing is hatched without a slow swing.

What to look for: a center that runs a full turn one way is a circulation, however the angle swings around it.

The math: the center

\(\sigma_c = \mathrm{lowpass}_{W_c}(\sigma_f)\) with \(W_c = 3P_{\rm cyc}\) (LIBRATION_CENTRE_CYCLES), and the center's turns are found with a larger prominence than those of \(\sigma_f\). Details: the center and circulation.

docs.title: (j) The centers of related angles
docs.text:
Each line is the center of an angle minus its mean, in degrees, with its key at the right end: red the catalog angle, pale colors other members of its multiplet (the same commensurability with other perihelion terms), orange an accepted subresonance, purple dashed the owner resonance.

What to look for: a flat line is the angle that librates. If the catalog angle wanders while a member's line is flat, the libration belongs to that member.

When the slow scale's cause is a secular cycle (slow_cause 2ω or \(g - g_j\), at any level), the panel adds \(p\varpi\) of that scale, detrended, orange dashed, labeled with \(p\) and the secular period from its column (−9ϖ 7.11 kyr): the line that would explain the slow swing of the red center.

For a kinematic libration (or a non-resonant row whose slow scale is a secular cycle) the panel shows instead \(\sigma = (\lambda\ \text{part}) + p\varpi\) on the scale of that swing, in degrees, each term with its straight-line trend removed: red \(\sigma\), orange dashed \(p\varpi\) with its secular period (−4ϖ 18 kyr), gray dotted the \(\lambda\) part. The scale is the deciding episode at its response cutoff (285637: the 18-kyr cycle at 1.8 kyr), or the slow scale, detrended over each slow episode (37087: 506 yr). When \(\sigma\) follows \(p\varpi\) and the \(\lambda\) part stays flat, the perihelion's own precession bounds the angle, not the resonance; compare the swings, not the mean rates.

The math: the members' centers

A member \(\sigma_s\) differs from the catalog angle \(\sigma_0\) by perihelion terms, \(\Delta_s = \sigma_s - \sigma_0\), computed from the smoothed \(\varpi\) of the body and the planets; its center is drawn as \(c_s = c_0 + \mathrm{smooth}_{W_c}(\Delta_s)\). Details: subresonances, another resonance owns the oscillation, kinematic origins.

docs.title: (k), (l) Phase portraits
docs.text:
(k) is the whole record, (l) the accepted episodes (title (l) episodes, counted solid: the five longest, the counted ones first, each in its episode color, up to 12 cycles each, a dot at its first sample). A counted episode is solid; an accepted run the status does not count is dashed and labeled #3 cand (a candidate, faint in (a)), #3 not counted, or by what it is: #3 wave, #3 forced (strength), #3 ripple. #2 induced is an episode another resonance induces. (l) draws each episode over the same interval as its fill in (a), cut to the window of (k): solid between its first and last turning point, dashed beyond them. An episode that covers the whole record is the whole window, so its (l) holds the same samples as (k). Both show \(\sigma_f\) (modulo 360°) against \(\dot\sigma\) in rad/kyr, with the same scales; color is time in (k). Red line: \(\dot\sigma = 0\); red +: the center of each accepted episode.

What to look for: a libration draws closed loops around the +; a circulation draws a band across the whole width. A frame crossed out says why the samples cannot be drawn (an aliased step). When (k) is much wider than the episodes, it uses the episodes' view and marks the clipped part with ▲▼.

docs.title: (m) The FAIR plane
docs.text:
The mean anomaly \(M\) against the longitude difference to the planet, colored by time (Forgács-Dajka, Sándor & Érdi 2018). A libration draws slanted bands with empty gaps between them, since the body avoids some phases relative to the planet; a circulation fills the square over time. It is drawn only for a prograde two-body angle, with the planet's longitudes saved and an output step of at most 1/4.2 of the orbital period. Otherwise there is no (m) frame: the header says FAIR no (reason), the legend takes the slot, and one orange line at its top gives the reason in words, e.g. FAIR not drawn: planet longitudes not saved (SAVE_PLANETS); for a 1:1 FAIR = (M, σ) repeats (b) (for a 1:1, \(q = 0\): the plane would only show the range of σ again).

The math: FAIR coordinates

\(x = M \bmod 360°\), \(y = (\lambda_P - \lambda) \bmod 360°\) for a body inside the planet's orbit and \((\lambda - \lambda_P) \bmod 360°\) for one outside.

docs.title: The right column
docs.text:
The right column states the verdict in ten blocks. The blocks come in the same order and the same place on every figure: MMR, co-orbital, secular and Lidov-Kozai. The left half of the column holds the header, subtitle, key facts, Why, Confidence and Checks; the right half always starts with Evidence, then Caveats, Numbers and the footer, so that figures leafed through in a batch show each block at one place. Read it top down like a short report: the verdict, what is seen, why, how firm, then the checks, the evidence and the numbers. Every number is a column of the output files or a ledger value. Codes (rule IDs, column and flag names) appear only as small gray tags and in the footer.

Icons and colors. One set of icons serves the checks, the pills and the evidence. The color says how closely to look, not whether the row is for or against the resonance.

icon meaning ✓ (green) clean: passed, or the input is in its best state ⚠ (amber) marginal: passed near its threshold, or the input that holds the level ✗ (red) failed: a measured objection ? (gray) not measured (a gap) – (light gray) not needed, not applicable, or shown for reading only ◆ (status color) the one step that set the status

The status colors are the same in the plaque, on ◆, on the status words in the text and on the clone figures: resonant green, transient orange, near_separatrix purple, non_resonant gray, uncertain blue, invalid red (style.STATUS_COLOURS). Gray monospaced numbers in parentheses back the statement before them. Gray letters in parentheses, such as (a, b), name the panels that show it.

  1. Header. The status word on a plaque in the status color, then the level as four dots (●●●○ high; no level for uncertain and invalid), then one action chip. The chip takes one of five forms:

    • no action needed (gray);
    • glance at (b), (i) (amber, action spot_check): the panels of the inputs that hold the level (the map is below);
    • review figure + numbers (red);
    • extend to 200 kyr (blue), always with the length (extend_to_years);
    • resample to 0.5 yr (blue), with the step (resample_step_yr).

    The action appears only in the chip; the text never repeats it.

  2. Subtitle. The resonance and the subtype in words, for example its own libration over the whole record, induced: borrowed from 5E−16+0+11, kinematic (forced) libration of the background or too short to decide: slow swing in the well. Under it, in gray, come the type (two-body, Jupiter 2:1 (period ratio 1:2), order 1: the ratio of mean motions n : n_planet, then the period ratio, which the outer-belt literature uses; three-body Mars–Jupiter, order 1) and the step that decided (decided at step 6 (behavior)). When a check showed the angle's own force, the line also names it (own force shown by the potential).

  3. Key facts. Five to seven label value lines:

    • σ: the share of the record it librates, its episodes, how it ends and the angle word;
    • the libration: period, median and largest half-amplitude, and center;
    • the episodes, when there are several, with ◆ on the deciding one (#1 61.3–99 kyr P 8.62 kyr A 92.4° (139°) ◆);
    • the driver of an induced row, otherwise the resonance (a_res, mean a, order);
    • the orbit: the e and i ranges, q_min and Q_max;
    • the radial overlaps with the eight planets' bands. An overlap is needed for an encounter but is not enough for one;
    • the run: span, output step and cutoff.

  4. Why. Three to five plain sentences in a fixed order:

    1. what is seen, with panel letters;
    2. what it means: whose force makes the cycles, or why they are not this resonance's own;
    3. what was ruled out. Only measured tests count here;
    4. what holds the level.

    The package's terms keep plain glosses:

    • induced: borrowed from X, where X is the owner;
    • kinematic (forced) libration: σ is bounded by X, not by this resonance's force;
    • overruled by X: a veto.

    A forced-wave veto says that σ circulates and that its short runs are the background's forced wave (2012 KL9). The last sentence says what limits the level (The confidence stops at high: …), or Nothing limits the confidence. When the code computed one, a last line follows: Needed: … for an uncertain or invalid row, else Would change the verdict: …, Next check: … (an extension that tests, with no promise) or A longer record cannot make it resonant: …. For 79653 3M+3J-7, σ circulates during 32.5–61.3 kyr, so the row stays transient.

  5. Confidence. Confidence: high — not certain because … names the inputs that hold the level. Then comes one pill per input of the level, as the minimal policy read it (column pol_level_inputs):

    • ✓: the input is in its best state (4.12 cycles counted (…; ≥ 3 allows certain), alternatives ruled out, own force shown (potential));
    • –: the input is limited, but another input holds the level lower. The pill says where the input alone would cap the level (… — alone it would cap the level at high);
    • ⚠: the input holds the level (filter-sensitive, close to the separatrix, overruled by the kinematic bound (by a thin margin));
    • ?: the input is not measured, and that holds the level (separatrix margin not measured);
    • ✗: a measured objection the level reads, named by its check (objection: σ̇ does not follow a (identity fails), column pol_objection_check).

    N, the cycles counted, is (turning points − 1)/2 of the deciding episode plus its covered edges in periods; the core pill counts the same episode without the edges. A bar says which level it opens (high needs ≥ 2). The former caps that the level still reads are pills too: a second capture not ruled out, a candidate episode, a thin veto, the filter, a gate without a verdict. An uncertain or invalid row reads Confidence: no level —, then what is missing, each item a ? pill.

  6. Checks. The steps of the status tree as questions. Each step has a short answer, gray numbers and a small gray rule ID (names). Q · Can the data show it? comes first: the output step, the filter, aliasing and the record length. The tree's steps follow:

    • 0 · Does σ librate?;
    • 1 · Does a sibling angle hold the center?;
    • 2 · Does another resonance drive a?;
    • 3 · Does a (semi-major axis) swing with σ?;
    • 4 · Does the center drift without a cause?;
    • 5 · Is it σ's own force?;
    • 6 · How does σ behave?.

    A circulation leaf (C, C5, G4c, G4h) is step C. Each margin hangs under the step it belongs to:

    step Q 0 1 2 3 5 6 margins L8, C5 N, C1–C4, L1, L6, L7 S W L3, K1, K1e, B5 L4, R0, F, L5, O1 L2, Z

    A sub-check whose printed comparison fails is named by what was measured (center moves (shift/amplitude 5.77 > 0.5), the output step is too coarse for σ), never by the passing condition; Q then answers Partly: (⚠) or No: (✗) with those words. The deciding step carries ◆. Any other step shows its worst sub-check (✗, then ?, then ⚠; a ✗ that the step's answer does not read is named in it, …; but dσ/dt ≠ c (a − a*) (below)); ✓ means it was answered cleanly, ? that it did not run (a gap), – that it was not needed or does not apply. The steps after the deciding one collapse into one quiet line (3–6 · a swings · drift · own force · behavior — not reached). The margins measured anyway hang under that line.

    When the minimal policy, not the tree, set the status (pol_decided_by other than tree), the ◆ moves to a last line, for example P · Is it the background's forced wave? Yes → NON-RESONANT. The tree's leaf then reads overruled: the policy decides at step P and shows its own result: ✗ when a check it read fails (or the policy did not uphold its veto), ? when neither the force law nor the potential was measured.

    The three-body strength from the scale μ_i μ_j e^q is a gray – line: scale only (×39.5; an objection only from ×10³ after small divisors). The level does not read it.

  7. Evidence. The physics, one row per test (icon, short label, value), in two groups:

    • is this X's own pendulum?: the period, strength and width in a that the cycles need, against what the averaged potential gives (on a co-orbital, the 1:1 force law);
    • what makes the cycles?: the owner search and its best candidate, the identity σ = φ/u + Ψ/u of an induced row, a forced wave, and both resonances at once?. That last row asks whether σ is held by its own term too while the owner pins φ. Its answers are excluded, not ruled out or both resonances at once.

  8. Caveats. The sentences a reader must know before using the verdict. They come from the flags through one table (verdict_vocab.FLAG_CAVEATS: a flag, the statuses it is said on, its sentence). Examples: episodes_in_separatrix_zone on a transient row, exit_suspected, last_regime_after_jump, a_short_period_scatter and strength_scale_only. A failed check that the level does not read is said here, with its numbers and the reason it is not read (79653: the three-body strength scale). A flag that is an input of the level is a pill, not a caveat. A diagnostic flag goes only to the footer. The block reads none when there is nothing to say.

  9. Numbers. The block opens with the framed DECISIVE lines: the comparisons of the rule that set the status, with its ID (energy fits the potential [R0]: …). The lines also say in words which tests limited the level, conflicted with the verdict or were not measured (not measured: a obeys the force law [L4]: …). Fixed groups follow, labeled in words with units:

    • EPISODES: ◆ marks the deciding episode; accepted runs the status does not count say not counted; ✗ marks the rejected runs, with their reason;
    • LIBRATION;
    • RESPONSE OF a;
    • PENDULUM, ENERGY;
    • RESONANCE;
    • ORBIT (min / med / max);
    • REFERENCE PERIODS: synodic, orbital, secular and great-inequality periods, to name a period seen on σ;
    • KINEMATICS;
    • SLOW SCALE;
    • SUBRESONANCES, DRIVER;
    • STEP, FILTER.

    The secular and Lidov-Kozai columns keep this order with their own groups (LIBRATION, the gate or the response, ORBIT, FREQUENCIES where the MMR column has REFERENCE PERIODS, STEP, FILTER last).

    A number is printed wherever it is needed; there are no pointers to other blocks. A gray (not used) number belongs to a test skipped by design. The pendulum labels name the source of each number:

    • observed cycle period P is measured on σ;
    • small-swing period T0 (from observed cycles) is inferred from those cycles (T0 = P/F(A); never a theory), and so are the well's half-width and μ_eff;
    • cycle energy h is normalized to the fitted potential.

  10. Record (the footer). The raw codes, small and gray, in this order:

    • the status code;
    • the leaf and the angle rule (leaf G6 · angle rule G5w);
    • reason, origin, origin detail and veto;
    • the policy step that decided (decided by tree);
    • the flags;
    • the settings hash;
    • the docs pages.

The panels of the glance at chip come from one map, from the input that holds the level to its panels (verdict_vocab.GLANCE_PANELS). The chip names at most three letters, in panel order. A ZLK co-orbital of a planet whose modes the free elements do not fit (gate detail coorbital_unfitted_forcing) points V at (a), (d) instead: its free ω and free e vector are no measurement.

input that holds the level MMR panels secular/ZLK panels N (cycles), core (own cycles of the deciding episode) (a), (l) (a) M (separatrix margin) (h) (h) S (filter stability) (b), (i) (b), (h) V (objections, alternatives) (e), (j) (g), (j) F (own force) (e), (h) — veto (j) (g), (j) thin veto (j) (g) second capture (j) — candidate episode (a) (a) circulation (b), (i) (b), (h) table (a level the rule fixes) (j) (a) status (near_separatrix) (h) (h)

When the column is long, the figure grows downward by up to COLUMN_MAX_GROWTH_IN (6 in) over its 13.5 in, and the left panels keep their place at the top. Past that limit the column trims in this order:

  1. the Numbers groups, from the last (DECISIVE and ORBIT stay);
  2. the ✓ sub-checks of each step, into one line;
  3. Evidence, to one line per row.

Nothing else is dropped. The text export is always complete. verdict_column_mmr.figure_column(analysis, rows, settings) returns the column the figure draws; for secular and Lidov-Kozai rows it is verdict_column_long.figure_column(analysis, row, free_elements, settings). verdict_column.column_text(column) writes that column as text, block by block.

With plot_options={'combined': {'numbers': 'all'}} the right column lists every number of the decision in blocks instead of the ten blocks.

docs.title: Co-orbital (1:1) figures
docs.text:
2002 AA29, an Earth co-orbital: horseshoe, a compound orbit, horseshoe again (Gallery).

The figure is the same, with these differences:

  • the header names the regime (tadpole L4, horseshoe, quasi-satellite, compound (horseshoe ↔ quasi-satellite)), or for one episode in several wells orbit: …, the wells of its sub-regimes in time order (orbit: horseshoe → tadpole L4, 2016 JA; more than four are shortened with … and their count; summary geo_orbit_type_sequence);
  • (a) holds a hatched gray strip at its foot labeled bounded, not counted (audit) where the coverage audit found a bounded run of the orbit-averaged angle that no counted episode covers (flag uncovered_bounded_run, columns aud_unc_*; the row is in the review queue, its status unchanged);
  • (a) brackets the sub-regimes and hatches the inferred residence, and (d) marks the kicks of \(a\) (above). The EPISODES group of the right column lists the stay under the episode (stay start–end (inferred)) and the marks (well 339 yr, amplitude 326–446 yr, kick 4.69 kyr; no well 856–929 yr for the cycles of an episode beyond its well-holding core, rule coorbital_well_core: 2024 JR16 clones);
  • (e) draws no sine windows: a co-orbital is judged by its own force law, and the panel prints its \(R^2\) (with the two halves) and \(K/K_{\rm th}\), the fitted strength over the planet's (1 means the planet's own mass);
  • in the right column, Evidence names the 1:1 force law, what makes the cycles? is left out, and step 2 says that the owner search does not apply to a 1:1 angle;
  • the Confidence pill of the separatrix margin (M) reads the separatrix zone of the counted episode, not the L2 row, because a horseshoe's half-amplitude near 180° is its topology. So the pill can read clear of the separatrix while L2 shows ? (2002 AA29);
  • FAIR is drawn when the output step allows it.
The math: the co-orbital force law \[ \dot a = 2\mu n a\,\tilde F(\theta), \qquad \dot a_{\rm data} = K\,\dot a_{\rm model} + C, \]

with \(\tilde F\) from the averaged direct and indirect potential of the planet. Details: co-orbital force law, co-orbitals.

docs.title: The secular and Lidov-Kozai figure
docs.text:
(1222) Tina in the ν6 secular resonance (Gallery).

The page and the right column follow the MMR figure, but the time panels are fewer and their letters differ ((d) is \(a\), before \(e\)). The header gives the span, step, number of rows, the cutoff \(P_c\) and what set it, and the scale the verdict rests on (fine, or center when the slower center scale decided). A Lidov-Kozai figure adds the plane \(\omega\), \(i\) and \(\Omega\) are measured from (ω, i, Ω from the invariable plane, ZLK_ANGLE_FRAME): (a), (a′), (f) (labeled i (invariable)), (g) and (i)–(l) all read that frame, the free elements included. Below the time panels are four squares, (i)–(l), and under them the legend in two columns (the page is 1.45 in taller than the MMR one; the paper figure has no legend, leaves an empty square out and letters the rest on from (i)).

panel what it shows (a) \(\sigma\) in degrees: gray the angle the classifier reads (the reduced proper angle by default), black the angle filtered at the scale the verdict rests on, a thin gray line the angle at \(P_c\) when the center scale decided, red the center, ▼▲ turning points, fills the counted episodes, faint dashed cand the candidates, other runs not drawn (as in MMR (a)) (a′) Lidov-Kozai, an induced libration only (attributed to a forced mode, or a center whose slow line is a beat of the forced vector): \(\omega_f\) with the forced direction against the node and the dominant mode against the node (below); other rows have no (a′) and keep the eight panels in place (b) \(\sigma\) modulo 360° around the center: gray dots and black \(\sigma_f\) (c) \({\rm d}\sigma_f/{\rm d}t\), in ″/yr for a secular angle and °/kyr for Lidov-Kozai; red line at 0 (d) \(a\) (au): gray osculating, black filtered at \(P_c\), with min – max; when the median \(a\) lies in a planet's co-orbital zone, \(\lvert\langle a\rangle/a_P - 1\rvert < k\,(m_P/3M_\odot)^{1/3}\) (ZLK_COORBITAL_HILL_FACTOR \(k\)), the planet's \(a_P\) dashed and the zone's edges dotted, named top right (for drawing only: a Jupiter Trojan gets the lines too) (e), (f) \(e\) and \(i\) (degrees): gray osculating, black filtered at \(P_c\), with min – max (g) secular: the rate of the element the angle contains against a sine of \(\sigma_f\) (below); Lidov-Kozai: the drift of the free and the osculating \(\omega\) in turns (below) (h) the center of \(\sigma_f\), its turns, and its longest one-way run when it reaches a full turn (as MMR (i)) (i) the portrait \((e\cos\sigma, e\sin\sigma)\) of the unfiltered angle and \(e\), or \((\sin\frac i2\cos\sigma, \sin\frac i2\sin\sigma)\) for an angle of \(\Omega\) alone; color: time; red + at the origin (j) secular: \(\sigma_f\) against \({\rm d}\sigma_f/{\rm d}t\); Lidov-Kozai: the free eccentricity vector, or \(\sigma_f\) against its rate when the free elements were not built (the axis labels say which) (k) the Charlier portrait \((R\cos\sigma_f, R\sin\sigma_f)\): \(\sigma\) and \(e\) filtered at the cutoff the verdict rests on (\(P_c\), or the center scale's), inside the filter's window, \(R = \sqrt{2(1-\sqrt{1-e_f^2})}\); for an angle of \(\Omega\) alone \(R = \sqrt{2\sqrt{1-e_f^2}\,(1-\cos i_f)}\) (labeled R(e, i)); color: time; red + at the origin (l) the same over each episode of (a) (the counted ones and the candidates under the minimal policy), in its color of (a): ○ its start, solid between its first and last turning point, dashed beyond them and for a candidate; at most the five longest

What to look for: in (a) a libration needs at least three turning points, one full cycle (LIBRATION_MIN_TURNING_POINTS); a drift is a ramp of less than a turn; a single U is half a cycle; circulation is a ramp of several turns. In (i) a libration draws loops around the resonance center: a ring off the origin, or a crescent when the libration is wide and the center close to the origin. A ring around the origin is circulation. (i) mixes every regime of the record and every short wave of \(e\); (k) shows the same plane without the waves the filter removes (Carruba, Aljbaae & Winter 2016, Fig. 3B), and (l) one episode at a time: an episode whose curve goes round the origin is not a libration of this angle. \(R\) is the momentum conjugate to the angle in units of \(\sqrt{L}\), \(R \approx e\) (or \(2\sin\frac i2\)) for small \(e\) and \(i\). These panels change no status.

(g) for a secular angle. Black is \(\dot e_f\) for an angle with \(\varpi\), or \({\rm d}\sin(i_f/2)/{\rm d}t\) for an angle of \(\Omega\) alone (both, \(i\) dashed on a right axis, when the angle has both); blue is the fit \(A\sin\sigma_f + B\cos\sigma_f + C\), with its \(R^2\) written in blue. That \(R^2\) is a column of the output and changes no status. Black, blue and \(R^2\) are one fit, the analysis' own: the element and \(\sigma_f\) filtered at the decisive cutoff, on its window. When the center scale decided (header scale center) that cutoff is the center's, longer than the \(P_c\) of (e) and (f), and the panel says at the center scale … kyr after the \(R^2\).

(g) for Lidov-Kozai. The drift of \(\omega\) from its first value, in turns (as the standalone free-ω drift figure), with a legend: gray the osculating \(\omega\), blue the free \(\omega\) with the forced terms of the planets removed; the free \(\omega\)'s net turns are written top right (the panel says free elements not built when there are none).
