A free \(\omega\) that winds through full turns while the osculating one stays near zero points to a kinematic libration: the planets' forcing holds \(\omega\), not the Lidov-Kozai mechanism (591986: 83 turns; Gallery: kinematic); one that stays within a fraction of a turn supports Lidov-Kozai. The picture is not the verdict: the right column states the free-ω gate's outcome (confirmed, kinematic or no verdict) with \(T/P_{\rm cyc}\), the cycles of the osculating \(\omega\) in the record, and the minimum needed. Too short a record, an undefined phase, a planetary frequency left in the free elements or a co-orbital of Mercury to Mars give no verdict, and an angle that does not librate throughout is demoted only under the extra condition \(\rho_{\max} < 1\) (the free-ω gate). Without a verdict the angle's shape decides (flag gate_unavailable) at most at medium, unless the forced terms are small and the \(e\)–\(i\) integral holds in the deciding episode (flag kinematic_excluded: 1981 Midas is certain).

(a′) for an induced Lidov-Kozai libration. Gray \(\omega_f\); orange \(\arg z_{\rm forced}(t) - \Omega(t)\), the direction of the fitted forced eccentricity vector against the node: the point the free circle turns about, so \(\omega_f\) oscillates around it with the free–forced beat (\(P_{\rm cyc}\), written bottom right), and it carries the beat of the forced modes (the legend names the two largest \(|c_j|\) and their beat: 591986, g5 + g6, 54 kyr); purple dashed \(\varpi_j - \Omega\), the longitude of the dominant mode against the node, with the node lock when there is one (591986 over 4 Myr: locked to g5, 50–130°, a slow wave of 1.4 Myr) or the rate \(\dot\Omega - g_j\). A libration of \(\omega\) that follows the orange curve is the forcing's, not the Lidov-Kozai mechanism's. When the curves leave a turn (624 Hektor: \(\omega\) circulates between its episodes, the center \(\varpi_5 - \Omega\) turns with the node) the panel is drawn modulo 360° about the forced direction, and \(\omega_f\) only inside the librating episodes.

The right column has the ten blocks of the MMR figure (the right column), with these differences:

  • Subtitle and Key facts. They name the angle, its period and amplitude, and, for Lidov-Kozai, the free ω (g − s) with its net turns in the record and the forcing mode (|c|, e_free/|c|). The orbit line gives i in the invariable plane. The run line names what set the cutoff. A secular row does not name an origin, because no force test exists there by construction. A Lidov-Kozai row says it in gate words: confirmed, no verdict, or the free ω winds.

  • Checks. The steps are:

    • Q · Can the data show it?: the filter guard (SZ.F). An unphysical orbit is decided here (INVALID, e reaches 2.11 > 1: 2010 HY22);
    • 0 · Does σ (ω) librate?: the turning points (SZ.N), a stationary center (SZ.S), a circulating center (SZ.P) and a center that turned back (G5s);
    • secular step 1, Does its center librate at the slower center scale?;
    • secular step 2, Is the swing larger than the error of the mode phases? (G5p): the swing against the uncertainty of the linear mode phases;
    • Lidov-Kozai step 1, Does the free ω librate too?: the free-ω gate (SZ.G), with its cycles, the free e against the forced e, the forcing's beat, a node not yet separated from s_j, and a co-orbital the free elements cannot fit;
    • Lidov-Kozai step 2, Do e and i trade as a ZLK cycle in the deciding episode?. It carries ◆ when the veto zlk_integral decided;
    • P · Is the record long enough? when the policy decided a record too short for one cycle (pol_decided_by insufficient_time): No, but σ_f ends in circulation → NON-RESONANT, with the range σ_f spans to the end in turns. Below 1 + CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND turns it adds at most medium (pill ends in circulation by a thin margin of one turn). Step 0 keeps its Not yet and adds the policy decides at step P.

    The gate decides only when it gives a verdict, confirmed or kinematic. Without one, the shape decides, at most at medium (a pill, flag gate_unavailable), unless the forced terms are small and the e–i integral holds in the deciding episode (flag kinematic_excluded: 1981 Midas is certain). The margins N, S, F, P and G (secular and Lidov-Kozai margins) hang under their steps.

  • Evidence. A Lidov-Kozai row asks what holds ω?. Its rows are:

    • the forced vector and its mode cluster;
    • the center's slow wave (591986: 53.8 kyr, the g6 − g5 beat);
    • the node lock;
    • the e–i coupling over the record (zlk antiphase at the constant-H amplitude, or forced beat; coupling is not libration).

    A secular row asks what makes the cycles?. It answers with the period seen on the angle, matched against the FREQUENCIES rows within the resolution 1/T (≈ g − g5, or unidentified with the nearest row), the mean rate of σ and the center's wave. What these mean: Free elements: beyond the gate.

  • Caveats. The flag table of the MMR figure, plus the long-period sentences:

    • a libration that rests on three turning points;
    • a gate that needs a longer record;
    • only one independent center estimate;
    • a failed e–i exchange that the level does not read;
    • a forcing fitted as a cluster of modes.

    The secular e-response check (\(e\) or \(\sin(i/2)\) against the angle, panel (g)) is not a caveat. Until its role is decided, it appears only in Numbers and in the footer.

  • Numbers. The groups are, in the MMR column's order:

    • LIBRATION OF σ (or ω), for the deciding episode;
    • FREE-ω GATE (Lidov-Kozai): the outcome, the cycles of ω (T/P_cyc) against those needed, the period read, ρ_max, and the e–i coupling over the record and in the deciding episode;
    • RESPONSE OF e AND i (secular): a column that no status reads;
    • ORBIT (min / med / max), with a in au;
    • FREQUENCIES (below);
    • STEP, FILTER: span, step, \(P_c\), scale, and what set the cutoff.

The FREQUENCIES table lists rates in ″/yr with their periods \(1\,296\,000''/|f|\) (the time a rate needs for a full turn). Use it to name the periods seen on \(\sigma(t)\):

  • secular: the body's \(g\) and \(s\) (the mean rates of its free vectors), \(\sigma\)'s rate from them and the modes, the modes g5, g6, s6 and those of the angle (in σ −1: the mode and its coefficient), and for an angle of two or more modes the forced waves \(g - g_j\), \(s - s_k\) (2306 \(g-g_6+s-s_6\): 43.9 and 43.6 kyr);
  • Lidov-Kozai: the free rates \(g\), \(s\) and \(g - s\) (the free \(\omega\)), every fitted forced mode with its amplitude \(|c_j|\) (◀ the mode that holds \(\varpi\)), the beats \(g - g_j\) of the two largest forced modes (kinematic: the cycle of a kinematic \(\omega\)), their mutual beat (beat: the slow wave of the forced vector) and, when flagged, the node lock \(\Omega - \varpi_j\) with its period and range. 591986 over 4 Myr: g5 304 kyr |c| 0.045 ◀, \(g - g_5\) 6.11 kyr kinematic, g6 − g5 54 kyr beat, \(\Omega - \varpi_5\) lock 1.4 Myr 50–130°.

The planetary rates are the package's constants (PLANETARY_FREQUENCIES), the body's are measured on the record: their precision is about one turn over the record, \(1\,296\,000''/T\).

The math: the secular angle and the free ω

A secular angle combines the body's proper longitudes of perihelion and node with the planets' mode phases, \(\sigma = p\varpi + q\Omega + \sum_j(p_j\ell_{g_j} + q_j\ell_{s_j})\), on the body's vectors with the forced terms at the other planetary frequencies removed (the secular angle). The cutoff is the largest of the great-inequality term, the forced waves near the angle's frequency and half the shortest libration allowed (secular signal).

For Lidov-Kozai, \(z_e = e\,e^{i\varpi}\) and \(z_i = \sin\frac i2\,e^{i\Omega}\) are split into forced parts (fitted at the planets' frequencies) and free parts, and \(\omega_{\rm free} = \varpi_{\rm free} - \Omega_{\rm free}\) (what is computed, the gate, why a bounded ω is not enough).

docs.title: Standalone figures
docs.text: Each kind below is drawn when it is listed in plots. The examples are drawn by the package from the saved benchmark series.

docs.title: evolution
docs.text: Stacked panels (preset PLOT_CONFIG, full by default): the angle as integrated and filtered (wrapped and unwrapped, radians), the filtered \(a\) (au), \(e\), \(i\) (radians), then Lomb-Scargle periodograms of the filtered angle, \(a\) and \(e\). The time axes are in years; the periodograms are drawn against period, from 0 to the length of the record, not against time. Blue × marks a peak, gray dashed lines its width; the red and green dashed lines are the power levels 0.05 and 0.1. The semi-major axis here is smoothed by the body-level filter (LIBRATION_FILTER_CUTOFF: by default periods shorter than 2000 yr are removed), not at the analysis' cutoff.

docs.title: recurrence (MMR)
docs.text:
Each pixel compares the state of the angle at two times \(t_1\) and \(t_2\): dark means the angle and its rate are almost the same at both times. A libration gives a pattern of dark diagonal stripes, one per period, as here for (463) Lola (period about 10 kyr); a circulation never returns to a state it left, so it stays light away from the diagonal. The white band along the diagonal is left out on purpose.

The math: the recurrence distance \[ D(t_1, t_2) = \sqrt{\left(\frac{\Delta\sigma}{s_\sigma}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\Delta\dot\sigma}{s_{\dot\sigma}}\right)^2} \]

on the unwrapped \(\sigma_f\), with \(s_\sigma\) half the median diameter of a cycle and \(s_{\dot\sigma}\) half the 5–95 % spread of \(\dot\sigma\). These are the object's own scales: D compares states within one figure, not between objects. The matrix is thinned to about 8 samples per cycle (700–2500 points).

docs.title: fair (MMR)
docs.text: The same plane as panel (m) of the combined figure, for a prograde two-body angle. A libration leaves empty gaps between slanted bands, as for (1921) Pala in the 2:1 resonance here; a circulation fills the square over time. Unlike (m), this figure is drawn even when the output step is too coarse: above fair.max_step_fraction (¼) of the orbital period it warns that the strips are aliased.

docs.title: portrait (MMR)
docs.text: \(\sigma_f\) (shifted by whole turns only) against \(\dot\sigma\) in degrees per display unit, colored by time; gray dots are the osculating values; red line: \(\dot\sigma = 0\). With portrait.y='axis' the y axis is \(a - a_0\) in \(10^{-3}\) au: the analysis' own \(a_f\), as in the cycles below, \(a_0\) its median over the focus (the osculating \(a\) when the analysis' arrays are not held). A libration draws a closed loop. The first and last 1/LIBRATION_FILTER_CUTOFF years (2000 yr by default) are left out, where the filter is distorted.

docs.title: cycles (MMR)
docs.text: Every cycle of \(\sigma_f\) from one maximum to the next, stretched to [0, 1] and laid on top of each other (left), and \(a\) over the same cycles minus each cycle's median (right, \(10^{-3}\) au), colored by the cycle's midpoint; \(n\) is the number of cycles. Cycles that lie on top of each other are a steady libration, and \(a\) swings in step with \(\sigma\), a quarter cycle apart. A cycle here is a candidate oscillation, not a confirmed libration. The right panel uses the analysis' own filtered \(a_f\) (at the angle's cutoff, as panel (d) of the combined figure); when the analysis' arrays are not held (a row not selected for plotting) it uses the osculating \(a\), never the body-level filter of evolution, which would erase a libration faster than 1/LIBRATION_FILTER_CUTOFF (2000 yr by default).

docs.title: angle, rate, portrait (secular and Lidov-Kozai)
docs.text:
angle: \(\sigma(t)\) in degrees; gray the osculating angle (folded into the band of the black curve when that one is bounded), black the angle at the scale the verdict rests on (\(P_c\), or the center scale), red circles the turning points. Read it as panel (a) of the combined figure: (1222) Tina librates through 33 turning points in 10 Myr. A slow libration needs a long record: (1020) Arcadia in z1 turns back three times in 10 Myr and is resonant (Gallery); (3701) Purkyne, also in z1 with a period of about 8 Myr, turns back only twice in 10 Myr and is uncertain (insufficient_time).

rate: the rate of the black curve in ″/yr (also for Lidov-Kozai, unlike the combined figure), the red line at zero and a dashed line at the mean rate, the "divisor" printed in the title. A libration swings about zero; a drift runs parallel to it.

portrait: \((r\cos\sigma, r\sin\sigma)\); gray from the osculating elements, colored by time from the classified angle; red + at the origin. Here \(r\) is \(e\) when the angle contains \(\varpi\), otherwise \(i\) in degrees from the invariable plane (the combined figure's (i) uses \(\sin\frac i2\) instead). Tina's ring sits off the origin: a libration.

docs.title: ecc_vector
docs.text:
The plane \((k, h) = (e\cos\omega, e\sin\omega)\), colored by time, in a square window centered on the origin; one figure per body. A cloud that does not enclose the origin keeps \(\omega\) bounded whatever the dynamics: it explains why \(\omega\) librates, not whether the libration is a resonance. Here (591986)'s cloud is off the origin, yet its libration is kinematic (below).

The math: forced and free eccentricity

The cloud's center is offset from the origin by \(e_{\rm forced}\) and its radius is about \(e_{\rm free}\), the columns e_forced and e_free of summary.csv (forced and free eccentricity).

docs.title: free_omega (Lidov-Kozai)
docs.text:
Three figures from the forced/free split (Free elements), in the frame of the Lidov-Kozai row (ZLK_ANGLE_FRAME, the invariable plane by default): the osculating ω of the drift figure is the row's classified angle.

drift: how far \(\omega\) has moved since the start: blue the free \(\omega\), a thick gray line the osculating one, in degrees, or in turns when the drift exceeds three turns. A confined band is a libration, a ramp a circulation. Top: (3040) Kozai, where both stay within a band of some 70°: a Lidov-Kozai libration. Bottom: (591986), where the osculating \(\omega\) stays bounded but the free \(\omega\) winds about 80 turns in 500 kyr: kinematic.

portrait: free \(e\) against free \(\omega\) (0°–360°), colored by time, with red dotted lines at 90° and 270°. A librator draws closed loops around one of them (the center can shift inside a mean-motion resonance); a circulator draws a wave through every \(\omega\).

vector: the free eccentricity vector \((e_{\rm free}\cos\omega_{\rm free}, e_{\rm free}\sin\omega_{\rm free})\) on exactly the window of the osculating ecc_vector figure, so the two can be compared by eye. For (591986) the free vector circles the origin while the osculating cloud is offset from it: the forced eccentricity, not a resonance, kept the osculating \(\omega\) bounded.

docs.title: cross_spectrum
docs.text:
Coherence and phase of two series (for example \(e\) and \(i\)) against period on a log axis, and below them the two series band-passed at the decisive line over 16 of its cycles. Everything is cropped to the search band, and the axes pick their own unit (yr, kyr, Myr).

  • Coherence panel. Each segmentation level has its own shade of blue: its full spectrum faint, a dotted line at its significance threshold, and a stem at each detected line; open red rings mark up to five strongest lines of each level. A red dashed vertical line marks the decisive line (the strongest at the coarsest valid level; it need not lie in a yellow band).
  • Yellow bands mark where to look: every level whose validity band covers that period is above its own threshold (at least two such levels; a level that cannot see the period abstains), and the band holds one of the decisive level's three strongest lines. Agreement alone would not be selective: when the Kozai integral \(\sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\) is conserved, \(i\) is a smooth function of \(e\) and the two are coherent at every period with power, so a highlight of all agreement would say only that the integral holds.
  • Phase panel. Each line is a marker sized by its cross-amplitude, filled when every level agrees; light green bands are the expected phase ± tolerance (180° ± 30° for the exchange of \(e\) and \(i\)).
  • Band-passed panel. This one settles it: two curves in antiphase are an exchange, two curves drifting past each other are not.

The method: Cross-spectral coherence. No example image: the benchmark examples are saved without coherence.

docs.title: clones
docs.text: Three panels for a body integrated with clones (Clones): (a) the angle (0°–360°) of every clone, colored by its status, the nominal orbit in black; (b) each clone's status against its initial \(a\) (minus the nominal's), the nominal a black ★, with the catalog resonant axis \(a_{\rm res}\) of an MMR (dotted, a_res (catalog): from the mean motions, not moved into the osculating frame of the x axis) and \(a_{\rm res}\) ± the median half-width of the clones' episodes (blue dashed); (c) the share of each status with its Wilson 95 % interval, ★ at the nominal's status (over the bound draws; when more than CLONES_MAX_INVALID of the draws are no bound orbit, (c) draws no bar and says 'no shares', and the title says so too). The title gives the number of clones, the source of the orbit solution, its epoch and the most common status. No example image: drawing it needs an integration of the clones.

docs.title: What to look at first
docs.text:
Start from the plaque, then check the panels the verdict rests on. The Gallery has a figure for each case below.

  • resonant (two-body, three-body): in (a) the fills cover the record from edge to edge; in (c) the line changes sign at each turning point and stays near its episode's blue dashed limits (not necessarily ±1, and only roughly for a well that is not a cosine); in (h) the dots lie below 1; (k) and (l) show closed loops around the +; (e) shows high \(R^2\).
  • transient (capture and release, after a jump): fills in part of (a) only; circulation or a drift between them; hatched fills and jump lines when a jump of \(a\) ended the libration; the σ line of Key facts says how the record ends.
  • a subresonance (example): in (j) a member's line is flat while the catalog angle wanders.
  • near_separatrix (example): no accepted episode, but the angle stalls: ○ slips on the zero line of (c), or revolutions in (h) close to the separatrix zone (near the separatrix).
  • non_resonant, circulation (example): the center in (i) runs a full turn one way (shaded); the recurrence figure stays light away from its diagonal.
  • non_resonant with a libration (kinematic, induced): the angle librates in (a) (its episodes faint, cand: the status does not count them), but in (j) \(\sigma\) follows \(p\varpi\) (kinematic) or the owner's purple line is the flat one (induced); the header reads episodes about X° (not this resonance).
  • an alias (example): the red ALIAS note in (b), and the portraits crossed out.
  • uncertain (too short, an unexplained drift): the line Needed: … under Why and the action chip say what is missing (a longer record, a finer step) and how long to integrate.
  • secular (ν6, z1): read (a) with the turning-point rule above and (i), (k), (l) for a ring off the origin.
  • Lidov-Kozai (confirmed, kinematic): in (g) a free \(\omega\) that winds points to kinematic, a confined one supports the libration; the gate's outcome in the right column decides when it gives one, else the angle's shape does. An offset eccentricity-vector cloud alone proves nothing.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
The physics pages cite these works. Page and equation numbers refer to the printed pages.

Resonant dynamics

  • Murray, C. D., & Dermott, S. F. (1999). Solar System Dynamics. Cambridge University Press. Used: co-orbital frequencies (eq. 3.151, p. 94; eqs. 3.178–3.179, p. 105), the disturbing function (eq. 6.13, p. 227), Lagrange's equation for \(a\) (eq. 6.145, p. 251), secular vectors (eqs. 7.18–7.19, p. 277), the resonant angle and its rate (eq. 8.18, p. 329; eq. 8.22, p. 331), the pendulum model, its period and width (eqs. 8.45–8.58, pp. 335–338).
  • Morbidelli, A. (2002). Modern Celestial Mechanics: Aspects of Solar System Dynamics. Taylor & Francis. Used: the pendulum frequency \(\sqrt{\beta c}\) of a resonant normal form (Eqs. 4.3–4.4, pp. 72–74), single-resonance normal forms and three-body terms at second order (§9.3, pp. 221–223), multiplets and modulated resonances (§9.4, pp. 224–226).
  • Gallardo, T. (2006). Atlas of the mean motion resonances in the Solar System. Icarus, 184, 29–38. doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2006.04.001. Used: the averaged disturbing function at fixed \(\sigma\) (eqs. 1–6, p. 30) and the stable centers (§3).
  • Nesvorný, D., & Morbidelli, A. (1998). Three-body mean motion resonances and the chaotic structure of the asteroid belt. Astronomical Journal, 116, 3029–3037. doi:10.1086/300632. Used: three-body angles (eqs. 1–2, p. 3029), filtering before decimation (§2, p. 3030), membership judged by the correlation of the filtered \(a\) with the angle (§2, pp. 3030–3031), the strength scale of three-body resonances (§3, pp. 3031–3032).
  • Gallardo, T., Coito, L., & Badano, L. (2016). Planetary and satellite three body mean motion resonances. Icarus, 274, 83–98. doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.03.018. Used: two critical angles that both librate while only one moves \(a\) (p. 89).
  • Nesvorný, D., & Morbidelli, A. (1998). An analytic model of three-body mean motion resonances. Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy, 71, 243–271. doi:10.1023/A:1008347020890.
  • Wisdom, J. (1985). A perturbative treatment of motion near the 3/1 commensurability. Icarus, 63, 272–289. doi:10.1016/0019-1035(85)90011-9. Used: the action of the pendulum (§III, p. 277) and adiabatic changes of the well (pp. 274, 279).
  • Henrard, J., & Lemaître, A. (1983). A second fundamental model for resonance. Celestial Mechanics, 30, 197–218. doi:10.1007/BF01234306.
  • Lemaître, A. (1984). High-order resonances in the restricted three-body problem. Celestial Mechanics, 32, 109–126. doi:10.1007/BF01231119.

  • Henrard, J. (1982). Capture into resonance: an extension of the use of adiabatic invariants. Celestial Mechanics, 27, 3–22.

  • Li, M., Huang, Y., & Gong, S. (2019). Survey of asteroids in retrograde mean motion resonances with planets. Astronomy & Astrophysics, 630, A60. doi:10.1051/0004-6361/201936117. Used: the angle of a retrograde resonance.

Secular resonances: libration periods

  • Morbidelli, A., & Henrard, J. (1991). Secular resonances in the asteroid belt: theoretical perturbation approach and the problem of their location. Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy, 51, 131–167. doi:10.1007/BF00048606. Used: the local resonant Hamiltonian (Eqs. 35–39, pp. 147–149).
  • Milani, A., & Knežević, Z. (1992). Asteroid proper elements and secular resonances. Icarus, 98, 211–232. doi:10.1016/0019-1035(92)90091-K. Used: \(z_1\) libration periods of (339) Dorothea and (221) Eos (p. 227).
  • Vokrouhlický, D., Brož, M., Bottke, W. F., Nesvorný, D., & Morbidelli, A. (2006). The peculiar case of the Agnia asteroid family. Icarus, 183, 349–361. doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2006.03.002. Used: the \(z_1\) cycle of (3701) Purkyne (Fig. 4).
  • Carruba, V., Aljbaae, S., & Winter, O. C. (2016). On the Erigone family and the \(z_2\) secular resonance. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 455, 2279–2288. doi:10.1093/mnras/stv2430. Used: the \(z_2\) cycle of (8089) Yukar (Fig. 3, pp. 2281–2282) and its portrait in Charlier variables (Fig. 3B), the model of panel (k).

Lidov-Kozai

  • Lidov, M. L. (1962). The evolution of orbits of artificial satellites of planets under the action of gravitational perturbations of external bodies. Planetary and Space Science, 9, 719–759. doi:10.1016/0032-0633(62)90129-0. Used: the two integrals \(c_1, c_2\) (eqs. 58–60, p. 741).
  • Kozai, Y. (1962). Secular perturbations of asteroids with high inclination and eccentricity. Astronomical Journal, 67, 591–598. doi:10.1086/108790. Used: the quadrupole energy integral (eqs. 24, 26–28, p. 594).
  • Shevchenko, I. I. (2017). The Lidov-Kozai Effect — Applications in Exoplanet Research and Dynamical Astronomy. Astrophysics and Space Science Library 441, Springer. doi:10.1007/978-3-319-43522-0. Used: Lidov's integrals \(c_1, c_2\) and the libration criterion (eqs. 3.35–3.36, pp. 35–36; eq. 3.43, p. 42), the quadrupole Hamiltonian in the Kinoshita–Nakai form (eq. 3.41, p. 41).

Signal processing and statistics

  • Knežević, Z., & Milani, A. (2000). Synthetic proper elements for outer main belt asteroids. Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy, 78, 17–46 (reprinted in Dvorak, R. & Henrard, J., eds., New Developments in the Dynamics of Planetary Systems, Springer, 2001). Used: aliasing of a sampled angle and filtering before decimation (§2.2, pp. 22–23).
  • Wilson, E. B. (1927). Probable inference, the law of succession, and statistical inference. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 22, 209–212. doi:10.1080/01621459.1927.10502953.

docs.title: Secular resonances
docs.text: A secular resonance is a commensurability between the slow precession of the body's perihelion (g) or node (s) and the fundamental frequencies of the planets (g1…g8, s1…s8, Mercury…Neptune). How the status of a secular angle is decided: Secular and Lidov-Kozai.

docs.title: Creating resonances
docs.text:
import resonances

nu6 = resonances.create_secular_resonance('nu6')  # g-g6
nu14 = resonances.create_secular_resonance('nu14')  # s-s4
z1 = resonances.create_secular_resonance('g-g6+s-s6')
z2 = resonances.create_secular_resonance('2(g-g6)+(s-s6)')
other = resonances.create_secular_resonance('-g+s+g5-s7')

Aliases: nu1…nu8 are g-g1…g-g8, nu11…nu18 are s-s1…s-s8 (no nu15: s5 is identically zero), z1…z4, 2nu6-nu5, 3nu6-2nu5. A formula needs at least one term of the body (g or s); planet indices run from 1 to 8. A string is recognized as secular by detect_resonance_type if it is an alias (any case) or its only letters are a lowercase g and s. Capital letters are MMR notation, so 2S-1 and 4J-2S-1 are MMRs with Saturn.

docs.title: How the angle is built
docs.text:
With secular_angle_mode='proper' (the default), the angle that is classified, plotted and saved compares the body's perihelion and node with the planets' mode longitudes \(g_j t + \phi_j\) (the frequencies PLANETARY_FREQUENCIES and the J2000 phases PLANETARY_PHASES of resonances/data/const.py, shifted to the simulation date), with the body's node measured from the invariable plane (INVARIABLE_PLANE). The formulas and the fitted basis: The secular angle. This section explains why.

Both matter. Measured from the ecliptic, the node of every planet is dominated by the constant 1.58° tilt of the invariable plane and does not circulate at all (Jupiter's and Saturn's mean rate is 0, not s6); the osculating perihelia of Venus, Earth, Mars, Uranus and Neptune do not turn at their own mode either (Uranus' turns at ~5.8″/yr, not g7). Only Mercury's, Jupiter's and Saturn's perihelia follow their mode. So an angle built from the planets' osculating elements is wrong for every term but g1, g5, g6: built so, the z1 angle g+s-g6-s6 of (847) Agnia turns at −26″/yr, exactly −s6, the rate of the planets' artificial node. The same holds for a body of low free inclination, whose ecliptic node librates around the invariable node instead of turning at s.

Reduced angle (secular_remove_forced=True, the default). The body's e and i vectors carry forced terms at every planetary fundamental. Those at frequencies that are not in the angle (g5 for z1 or ν6, s7 for z2, …) only shake it, and when the free e or i is not much larger than the forced one they decide whether the angle turns at all: (363) Padua's z1 angle from the osculating elements circulates for 6 of 10 Myr while the resonance holds. The literature removes them by low-pass filtering (Carruba et al. 2016 filter the z2 angle at 700 kyr "to eliminate all short-period perturbations such as the g5 frequency"); here they are subtracted by least squares at the known frequencies (proper_angle.reduced_vectors). The terms at the angle's own frequencies (g6, s6 for z1; g6 for ν6) are the resonance and stay — one rule for linear and nonlinear resonances. Removing all of them would give the free-phase angle of Vokrouhlický et al. (2006, Agnia), which for a linear resonance removes the resonance itself.

The angle from the osculating elements (same mode longitudes, nothing removed) is saved as <resonance>_angle_osculating; secular_angle_mode='osculating' classifies the integration's angle instead. The analysis of the angle (cutoff, center scale, turning points: a libration needs LIBRATION_MIN_TURNING_POINTS = 3 turning points, one full cycle) is described in Secular and Lidov-Kozai.

Free divisor (summary.csv free_divisor, ″/yr; a diagnostic, no status depends on it): \(p g + q s + \sum_j(p_j g_j + q_j s_j)\) with the body's own \(g\) and \(s\) — the rates of its free vectors, every fundamental removed (proper_angle.free_rates). Near 0 the free vector itself keeps pace with the planets' modes (16712 and 48717 in ν6, the z1 and z2 librators). A libration whose period is \(P = 1\,296\,000/|D|\) yr, with the free divisor \(D\) in ″/yr (one turn = 1 296 000″), is one around the forced equilibrium: the angle's own forced term is larger than the free amplitude and the free vector turns at its own rate — Tina in ν6 (2.18″/yr, 592 kyr), the anti-aligned ν6 libration of Carruba & Morbidelli (2011). The two cannot be told apart by this number alone, so it changes nothing.

docs.title: Planetary frequencies and phases
docs.text:
g5…g8, s6…s8 are the AstDyS values (Knežević & Milani 2000). g1…g4, s1…s4 and all the phases are measured on the package's own model (Sun, eight planets, Pluto, Newtonian, Earth = Earth–Moon barycenter) by a frequency analysis of a 10-Myr integration. Against Laskar (1990, Icarus 88, 266, Tables II–III) the outer planets agree to 0.01–0.02″/yr and 1–2° in phase, g3, g4, s3, s4 to 0.01–0.06″/yr; g1 is lower by 0.38″/yr, g2 by 0.12, s1 higher by 0.11 — the model has no general relativity. The inner frequencies drift by ~0.01″/yr over 10 Myr, and their phases are uncertain by tens of degrees. s2 is split into several lines in this model and is the least certain of all.

Measured phases (secular_planet_phases='measured', needs save_planets='all' (or True)). Over tens of Myr the linear law drifts away from the integrated planets: in a 20 Myr run of the package's model the phase of s4 is off by 80° after 17 Myr, s3 by 23°, g3 and s2 by 20°, and even s6 by 16° (the AstDyS s6 is 0.003″/yr off the model's). resonances/secular/planet_modes.py fits the phase of mode j in planet j's own vector (e·exp(iϖ) for g_j, sin(i/2)·exp(iΩ) for s_j) by least squares on all eight modes of that kind, in windows of secular_phase_window (5 Myr: g3 and g4 are 0.54″/yr apart), a tenth of a window apart, and builds the longitude as g_j t + φ_j(t). Within half a window of either end the phase goes on along its slope. A baseline shorter than the window keeps the linear law: a shorter fit cannot separate g3 from g4 (over 200 kyr it puts g3 51° off).

docs.title: Mode phases
docs.text: How far the linear phases stray (resonances/data/mode_phase_uncertainty.json). For every mode, range_j(T) is the largest max − min of φ_j(t) over a window of length T, from the same 5 Myr fits, in three runs of the model (SABA dt 0.5 and 0.25 over 50 Myr, WHFast 3 d over 20 Myr), the maximum over the runs. Up to 20 Myr the windows lie anywhere inside the first 20 Myr from the epoch, the span the three runs agree on; a longer T starts at the epoch (both SABA runs show a jump of the inner modes 22–25 Myr ahead, where g3 moves by 125° in 2.5 Myr). At T = 10 Myr: g1 18°, g2 2.7°, g3 24°, g4 30°, s1 17°, s2 87°, s3 23°, s4 81°; every outer mode below 10° (s6 9.5°, g5 1.4°, g6 0.9°). The fit smooths φ_j over 5 Myr, so below that length range_j is the phase's drift, not its faster wobble. Under the linear law a secular libration must swing more than Σ|k_j| range_j(T) over the angle's modes, or it is insufficient_time / phase_unresolved (the rule). The table was measured with a research script on local runs; neither is part of the package.

docs.title: Which resonances to check
docs.text:
SECULAR_FORMULAS is the catalog: the linear ν_j, ν_1j of all planets, the classical degree-4 set, z1…z4 and the g-type terms (75 distinct angles). For a complete search around one body use resonances.secular.combinations.near_resonant(g, s, max_order=6, thresholds={2: 5.0, 4: 2.0, 6: 1.0}, modes=...) (g, s and the windows in ″/yr; pass modes by name). For \(\sigma = p\varpi + q\Omega + \sum_j(p_j\varpi_j + q_j\Omega_j)\) it builds every angle allowed by the d'Alembert rules, \(p + q + \sum_j(p_j + q_j) = 0\) and \(q + \sum_j q_j\) even (the sum of the node coefficients, not the number of node terms: 2s − s4 − s6 is allowed), up to the order \(|p| + |q| + \sum_j(|p_j| + |q_j|)\), and keeps those whose divisor \(p g + q s + \sum_j(p_j g_j + q_j s_j)\) is inside the window for its order. It returns SecularCombination records (formula, order, divisor, key); resonances.create_secular_resonance(formula) turns a chosen formula into a resonance. Order 6 with all fifteen planetary modes gives ~900 angles within 1″/yr of a main-belt body — the window and the modes have to be chosen physically.

The catalog is wider than what the literature reports. Librations are shown for ν5, ν6, ν16, ν4 (one Hungaria), z1, z2, g+g5−2g6, g+2g5−3g6, 2g−3g5+g6, g−g5+s−s7, 2g−g5−g6+s−s6 and, among the Hungarias, g−s−g5+s6; s−g5+g8−s6, s+g5−g8−s3, 2s−s4−s6 and 2g−g5−g6 are located there but shown only as temporary interactions (Warner et al. 2009; Milani et al. 2010; Knežević 2022). Nothing is reported for combinations with g1, g2, s1, s2 or mixed degree-4 terms of the inner planets with Uranus or Neptune; their divisors in this model are also off by 0.1–0.3″/yr (no general relativity). A degree-4 resonance (half-width ~0.3″/yr) librates in ~9 Myr, a degree-6 one (~0.1″/yr) in ~26 Myr. To plan the baseline, use the rule \(T_{\rm req}\) of Confidence (one and a half periods plus the two filter edges).

SecularResonanceFinder evaluates the catalog's divisors on AstDyS synthetic proper elements (resonances secular-candidates on the command line).

docs.title: Example: (1020) Arcadia in z1
docs.text:
The benchmark example of a z1 librator (SABA(10,6,4), dt = 0.5, 10 Myr from 2026-09-29, a 100-yr output step; the benchmark keeps every fifth point, a 500-yr step, which the Gallery verdict reads):

sim = resonances.Simulation(
    date='2026-09-29',
    integrator='SABA(10,6,4)',
    dt=0.5,
    integration_years=20_000,  # the benchmark run: integration_years=10_000_000, Nout=100001
    Nout=201,
)
sim.create_solar_system()
sim.add_body(1020, [resonances.create_secular_resonance('z1')], name='Arcadia')
sim.run()
print(sim.bodies[0].statuses)  # {'g-g6+s-s6': 'resonant'} over 10 Myr in the benchmark; 20 kyr is too short

(847) Agnia, the classical z1 family, circulates slowly in the same benchmark (Gallery): its free vector keeps near pace with the planets' modes without turning back.

docs.title: Serialization
docs.text: This page explains how resonances saves and restores simulations. The logic lives in resonances/simulation/serializer.py (class SimulationSerializer).

docs.title: What is saved
docs.text:
After a simulation run, the output directory contains (the series in data/, data_folder; the manifest simulation.data_files of simulation.json lists them relative to the run folder, and restore reads them from there):

  1. simulation.json – the metadata and configuration.
  2. data/data-<body>.csv – time series of each body with at least one resonance that passed the save mode, and only those resonances' angles.
  3. data/data-<body>-periodograms.csv – their periodograms (when there are any).
  4. data/<body>-omega-free.csv – the forced/free series of a saved body with a Lidov-Kozai resonance.
  5. The tables at the top: summary.csv (one row per body and resonance, derived subresonance rows included, for every body whatever its status: save_summary), episodes.csv, coherence.csv and, with MMRs, mmr_numbers.csv, candidates.csv, constants.csv. Writing a body again replaces its rows. Their columns: Output data.
  6. data/data-planet-<planet>.csv – planets time series: the planets save_planets keeps (all, analysis = those the analysis reads, none; with clones, also the planets of the clones' own rows).
  7. With clones: clones.csv at the top, and data/ensemble-<body>.csv/.json (the draws) and data/ensemble-<body>-results.npz (the clones' verdicts and thinned angles) with SAVE on (Clones).

The columns of every file, the data files included, are listed in Output data. The JSON file is the entry point for restore.

docs.title: simulation.json structure
docs.text:
The JSON file has three sections:

{
  "config": { ... },
  "simulation": { ... },
  "timing": { ... }
}

docs.title: config
docs.text: This is a full snapshot of SimulationConfig, including derived values such as tmax and tmax_yrs.

docs.title: simulation
docs.text:
This section stores:

  • number_of_bodies
  • bodies – for each body:
  • name, type, mass
  • initial_data (orbital elements used for initialization)
  • resonances (string representation); a derived subresonance row also has added_by and parent
  • data_files – the CSV files of the run that are on disk (clones = clones.csv)
  • planets_saved – the planets the run kept
  • free_elements – the forced/free setup of the run (Lidov-Kozai only)
  • ensembles – with clones: {"version": 1, "items": [...]}, per ensemble parent, nominal_in_run, resonances, n_clones, n_valid, complete (every clone batch finished), manifest and results (paths relative to the run folder; null while the clones run, or with SAVE off), nominal_offset_sigma, source, seed, clone_verdicts. simulation.json is written after the ordinary bodies (the ensembles not complete) and again after the clones; it is replaced atomically. The clones are not in bodies.

docs.title: timing
docs.text: running_time contains timestamps (if available), and running_time_differences contains durations between stages.

docs.title: How restore works
docs.text:
from resonances import SimulationSerializer  # noqa: E402,F811

sim = SimulationSerializer.restore("output/my_run/simulation.json")

The restore method:

  1. Rebuilds SimulationConfig from config.
  2. Recreates Body objects and their resonances, derived subresonance rows included (also those known only from summary.csv, registered before the series are read so that their saved angles load too).
  3. Loads the saved time series, periodograms, free-omega series and planets (to the last bit: the numbers are those the run analyzed).
  4. Sets the verdicts from summary.csv: body.statuses[key] (the status string) and body.librations[key] (a Verdict rebuilt from the row's verdict columns). Only the format the current version writes is read: a summary.csv without a verdict column (a run of an earlier version) raises an error.
  5. With ensembles: rebuilds sim.ensembles from each manifest and results archive (the clones' names, their elements at the date to the bit, the stored verdict rows and thumbnails) and sim.clone_summary from clones.csv; without a manifest (SAVE off) only sim.clone_summary, with a warning. A run without clones has no ensembles.

A run (and every batch worker) handles one body at a time from its verdicts to its data files and figures, then releases the arrays of its analyses, so only one body's analyses are in memory; summary.csv and the tables are written after the last body, from the same rows.

After a restore the numbers of the analysis stay in the CSV files: body.mmr_analyses and body.classifier_numbers are empty, and save_data/save_simulation_summary write and replace only the rows analyzed in memory, so the rows on disk stay. To analyze again from the saved series:

sim = SimulationSerializer.restore("output/my_run/simulation.json", recompute_librations=True)

An MMR is analyzed again by analyse_mmr on its raw saved angle and elements, with the settings of simulation.json (current_settings=True: the fields of AnalysisSettings and DryRunSettings are taken from the current configuration; the free-element and free-gate settings such as FREE_GATE_ENABLED, FREE_GATE_MIN_CYCLES, FREE_GATE_MASK_QUANTILE, the coherence settings and the secular-angle construction keep the saved run's values); its derived rows come out of that analysis again. A secular or Lidov-Kozai angle is analyzed again by analyse_secular/analyse_zlk on its saved unwrapped angle and elements (the center scale and the free-omega gate are steps of it). Only the resonances whose series were saved are analyzed again (their periodograms are rebuilt); the others keep their summary.csv verdict. A saved derived row whose parent was not saved (SAVE=resonant keeps a resonant subresonance of a non-resonant angle) is analyzed alone, at depth one. With clones only the nominal is reclassified: the clones keep their stored verdicts, and in the run's folder (the one simulation.json is in) the nominal columns of clones.csv and the nominal's rows of summary.csv (and of mmr_numbers, episodes, candidates) are rewritten from the nominal's new verdict, so the two files agree. Other bodies' rows are not written: call sim.data_manager.save_simulation_summary(sim.bodies) for them.

docs.title: Batch runs
docs.text: Above batch_threshold bodies (BATCH_ENABLED), run() integrates the bodies in batches, each in its own process, which writes its files. Every worker keeps the planets of the whole run. The derived rows the workers added are put on the parent's bodies before simulation.json is written, and the bodies in memory get their verdicts back from summary.csv (none without save_summary); body.mmr_analyses stays empty. The rows of a batch completed before an interruption come back the same way on resume (restore_statuses adds the derived rows it finds).

docs.title: Resuming interrupted batch simulations
docs.text:
If a batch run is interrupted (crash, OOM, manual stop), it can be resumed.

During the run, simulation_state.json in the output directory records the completed batches, written after each one (also for batches still running when another failed). It also holds a hash of everything the results depend on: the config except names, paths, plot settings and n_cores, which includes date and source, the batch layout (body names and resonances of every batch) and every body's initial elements as they were used (exact floats, with the sha256 of an MPC get-orb answer).

To resume, run the same script again with the same bodies, settings and save_path. Completed batches are skipped. A batch that was interrupted after writing some of its rows is run again and its rows in summary.csv, episodes.csv, coherence.csv, mmr_numbers.csv and candidates.csv are replaced, not repeated.

If the hash differs, run() raises ValueError instead of mixing two runs. The usual cause is the date: without date= a nasa run starts at today's midnight, so a resume on another day must pass the original date (date=). With batch_size unset the layout depends on n_cores, so keep it too. The elements count as obtained, not as requested: AstDyS and MPC elements come from the cached catalog and are the same on a rerun, but a refreshed get-orb answer (MPC_LOOKUP=file_then_api), a new catalog or a Horizons re-query (astroquery keeps its answers a week) that returns a new orbit solution makes another run, and the error names the bodies whose elements changed. To start over, delete simulation_state.json (and the old files). A simulation_state.json written by a version before 1.0 (a hash without the elements, or of only a few settings) is refused like any other mismatch.

import resonances

asteroids = [463, 490]  # the original run's list, in the same order
settings = dict(integration_years=1_000, batch_threshold=1, batch_size=1, planets=['Jupiter', 'Saturn'], type='mmr')


def main():
    sim = resonances.find(
        asteroids=asteroids,  # the same list, in the same order
        name="my-simulation",
        date="2026-10-13",  # the date of the interrupted run
        save_path="output/resume",  # the same folder
        plot_path="output/resume-plots",
        **settings,  # the same settings as the interrupted run
    )
    sim.run(progress=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':  # a batch run starts worker processes: the guard is required
    main()

These are the settings of the demonstration run; for a real resume use the original run's asteroid list and settings.

Progress so far:

python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/path/to/output/simulation_state.json')); print(len(d['progress']['completed_batches']), '/', d['batch_config']['total_batches'])"

A run with clones is resumed the same way, as a whole: its checkpoint clones_state/ (the run identity, the clones' starts, one file per finished clone batch) and simulation_state.json stay until the clones are done too; a finished ordinary part and the finished clone batches are not run again (Clones).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• simulation.json is always written by DataManager.save_configuration_details.
  • All file paths are relative to the simulation save directory.

docs.title: Confidence
docs.text: The status says what the record shows; the confidence says how close the record came to showing something else. It is built from the comparisons the analysis made on the way to the status, not from a statistical model of asteroid orbits. uncertain and invalid verdicts have no level: they claim nothing to be confident about.

docs.title: Minimal policy (default)
docs.text:
The minimal policy's level is a pure function of five pieces of evidence (policy.level, column confidence_basis; policy.level_inputs, column pol_level_inputs, lists each input the level read with the highest level it allows, and the level is the lowest of them):

  • N, complete libration cycles: \((n_{TP} - 1)/2\) of the decisive episode, plus the gap of each covered edge in periods (a 2-TP run closed by its phase return counts 1, one 1:1 leg 0.5); a resonant row over several episodes sums them, an overlap counted once; a subresonance parent's N is its member's (N=…(member): no episode of its own);
  • M, the amplitude margin: L2 full (1:1: the zone known and no cycle in it; long-period: the largest half-amplitude below \((1 -\) CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND\()\) of the run break);
  • V, the vetoes: clean (the identity passes and the owner search found none, or does not apply; ZLK: the gate confirmed), partial (owner search not measured, a probable owner, W or the gate's cycles thin), not_measured (the identity or the gate gave no measurement; a failed identity on a step that turns only \(\varpi\) fast, flag varpi_fast_low_e, where \(\dot\sigma\) reads that \(\varpi\): 17346 2J-1), ambiguous (a measured objection, a failed onset, a failed identity that moved nothing, a kinematic gate that pins no episode);
  • S, filter stability: L1 full and no decisive number changing at the cutoff ×2 (flag filter_sensitive; long-period: F full and no filter_too_slow).
  • F (MMR), the angle's own force: shown when the force law on a (L4, the 1:1 law), the energy and period law (R0) or the strength (F) passes, else none. The identity \(\dot\sigma = c\,(a - a^*)\) is no force: it holds for any orbit, and below a 45° half-amplitude L4 and R0 cannot tell a force from it. A resonant or transient MMR row with F none is at most CONFIDENCE_GEOMETRY_ONLY_MAX (low): the angle is bounded, the mechanism is not shown (no resonant/transient by the geometry alone; Gallardo, Coito & Badano 2016, p. 89, show librating angles without a dynamical effect).
status level resonant, transient V ambiguous or N < CONFIDENCE_MEDIUM_CYCLES (1.5: one closed cycle, a single 1:1 leg) → low; N ≥ CONFIDENCE_CERTAIN_CYCLES (3), at least CONFIDENCE_CERTAIN_CORE_CYCLES (3) observed cycles \((n_{TP}-1)/2\) inside the decisive episode, with M, S and V clean → certain; N ≥ CONFIDENCE_HIGH_CYCLES (2) with V clean or partial → high; otherwise medium; MMR with F none: at most low near_separatrix medium (low when V is ambiguous) non_resonant by a veto medium when the veto is thin or a second capture is unresolved; else high (a stable vetoed episode is still drawn as a candidate) non_resonant medium with a candidate (a leg, a half-swing, a near-episode run); certain for a clear circulation (MMR: C1 and C2 full, an alias C5 and C2 full; long-period: P full and no turning point at any cutoff); else high. A secular or ZLK record too short for one cycle that the policy decides as ending in circulation with an end travel below \(1 +\) CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND turns is at most medium (input end_travel; the travel is a range of \(\sigma_f\), the swing included, so 1.09 turns may still be part of a slow libration: 143662 s+g5−g8−s3)

The counts are the same for every resonance type: in units of its own period two returns of a 4-Myr secular libration carry the same information as two of a 500-yr one, so a long period is no reason for a lower count; what a long-period row lacks is said by V (a gate, the mode phases), not by N. The literature on resonance identification from integrations sets no cycle count (Nesvorný & Morbidelli 1998; Gallardo 2014; Huaman et al. 2017; Christou & Asher 2011): the numbers are conventions. The level never falls as N rises. Caps become flags; confidence_raw equals confidence; the calibration cell is not reported. The action: extend by the extend rule, resample when the alias rule withdrew a needed check (the output step folds a short period, rsp_short_period_unmeasured), review for uncertain or for a needed veto beyond the extend budget, then medium spot_check, low review.

docs.title: The full tree: margins and caps
docs.text: The rest of this page is the confidence of the full status tree (its level, in v2_verdict); its margins stay columns.

docs.title: Margins
docs.text:
Every test that can support or undermine the status is graded as a margin:

margin meaning full the test passed with room to spare thin it passed, but close to its threshold, or it rests on too little (one cycle, one window) fail it did not pass not_measured it applies, but the record could not measure it; counts as thin (a check that could not be made is not a pass) not_applicable the test has no meaning for this verdict (e.g. the onset of a capture for a forced wave)

Each margin belongs to a class:

  • D, decisive: a test the status tree itself relied on. In a final verdict it cannot fail (the verdict would be a different one); it can only be full, thin or unmeasured.
  • S, support: a test that may fail without changing the status; each failure lowers the level.
  • cap: a test whose failure limits the level directly (below).

Margin U. Many thresholds are conventions rather than physics: chosen values such as \(R^2 \ge 0.7\). When a decision of the tree compared a value with a convention and the value lay within CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND = 10 % of it, \(\lvert x/x_{\rm thr} - 1\rvert < 0.1\), that decision would flip under a slightly different convention. It becomes a thin margin U:<name of the comparison>. Thresholds that follow from physics (one full turn, \(h = 1\) at the separatrix) never make a margin U. Which settings are conventions is marked "(convention)" in resonances/.env.dist.

docs.title: The margins of a mean-motion resonance
docs.text:
id class physical question full when L1 D Does the libration survive a different filter? the decisive episode keeps ≥ MMR_L1_TP_FULL = 7 turning points at \(P_c/2\), \(P_c\) and \(2P_c\) L2 D Is it far from the separatrix? no cycle lies in the separatrix zone; without a measured zone, amplitude ≤ MMR_L2_AMP_FULL_DEG = 120° (thin to MMR_L2_AMP_THIN_DEG = 160°) L3 S Does \(\dot\sigma \simeq c\,(a - a_*)\) hold? the identity passes (not applicable to a kinematic verdict) L4 D Does \(\dot a\) follow the force law? \(R^2 \ge\) MMR_FORCE_R2_FULL = 0.7 in both halves of the record L5 S Is it one pendulum? \(r\) = max/min of \(T_0\) over the amplitude regimes ≤ \(b\) = MMR_L5_RATIO_FULL = 1.15 × \(\omega_{\max}/\omega_{\min}\) (the modulation of the force; 1 without one); thin to MMR_L5_RATIO_FAIL = 2 × \(b\), failed above; above \(b\) only thin when the median \(e\) > MMR_L5_E_CAVEAT = 0.2 L6 D Is the center fixed? the center shifts by ≤ MMR_L6_SHIFT_FULL = 0.5 of the mean amplitude L7 D Does the libration reach both ends of the record? the gaps at the edges are ≤ MMR_L7_GAP_FULL = 0.7 periods L8 S Do the step and the filter resolve the cycle? \(\sigma\) turns by < MMR_L8_STEP_FULL_DEG = 10° per step, the filter keeps ≥ MMR_L8_GAIN_FULL = 0.94 of the cycle (failed below 0.5), no aliased line in the band; not graded for a circulation ≥ MMR_FAR_FROM_RES_FACTOR = 10 \(a\)-scales from \(a_*\) O1 cap Is this a capture, not a wave that was already there? the \(a\)-wave before the episode is < MMR_O1_RATIO_THIN = 0.25 of the one inside (≥ MMR_O1_RATIO_FAIL = 0.5 fails, cap low, only when that wave is coherent at \(P\), in phase and not the episode's own law; else thin) Z D Is the separatrix zone measured? measured without caveats R0 D Is the energy from \(a\) conserved in a potential of \(\sigma\)? passes S D Does a member of the multiplet own the libration? see below W D Does another resonance own it? see below C1–C5 D/S (circulation) Is it really a circulation? see below K1 D (kinematic) Does the angle follow the geometry? rate correlation ≥ MMR_K1_FULL = 0.97 B5 S Is a libration slower than the record excluded? the center's rate is ≥ MMR_B5_RATIO_FULL = 2 × the slowest rate a libration in the record's range of \(a\) would allow F S Is the required strength available? required / theory within [1/x, x], x = MMR_STRENGTH_CHECK_RATIO = 10 (inverted for a kinematic verdict, below) N cap Was the record one turn short of an episode? no near-episode

What each test measures is explained in Is it this resonance? and What the angle does.

S and W support whichever origin the verdict names; they are not tests of absence only.

  • S, an accepted member: full when the member's theoretical check confirms it and no tie between members was broken by order alone; otherwise thin. No accepted member: the closest member's center range over \(\sigma\)'s, full above MMR_S_CLOSE_RATIO = 0.8 (a member nearly as still as \(\sigma\) is a near miss: thin).
  • W, an accepted owner: full when its median \(R^2 \ge\) MMR_W_R2_FULL = 0.85 and its force is reachable (for the potential route: every window scale within \([1/1.5,\ 1.5]\), MMR_OWNER_POTENTIAL_SCALE_FULL); an owner covering less than MMR_OWNER_COVER_MIN of the episode is thin. No owner: full while the best candidate's \(R^2\) stays below MMR_W_R2_NONE = 0.4. W is not measured when the phases cannot separate the best candidate or the search could not run, and not applicable to 1:1.

C1–C5 grade a circulation:

  • C1: the center passes \(\ge\) MMR_C1_REV_FULL = 10 turns (not for an alias);
  • C2: full when no turning point is found at \(P_c\), \(P_c/2\) or \(2P_c\); otherwise thin;
  • C3: full when the rate never runs against its mean direction, its modulation is below MMR_C3_MODULATION_MAX = 0.3 and pattern B is absent; otherwise thin. The modulation is \(\sqrt{b_c^2 + b_s^2}/\lvert b_0\rvert\) from the fit \(\dot\sigma = b_0 + b_c\cos\sigma + b_s\sin\sigma\);
  • C4: \(r = \langle\lvert\dot\sigma\rvert\rangle / (2\sqrt{\lvert c\rvert K})\), \(K\) the fitted force amplitude: the rate against the fastest a pendulum of that force could turn at the separatrix. Full for \(r \ge\) MMR_C4_RATIO_FULL = 1.5, thin for \(1 < r < 1.5\), failed for \(r \le 1\). A failure counts as not measured when no force law explains \(\dot a\) anywhere (best \(R^2 <\) MMR_FORCE_R2_FAIL = 0.4). Not for an alias;
  • C5, resolved step: full when the measured rate and the rate expected from the mean motions have the same sign and agree within MMR_C5_RATE_TOL = 0.2; otherwise thin. On an alias: full only when the far ratio reaches MMR_FAR_FROM_RES_FACTOR = 10 and the distance from \(\nu\Delta t\) to the nearest half-turn exceeds MMR_C5_BRANCH_RESID_FACTOR = 2 × the largest unwrap residual of a step; otherwise thin.

F for a kinematic verdict. For a verdict that claims this resonance's own dynamics, F grades the agreement of required and theory. For a non_resonant verdict of kinematic origin with a directly computed strength (direct averaging or the extended-precision harmonic), F reads in the inverted sense: full when the strength check fails (the force available cannot make the observed cycle, which supports the kinematic reading), not measured otherwise. The order-of-magnitude \(e^q\) scale gives no such margin. The column check_mmr_strength keeps its ordinary meaning.

docs.title: Secular and Lidov-Kozai margins
docs.text: N (turning points of the decisive episode; thin at the minimum of three), S (the center stationary over enough independent cycles), F (the libration period ≥ FILTER_MIN_LIBRATION_CUTOFFS = 2 × \(P_c\)), P (a circulation's center passes a full turn at every smoothing) and, for Lidov-Kozai, G (the free-\(\omega\) gate decided with its number of cycles clear of FREE_GATE_MIN_CYCLES = 3 by more than the thin band).

docs.title: From margins to a level
docs.text:
The raw level, confidence_raw:

level rule certain every applicable margin full: no thin, no unmeasured and no U margin high no failure; any number of thin (or unmeasured) margins medium exactly one failed support margin low two or more failed support margins

The shown level, confidence, is the raw level lowered by every cap the verdict carries: \(\text{confidence} = \min(\text{raw},\ \text{ceilings of the caps})\). A failed cap margin (O1, N) is not counted as a failure: its cap does the limiting, so the figure lists the limits apart from the support margins.

A catalog row that takes the status of its accepted member (subresonance_librates) takes the member's confidence too, with its raw level, thin and failed margins and caps; its mrg_* columns and calibration cell stay its own. Read the member's row (owner) to see why.

One cap is general: when none of the physics of the angle's own force could be measured (for an MMR: the force law L4, the potential R0, the zone Z, the owner search W, and the strength F by direct averaging), the level is at most medium (all_physics_not_measured). The identity and the response of \(a\) (L3, B1, L5) are not in this list: they show that \(a\) carries the oscillation, which is just as true of a libration induced by another resonance. A kinematic verdict has one more physics margin, K1e: the episode's \(\sigma\) follows \(p\varpi\), \(a\) is flat (B1 < MMR_KIN_B1_CLEAR) and the period is a secular one, all three together (kinematic origins); when it is full the cap does not apply and the kinematic libration can reach high (rule kinematic_high).

A verdict that claims the angle's own libration (resonant, transient or near_separatrix of its own dynamics) is high only when at least one physical support of the own force passes with its full margin: the force law L4 (for a 1:1 angle the co-orbital law, which takes L4), the potential R0 or the strength F by direct averaging. Otherwise the level is at most medium (no_full_physics_support, MMR_HIGH_NEEDS_FULL_SUPPORT). The zone Z and the owner search W exclude rivals and do not count as a support; when every physics margin is not_measured, all_physics_not_measured applies instead. Kinematic, induced and subresonance verdicts rest on other evidence and are not limited by it.

docs.title: Caps and the other reading
docs.text:
A cap names a specific way the record could be read differently. Every cap that brings the level down to medium or low names, in the right column of the combined figure, the verdict the record might hold instead and the panel that decides between the two.

cap ceiling the other reading three_tp_episode high no libration yet: three turning points are one cycle zone_not_measured high the cycles may sit in the separatrix zone exit_suspected, entry_suspected medium the libration goes on past the record's edge, or \(\sigma\) leaves (enters) only here one_return_cycle medium no libration yet: one cycle closed only by its phase return (two turning points) transient_unexplained medium near_separatrix: \(\sigma\) wanders across the separatrix without a capture or an escape episodes_in_separatrix_zone medium the edges of the librating stretches are crossings of the zone, not a capture or an escape force_law_disagrees medium uncertain: the potential holds while \(\dot a\) does not follow \(\sin\sigma\) episode_force_law_mixed medium only one episode librates in this resonance; the others carry another force episode_before_jump medium the episodes belong to a regime that ended with the jump of \(a\) action_step_provisional medium one libration over the whole window: the step in amplitude is a large modulation, not two energy levels slow_libration_not_excluded medium a slower libration of \(\sigma\) about a moving center near_episode medium transient: one more turning point would make a librating episode (a 1:1 leg between passages, or one whose two turns are kicks, counts: leaf G4c) near_separatrix_without_zone, l2_without_zone medium a circulation, or a libration close to the separatrix second_capture_unresolved medium \(\sigma\) is held by its own term as well: both resonances at once owner_search_skipped, catalogue_longitudes medium another resonance drives \(a\) (rerun with the search on, the planets saved) planets_missing, nodal_subresonance_candidate, subresonance_tie, subresonance_t6_only, subresonance_theory_unconfirmed, subresonance_undetermined medium a member of the multiplet holds the center jitter_low_e medium invalid: \(\varpi\) is undefined at small \(e\) short_period_aliased medium the turning points are partly the output step's: short-period terms folded into \(\sigma_f\) and \(a_f\) one_cycle_energy_not_conserved medium (1:1) the one cycle may be a passage, not motion in the averaged well record_ends_unresolved medium a capture at the end of the record: after circulating, \(\sigma_f\) slowed to an arc or a stall that lasts longer than twice its longest revolution (the record's edges); a longer integration forward decides one_coorbital_leg medium (1:1) uncertain: the transient rests on one clean leg between passages (law, energy, two reflecting turns), no closed cycle strength_scale_only medium uncertain: only the order-of-magnitude strength agrees, the force is not computed all_physics_not_measured medium uncertain: nothing measured shows this angle's own force no_full_physics_support medium the oscillation is not this angle's own: each physical support is only thin force_law_theory_only medium uncertain: the slow \(\dot a\) fits the averaged force of the term, but the harmonic force law fails; a rival force hidden by the smoothing is not excluded slow_scale_provisional medium L4 untested: read at a shorter cutoff of the scale ladder (signal) with neither the force law nor R0 with \(a\) measured; a record of \(\ge 5.25\,P\) decides geometry_only low uncertain: only the shape of \(\sigma\) says libration implausible_strength low a libration whose force the first-order average misses onset_failed low non_resonant: \(\sigma\) rides a coherent \(a\)-wave at its period that began before the episode, continues into it in phase and is not this resonance's own force

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
How often a level was right is reported next to it, never mixed into it. The verdicts are grouped into cells (status, angle_status, reason). For each cell, the benchmark (Benchmark) counts the author-labeled verdicts at high or certain, \(n\), and the wrong ones among them, \(n_{\rm err}\). With \(\hat p = (n - n_{\rm err})/n\) and \(z = 1.96\), the Wilson (1927) 95 % interval of the accuracy is

\[ \frac{\hat p + \dfrac{z^2}{2n} \pm z\sqrt{\dfrac{\hat p(1-\hat p)}{n} + \dfrac{z^2}{4n^2}}}{1 + \dfrac{z^2}{n}} . \]

The columns cell_n_examples, cell_n_errors, cell_accuracy_low_95 and cell_accuracy_high_95 carry them (from resonances/data/confidence_cells.json, written by benchmark/tools/calibrate.py). With tens of labels per cell the interval is wide. The level is therefore ordinal evidence: certain is stronger evidence than high, which is stronger than medium; it is not a probability that the status is right.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Each verdict ends with an action, the cheapest step that would make it stronger:

action when none certain (always, even when a longer record could still test something) or high spot_check medium: look at the figure review low; uncertain / origin_unknown; invalid other than an alias or an undersampled step; a record whose period already fits it while it is still too short to decide (more time cures nothing) extend other uncertain verdicts, and an uncertain / origin_unknown one whose deciding measurement is missing only for lack of length (below): integrate longer, to extend_to_years resample or review an uncertain 1:1 stall that stays long enough in the quasi-satellite well (G1q) with \(P_{QS} < P_c\): the filter erased a possible quasi-satellite libration, so more time at the same step cures nothing. resample when the record's step cannot hold the quasi-satellite cutoff, else review resample invalid / alias or undersampled, or a level held down by a check the folded short periods withdrew (R-ALIAS-A, rsp_short_period_unmeasured): integrate again with the output step resample_step_yr

How long to extend. A libration needs at least \(N_{\rm TP}/2\) periods plus the edges the filter trims:

\[ T_{\rm req} = \frac{N_{\rm TP}}{2}\,P + 2\,f_{\rm trim}\,P_c , \]

with \(N_{\rm TP}\) = LIBRATION_MIN_TURNING_POINTS = 3, \(f_{\rm trim}\) = FILTER_EDGE_TRIM_CUTOFFS = 1 and \(P\) the time scale that decides: the measured cycle, or for a too-short record the slowest lower bound its shape allows (twice the spacing of its turning points, a slow arc of the center, the rate of a stall). The physical estimate is \(N\), a round value \(\ge \max(T_{\rm req},\ f_{\min} T)\), \(f_{\min}\) = MMR_EXTEND_MIN_SPAN_FACTOR = 2, \(T\) the record length (column base_extend_to_years). For insufficient_time the action asks only for the next check,

\[ T_{\rm next} = \mathrm{round\ up}\big(\max(f_{\min}T,\ \min(N,\ f_{\rm next}T))\big), \]

with \(f_{\rm next}\) = MMR_NEXT_CHECK_SPAN_FACTOR = 4: a budget after which the record is analyzed again, not a promise that it is enough. A drift or another uncertain verdict asks for \(N\) itself. When \(T_{\rm req} \le T\), time is not what is missing: base_cause names what is, and the action is review.

Length-limited origin_unknown (rule extend_length_limited). Leaves 5e, 5g and 5x are decided while the force law L4 is not measured; leaf 5n by one independent cycle. When L4 has fewer than MMR_FORCE_MIN_WINDOWS = 2 windows of MMR_FORCE_WINDOW_CYCLES = 3.5 periods (not when the swing is below 45° with enough windows, nor for a forced line), or 5n's decisive episode is the last one, and the last librating episode reaches the record's end, the action is extend to

\[ T_{\rm FW} = \mathrm{round\ up}\big(t_{\rm start} + n_{\rm FW}\, W\, P\big) \]

for the windows (\(t_{\rm start}\), \(P\) of that last episode, \(n_{\rm FW}\) = MMR_EXTEND_FORCE_WINDOWS = 2, \(W\) = MMR_FORCE_WINDOW_CYCLES; 2003 TX9 3E+2J-10: \(2210 + 2 \cdot 3.5 \cdot 3136\) → 30 kyr), and to \(T_{\rm next}\) with \(N\) = the last turning point + the missing turning points × \(P/2\) + \(f_{\rm trim} P_c\) for 5n (2003 ND 6J-6S-1: 40 kyr; its L4 windows ask for 60 kyr), whichever is longer. An episode that ended before the record's end gains nothing from a longer record: review. A failed check (5a, 5b, 5o, R0 of 5e) stays: the extension serves the regime at the end (TX9's early R0 failure remains). No status changes.

The flag extend_time (rule end_arc_extend) is not an action: it says that a longer integration in extend_direction (forward, backward, both) would show how a record edge ends, whatever the action (the record's edges). Without an estimate its length is the next check \(T_{\rm next}\) with \(N\) unknown, round up(\(f_{\min} T\)) (2022 BB2: 1 kyr → 2 kyr); with action extend the action's length stays in extend_to_years. A backward extension means integrating from the record's start into the past (2008 EZ84's one reflection at 144 yr). No status or level changes; a review row stays at review.

Which time scale decides (base_period_source)

For few_cycles: twice the median spacing of the turning points, and the slow scales. For arc: twice the longest stretch without a turn of the slow center, the \(2\omega\) or \(e\)-cycle when the kinematic test fails, and B5's bound. For stall: one revolution at the stall's mean rate, and the force bound \(P_\text{lib,min}\) (The lower bound of an arc or a stall). The column base_period_source names the one that decided.

Which step to resample at. For an alias or a coarse step, resample_step_yr is the largest value of MMR_RESAMPLE_STEPS_YR that keeps one alias branch over the range of \(a\), samples the libration at least MMR_RESAMPLE_STEPS_PER_CYCLE = 20 times per cycle and lets the filter exist (\(P_c > 2\Delta t\)); review when the record's step already meets these bounds. When a check the folded short periods withdrew holds the level down, the step is smp_fold_free_step_yr: the largest grid step below the record's at which no short period folds.

Secular and Lidov-Kozai. The same table, and every extension is a next check \(T_{\rm next}\) with an \(N\) by cause (column base_extend_cause; module analysis/secular/extend.py). No status changes:

cause \(N\) action baseline (baseline_needed: drift, insufficient_time) \(T_{\rm req}\) with \(P = \max(P_{\rm floor}, P_{\rm cyc})\), \(P_c\) the decisive cutoff (secular with no cycle, \(P_c\) = 100 kyr: 500 kyr) extend gate_cycles (gate short_window) \(n_{\min} P_{\rm cyc}\) + what the free elements lose of the record (\(T - T_{\rm free}\)), \(n_{\min}\) = FREE_GATE_MIN_CYCLES extend gate_resolution (gate planetary_residual) a free rate \(d_{\min}\)″/yr from a planetary one, inside the Rayleigh width \(1\,296\,000/T_{\rm free}\): \(m \cdot 1\,296\,000/d_{\min} + (T - T_{\rm free})\), \(m\) = ZLK_EXTEND_RESOLUTION_MARGIN = 1.25 (373136 at 100 kyr, \(d\) = 3.5: 400 kyr; 1981 at 500 kyr, \(d\) = 1.9: 1 Myr) extend gate_unresolvable that baseline above ZLK_EXTEND_MAX_YR = 100 Myr, or \(d_{\min} = 0\) review gate_undefined_phase, gate_unavailable, unusable_series a longer record does not define the free phase, build missing free elements or repair a series review

The geometric \(T_{\rm req}\) joins every gate cause (the larger \(N\)). Columns as for an MMR: base_required_kyr, base_period_yr, base_period_source (cycle or period_floor), base_extend_to_years.

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text:
One benchmark example for every status, every way of reaching it and every resonance type, each with its one-page verdict figure. The figures are drawn by the package itself from the saved integrations; the verdict line under each caption is the package's verdict on that record (status · angle_status · reason · confidence), so a caption and its figure always agree. Click a figure to open it at full size.

A resonance key lists integer coefficients: first those of the mean longitudes of the planets (J Jupiter, S Saturn, E Earth, M Mars, V Venus, N Neptune) and of the body, then those of the longitudes of perihelion in the same order (and of the nodes, when present): 4J-2S-1+0+0-1 is \(4\lambda_J - 2\lambda_S - \lambda - \varpi\). See Resonance matrices. Secular keys name the frequencies (\(g - g_6 + s - s_6\) is z1), LK is the Lidov-Kozai angle \(\omega\).

docs.title: How to read the figure
docs.text: The left half of each figure holds the time series and the phase portraits, the right half the verdict: the plaque with the status, the verdict in words, the steps of the status tree, the evidence the confidence level rests on and the numbers behind them, each a column of the output files. What every panel, line and icon means: How to read the figures.

docs.title: Resonant
docs.text: The angle librates over the whole record and the libration belongs to this resonance.

docs.title: A two-body resonance: the textbook pendulum
docs.text:
\(\sigma\) librates about a fixed center over the whole record, \(a\) oscillates in step with it, and every test of the force law and of the pendulum's energy passes.

1921, 2J-1+0-1: resonant · libration · dynamic_libration · certain. Record: 100 kyr, step 1 yr, SABA(10,6,4).

docs.title: A three-body resonance with Jupiter and Saturn
docs.text:
The same reading for a three-body angle: \(\sigma\) librates over the whole record and \(a\) follows it as the pendulum of this resonance requires.

2487, 4J-2S-1+0+0-1: resonant · libration · dynamic_libration · certain. Record: 100 kyr, step 1 yr, SABA(10,6,4).

docs.title: The body of the quick start
docs.text:
The resonance checked in the Quick start. The libration is as clear as above: about nine cycles over the whole record, more than the three that certain needs, the amplitude clear of the separatrix and nothing objecting, so the confidence is certain.

463, 4J-2S-1+0+0-1: resonant · libration · dynamic_libration · certain. Record: 100 kyr, step 1 yr, SABA(10,6,4).

docs.title: An Earth co-orbital
docs.text:
The angle \(\lambda - \lambda_E\) goes from horseshoe motion to a compound orbit (horseshoe and quasi-satellite in turn) and back to horseshoe, and never circulates: one episode in three sub-regimes. A 1:1 angle is judged by its own force law, from the averaged direct and indirect potential of the planet.

2002 AA29, 1E-1+0+0: resonant · libration · dynamic_libration · certain. Record: 1 kyr, step 0.05 yr, ias15 + Moon.

docs.title: Two co-orbital regimes in turn
docs.text:
Quasi-satellite motion, a compound orbit, then horseshoe motion: regimes of the same 1:1 resonance follow each other without a circulation in between. A 1:1 episode ends only at a separatrix, so this is one episode with changes of well (the mark well_change in episodes.csv; subtype regime_change). The header names the wells in time order (orbit: …) and (a) brackets each sub-regime with its well.

164207, 1E-1+0+0: resonant · libration · dynamic_libration · certain. Record: 1 kyr, step 0.05 yr, ias15 + Moon.

docs.title: Libration about a moving center
docs.text:
The center of libration follows the slowly moving minimum of the averaged potential; the libration is tested in \(\psi = \sigma - \sigma_c(t)\). The output step folds short periods: the flag short_period_aliased warns but lowers nothing. 131 cycles would give certain, but another resonance comes close to driving \(a\) (best \(R^2\) 0.63, margin W thin), so the objections count as only partly measured and the confidence is high.

2013 AS27, 31E-36+0+5: resonant · libration · dynamic_libration · high. Record: 20 kyr, step 5 yr, ias15.

docs.title: A slow libration on a long record
docs.text:
A high-order resonance with Neptune whose libration period is long (64 kyr): over this record the angle closes 4.6 cycles and is resonant. The other resonances are tested on two windows fitted to this short record: none of 14 drives \(a\), and the confidence is certain, with no action asked (the force law, which needs two windows of 3.5 periods, is not tested on this record). The same body on a shorter record is uncertain.

385458, 9N-17+0+8: resonant · libration · dynamic_libration · certain. Record: 300 kyr, step 1 yr, SABA(10,6,4).

docs.title: Libration decided by the geometry alone
docs.text:
\(\sigma\) librates over the whole record, but neither the force law nor the energy of the pendulum could be measured (a half-amplitude of 21°: \(\sin\sigma \approx \sigma\)). The geometry decided (reason geometric_libration, origin unknown). The resonance's strength agrees with the period of the cycles to an order of magnitude (margin F), so the level is not held at the low of a geometry-only row; nothing objects, and 14 clean cycles give certain. The missing measurements are a flag (no_full_physics_support).

2348, 4J-2S-1+0+0-1: resonant · libration · geometric_libration · certain. Record: 100 kyr, step 1 yr, SABA(10,6,4).

docs.title: A libration the physics questions
docs.text:
\(\sigma\) librates over the whole record (its center moves, but the bands of the cycles overlap), but the energy test of the pendulum fails. The objection is measured but does not decide (flag measured_objection): the tree's leaf said uncertain, the minimal policy keeps the geometry's status, resonant, at low (a measured objection, and the angle's own force is not shown), with action extend.

2003 TX9, 3E+2J-10+0+0+5: resonant · libration · geometric_libration · low. Record: 20 kyr, step 5 yr, ias15.

docs.title: Transient
docs.text: Librating episodes in part of the record, circulation or a drift in the rest.

docs.title: Repeated capture and release
docs.text:
Librating episodes alternate with circulation (subtype recurrent). The deciding episode closes 3.5 cycles, enough for certain, but the episodes reach the separatrix zone (flag episodes_in_separatrix_zone: the amplitude margin is thin), so the confidence is high.

52356, 5J-2S-2+0+0-1: transient · episodic · dynamic_episode · high. Record: 100 kyr, step 1 yr, SABA(10,6,4).

docs.title: A co-orbital that leaves the 1:1 resonance
docs.text:
A horseshoe libration over most of the record. The exit is seen in the orbit-averaged angle: after it \(\lambda - \lambda_E\) circulates to the end of the record (final_regime circulation).

2017 UM52, 1E-1+0+0: transient · episodic · ends: circulation · dynamic_episode · high. Record: 1 kyr, step 0.05 yr, ias15 + Moon.

docs.title: An episode, then circulation
docs.text:
A libration episode followed by circulation to the end of the record. The episode closes only one cycle, fewer than the 1.5 that medium needs, so the confidence is low and the action asks for a review.

115978, 11M-19+0+8: transient · episodic · ends: circulation · dynamic_episode · low. Record: 50 kyr, step 0.6 yr, ias15.

docs.title: An episode ended by a jump of the semi-major axis
docs.text:
Two episodes, both before the jumps of \(a\) (hatched; flag episode_before_jump): the long first one closes 87 cycles. From about 30 kyr \(a\) jumps (kicks, as at close approaches to a planet) and the angle circulates to the end. Its amplitude, up to 138°, is near the separatrix, so the confidence is high, not certain.

2003 UG22, 10E-17+0+7: transient · episodic · ends: circulation · dynamic_episode · high. Record: 40 kyr, step 0.25 yr, ias15.

docs.title: Episodes made by a member of the multiplet
docs.text:
The catalog angle librates in episodes about a center that moves with \(2(\varpi_M - \varpi)\), while its member \(\sigma + 2(\varpi_M - \varpi)\) (13M-24+2+9) keeps a fixed center: the episodes belong to that member (reason subresonance_librates), and this row takes the member's status and its 36 cycles. Its own figure draws the episodes faint (cand, not counted here); the second figure is the member's own verdict, with them counted.

82831, 13M-24+0+11: transient · episodic · ends: circulation · subresonance_librates · high. Record: 100 kyr, step 0.5 yr, SABA(10,6,4).

82831, 13M-24+2+9: transient · episodic · ends: circulation · dynamic_episode · high. Record: 100 kyr, step 0.5 yr, SABA(10,6,4).

docs.title: An episode decided by the geometry alone
docs.text:
