The outer modes stray too little to matter: the narrowest \(z_1\)/\(z_2\) libration of the benchmark swings 4.6 times its \(\Delta\phi\) (52773), \(\nu_6\) 78 times.

The center scale. A slow secular libration often carries faster waves that break its turning points into fragments. When the fine scale shows no libration, the angle is filtered again at the scale of its center, \(W_c\) = LIBRATION_CENTRE_CYCLES × \(P_{\rm cyc}\) = \(3P_{\rm cyc}\); if the center itself librates there (or shows episodes the fine scale lacks), that scale decides (sec_scale = centre). There the shortest libration is \(\max(P_{\min},\ 2W_c)\) and a turning point needs the prominence of a center turn. When \(W_c\) shows no more libration than the fine scale, a secular angle tries the scale of its center's own turns (the fine turning points at the prominence of a center turn, \(W\) = their median period / FILTER_MIN_LIBRATION_CUTOFFS; the MMR second scale, SECULAR_CENTRE_TURNS_SCALE): \(P_{\rm cyc}\) of fast waves sets \(W_c\), and its edge trim of \(W_c\) per end, far above what the slow turns need. 101703 g−2g6+g7 over 20 Myr: \(W_c\) = 3.1 Myr from 1-Myr waves trims 3–17 Myr and loses the turn at 18.2 Myr; the turns give 1.6 Myr and one libration of 12 Myr from 6.3 to 18.25 Myr (resonant, extend).

A wave on a slower motion is no episode. An accepted episode can be a ripple that the slow motion of the angle carries (SECULAR_SLOW_WAVES; secular.decide.slow_waves). The slow motion around it is \(\sigma_f\) between the turns of the center track that bracket it (or the record's edges), of range \(R\):

  • \(R\) below a turn (a slow swing): the episode is a ripple on it when \(A_{\max} \le\) SECULAR_SLOW_SWING_RIPPLE_RATIO × \(R/2\) (0.5, the MMR ratio, a convention) and the swing carries it: the slow track \(S\) (below) moves inside the episode at least SECULAR_SLOW_SWING_CARRY_RATIO (1/16, a convention) of its fastest rate beside it. A wave at a smooth turn of the slow motion reads at least 1/8 (a parabola centred on the episode: \((D/2)^2\) inside against \((3D/2)^2-(D/2)^2\) on an arm as long again); a libration on a plateau of the slow motion, which moves only beside it, reads the filter's leak and stays an episode (two stationary librations joined by a monotone transition: ≤ 0.04). 101703 g−2g6+g7: 8–19° waves of 1 Myr at the turns of the 12-Myr libration (\(R\) = 315°, carried 0.16 and 0.12); 56700 s+s7−2s6: a 13° ripple on a 322° arc of 20 Myr (0.51), which becomes insufficient_time, extend (possibly a slow libration longer than the 20-Myr record);
  • \(R\) a turn or more (a circulation): a capture stops the circulation, a stall only slows it. The slow track \(S\) (\(\sigma\) low-passed at LIBRATION_CENTRE_CYCLES × the episode's period) must carry the angle out of the episode's band beside it (\(\ge A_{\max}\) over as long again before or after; an arm the record cuts below SECULAR_STALL_ARM_MIN_FRACTION of the episode's span is not read) and keep inside the episode at least SECULAR_STALL_RATE_RATIO (0.5, a convention) of that rate. 348018 g−g5+s−s7: a 4° ripple on 4.4 turns, 0.73: non_resonant; the captures of 19289 and 278067 s−s6 read 0.04–0.05, 455327 s−s3 0.24.

A record-covering episode is never a wave (no motion beside it). The rule runs at every scale (a ripple filtered at the center scale is still one), and the exit and entry are read again on the episodes left.

Exit and entry. As for an MMR (Geometry), an arc of more than a turn is no piece of libration: when \(\sigma_f\) runs at least LIBRATION_EDGE_ARC_REV = 1 turn monotonically after the last turning point (before the first), the exit (entry) is observed, that end is not covered however short the gap, the angle is episodic and final_regime is a circulation from the exit. A secular angle has no orbit to average, so \(\sigma_f\) itself is read, against the episode's mean center; the center scale is then not tried. 2012 AX10 and 33325 in 2s − s4 − s6 over 20 Myr leave their libration near 16 Myr and run 1.9 and 1.7 turns to the end: transient (the end gap of 0.8 P does not count as covered). An exit that runs less than a turn stays exit_suspected.

Every angle_status rule condition angle_status an accepted episode covering the record (both ends within LIBRATION_COVERAGE_PERIODS periods, no observed exit or entry) libration (stationary or modulated center) accepted episodes, none covering episodic no episode; the center's largest monotone pass ≥ 1 turn circulation no turning point; the filtered angle turns ≥ 1 time circulation no turning point, less than a turn insufficient_time (arc when it spans at least half a turn, else stall) runs rejected for a moving center cover ≥ LIBRATION_DRIFT_MIN_WINDOW_FRACTION (0.5) of the window, the slow center monotone drift the same, the slow center turned back (largest pass < 1 turn) insufficient_time (few_cycles) otherwise (fewer turning points than one cycle) insufficient_time (few_cycles) a libration or episode under linear phases swinging no more than SECULAR_PHASE_UNCERTAINTY_FACTOR × \(\Delta\phi(T)\) insufficient_time (phase_unresolved) angle_status status reason libration resonant dynamic_libration episodic transient dynamic_episode circulation non_resonant circulation drift, insufficient_time uncertain baseline_needed (action extend; phase_unresolved: review) undefined invalid / uncertain unphysical (\(e > 1.3\), \(a < 0\)) / unusable_series

The response of \(e\) and \(i\). To leading order in \(e\) and \(i\), a secular term \(K\,e^{\lvert p\rvert}\sin^{\lvert q\rvert}(i/2)\cos\sigma\) of the averaged disturbing function drives \(\dot e \propto p\sin\sigma\) and \(\frac{d}{dt}\sin\frac i2 \propto q\sin\sigma\) (Lagrange's equations; Murray & Dermott 1999, eqs. 6.146 and 6.150, pp. 251–252). At finite inclination the equation for \(i\) also contains the perihelion derivative, so even \(q = 0\) need not give a zero response of \(\sin\frac i2\). The package fits \(\dot x = A\sin\sigma_f + B\cos\sigma_f + C\) for \(x = e\) and/or \(x = \sin\frac i2\), whichever the angle contains, with free amplitudes: a phase and shape diagnostic that does not enforce the theoretical coefficient. It is reported as check_secular_e_response (pass at \(R^2 \ge\) SECULAR_RESPONSE_R2_MIN = 0.5), a column only: it changes no status and no confidence.

How long to integrate. An uncertain verdict names the next check in extend_to_years: the baseline \(\tfrac32 P + 2P_c\) with \(P\) at least the shortest libration (500 kyr for a secular angle at the defaults), capped at four and at least twice the record; for ZLK the free-ω gate's cycles or frequency resolution, or review when no length would help (How long to extend). Before a run, the dry-run warns about a record shorter than that baseline (Dry-run).

Examples: 1222 in \(\nu_6\), 1020 in \(z_1\), 2306 one unfinished slow swing, 847 circulates, 363 too short.

docs.title: The Lidov-Kozai angle
docs.text:
What should librate? For a highly inclined orbit perturbed by a distant planet, the quadrupole problem makes the argument of perihelion \(\omega\) librate about 90° or 270° (Lidov's integrals). The package reports \(c_1\), \(c_2\) and \(h_{\rm quad}\) as diagnostics only; no threshold on them enters the status.

From which plane? The quadrupole problem's reference plane is the perturbers' orbital plane; the package measures \(\omega\), \(i\) and \(\Omega\) from the invariable plane (ZLK_ANGLE_FRAME, default invariable; ecliptic is kept for comparison), by rotating the orbit's angular momentum \(\mathbf h\) and perihelion vector \(\mathbf P\) exactly, never by subtracting angles. The free elements of a ZLK body, the gate, the attribution, the node lock, the e–i coupling and the figure use the same frame. The ecliptic is tilted by \(I = 1.58°\) from that plane: the ecliptic node of an orbit with \(i_{\rm inv} < I\) cannot turn (the orbit's pole circles the invariable pole without enclosing the ecliptic pole), so it librates about the plane's node, and with a bounded \(\varpi\) the ecliptic \(\omega\) looks confined while the invariable one circulates (555527, \(i_{\rm inv} \approx 1.6°\): non_resonant / circulation / certain on both records). At \(i \gtrsim 20°\) the two frames give the same number of turns. Rule zlk_invariable_frame marks a row whose two \(\omega\) part by a whole turn or more (zlk_frame_shift_turns).

The geometry of \(\omega\) is that of a secular angle with \(P_c = \max(F_{\rm GI} P_{\rm GI},\ P_{\min}/f_{\min})\) and no forced waves: \(F_{\rm GI}\) = ZLK_FILTER_GI_FACTOR = 2, \(P_{\min}\) = ZLK_LIBRATION_PERIOD_MIN_YR = 2 kyr, the prominence from ZLK_TP_PROMINENCE_DEG and ZLK_TP_RIPPLE_FACTOR. The shortest libration is then \(\max(P_{\min},\ 2P_c)\) = 3748 yr, not 2 kyr.

docs.title: Why a bounded \(\omega\) is not enough
docs.text:
The osculating \(\omega\) can be bounded without any Lidov-Kozai dynamics. When the forced eccentricity vector is longer than the free one, the point \((e\cos\varpi, e\sin\varpi)\) circles around the tip of the forced vector without enclosing the origin, so \(\varpi\) follows the forced vector's phase instead of turning on its own. The forced vector itself turns at the planets' frequencies, so this does not fix \(\varpi\); but when its phase and the node move together, \(\omega = \varpi - \Omega\) stays confined by the forcing alone. A true ZLK libration lives in the body's free elements, which is why the gate tests the free perihelion against the free node.

The free-\(\omega\) gate removes the forced parts of \(z_e\) and \(z_i\) at the planetary fundamentals and asks whether \(\omega_{\rm free} = \arg z_{e,\rm free} - \arg z_{i,\rm free}\) stays within a turn. Its outcome is confirmed (confined), kinematic (the free \(\omega\) winds) or no verdict (short_window, undefined_phase, planetary_residual, unavailable); the conditions are in Free elements: the gate. It judges every \(\omega\) that stays within a turn (libration, episodic, drift, insufficient_time).

From the outcome to the status (decide_status, check check_zlk_free_omega):

angle_status confirmed kinematic no verdict libration resonant / dynamic_libration (check pass) non_resonant / kinematic_libration, origin kinematic, detail free_omega_winds (check fail) uncertain / gate_unavailable, origin unknown episodic unchanged (also when confirmed inside its episodes, below) non_resonant / kinematic_libration only if \(\rho_{\max} < 1\) or every episode pinned (below), else read inside the episodes transient only if \(e\) and \(i\) trade at constant \(H\) inside the deciding episode, else uncertain / gate_unavailable (below) drift, insufficient_time unchanged non_resonant / kinematic_libration only if \(\rho_{\max} < 1\), else unchanged unchanged

With FREE_GATE_ENABLED off the outcome is disabled and the geometry's status stands. On a record that does not librate throughout, free elements fitted over the whole record cannot judge a change of regime, so only the strongest case changes it:

\[ \rho_{\max} = \max_t \frac{\operatorname{rollmed}_W \lvert z_{e,\rm free}\rvert}{\operatorname{rollmed}_W \lvert z_{e,\rm forced}\rvert} < 1, \qquad W = \max\bigl(\tfrac{1}{10}\text{ of the shortest beat of the fitted modes},\ k\,P_{\rm cyc}\bigr), \]

\(k\) = ZLK_RHO_WINDOW_CYCLES (1, a convention). Each radius is a rolling median over about one libration cycle, so the free radius of every part of the record is compared with the forced one of the same part: a free circle that grows in part of the record (and there encloses the origin) is seen, which one median free radius for the whole record missed. Below one, \(\varpi\) stays tied to the forced phase throughout; the condition is applied only together with a kinematic gate outcome (the free \(\omega\) winds). 555527: 0.66 at 100 kyr, 0.63 at 500 kyr (non_resonant, as the author labeled it). The former median ratio is the column zlk_gate_rho_global.

An episodic \(\omega\) is also kinematic when every librating episode is the forced vector's: inside each, the median of \(\lvert z_{e,\rm free}\rvert / \lvert z_{e,\rm forced}\rvert\) (instantaneous: a window as long as a forced beat would mix in the surroundings) is below 1, so the free circle stays off the origin there, and over the episode's whole cycles (first turning point to the last of the same kind) the free \(\omega\) advances at least ZLK_EPISODE_FREE_TURNS_PER_CYCLE = 0.5 turns per cycle (a convention: a kinematic cycle is one turn of the free vector about the forced one, since \(P_{\rm cyc}\) is their beat; a free \(\omega\) that librates with the osculating one returns after whole cycles, about 0). An episode the free elements do not measure (outside their baseline, a masked sample in it, fewer than two samples per cycle) pins nothing. Columns zlk_gate_rho_episodes (the largest median) and zlk_gate_free_turns_episodes (the fewest turns per cycle). 624 Hektor: its \(\omega\) circulates but swings back for one to three cycles wherever the free radius dips just below the forced one (0.99 at most inside, 2.0 over the record; 0.94 turns per cycle at least): non_resonant, episodic, kinematic. The real ZLK transients of the benchmark have 3.0–13.7 and at most 0.04.

The gate inside the episodes (ZLK_GATE_EPISODES). Between its episodes an episodic \(\omega\) circulates, so its free \(\omega\) winds over the record whatever it does inside them, and the record's outcome (kinematic, or a planetary_residual on the winding branch: over 500 kyr some \(g_j - s_k\) always lies within a width of \(b_\omega\)) says nothing about the episodes. Such a row is read inside its librating episodes with the confirmation test: in every one the free vector is the longer one (median \(\rho \ge 1\), column zlk_gate_rho_episodes_min) and the free \(\omega\) advances fewer than ZLK_EPISODE_FREE_TURNS_PER_CYCLE turns per cycle (zlk_gate_free_turns_episodes_max), and \(b_\varpi\), \(b_\Omega\) stay off the \(g\) and \(s\) modes → confirmed, zlk_gate_detail = episodes; a residual at a mode → planetary_residual; an episode the free elements do not measure keeps the record's outcome. 88899 over 500 kyr: 3.0 turns over the record, 0.005 turns per cycle and \(\rho \ge 8.2\) inside both episodes → confirmed; its \(e\)–\(i\) integral is not held there, an objection (transient/low, flag ei_integral_not_held). 1866, 373136, 3752 and 797204 (500 kyr) are confirmed the same way (origin dynamic).

kinematic_libration is a measurement and gate_unavailable the absence of one: keep them apart (legacy codes). A co-orbital of a planet whose own modes the split does not fit (Mercury to Mars) gets no verdict (unavailable, detail coorbital_unfitted_forcing): uncertain / gate_unavailable whatever bounded \(\omega\) it has, an episodic one, a drift or too few cycles included, since the model does not apply (2020 PP1 and 10563 over 500 kyr; rule zlk_coorbital_episodic). A Jupiter Trojan is covered, its forced vector being Jupiter's g5 + g6 (Free elements).

An episodic \(\omega\) without a gate verdict (any other no-verdict outcome) needs the physics of a ZLK cycle inside its deciding episode: \(e\) and \(i\) must trade so that the quadrupole integral \(H = \sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\) stays constant. At the episode's own period \(P\), on its samples only (the whole record also holds stretches where \(\omega\) circulates, which trade \(e\) for \(i\) near \(P\) as well), \(e\), \(i\), \(G = \sqrt{1-e^2}\), \(H\) and \(K = G(1-\cos i)\) are high-passed by a one-period running mean over the whole record and demodulated at \(P\) cycle by cycle; then

\[ \eta_H = \frac{\operatorname{rms}\,\delta H}{\lvert\cos i\rvert\,\operatorname{rms}\,\delta G} \]

is 0 when \(H\) is held and 1 as if \(i\) were frozen. The coupling zlk_ei_episode_coupling is zlk when \(i\) is in antiphase with \(e\) (within ZLK_EI_PHASE_TOL_DEG), the demodulated coherence is \(\le -\)ZLK_EI_EPISODE_MIN_COHERENCE and \(\eta_H \le\) ZLK_EI_H_RESIDUAL_MAX (0.5, a convention: the benchmark's ZLK episodes measure at most 0.28, the others at least 0.58); forced_beat the same in phase with \(K\); none; not_measured when the episode spans fewer than ZLK_EI_MIN_CYCLES = 3 periods (two independent estimators agree only by chance below that). In the full tree (v2_verdict) the row stays transient only on zlk, otherwise it is uncertain / gate_unavailable (−9), rule zlk_gate_unconfirmed; the minimal policy reads the same coupling as the e–i integral (below). 373136, 3752 and 797204 over 500 kyr stay transient (\(\eta_H\) 0.05–0.23 over 4.6–8 periods); 88899 over 500 kyr (\(e\) and \(i\) out of antiphase, \(\eta_H\) 1.2) and 797204 over 100 kyr and 2023 RS2 (deciding episodes of 1.5 and 2.4 periods) become uncertain. The record's coupling (zlk_ei_coupling) stays a column.

Under the minimal policy (the table above is the full tree's, kept in v2_verdict): the quadrupole problem, its integral thresholds (\(h^2 < 3/5\), \(c_1\), Kozai's 39.2°) and its half-turn symmetry hold only for a hierarchical, axisymmetric perturber, outside their domain for main-belt and planet-crossing asteroids (Gronchi & Milani 1999; Gallardo et al. 2012); none of them decides. The geometry of \(\omega\) gives the status (one revolution is \(2\pi\)), and the physics reads two measurements on the deciding episode:

  • the \(e\)–\(i\) integral above, measured on every bounded \(\omega\) (a libration too): broken (measured, not zlk) where the forced terms are small, \(\rho_{\max} \ge\) ZLK_RHO_KINEMATIC_EXCLUDED (3, a convention: a non-resonant forced \(e\) is at most ~0.1), is a veto, non_resonant / kinematic_libration, detail ei_integral_not_held (88899 over 500 kyr, \(\eta_H\) 1.24, \(\rho_{\max}\) 13); with larger forced terms it is an objection (flag ei_integral_not_held, level low), since the forcing itself breaks \(\sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\);
  • the forced vector: a gate kinematic on a libration is a veto (zlk_kinematic), and so is \(\rho_{\max} < 1\) over the record together with a kinematic gate on an episodic angle, a drift or too few cycles (zlk_free_e); the per-episode pin (a median) and an undefined free phase veto only together with a broken integral (624 Hektor: \(\eta_H\) 1.04), otherwise they are objections. \(\rho_{\max}\) is a ratio of two parts of one split, not a fact independent of it: 591986 refitted with g7 for the unresolved g5 gives 2.9 instead of 0.43, a planetary residual 0.83″/yr from g5 and resonant/low with gate_unavailable; the default split (g5, the one the 4-Myr record resolves) is kinematic.

A gate without a verdict keeps the geometry's status with the flag gate_unavailable at most medium, except when the integral holds and \(\rho_{\max} \ge\) ZLK_RHO_KINEMATIC_EXCLUDED: the forced vector cannot hold the perihelion, so the abstention (1981 Midas: its free node near \(s_6\)) is no cap and asks no extension (flag kinematic_excluded). Only a confirmed gate names a dynamic origin; otherwise the reason is geometric_libration/geometric_episode.

The scale. The gate's period is that of the deciding librating episode (the covering one, or the one with the most turning points; sec_decisive_period_yr), and zlk_gate_n_cycles = \(T/P\) counts cycles of the osculating \(\omega\). F, the \(e\)–\(i\) coupling, the \(\rho\) window and the extension read the same \(P\). Without a librating episode it is the median full period of the runs not faster than the floor. The median over every episode (\(P_{\rm cyc}\), geo_period_cycle_yr) is a column only: 2020 PP1's five episodes run from 2.3 to 34 kyr. The attribution of an \(\omega\) pinned inside every episode tests the beat against the episodes' pooled period, since each episode is a cycle of the same beat (624 Hektor). A libration at the center scale whose period is within a Rayleigh width of a beat \(2\pi/|g_k - g_j|\) of two fitted forced modes with nonzero amplitudes, whose reconstructed forced phase wave explains the center (correlation \(\ge\) ZLK_CENTRE_MODEL_R_MIN, swing within a factor ZLK_CENTRE_MODEL_AMP_FACTOR), while \(\rho_{\max} < 1\) at the fine period, is the forced vector turning its direction, not a libration of \(\omega\): the fine scale stays decisive (sec_centre_rejected = forced_beat:<gk>-<gj>). Without the per-mode amplitudes (an old file) there is no measured beat and no rejection. The guard acts only where the gate does: with the gate disabled, without a split or for a co-orbital whose forcing the split does not fit, the geometric scale stands.

Columns that change no status (Free elements: beyond the gate): the \(e\)–\(i\) coupling of the whole record at the decisive period (zlk_ei_coupling, every row; check_zlk_ei and confirmed_ei are zlk coupling; the deciding episode's own coupling zlk_ei_episode_* is a column too, except for an episodic row without a gate verdict), the attribution of a kinematic libration to a forced mode (zlk_forcing_*), the node lock (zlk_node_lock*) and the slow line of the center (zlk_centre_*, 591986: the g6−g5 beat). The strongest coherent line of the \(e\)–\(i\) cross-spectrum (Cross-spectral coherence) is the columns zlk_coherent, zlk_check.

Examples: 3040 librates, 591986 kinematic, 162474 over 1.5 Myr, 1981 without a verdict, 15527 circulates, 2010 HY22 unphysical.

docs.title: Confidence and output
docs.text:
The level follows the shared rule (Confidence); a suspected exit or entry caps it at medium. A secular angle has no physics margin; for ZLK it is G.

The margins and their classes

S = support, D = decisive (Confidence).

margin what full when N (S) turning points of the decisive episode above the minimum (thin at it, with the cap three_tp_episode, ≤ high) S (S) its center every cycle's band overlaps, with enough independent cycles; not measured with one; not applicable to a modulated center F (S) the filter the libration period ≥ FILTER_MIN_LIBRATION_CUTOFFS × \(P_c\); else not measured (flag filter_too_slow) P (D) a circulation its largest center pass ≥ 1 + CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND = 1.1 turns at every smoothing (×0.5, ×1, ×2); else thin G (D) ZLK: the gate confirmed with its cycle count clear of FREE_GATE_MIN_CYCLES by CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND; a kinematic outcome that decided the status is full

The summary row carries the analysis' columns (flt_*, geo_*, sec_*, rsp_*, zlk_gate*, ep_*; Output data); the runs of turning points go to episodes.csv; the figure is the one-page combined figure (Plots).

docs.title: From the integration to the angle
docs.text: The integration saves the elements of the body and of the planets every \(\Delta t\) years. Before anything can be said about libration, three questions must be answered: can this step follow the angle at all, which part of the signal is the libration, and is the answer stable when the filter changes? This page describes these steps for a mean-motion resonance; secular and Lidov-Kozai angles use their own cutoff (Secular and Lidov-Kozai). The dry-run applies the same rules to the initial elements, before the integration starts.

docs.title: The angle and its rate
docs.text:
The angle \(\sigma\), its rate model \( u(a)\) and the exact resonance \(a_*\), where \( u(a_*) = 0\), are defined on The resonant pendulum. Here \( u(a)\) is used only to predict how far the angle turns between two saved points; whether \(\dot\sigma\) really follows it is tested later (Is it this resonance?).

\(\sigma mod 2\pi\) is exact at every saved point. What can go wrong is the count of whole turns between two points, and the presence of short-period terms that the step cannot resolve.

docs.title: What the output step can resolve
docs.text:
Question: between two saved points, does the angle turn by less than half a revolution? Only the \(\lambda\) part of \(\sigma\) can turn fast; \(\varpi\), \(\Omega\) and the planets' slow angles are sampled exactly. If the angle turns by \( u\Delta t\) per step, the sampled series cannot distinguish \( u\) from \( u - 2\pi m/\Delta t\) for any integer \(m\). The alias branch and the apparent rate are (Knežević & Milani 2000, §2.2, p. 22)

\[ m = \operatorname{round}\!\left( rac{ u\,\Delta t}{2\pi} ight), \qquad u_ ext{app} = u - rac{2\pi m}{\Delta t}. \]

The step is judged over the range of \(a\) the body visits (its 1st to 99th percentile):

smp_verdict condition meaning resolved \(\lvert u vert\Delta t \le\) MMR_STEP_RESOLVED_DEG = 90° everywhere the step follows the angle marginal \(\lvert u vert\Delta t \le 180°\), branch \(m = 0\) followed, with little margin aliased_unambiguous one branch \(m e 0\) a circulation the step folds; its true rate is known ambiguous several branches the step cannot tell the rate

Two derived numbers help to read an aliased record:

  • the ghost: the semi-major axis \(a_m\) where branch \(m\) looks like an exact resonance, \( u(a_m) = 2\pi m/\Delta t\). A body near \(a_m\) shows an almost stationary sampled angle, a perfect imitation of a libration;
  • the Nyquist half-width: the offset from \(a_*\) at which \(\sigma\) turns by \(\pi\) per step. With \(\lvert c vert = 3\lvert k vert n/(2a)\),
\[ \delta a_N = rac{\pi}{\lvert c vert\,\Delta t} = rac{a^{5/2}}{3\lvert k vert\,\Delta t}\quad( ext{au, yr}). \]

Threshold. An aliased circulation (circulation, subtype alias) is non_resonant with reason alias only when the branch is unique and the body is far from the resonance: a libration needs \(\dot\sigma \simeq c\,(a - a_*)\) to change sign, so the slow \(a\) must reach \(a_*\). The far ratio is

\[ ext{far ratio} = rac{\lvert\langle a angle - a_* vert}{\max\!\left( frac12(a_{99} - a_{1}),\ \lvert a(\dot\lambda) - \langle a angle vert ight)} \ \ge\ exttt{MMR\_C5\_FAR\_RATIO\_MIN} = 3, \]

where \(a(\dot\lambda)\) is the semi-major axis that the measured mean motion implies. Several branches, or one branch close to \(a_*\), cannot exclude a libration hidden by the step: the verdict is invalid / alias with action = resample and a suggested step (resample_step_yr).

docs.title: Counting the turns: the predictive unwrap
docs.text:
numpy.unwrap adds, at each step, the increment of smallest modulus; at an aliased step that is the wrong one. The package unwraps by the rate model instead, separately for the fast and the slow part of the angle. Write \(\sigma = \psi_\lambda + s\), with \(s = p\varpi + v\Omega + \sum_j(p_j\varpi_j + v_j\Omega_j)\) the slow part. The longitude part \(\psi_\lambda = (\sigma - s) mod 2\pi\) is unwrapped with the rate model without the slow rate:

\[ \psi_i = \psi_{i-1} + ar u_{\lambda,i}\Delta t + \operatorname{wrap}\!\left(\psi_i^{ mod 2\pi} - \psi_{i-1} - ar u_{\lambda,i}\Delta t ight), \qquad ar u_{\lambda,i} = u\!\left( frac{a_{i-1} + a_i}{2} ight) - u_ ext{slow}, \]

with \(\operatorname{wrap}\) into \([-\pi, \pi)\) and \( u_ ext{slow}\) the mean rate of the slow part measured on the record (column ctx_slow_rate_arcsec_yr). The slow part is then put back with its own winding: the body's \(\varpi\) takes its turns from the low-passed eccentricity vector \(\operatorname{LP}[e\,e^{i\varpi}]\) (band MMR_JITTER_BAND_YR), not from the osculating \(\varpi\), so that fast loops of the eccentricity vector around zero insert no spurious slow turns. If a planet's slow element needed by \(s\) was not saved, the full angle is unwrapped with the full \( u\). The residual of the \(\lambda\) part measures how well the model predicts every step. Question: can the record be stitched? Yes when its 99th percentile is \(\le\) MMR_UNWRAP_MAX_RESID_P99_DEG = 45° and its largest value \(\le\) MMR_UNWRAP_MAX_RESID_DEG = 135°. Otherwise the angle is undefined / alias and the verdict invalid. Where the eccentricity passes near zero, \(\varpi\) itself can turn by up to \(\pi\) between two points at any step; this is not an alias (flag varpi_fast_low_e). Question: is the phase defined at all? The verdict is invalid / undefined_phase when three things hold together: the perihelion jitter \(\lvert p vert\,\delta e/ ar e\) exceeds MMR_JITTER_MAX_RAD = 0.785 rad, the full angle fails the residual limits above, and \(\varpi\)'s own scatter about the low-passed vector \(e\,e^{i\varpi}\) exceeds that limit on more than MMR_VARPI_UNDEFINED_MAX_SHARE = 0.5 of the record. The jitter alone, with \(\varpi\) defined, is only a flag and the cap jitter_low_e (at most medium).

docs.title: The cutoff: what is libration and what is noise
docs.text:
Question: which periods can a libration of this angle have? The filtered angle \(\sigma_f\) must keep every libration and remove the short-period terms: the orbital period and the synodic periods with the planets of the angle, \(P_{\text{syn},j} = 2\pi/\lvert n - n_j\rvert\) (\(2\pi/(n + n_j)\) for a retrograde orbit, with \(n, n_j > 0\)). The cutoff period is

\[ P_c = \max\!\left(1.5\,\max_j P_{\text{syn},j},\ \ 1.5\,P_\text{orb},\ \ \frac{P_\text{floor}}{2}\right), \]

with the factors MMR_FILTER_SYNODIC_FACTOR = 1.5 and MMR_FILTER_ORBIT_FACTOR = 1.5 (a convention), the body's own period \(P_\text{orb} = 2\pi/n(\langle a\rangle)\) and the divisor FILTER_MIN_LIBRATION_CUTOFFS = 2 (flt_cutoff_binding names the bound that sets \(P_c\)).

The orbit bound is there because heliocentric elements osculate about \(GM_\odot\) alone, while a body moves about the Sun and the planets inside its orbit, of mass \(\varepsilon M_\odot\) (\(\varepsilon \approx 1.34\times10^{-3}\) for Jupiter to Neptune). From the energy integral, \(1/a_\text{osc} = (1+\varepsilon)/a - 2\varepsilon/r\), so \(a\) (and \(\lambda\)) carry a wave at the body's own \(P_\text{orb}\) of half-amplitude \(\approx 2\varepsilon e a\): measured 0.126 au for 15874 (0.128 predicted), 0.038 au for 523683 (0.038). An inner body has \(P_{\text{syn},j} > P_\text{orb}\) with every outer planet, and so has an outer body inside the planet's 1:2, so the orbit bound acts only beyond a 1:2 (\(P_\text{orb} > P_{\text{syn},j}\)): TNOs and Centaurs against Uranus or Neptune. Without it the synodic bound let that wave through as libration cycles (523683 2U-9, 379 yr). Barycentric elements would remove the wave at its source; they change \(a\) and every angle and are a separate study. \(P_\text{floor}\) is the shortest libration the angle may have:

  • MMR_LIBRATION_PERIOD_MIN_YR = 150 yr for every MMR except the 1:1. This is a convention, not a physical minimum. Faster "episodes" are treated as forced waves of nearby commensurabilities. Hence \(P_c = 75\) yr whenever the synodic periods are below 50 yr;
  • for a co-orbital (1:1) angle, MMR_COORBITAL_PERIOD_FLOOR_FACTOR = 0.5 times the linear tadpole period of the planet, \(P_\text{orb}/\sqrt{27\mu/4}\) (Murray & Dermott 1999, eq. 3.151, p. 94): 147.8 yr for Jupiter, giving \(P_\text{floor} = 73.9\) yr and \(P_c = 36.9\) yr; 222 yr for the Earth. The planet of a 1:1 angle does not enter the synodic bound: its synodic angle is the resonant angle itself. A quasi-satellite librates faster than a tadpole; when the orbit-averaged angle stays in the quasi-satellite well long enough, the record is analyzed again with the floor set by the period of that well (rule G1q). A horseshoe that turns close to the planet is faster than a tadpole too: a run whose turning points, read on the orbit-averaged angle, all reflect on a top of the averaged potential (the planet's or L3's) gets its own floor, 0.5 times the period of the loop through those turns, provided its local 1:1 law has \(K/K_\text{th} > 0\) (rule coorbital_floor_profile, pendulum; 2003 YN107: a 103-yr cycle turning 2° from the Earth, loop 119 yr, floor 59 yr instead of 111 yr). Other runs keep the tadpole floor. The cutoff stays the tadpole floor's; what the prominence counts as fast is what is faster than the shortest floor any run can get, 0.5 times the fastest horseshoe loop turning MMR_COORBITAL_MIN_TURN_HILL = 3 Hill radii from the planet (at most the tadpole floor; Earth, circular: 57 yr), else the horseshoe itself raised the prominence over its own swing (YN107: 233°);
  • a two-body angle (not 1:1) keeps 150 yr, but a cycle below it can still be accepted by a second pass at the floor of its own averaged potential, \(T_{0,\text{th}}/\sqrt{x}\) (\(x\) = MMR_STRENGTH_CHECK_RATIO), when the theory, the center and L4 confirm it (rule G1f, status tree); preprocess.profile_period_floor is the shared hook (the 1:1 floor is the run's own loop above; three-body angles keep 150 yr).

A short run counts as a near-episode (the confidence cap near_episode) when its period is at least its floor times \(1 - b\), \(b\) = CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND = 0.1, for every MMR: a run within the thin margin of the floor is a thin miss of an episode too.

MMR_FILTER_CUTOFF_YR overrides the rule. The output step does not enter \(P_c\): as in the classical proper-element filters, the band is set by the physics, and the filter is applied before any decimation (Nesvorný & Morbidelli 1998, §2, p. 3030; Knežević & Milani 2000, §2.2, pp. 22–23).

docs.title: The filter
docs.text:
\(\sigma\) (unwrapped, with its linear trend removed and put back afterwards, so the number of turns is kept) and \(a\) are low-passed by a Butterworth filter of order \(N\) = FILTER_ORDER = 2, applied forward and backward. The forward-backward pass has zero phase shift and the steady-state amplitude gain

\[ G(P) = \left[1 + \left(\frac{\tan(\pi\Delta t/P)}{\tan(\pi\Delta t/P_c)}\right)^{2N}\right]^{-1} \ \xrightarrow{\ \Delta t \ll P_c\ }\ \left[1 + \left(\frac{P_c}{P}\right)^{4}\right]^{-1}. \]

\(G(P_c) = 0.5\) exactly. In the small-step limit \(G(2P_c) \approx 0.94\) and \(G(P_c/1.5) \approx 0.165\): where the floor sets \(P_c\), the shortest libration keeps 94 % of its amplitude, and the synodic terms, at most \(P_c/1.5\), keep at most 16.5 %. At a finite step the digital expression is sharper (for \(\Delta t = P_c/3\), \(G(2P_c) = 81/82\)); the analysis uses it. The filter's edges spread over about \(P_c\); turning points and everything measured on them are taken in the window \([t_0 + P_c,\ t_1 - P_c]\) (FILTER_EDGE_TRIM_CUTOFFS = 1).

When the planets' longitudes are saved, the planets' own slow inequalities (the 900-yr Jupiter–Saturn great inequality) enter \(\sigma\) linearly through \(\sum_j k_j\lambda_j\) and are subtracted exactly before filtering.

The ripple in detail

\(\sigma_\text{clean} = \sigma - \sum_j k_j\,\delta\lambda_j^\text{slow}\) (MMR_RIPPLE_REMOVE, band MMR_RIPPLE_BAND_YR). Without saved planets the flag ripple_not_removed is set and the predicted ripple raises the turning-point prominence (What the angle does). A co-orbital angle keeps its planet's longitude as it is: the body follows the planet's slow longitude.

docs.title: Can the record be filtered at all?
docs.text: Question: does a filter with this cutoff exist at this step? A digital low-pass needs its cutoff above the Nyquist period, \(P_c > 2\Delta t\). If \(P_c \le 2\Delta t\) the verdict is invalid / undersampled before anything is measured, with action = resample at a round step from MMR_RESAMPLE_STEPS_YR that keeps MMR_RESAMPLE_STEPS_PER_CYCLE = 20 samples per shortest libration. For an ordinary MMR this happens at \(\Delta t \ge 37.5\) yr; for a Jupiter Trojan at \(\Delta t \ge 18.5\) yr.

docs.title: Is the libration itself shaped by the filter?
docs.text: Question: does the filter keep the observed libration? If the gain at the measured libration period is below MMR_L8_GAIN_FULL = 0.94 read with the thin band CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND of its ratio (0.911: roughly \(P_\text{cyc} < 1.8P_c\), as the period floor is read at × 0.9; 2001 WK15 32E-39, 143 yr at \(P_c\) = 75 yr), the shape of the libration (its amplitude, center and energy) is partly the filter's. The flag filter_too_slow is set and the checks that read the shape are not_measured: the identity L3, the force law L4 and the amplitude check B1 of the response, both potential checks R0, one pendulum, and the margins L2 (separatrix distance), L5 and L6 (center shift). A margin that already failed or does not apply keeps its value; the numbers themselves stay in the output.

docs.title: A shorter cutoff for a slow libration: the scale ladder (G2c)
docs.text:
Question: is the center scale itself hiding the libration's cycles? The center scale \(W_c\) (geometry) trims \(W_c\) from each end of the record. For a slow libration (\(P_\text{slow}\) comparable to the record) the trimmed window may hold fewer than LIBRATION_CENTRE_MIN_ESTIMATES = 2 slow periods, so the tree sees one cycle where the record holds two. Then shorter cutoffs are tried,

\[ W_k = f_k\,\min\!\left(W_c,\ \frac{P_\text{slow}}{2}\right),\qquad f_k \in \texttt{MMR\_SCALE\_LADDER} = 0.71, 0.5, 0.35, \dots, \qquad W_k \ge \max(P_c,\ 3\,P_\text{fast}), \]

\(P_\text{slow}\) being the libration's period at \(W_c\) (from its phase return when it closes only one cycle) and \(P_\text{fast}\) the shortest full period of the fine turning points (the fast wave: at \(3P_\text{fast}\) the filter keeps \(G \approx 0.012\) of it; the factor is LIBRATION_CENTRE_CYCLES). Walking down, a rung holds while its turning points at the center prominence \(p_c\) agree, in their common window, with those at \(W_c\) and at the rung above: the same number and kind, each within MMR_SCALE_TP_TIME_TOL = 0.1 \(P_\text{slow}\). The shortest rung that holds is taken when it shows more slow extrema than \(W_c\), and its verdict is kept when it again decides libration (columns geo_scale_ladder_*, rule scale_ladder). With neither the force law L4 nor R0 with \(a\) measured there, only the directly averaged strength supports it: the cap slow_scale_provisional holds it at medium; a record of \(\ge 5.25\,P\) decides.

385533 in 7N−12 (100 kyr): at \(W_c\) = 22.7 kyr only the extrema at 44.8 and 67.6 kyr remain (one cycle closed by its phase return, \(P\) = 45.4 kyr; uncertain). \(P_\text{fast}\) = 1.95 kyr (the residual's spectral peak, 3°), so the ladder stops above 5.85 kyr; at 7.95 kyr four extrema 19.5–89.5 kyr agree with \(W_c\) within 0.004 \(P\), F by direct averaging passes (\(T_{0,\text{th}}\) 33.9–36.8 kyr against 34.4 kyr observed): resonant, medium. The other G2c rows of the benchmark hold 1.5–8.5 slow periods in their window (136108, 15875, TX9) or find no libration at the rung (182223) and keep \(W_c\).

docs.title: Short periods folded by the step
docs.text:
Question: do the short-period terms of the elements fold into slow, fake lines? A step at or above half the shortest of the orbital and synodic periods,

\[ \Delta t \ \ge\ \tfrac12\min\left(P_\text{orb},\ P_{\text{syn},j}\right), \]

folds those terms to low frequencies, \(\lvert m/P - \operatorname{round}(m\Delta t/P)/\Delta t\rvert\), where no filter of the record can remove them. Below that step the same happens when a harmonic \(m \le\) MMR_SHORT_PERIOD_HARMONICS = 2 of \(P_\text{orb}\) or \(P_{\text{syn},j}\) folds to a period longer than the shortest libration. Either case sets the flag short_period_aliased. How much of the folded terms reaches \(\sigma_f\) and \(a_f\) depends on their amplitude, which the record cannot measure. The folded lines move \(\sigma_f\) little, but they enter \(a_f\), and the checks that read \(a\) (the identity and the force law). Hence:

  • the full tree caps every record with the flag at medium (cap short_period_aliased, in v2_verdict); the minimal policy keeps it as a flag only (Confidence);
  • except a plain geometric circulation (reason circulation or alias with no forced-wave runs): it reads neither the identity nor the force law, so the flag stays and the cap does not apply (MMR_SHORT_PERIOD_CAP_CIRCULATION = False);
  • the record itself never lifts the cap (MMR_SHORT_PERIOD_CAP_RATIO = 0; a positive value enables an opt-in lift);
  • the record gets smp_fold_free_step_yr, the largest step of MMR_RESAMPLE_STEPS_YR below its own at which nothing folds (sampling.fold_free_step). When the cap is what holds the confidence down (confidence.cap_binds), the action is resample at that step.

The same test (sampling.short_period_trigger) is the dry-run's predicate.

The scatter of \(a\) at short periods against the libration's own swing of \(a\) (smp_da_sp_over_a_excursion) above MMR_SHORT_PERIOD_A_RATIO = 0.5 sets the warning flag a_short_period_scatter. On a folding step with that much scatter, a failed identity or force law is read as not_measured (not as a failure) when the strength of the directly averaged potential passes (MMR_SHORT_PERIOD_A_UNMEASURED = True); a failure never becomes a pass.

docs.title: Smoothing for derivatives
docs.text:
\(\dot\sigma\) and \(\dot a\) multiply whatever leaks through the filter by \(P_\text{cyc}/P_\text{syn}\). The response of \(a\) (Is it this resonance?) is therefore read after a second smoothing at

\[ \max\!\left(P_c,\ 0.1\,P_\text{cyc}\right), \]

with the fraction MMR_RESPONSE_CUTOFF_CYCLES = 0.1. When \(0.1\,P_\text{cyc}\) sets this cutoff and the step is small, the libration and its harmonics up to the fifth keep \(G \ge 0.94\) of their amplitude. When \(P_c\) is larger, it sets the bandwidth: harmonic \(m\) keeps \(G(P_\text{cyc}/m)\) at cutoff \(P_c\). The energy and the separatrix zone read the angle at \(\max(P_c,\ 0.2\,P_\text{cyc})\) (SEPARATRIX_CUTOFF_CYCLES = 0.2).

docs.title: The ×2 filter guard
docs.text:
Question: would a slightly heavier filter tell a different story? A forced wave that \(P_c\) lets through makes turning points and stalls of its own; a filter twice as long damps it, while a real libration with \(G(P_\text{cyc}) \ge 0.94\) survives. The decisive numbers are measured again at \(2P_c\) on the interval both filters see, on the episode the status rests on and its counterpart at \(2P_c\) (the episode that overlaps it most in time):

quantity changed when setting turning points the counts differ by more than \(\max(2,\ 0.1 N)\), or one full cycle appears or vanishes MMR_FILTER_GUARD_TP_ABS = 2, MMR_FILTER_GUARD_TP_REL = 0.1 episode not reproduced, or its start or end moves by more than one libration period MMR_FILTER_GUARD_BOUNDARY_PERIODS = 1 stalls appear or vanish — energy \(h\) (median per cycle) crosses \(h = 1\), or changes by more than \(0.1\max(1, \lvert h\rvert)\) MMR_FILTER_GUARD_H_TOL = 0.1 shape the largest half-amplitude changes by more than 20 %, or the amplitude or center-shift check flips MMR_FILTER_GUARD_AMP_REL = 0.2

The energy and the shape are compared only when \(2P_c\) itself keeps the libration (\(G \ge 0.94\)). A change sets the flag filter_sensitive and empties the checks that read the changed quantity. The guard runs before the status tree: a passed energy check (the pendulum test R0 with \(a\)) that the guard withdraws is not_measured for the tree too (column flt_withdrawn_before_tree), so the withdrawal can change the branch the tree takes. A failed check stays an objection: the guard never turns a failure into support.

docs.title: Worked example: 1999 UQ in 7E+2M−9
docs.text:
The near-Earth asteroid 1999 UQ (\(a = 1.094\) au, \(e = 0.016\)) was integrated for 20 kyr and saved twice, every 5.0012 yr and every 1 yr. The angle \(\sigma = 7\lambda_E + 2\lambda_M - 9\lambda\) turns at \(\nu \approx 72°\)/yr, once every 5.0 yr; the exact resonance is at \(a_* = 1.0760\) au.

step 5.0012 yr step 1 yr turn per step \(\lvert\nu\rvert\Delta t\) 354°–365° 71°–73° branch \(m\), smp_verdict 1, aliased_unambiguous 0, resolved apparent rate ≈ 0°/yr (−0.004°/yr measured) 72°/yr revolutions in 20 kyr: numpy.unwrap / predictive −0.16 / 3998.8 3998.9 / 3998.9 ghost \(a_1\) 1.094176 au, \(4\times10^{-6}\) au from \(\langle a\rangle\) — Nyquist half-width \(\delta a_N\) 0.0093 au 0.046 au far ratio 66 66 verdict non_resonant / circulation (alias), reason alias, certain non_resonant / circulation, reason circulation, certain

At the 5-yr step the record is a stroboscope: the body sits on the ghost of branch 1, and the plainly unwrapped angle stands almost still for 20 kyr. The step verdict (one branch) and the far ratio (the body is 66 of its own \(a\) swings from \(a_*\)) prove that this is a circulation folded by the step, so the verdict is non_resonant / alias, not invalid. Both steps fold the orbital period (\(P_\text{orb} = 1.14\) yr, so \(\Delta t \ge 0.57\) yr) and carry the flag short_period_aliased, but as plain circulations they are not capped. The fold-free step of this record is 0.5 yr. Both figures are in the Gallery.

docs.title: The status tree
docs.text:
The geometry (What the angle does) says what \(\sigma\) does over the record: angle_status. The physics (Is it this resonance?) measures whether \(a\) answers \(\sigma\) as the pendulum of this resonance requires. The status tree combines the two, always in the same order, into status, reason and libration_origin. The first question that has an answer decides; the later ones are not asked.

The order follows one principle: a cause outside this resonance is looked for before the libration is credited to it. A bounded \(\sigma\) is first checked against the sampling (can the record be read at all?), then against other resonances (a member of the same multiplet, another commensurability), then against pure geometry (the perihelion term), and only then is its own force law measured.

This page describes mean-motion resonances (two-body, three-body, retrograde, co-orbital). Secular and Lidov-Kozai angles use a shorter tree, given in Secular and Lidov-Kozai.

docs.title: Minimal policy (default)
docs.text:
The tree below runs first and measures everything; a policy layer (resonance/analysis/policy.py) then re-reads the finished analysis by a few principles:

  1. Status from the geometry of \(\sigma_f\). libration → resonant, episodic → transient, near_separatrix → near_separatrix, circulation → non_resonant. A drift whose slow center passes ≥ one own revolution → non_resonant/modulated_circulation, less → uncertain. insufficient_time → uncertain, or non_resonant/circulation when the record ends in circulation (\(\sigma_f\) travels ≥ one own revolution after the last turning point of an accepted or candidate run; for an MMR, of any run, accepted or rejected, or candidate span in the window, one that runs past the window's end counting at that end; a secular or ZLK travel below \(1 +\) CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND turns holds the level at medium). One own revolution is \(2\pi\), for a ZLK \(\omega\) too (the half-turn symmetry of the quadrupole's \(\cos 2\omega\) is not general; ZLK runs still break at half a turn). The geometry alone names no mechanism: a secular or ZLK libration is geometric_libration/geometric_episode, origin unknown, unless a confirmed ZLK gate makes it dynamic.
  2. Only a measured contradiction vetoes a bounded angle (column veto): an owner that induces the episode (step 2), a kinematic origin (step 3, K2, K3s), a two-body strength from the disturbing function far below the need (5s; the angle's word is then circulation or drift: no run is its libration), every counted episode below 45° being the forced wave its background carries (forced_wave: at the episode's own period the envelopes of \(\sigma\) and \(a\) inside stay within the band the same steady wave shows within MMR_FORCED_WAVE_REFERENCE_PERIODS periods around it; a libration adds its own swing; some such episodes leave the count; 2012 KL9; runs found forced join the background of the others; when the slow center passes less than a revolution the drift rule decides instead: uncertain / drift), the ZLK gate measured kinematic on a libration, the free \(e\) below the forced \(e\) over the record (zlk_free_e; inside every episode or with an undefined free phase only when the \(e\)–\(i\) integral is broken too), or the \(e\)–\(i\) exchange of the deciding ZLK episode breaking \(\sqrt{1-e^2}\cos i\) where the forced terms are small, \(\rho_{\max} \ge\) ZLK_RHO_KINEMATIC_EXCLUDED (zlk_integral; with larger forced terms it is an objection, ei_integral_not_held; Secular and ZLK). Every other leaf that moved a status (5a, 5b, 5e, 5f, 5g, 5o, 5x, 5n, 5s three-body, 5s*, 2j, a ZLK gate without a verdict) gives the geometry's status back with a flag: measured_objection and strength_scale_implausible set the level to low, gate_unavailable/gate_disabled to at most medium (not when the integral holds and \(\rho_{\max} \ge\) ZLK_RHO_KINEMATIC_EXCLUDED: flag kinematic_excluded, no cap, no extension). A veto within CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND of its threshold still moves the status, at medium (veto_thin).
  3. The level from the evidence (Confidence); no caps.
  4. Everything else is a flag: every cap of the full tree, zone, owner, subresonance and edge mark. The alias (C5) and the undersampled step stay.
  5. Extend only for an unfinished libration at the record's end (an end-edge 1:1 leg A1, an end-edge half-swing A2, insufficient_time or a last counted episode at the end with fewer than CONFIDENCE_HIGH_CYCLES cycles A), a deciding period above \(2T/\)LIBRATION_MIN_TURNING_POINTS (B), or a needed veto not measured for lack of length (flag veto_needs_length: MMR L4 short of force windows, a ZLK gate short_window/planetary_residual) whose record pol_veto_need_yr is within the next-check budget MMR_NEXT_CHECK_SPAN_FACTOR\(\,T\) (C, extend to that record). Never when the record ends in circulation or the level is certain (a certain row asks for nothing: action none) (column pol_extend_clause). A needed veto beyond the budget keeps the flag and goes to review. The length asked for is the next check of the deciding period's missing cycles, at least of the baseline's estimate when that is a slow swing seen in part (base_period_source arc_slow, b5, two_omega, modulation: its slow cycles), within MMR_NEXT_CHECK_SPAN_FACTOR\(\,T\) (523683 2U-9: 400 kyr, three slow cycles of 112 kyr).
  6. Episodes: the figure and n_counted_episodes show only the counted episodes; candidates are drawn faint. One clean 1:1 leg (G4c) is a transient of half a cycle; a half-swing between passages (G4h) is a candidate of a circulation; an end-edge one extends.
  7. ZLK and secular follow the same rules; a secular swing below the mode-phase uncertainty stays uncertain/phase_unresolved (review), never non_resonant.

The verdict of the full tree stays in v2_verdict (status/confidence/reason/action/angle_status); pol_decided_by names the step that gave the final status (tree when the policy kept the tree's, ;not_upheld:<leaf> when it did not uphold the leaf's veto) and pol_objection_check the checks behind a measured objection (Output).

docs.title: The tree
docs.text:
The rest of this page is the full tree itself: what v2_verdict reports, and what the minimal policy reads.

flowchart TD

    G0 -->|yes| T{angle_status}

docs.title: Before the tree: can the record be read?
docs.text:
These checks come before any geometry. A record that fails one of them gets status = invalid: the run says nothing about the resonance at these settings, and the action says how to repair it.

question test reason action Is the angle a resonance of this body at all? the coefficient of the body's \(\lambda\) is \(k \ne 0\) invalid_input review Is the orbit an ellipse? \(a > 0\), \(0 \le e < 1\), all values finite unphysical review Can the filter keep the shortest libration? \(P_c > 2\,\Delta t\) (signal) undersampled resample Can the angle be unwrapped without guessing turns? unwrap residuals at most MMR_UNWRAP_MAX_RESID_P99_DEG = 45° (99th percentile) and MMR_UNWRAP_MAX_RESID_DEG = 135° (largest) alias (angle_status = undefined) resample (review when no finer step helps) Is \(\varpi\) defined? (very small \(e\)) the \(p\varpi\) part jitters by more than MMR_JITTER_MAX_RAD = 0.785 rad, the full angle cannot be unwrapped, and \(\varpi\) is undefined over more than MMR_VARPI_UNDEFINED_MAX_SHARE = 0.5 of the record undefined_phase review

docs.title: Steps in order
docs.text:
The tree reads the angle as the status reads it: a record that librates in episodes and then circulates, or librates before a jump of \(a\), or is captured after one, is judged as the episodic angle its episodes show. The reported angle_status may then differ from the word the tree read; see below. The episodes the tree counts are the geometry's: for an angle that is not 1:1, a center step or a stall between two accepted pieces in one libration region is a mark of one episode, not a boundary (rule regime_cut_mark, geometry); a single half-libration between circulations is G4h below.

G6. Too short. angle_status = insufficient_time (too few turning points, an arc, a stall): uncertain, baseline_needed, action extend (Confidence gives the length asked for); action review when the period that decides already fits the record (base_cause): more time would decide nothing.

A ripple on an unfinished slow swing (rule ripple_on_arc, MMR_RIPPLE_ON_ARC) does not stop G6. An accepted episode is set aside before G2, as an unconfirmed ripple (forced_wave = unconfirmed_ripple), when its half-amplitude stays below MMR_A_RESPONSE_MIN_AMP_DEG = 45° (there neither the force law nor \(V_E pprox V_F\) can be measured), its identity does not pass (fails, or cannot be measured on so few cycles: nothing confirms it), and the slow center turns back once or twice within one revolution (fewer than three turns: no full slow cycle). A record-covering episode and a 1:1 angle are never set aside; a real small libration keeps its passing identity. G6 then counts only the turning points outside the ripples; with none the slow center decides: one turn → the G5a arc, else arc or stall by its range. 2004 YG1 9M-10J-4 over 20 kyr: a 3° ripple at the turn of a 281° slow swing → uncertain / insufficient_time (arc), extend to 50 kyr; 2002 BG 1E-10S-1 over 20 kyr: a 2° 735-yr ripple (identity not measured) at the one turn of a 1.68-rad slow swing → the same, extend to 50 kyr (the slow swing's baseline; over 100 kyr its center drifts 1.6 revolutions: non_resonant).

A slow swing in the resonance's own well (rule G5w, slow_swing_in_well, MMR_SLOW_SWING_IN_WELL). A drift needs a center that keeps going: G5a already reads one slow turn back as an arc. With two turns the record holds one half-swing between them, and the labeled drifts of 101703 and 142694 1V+3S-7 have two turns too, so the turns alone decide nothing. The half-swing reads as part of a slow libration of this resonance, insufficient_time / arc (instead of drift, or of few_cycles for the fast turning points riding on it), when it obeys the resonance's pendulum: the identity \(\dot\sigma_s = c\,(a_s - a_*)\) holds on σ and \(a\) low-passed at W_c, and between the turns both the \(a\) swing (one side: \(a_*\) to \(a_* + 2\omega_0\sin(A/2)/|c|\)) and the period \(2(t_2-t_1)\) agree with the directly averaged well at the half-swing's amplitude \(A\) (\(T_{0,\text{th}}\), \(T = T_{0,\text{th}}F(A)\), \(F = \tfrac{2}{\pi}K(\sin^2\tfrac{A}{2})\)) within \([1/\sqrt{x}, \sqrt{x}]\), \(x\) = MMR_STRENGTH_CHECK_RATIO (no new threshold). Anything unmeasured (three-body: no direct theory; 1:1; one or three turns) leaves the row as it was. The extension asks for MMR_EXTEND_SLOW_CYCLES = 3 slow periods (a budget). 523683 2U-9 over 100 kyr (its 379-yr cycles are its own orbital period, cut off by the cutoff ≥ 1.5 \(P_\text{orb}\)): turns at 11.9 and 67.7 kyr, \(A\) = 114°, identity 1.00, \(a\) swing 1.07 ×, period 1.00 × → uncertain / insufficient_time, extend to 400 kyr. 101703 and 142694 fail the slow identity (slope/c −0.27, −0.25) and stay drift.

A cycle faster than the floor (rule G1f, MMR_SUBFLOOR_PASS). The 150-yr floor stays, but a two-body angle (not 1:1) without a libration over the record is analyzed once more at the floor of its own averaged potential, \(\max(T_{0,\text{th}}/\sqrt{x},\ 2\Delta t \cdot\) FILTER_MIN_LIBRATION_CUTOFFS\()\), \(x\) = MMR_STRENGTH_CHECK_RATIO, when that is below the floor. \(T_{0,\text{th}}\) is the shortest small-amplitude period of the directly averaged potential at the snapshots whose swings lie in its well (no episode needed; a pendulum only gets slower with amplitude). The pass replaces the verdict only when its decisive cycle is faster than the floor, F passes by direct averaging, the theoretical center lies inside every observed swing and L4 passes; otherwise the first verdict stays (columns geo_subfloor_*). The cap short_period_aliased keeps reading the 150-yr floor; three-body angles have no computed theory and are never eligible (the forced 115–121-yr waves of 52356 and 23240). 2001 VC2 16E-17: \(T_{0,\text{th}}\) = 112 yr, a 105-yr libration over 20 kyr → resonant / libration / medium (the alias cap).

C. Circulation. The center of \(\sigma\) runs through a full turn.

  • If the sampled angle is an alias (the true rate \(\nu\) folded by the output step), the record can still exclude a libration when the alias branch is the same over the whole range of \(a\) and the body is far from the resonance: the far ratio (the distance \(|\langle a\rangle - a_*|\) over half the \(a\)-range, or over the offset of the \(a\) implied by the measured mean motion when that is larger; signal) is at least MMR_C5_FAR_RATIO_MIN = 3 (rule C5). Then non_resonant / alias; otherwise a libration may hide behind the step: invalid / alias, action resample.
  • If a member of the multiplet has a librating verdict of its own, the row takes the member's status (as in step 1 below).
  • If \(\sigma\) turns back at times but the energy measured from \(a\) does not follow a potential of \(\sigma\) (R0 fails): non_resonant / no_resonant_potential.
  • G4c, one 1:1 leg (MMR_COORBITAL_SINGLE_LEG). A co-orbital angle without a librating episode is judged on its single legs: the stretches of the orbit-averaged angle between two reversals, outside every accepted run, that do not sweep a turn and whose period \(2L\) is at least the floor less CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND. Each leg is read against the averaged potential (Local force and energy on a single leg): is it one swing of a co-orbital well (tadpole, horseshoe, quasi-satellite, not a lap past the planet), does its local 1:1 law hold with \(K > 0\), is its energy conserved, and is each turn a reflection (\(|\ln(\text{out}/\text{in})| \le\) MMR_COORBITAL_TURN_ENERGY_TOL, zone \(\le\) MMR_COORBITAL_TURN_ZONE_MAX)?
  • everything holds → transient / dynamic_episode, cap one_coorbital_leg (≤ medium): 2023 OE5, 586–665 yr;
  • one discrepancy → uncertain / one_coorbital_leg, action review (2018 KS: a lap past the Earth at 779–934 yr);
  • a clean leg cut by the record edge whose observed turn reflects → uncertain / baseline_needed, angle word insufficient_time, action extend;
  • both turns are kicks → the circulation below, with the cap near_episode (1991 VG: out/in 0.61 and 1.59); a turn that would reflect but for a zone within CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND above MMR_COORBITAL_TURN_ZONE_MAX is no kick: uncertain / one_coorbital_leg, review (2020 FN3: zones 1.11 and 1.15 against 1.1);
  • no leg at all (one reflection between passages, 2008 EZ84) → the circulation below, unchanged.

The strongest outcome among the legs decides (transient > uncertain > extend > near-episode). The legs of an accepted episode are never read again: its turns already closed a cycle. MMR_COORBITAL_LEG_FORCE_GATE (off) reads a failed 1:1 law as a kick instead of a discrepancy. - G4h, one half-swing of another resonance (MMR_SINGLE_HALF_LIBRATION, not 1:1). A bounded half-swing between two passages over the top (or a passage and the record edge), at least the floor less the thin band long, that follows the resonance's own one-harmonic law (\(\dot a = A\sin\sigma + B\cos\sigma + C\) with \(R^2 \ge\) MMR_FORCE_R2_FAIL on each half of its window, the force turning \(\sigma\) back at both turns) → uncertain / one_half_libration (review); at the record edge uncertain / baseline_needed, extend (42946 43S-6). A slow wide turn of a circulation does not follow that law and stays a circulation. - Otherwise non_resonant / circulation; an owner found for a circulating angle only names its origin.

1. Is a member of the multiplet librating instead? A resonance \(k\lambda + \sum k_j\lambda_j + p\varpi + \dots\) comes with members that differ by \(m(\varpi_P - \varpi)\) or by node terms (Morbidelli 2002, §9.3–9.4). If one member has a fixed center while \(\sigma\)'s center moves with \(\varpi_P - \varpi\), the libration belongs to that member: the catalog row takes the member's own status (an invalid member makes it uncertain), reason = subresonance_librates, origin subresonance, owner = the member, and also the member's confidence (Confidence); its angle_status stays its own. An accepted member without a verdict of its own gives non_resonant / subresonance_librates. When the catalog angle and the member both librate over the record, each keeps its own verdict. Example: 82831 13M-24.

2. Does another resonance drive \(a\)? The owner search looks for another commensurability \(\phi_o\) whose force explains \(\dot a\) better than \(\sigma\)'s own term. Since \(\dot\sigma \simeq c\,(a - a_*)\) holds for any oscillation of \(a\), an \(a\) driven by \(\phi_o\) makes \(\sigma\) oscillate too: an induced libration. The owner is accepted only if its intervals cover at least MMR_OWNER_COVER_MIN = 0.5 of \(\sigma\)'s decisive episode; then non_resonant / induced_libration, origin induced. The detail says whether the owner librates (owner_libration) or circulates at the oscillation's period (owner_forced_wave). Examples: 117306, 1997 GK3. The exception: when the remainder \(x = \Psi/u\) closes cycles of a well of its own ('both resonances at once?' confirmed, Response), the tree goes on and the row keeps its own reading with origin joint; one such cycle gives uncertain / baseline_needed, origin joint.

3. Does \(a\) carry the oscillation at all? In a resonance the swing of \(a\) follows from the swing of \(\sigma\): \(\delta a \simeq \delta\dot\sigma/|c|\). If \(a\) carries less than MMR_B1_RATIO_MIN = 0.1 of that (test B1), or the cycle runs at a secular period of the body (the \(e\)-cycle \(2\pi/|g - g_5|\) or the \(2\omega\) cycle, within MMR_KIN_PERIOD_TOL = 0.1) while the identity and every force law fail, the bound comes from the geometry of the angle (its \(p\varpi\) part, a secular cycle): non_resonant / kinematic_libration, origin kinematic. When the slow center itself follows the \(\lambda\) part plus the secular part (correlation of rates ≥ MMR_KIN_CORR_MIN = 0.9, over at least MMR_KIN_MIN_POINTS = 3 independent points), \(a\) does not answer (every force law fails, measured on at least MMR_FORCE_MIN_WINDOWS = 2 windows) and the librating stretches are only a ripple on it (their swing below MMR_KIN_RIPPLE_SHARE_MAX = 0.5 of the center's range), or a kinematic libration's center moves more than MMR_KIN_DRIFT_SHIFT_RATIO = 1 amplitude: non_resonant / kinematic_drift. If a libration slower than the record cannot be excluded and the center's rate is consistent with an exact commensurability (within MMR_B5_EXACT_SIGMA = 2 standard errors, B5): uncertain / baseline_needed. The kinematic drift is rule K2 (rec_rule 3k2), the exact commensurability rec_rule 3b5. Examples: 285637, 62243.

K3s, after the leaf: a circulation whose slow scale is a secular cycle. A non_resonant / circulation (no mechanism named, not 1:1) whose slow scale has the period of a secular cycle (within MMR_KIN_PERIOD_TOL) and fails its own identity becomes non_resonant / kinematic_libration, origin kinematic, detail secular_cycle (rec_rule K3s, MMR_SECULAR_CYCLE_KINEMATIC), whatever B1 or a thin L4. Only where the slow libration is the record's regime: the center leaves it by slips of one turn (largest monotone pass ≤ 1 + LIBRATION_SLIP_TOLERANCE rev); a center that circulates several turns in a row stays a circulation (285637 2 Myr, 4.7 rev). The status and the level stay those of the circulation; a librating row is never demoted. Example: 37087 3J+8S-3 (100 kyr and 1 Myr).

4. A drift without a cause. angle_status = drift with no kinematic explanation: uncertain / drift_mechanism_unknown. Example: 142694.

5. Is the libration this resonance's own force? Three measurements can show it (Is it this resonance?): the force law L4 (\(\dot a\) follows \(\sin(\sigma - \varphi_0)\)), the potential R0 (the energy \(\tfrac12\dot\sigma^2 + V(\sigma)\) built from \(a\) is conserved cycle by cycle) and the strength F (the force needed for the observed period against the force the disturbing function gives). Their combinations:

leaf measurements status / reason origin 5f L4 cannot be told from a forced line of the angle's lattice at the same period, and the \(\sigma\)-only potential test does not fail uncertain / origin_unknown (flag force_law_contaminated) unknown 5s L4 and R0 do not pass, and the period needs ≥ MMR_STRENGTH_IMPLAUSIBLE_RATIO = \(10^3\) × the strength computed from the disturbing function (two-body: direct or harmonic, not centre_outside_well unless MMR_STRENGTH_FIRST_OUTSIDE_WELL; three-body: \(\mu_i\mu_j e^q\) with the small-divisor residual still ≥ \(10^3\)); cap ≤ low non_resonant / implausible_strength unknown 5a L4 fails, R0 does not pass (5a* when R0 is not measured rather than failed) uncertain / origin_unknown unknown 5b L4 passes, R0 fails uncertain / origin_unknown (flag force_law_disagrees) unknown 5e R0 fails, L4 not measured uncertain / origin_unknown unknown 5g L4 and R0 not measured, the identity fails on an episode and passes on none uncertain / origin_unknown unknown 5c → 6 L4 fails, R0 passes by the behavior (below), cap force_law_disagrees dynamic 5d → 6 L4 passes and R0 does not fail; or R0 passes and L4 is not measured; or (a near_separatrix angle) neither is measured and nothing objects by the behavior (below) dynamic

A failed \(\sigma\)-only potential test (period law or fixed well, no \(\dot a\) in it) stays an objection even when L4 is contaminated: the tree then skips 5f and goes on through 5s and the other leaves.

For an angle of the near_separatrix type, the leaves 5a, 5e and 5g give non_resonant instead: no_resonant_potential, or modulated_circulation when the angle only slows down periodically (pattern B).

On an output step that folds short periods into slow ones, a failed L4 or identity is read as not measured when the directly averaged strength F passes and the short-period scatter of \(a\) exceeds MMR_SHORT_PERIOD_A_RATIO = 0.5 of the libration's half-swing in \(a\): the folded terms, not the dynamics, spoil the fit.

The unmeasured branch. When neither L4 nor R0 could be measured (a small amplitude, one force window) and \(\sigma\) librates, the first leaf that holds:

leaf condition status / reason origin 5d → 6 the strength computed by direct averaging passes, required / theory within [1/x, x], x = MMR_STRENGTH_CHECK_RATIO = 10 by the behavior dynamic 5s the period needs ≥ \(10^3\) × the strength (two-body: direct averaging; three-body: \(\mu_i\mu_j e^q\) even after the small-divisor envelope) non_resonant / implausible_strength unknown 5s* three-body ratio ≥ \(10^3\), but the envelope could close the gap uncertain / origin_unknown unknown 5o a measured objection: an episodic angle, whose episodes do not lie in the separatrix zone, with a strong \(a\)-wave already before the episode (O1 ≥ MMR_O1_RATIO_FAIL = 0.5, O1); or F by direct averaging fails uncertain / origin_unknown unknown 5x the order-of-magnitude strength (\(\mu_i\mu_j e^q\), three-body and 1:1) lies outside [1/x, x]: a scale known to a factor 1–100 is a diagnostic, no objection; origin not established (79653 3M+3J-7: 39.5 ×) uncertain / origin_unknown unknown 5n the decisive episode has fewer than LIBRATION_CENTRE_MIN_ESTIMATES = 2 independent cycles uncertain / origin_unknown unknown 5u → 6 nothing measured by the behavior, reason geometric_libration / geometric_episode, cap ≤ low (geometry_only) or ≤ medium (strength_scale_only, when the order-of-magnitude strength agrees) unknown

Two kinds of uncertain / origin_unknown leaves: a measurement contradicts the angle's own dynamics (5a, 5b, 5e's failed R0, 5g's failed identity, 5o), or nothing was measured (5n, 5x). Where the only missing measurement is missing for lack of length, the action is extend, not review (Actions).

6. By the observed behavior. When the force is measured, or nothing objects, the angle's own behavior gives the status:

angle (as the tree reads it) status reason (force measured) reason (geometry only, 5u) libration resonant dynamic_libration geometric_libration episodic transient dynamic_episode geometric_episode near_separatrix near_separatrix separatrix_zone — (the branch applies to librating angles only)

The separatrix zone and the energies of the cycles add flags here (libration_in_separatrix_zone, episodes_in_separatrix_zone) and confidence evidence; the zone never relabels a geometric libration as near_separatrix. It has one indirect effect on the status: episodes in the zone bypass the O1 objection (leaf 5o) of the unmeasured branch.

6u. A union of episodes. Librating episodes that together cover the record, with no circulation between them, are read first as episodic. Only if that reading reaches transient / dynamic_episode with a measured force (leaf 6, origin dynamic) is the record promoted to resonant / dynamic_libration (rec_rule gets the suffix u: 5d/6u). Every other outcome stays as it is. (For a co-orbital 1:1 angle the union is a libration directly: its episodes are the tadpole, horseshoe and quasi-satellite regimes of one resonance.)

After the tree. A non-resonant verdict next to a run of turning points one turn short of an episode (LIBRATION_NEAR_EPISODE_TP_DEFICIT = 1) and at least the floor less CONFIDENCE_THIN_BAND long gets the flag and cap near_episode; for a 1:1 angle such a run may also be one rejected over the top, when each of its half-swings crosses at most one of the planet and L3 (rule coorbital_near_episode); an owner search run on catalog planet longitudes caps the level (catalogue_longitudes). These change the confidence, not the status.

The columns libration_origin, origin_detail and owner are described in Output data; the leaf that decided is the column rec_rule of mmr_numbers.csv (5d/6, 5u/6, 3k2, C5, …).

Files before 2026-10-26 wrote dynamic_libration / dynamic_episode also for the geometric leaf (origin unknown). This renamed the reason only; it was not a new classification. Since 1.0 the package reads only the format it writes: a run of an earlier version is not restored (run it again).

docs.title: The reported angle word
docs.text:
The tree reads the angle as the status needs it; the reported angle_status describes what \(\sigma\) did over the whole record. They differ in four cases:

  • Episodes, then another regime. Librating episodes followed by a circulation, by a regime after a jump of \(a\), or a capture after a jump: reported episodic (recurrent with two or more episodes); how the record ends goes to final_regime (circulation, libration, …).
  • A union of episodes. Episodes covering the record together are reported libration (subtype regime_change) whatever the status: \(\sigma\) never went round.
  • A kinematic drift of the slow center. The word follows the mechanism, not the ripple: drift, or circulation when the center's largest monotone pass reaches a full turn or its net shift reaches LIBRATION_CIRCULATION_NET_REV = 2 turns (MMR_KINEMATIC_DRIFT_WORD = True).
  • Forced waves. Runs that are forced waves of another argument are not episodes for the status. If the record would otherwise be reported circulation or drift while \(\sigma\) loops in those runs, the librating word is reported.
  • Forced (strength). On a row decided by 5s (not 5s*) every accepted run is marked a forced wave of route strength once the verdict is made (MMR_FORCED_WAVE_STRENGTH): its period needs a force ≥ \(10^3\) times the one the disturbing function gives, so it is no libration of this angle. The mark names that ground, not a driver; nothing is measured again, and the status, word, reason and level stay as they are.

Only the output changes; the margins and the confidence read the angle as the tree did.

docs.title: How the record's edges end
docs.text:
After the tree, the MMR verdict reads how \(\sigma_f\) meets the record's edges (rule end_arc_extend, MMR_RECORD_EDGE_STRETCH). The edge pass is the stretch from the slow center's turn nearest the edge (or the other edge without one) to the edge.

  • End arc after circulation. The pass holds at least one revolution, and after its last completed one \(\sigma_f\) stays \(D\) to the end without completing another, with \(D >\) MMR_END_ARC_SLOWDOWN_FACTOR (2) × the pass's longest revolution and \(2D \ge\) MMR_END_ARC_MIN_FLOOR_PERIODS (1) × the floor, no librating episode in it. A circulation whose rate depends on \(\sigma\) alone completes the next revolution sooner than a full one takes, so this is a slowdown. final_regime becomes arc (range ≥ π) or stall from the last revolution, when it was empty or circulation, and the flag extend_time is set forward. A non_resonant / circulation verdict there gets the cap record_ends_unresolved (≤ medium): the record ends before it shows whether \(\sigma\) circulates on or is captured (2022 BB2: 600 yr after 52-yr revolutions).
  • Flag only. The same slowdown at the start, one reflection of the slow center cut by an edge (less than a revolution between the turn and the edge, at least one beyond it: 2008 EZ84 before 144 yr), a clean 1:1 edge leg whose turn reflects (G4c's extend) and an edge half-libration that holds its law (G4h) set extend_time with the direction of their edge (backward at the start, forward at the end, both); a window that starts at a jump of \(a\) has no record start to extend. One reflection is no cycle: no cap.

The flag changes no status and no level, whatever the action. extend_direction gives the direction and extend_to_years the length: the next check without an estimate, round_up(2T) (with action extend the action's length stays). The words libration, drift, insufficient_time and undefined already say how the record ends: no edge stretch is read under them.

docs.title: Secular and Lidov-Kozai angles
docs.text: Secular and Lidov-Kozai angles use their own shorter tree, without an owner, a subresonance or a force law step: geometry and status and, for Lidov-Kozai, the free-ω gate. A secular libration makes only a few cycles in a record, so which runs are its episodes is read as for an MMR but with four rules of its own (IDs G2p, G2t, G2w, G2e in the rule index): each run of turning points takes its own prominence; a bounded run whose center turns back once is modulated; an episode that is a wave on a slower motion of the angle does not count (secular only; the slower scale decides); and \(\sigma_f\) running a turn or more after the last turning point is an observed exit (transient, final_regime circulation), not a libration that goes on past the record.

docs.title: Legacy integer codes
docs.text:
Old runs stored one integer per angle. The column status_code keeps it for comparison only:

code MMR secular / ZLK 2 resonant resonant 1 transient transient 0 non_resonant (kinematic, induced, subresonance and alias included) non_resonant (circulation) −2 — non_resonant / kinematic_libration (ZLK: the gate measured a kinematic libration) −3 near_separatrix near_separatrix (old files) −4 — uncertain / insufficient_time −6 uncertain / baseline_needed uncertain / drift −9 other uncertain other uncertain (ZLK: gate_unavailable) −99 invalid invalid

−2 and −9 are different

−2 is a measurement (the free \(\omega\) was found to wind: the libration is geometry); −9 is the absence of one (the gate could not judge). Never merge them in a statistic.
